Koeppen's scheme is built on temperature and precipitation and linked to natural vegetation, which is why natural vegetation is called the true index of climate. Thornthwaite's scheme uses precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency.
Koeppen's Cfa is the humid subtropical type (warm temperate C, no dry season f, hot summer a). Tropical wet is Af, tropical wet and dry is Aw, and tundra is ET.
The kiwi is a flightless bird native to and found only in New Zealand, not in Australia, the Philippines or North America.
Silk produced by spiders is called gossamer silk (fine spider-web silk). Tussar and Muga are silkworm silks, and Ahimsa is peace silk, so they are wrong.

Karnataka is the largest raw silk producer (statement I true) and tropical tasar is led by Jharkhand and other states (III true). Andhra Pradesh is only 2nd, not the largest mulberry producer (II false), and Eri is mainly Assam, not Meghalaya (IV false).
Blue Revolution relates to fish production (pisciculture), not poultry, so 'Blue – Poultry' is the wrongly matched pair. The other pairs are correct.
Mount Everest lies on the Nepal–China (Tibet) border, in the Nepal Himalaya; of the options, Nepal is the expected answer.
Santosh Yadav, an Indian mountaineer, was the first woman to climb Mount Everest twice (1992 and 1993). The notes do not cover this fact.
K2 (Godwin Austen) is often given as India's highest peak, since it lies in claimed territory. Kamet, Nanda Kot and Nanda Devi are lower.
Everest is 8,848 m, Nanga Parbat 8,126 m and Nanda Devi 7,817 m. Kanchenjunga is about 8,586–8,598 m, which leaves option 4 and gives A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.
K2 is often given as India's highest peak, since it lies in claimed territory. Kanchenjunga is the highest under Indian control, and Everest and Kailash are not in India.

Bandarpunch feeds the Yamuna, Bara Shigri the Chenab, and Siachen the Nubra, so I, II and IV are correct. Milam is in Kumaon, not the Mandakini source, and Zemu is in Sikkim, feeding the Teesta rather than the Manas. The notes do not state these links.
Milam is a Kumaon Himalaya glacier in Uttarakhand. Hispar is in Gilgit-Baltistan and Zemu is in Sikkim.
Nathu La in Sikkim was the route for Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims until China halted it in 2017. Zoji La and Khardung La are in Ladakh.
West to east, the passes run Banihal (J&K), Mana (Uttarakhand), Nathu La (Sikkim), Bum La (Arunachal).
The September 2014 India–China agreement opened a new Kailash-Mansarovar route through Nathu La in Sikkim.

Indira Point, in Great Nicobar, lies at about 6°45'N, so statement III is true. Climate elements and the difference between day lengths both vary with latitude, so I and II are also true; hence all three are correct.

The Tropic of Capricorn is at 23.5°S, not 66½°N, so II is wrong. The International Date Line follows roughly 180° longitude, not 0° (the Prime Meridian), so III is wrong. I and IV are correct, so the wrongly matched pair is II and III.
The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S) passes through Chile, Brazil, South Africa and Australia, and also through Namibia. All four listed countries are crossed, so the answer is All of these.
The Prime Meridian passes through Algeria, France and Spain, but not Niger. Niger lies on the Tropic of Cancer instead.
The Arctic Circle crosses Norway, Sweden and Finland, but Iceland lies just south of it.
The 24°N parallel passes through more Indian states than the other options, because it runs across the broad middle of the country from Gujarat to the north-east. The notes do not cover this fact.
The point 0°, 0° lies in the Gulf of Guinea in the Atlantic Ocean, south of Ghana, so the South Atlantic Ocean option is correct.
The Tropic of Capricorn passes through Chile, Paraguay and Brazil, but not Bolivia, which lies north of it.
Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar mission, an orbiter plus Moon Impact Probe, i.e. a lunar probe. It was not manned, not a Mars mission and not a telescope.
India was the 4th to reach the Moon with an impact probe, after USSR, USA and Japan. Of the options, only Japan had landed one earlier.
Chandrayaan-1 was launched from SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota, which is in Andhra Pradesh.
The Chandrayaan-2 lander was named Vikram and the rover Pragyan. So Vikram is the correct option and Pragyan is the rover.
Chandrayaan-3 kept the Chandrayaan-2 names: the lander is Vikram and the rover is Pragyan. Option 1 swaps the two.
Pragyan's LIBS confirmed sulphur on the lunar surface in August 2023. The other listed elements were not the ones confirmed.
India became the 4th country to soft-land on the Moon, after the US, Russia and China.
Mangalyaan, India's first interplanetary mission to Mars, was launched on 5 Nov 2013 by PSLV-C25.

Mangalyaan is the Mars Orbiter Mission, and India was the first country to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt. Statement II is wrong because India was the 4th agency after NASA, Roscosmos and ESA, not the second after the USA.
India was the first country to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt. The other listed countries did not manage this on their first attempt.
Vidya Balan played a lead role in 'Mission Mangal', the film based on India's Mars Orbiter Mission.
Under the 17 SDGs, Goal 2 is Zero Hunger (Goal 1 is No Poverty, Goal 4 Quality Education, Goal 5 Gender Equality).
Namami Gange is matched with SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), along with Swachh Bharat and Jal Jeevan Mission.
Namami Gange is an SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) programme, so SDG 6 is correct.
No Poverty matches PM Garib Kalyan Yojana, Clean Energy matches PM Ujjwala, Health matches Ayushman Bharat, and Education matches Samagra Shiksha, giving A–i, B–ii, C–iii, D–iv.
Kerala topped the SDG India Index 2020-21, but the notes do not state this edition's leader; they only give Kerala first in 2019-20 and Kerala and Uttarakhand top in 2023-24.
In the SDG India Index 2020-21 the country scored below 50 on Goal 2 (Zero Hunger) and Goal 5 (Gender Equality), so these need special attention.
India's composite score in the 2020-21 (3rd) edition was 66, up from 60 in 2019-20, which is the 6-point rise.
The 6-point rise in 2020-21 was driven by Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy).
MoSPI develops the National Indicator Framework for SDGs; NITI Aayog only coordinates SDG work and publishes the SDG India Index.

NMP 2011 aimed at 12-14% manufacturing growth, 100 million additional jobs and enhanced global competitiveness, so statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. A 25% per annum export growth target is not part of its stated objectives; 25% refers to the GDP share target.
The National Manufacturing Policy was released on 4 November 2011, so 2011 is correct.
Make in India is nodally implemented by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), so option 1 is correct. The Ministry of Heavy Industries runs schemes like PM E-DRIVE, not Make in India.
Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014, so September 2014 is correct.
Make in India was launched in September 2014, not 2018, so statement I is wrong. Statement II (fostering innovation) is a stated objective of the initiative, so only II is correct.
The National Capital Goods Policy 2016 aims to raise domestic capital goods production and boost technology depth, not to increase imports of capital goods. So increasing imports is not a feature.
India is the second-largest mobile phone producer after China, a position retained in 2023, so 2nd is correct.
The ACI EDB Index 2018 ranked Andhra Pradesh 1st, Maharashtra 2nd and Delhi 3rd, matching option 3.
Andhra Pradesh has ranked 1st in the state ease of doing business rankings in several editions (2017, 2019 and consistently later), so 1st is correct.
The Advocate General is the highest law officer of the State and the official legal adviser to the State Government. The Attorney General serves the Union, not the State.
The Advocate General's remuneration is fixed by the Governor. It is not tied to the pay of a High Court judge, the Chief Secretary or a State minister.

Mukul Rohatgi is not the current Attorney General, so the statement is incorrect. The other three statements are correct: the AG is appointed by the President, appears for the Union in Supreme Court cases, and is the highest law officer.
Fa-hien's main interest was Buddhism: he came to visit Buddhist sites and collect Buddhist texts, not to study administration, women or peasants. He did not even name the king.
Fa-hien recorded a free hospital at Pataliputra funded by citizens, giving poor patients doctors, food and medicine. Tamralipti was only his port of departure.
The notes do not mention Medhatithi or his view on Shudras. Medhatithi, the commentator on Manusmriti, is the post-Gupta jurist credited with saying Shudras are not slaves by nature.
Gupta-era production centres in Gujarat (Lata), Bengal, the Deccan and the Tamil country were known for textiles, and textiles were a main export. Gems are not tied to these regions in the same way.
The fall of the West Roman Empire is the standard cause given for the decline of North Indian trade. The other options are not supported as causes.

Gradual decline of towns is a recognised feature of the Gupta period, with towns like Mathura, Hastinapur and Kaushambi declining and Pataliputra becoming a village. The other periods listed are not characterised this way.

The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed on 21 October 1943, and the INA (Azad Hind Fauj) was its army, so the question's date matches this option. The INA was first raised in 1942, but of the given options 21 October 1943 is the intended answer.
The Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) was proclaimed on 21 October 1943 at Singapore, not Rangoon, Tokyo, Berlin or Rome.
The Red Fort trial accused were Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sehgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon. Mohan Singh did not face the trials, which rules out the other options.
Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the Father of India's space programme; Nambi Narayanan and Madhavan Nair were ISRO scientists/chairman, and Kalam is the Missile Man.
PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) was proposed by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Har Gobind Khorana achieved the laboratory synthesis of DNA and the first synthetic gene; Miller did the origin-of-life experiment.
Panchanan Maheshwari is known for plant embryology and popularised embryological characters in taxonomy. Birbal Sahni was a palaeobotanist.
The mutation theory of evolution was put forward by Hugo de Vries, based on his work on evening primrose. Darwin proposed natural selection and Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired characters.
Sarabhai is the Father of the Indian space programme, Guru Gopi Krishna is linked with Kuchipudi, M.F. Husain is the Picasso of India and Amjad Ali Khan plays the sarod, so the code is 1 2 3 4.
Dilma Rousseff, President of Brazil, was impeached and removed from office by the Brazilian Senate in 2016. The notes do not cover this.

Rajya Sabha members are indirectly elected by the elected MLAs of the State Legislative Assemblies using STV. Lok Sabha members are directly elected, and the Chief Justice of a High Court and the Attorney General are appointed by the President.
Madhya Pradesh has no Legislative Council; the 7th Amendment allowed one but it was never created. UP, Bihar and Karnataka are among the six bicameral States.
Delhi (Art 239AA) and Puducherry (Art 239A) have their own legislative assemblies. Chandigarh and Daman and Diu do not, so the other pairs are wrong.
The PAC is described as the 'Watchdog' on departmental expenditure and irregularities. The Estimates Committee is instead the 'continuous economy committee'.
Ecology is the study of relationships between organisms and their environment, as the notes state; the other options are not what ecology studies.
The notes do not mention who first used the concept of 'ecological transition', so no line settles it. Bennett is the given answer.
The term 'ecology' was coined by Ernst Haeckel in 1866; Tansley coined 'ecosystem', not ecology.
The ecological order runs organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere, so population, community, ecosystem (then a larger unit) is the correct sequence.
Autecology is the study of a single species in relation to its environmental factors, whereas synecology studies communities. The notes do not cover this term.
The term 'deep ecology' was coined by the Norwegian philosopher Arne Naess (1973). The notes do not cover it.
Environment covers the natural surroundings and conditions of organisms, and is an interacting system of physical, biological and cultural elements, so all the definitions hold.
Environment is composite: biotic and abiotic factors interact, including physical and chemical elements, so all the listed factors are part of it.
Bionomics is synonymous with ecology and stresses the value of natural systems that influence human systems. 'Management of life' is not its meaning, so statement I is wrong.
Organisms must maintain body water balance to survive, and terrestrial life cannot tolerate high dissolved salts, which is why it needs fresh water. R therefore explains A.
Niche is the functional role of a species in its habitat, and it is unique to a species while many species share a habitat, so both statements are correct.
The fundamental niche is the full range of biotic and abiotic conditions and resources a species could use free from other species, so the answer is niche.
Hydrophytes are plants adapted to living in water, i.e. aquatic plants. They are not necessarily rootless, since the lotus is rooted.
Enzymes are the biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in living systems. Bacteria are organisms, and DNA and proteins in general do not define this catalytic role.

Histones are basic proteins found in the nucleus, where DNA wraps around them to form nucleosomes and chromatin. They are not in mitochondrial membranes or the cytosol bound to lipids or carbohydrates.
A change in the base sequence of a gene is a mutation. Transversion is only one specific type of base substitution, and conjugation and reproduction are unrelated processes.
RNA contains uracil in place of thymine, which is found in DNA. Adenine and guanine occur in both RNA and DNA.
The gene is the basic functional unit of heredity, a DNA segment that codes for a trait. A chromosome and DNA are carriers or larger structures, and the nucleus is only the organelle containing them.

Mapping gene positions helps trace livestock pedigree and breed disease-resistant animals, so I and III are correct. Statement II is wrong because it claims to explain the causes of all human diseases, and many diseases have non-genetic causes.
DNA is the genetic material that stores and passes on hereditary information. Enzymes and hormones do not carry hereditary information, and RNA mainly carries the message for protein synthesis.
DNA stores and transmits information because its two strands are complementary (A–T, G–C), so each strand can serve as a template for copying.

The British Committee of the INC was formed in London in 1889 with William Wedderburn as its chairman, so Wedderburn is correct. Naoroji helped found it but was not the chairman, and Bonnerjee was not its head.
Naoroji, G. Subramania Iyer and R.C. Dutt were all economic critics of colonialism, so all three statements hold. Hence option 4 is correct.

The early Congress aimed at self-government within the Empire and did not demand complete independence. Purna Swaraj was therefore not a demand of 1885-1905, whereas Indianisation of services and autonomy within the empire were.
The Moderates used prayers, petitions and protests, a strictly constitutional agitation. They distrusted mass action, so non-cooperation and civil disobedience do not fit.
Article 261(1) gives full faith and credit throughout India to the public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State.
The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263; Art. 262 deals with river water disputes.
Article 262(1) lets Parliament provide for adjudication of inter-State river water disputes. Art. 263 is the Inter-State Council.
Under Art. 304(b), a State bill imposing restrictions on inter-State trade needs the previous sanction of the President. So the bill cannot be moved without the President's sanction.
The Inter-State Council is established by the President under Art. 263 (by Presidential order, 1990), not by Parliament, the NDC or a Zonal Council.
The Inter-State Council decides all questions by consensus, not by any majority vote.
The 27th Southern Zonal Council meeting (2016) was chaired by Union Home Minister Rajnath Singh. Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister.
Both statements are true: Zonal Councils are described as sub-federal links that promote co-operation and integration among States. The notes do not state this directly.
Alam Ara (1931), by Ardeshir Irani, was the first Indian sound film. Kalidas is not the answer here, and the other two are later films.
Dadasaheb Phalke's Raja Harishchandra, India's first full-length feature film (silent), was made in 1913. The notes name the film but do not give the year.
Devika Rani married the Russian painter Svetoslav Roerich in 1945. The notes do not cover this.
Chiranjeevi received the Indian Film Personality of the Year award in 2022 at the 53rd IFFI, so (4) is correct.
Mahanati won the National Film Award for Best Telugu Film at the 66th National Film Awards. The notes do not state this.
K. Viswanath received the Phalke Award for 2016 and is the last Telugu awardee. Akkineni Nageswara Rao got it in 1990 and D. Ramanaidu in 2009.
Ramanand Sagar produced and directed the TV serial Ramayan (1987-88) on Doordarshan. B.R. Chopra is known for Mahabharat.
The notes do not give Kerala's share of rubber production. Kerala accounts for more than 90 percent of India's rubber output, which is why option 4 is correct.
Gestation in the goat is about 150 days, much shorter than the cow (about 280 days), donkey (about 12 months) or camel (about 13 months). So the goat carries its young for the shortest period.
Capra hircus is the scientific name of the domestic goat. Sheep is Ovis aries, cow is Bos taurus and horse is Equus caballus.
Holstein (Holstein-Friesian) is the world's highest milk-yielding dairy breed. Brown Swiss, Dutch Belted and Blaarkop give less milk.

Inland fisheries mean raising and capturing fish in fresh water (and brackish water) bodies such as rivers, tanks and reservoirs. Deep-sea or coastal fishing is marine fishing, so the other options are wrong.
Pisciculture is the raising of fish, i.e. fish farming. Sericulture is silk, mariculture is farming of marine organisms in the sea, and horticulture is fruits and vegetables.
The Act has 12 Parts, 108 sections and 13 Schedules.
The Act is structured into 12 Parts, 108 sections and 13 Schedules, so 13 is correct.
The Act is structured into 12 Parts, 108 sections and 13 Schedules, so 13 is correct.
The Act has 12 Parts, 108 sections and 13 Schedules.
Part V covers authorisation of expenditure and distribution of revenues; Part VI is assets and liabilities.
The President gave assent on 1 March 2014; 2 June 2014 was the appointed day.
Assent was given on 1 March 2014; 2 June 2014 is the appointed day when the split took effect, so it is the tempting wrong option.
The President's assent came on 1 March 2014, i.e. in March 2014.
The President assented on 1 March 2014.
The Act was assented to on 1 March 2014 (not 2 March); the split followed on 2 June 2014.
The appointed day for the territorial split was 2 June 2014; 1 March 2014 was only the date of assent.
The Greyhound Training Centre in Hyderabad is a common training centre for a maximum of three years.
Under Section 8 the common Governor is assisted by two advisors appointed by the Centre.
Section 95 provides equal opportunities for quality higher education.
Section 79 is the provision on continuance of officers in the same posts, but the notes do not state it.
The notes list 13 districts of 2014 for AP, with 175 seats in total.
Section 26 allows the AP Assembly to be raised from 175 to 225 after delimitation, subject to Article 170.

The notes describe the tropopause as the boundary between the troposphere and stratosphere that caps weather and vertical mixing, which fits 'zone of mixing'. The 8 km figure is for the poles, not the equator, so option 4 is wrong.

Temperature falls with height in the troposphere at the normal lapse rate of about 6.5°C per km, so option 4 (6.4°C, approximately) is the only option describing a decrease. Option 3 wrongly says it increases, and the stratosphere warms with height, so options 1 and 2 are wrong.
High insolation at the equator drives strong convection that lifts the tropopause, making the atmosphere thickest there (16-18 km). So both A and R are true and R explains A.
Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation from the Sun, shielding life on Earth. It does not supply oxygen or control Earth's temperature.
Excess UV radiation causes skin cancer (dermal cancer), cataract and weaker immunity. The other cancers listed are not linked to UV.
The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV-B and UV-C), not cosmic rays or infrared.
SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) is the share of NDTL that banks keep in liquid form such as cash, gold and G-secs, held by the bank itself. The other options are not real terms.
CRR is the share of NDTL kept as cash with the RBI, so option 2 (balances with the RBI) is right. Holding liquid assets describes SLR, not CRR.
SLR is the mechanism by which banks provide credit to the Government, since they hold G-secs to meet it. LAF is a liquidity tool and the other options are not real mechanisms.
CRR is fixed by the RBI, the central bank, not the Finance Ministry or the market.
The 'Required reserve ratio' means CRR, the share of deposits (NDTL) banks must keep as reserves with the RBI. The other options describe unrelated things.
The share of NDTL that banks must keep with the RBI is the Cash Reserve Ratio. SLR is kept by the bank itself.
Raising CRR leaves banks with less lendable money and reduces liquidity, so credit creation falls. It is a tight (contractionary) policy, not a liberal one.
A higher bank rate makes borrowing costlier and tightens money, so it signals a tight money policy. A lower bank rate is the expansionary one.
Buying G-secs through OMO injects liquidity and lowers interest rates. Raising reserve requirements or cutting money supply would tighten and raise rates.

Central bank purchase of securities (I) and government borrowing from the central bank (III) create new money and raise money supply. Deposits of currency (II) only shift money into banks, and sale of securities (IV) reduces money supply.
OMO means the RBI both buys and sells G-secs, so the answer is sale and purchase.
A higher CRR means banks must keep more of their NDTL as cash with the RBI, leaving them less to lend. The RBI and the Government are not affected in this way.
Singrauli region straddles MP and Sonbhadra (UP); the notes place the Singrauli area (Sonbhadra) in UP, so the Singrauli region is the UP coal area.

The notes only say Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves and give no full state ranking, so this order cannot be verified from them; the correct order is Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal.
Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves among the states, so it is the biggest reserve.
Namchik-Namphuk is a Tertiary coalfield in Arunachal Pradesh (Tirap/Changlang); the notes do not cover it.
Tamil Nadu produces the most lignite (48.65% of output), ahead of Gujarat and Rajasthan.
Odisha is currently the largest coal-producing state in India (ahead of Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand); the notes give no production ranking.
Fluids settle by density in a trap: water at the bottom, then oil, then gas/air on top, so the ascending order is water, oil, air.
Digboi in Assam is the oldest oil town, with commercial production from 1889, so it is the oldest oil field; Bombay High, Ankleshwar and Navagam were developed much later.
India's strategic petroleum reserves are at Padur, Visakhapatnam and Mangaluru; Ankleshwar was not selected, so it is the answer.
Tilak was radical in politics, demanding Swaraj, yet socially orthodox; he opposed the Age of Consent Bill. Gokhale and Lajpat Rai were not described this way.
Lajpat Rai was the first to use the safety-valve theory (in Young India) to attack the Moderates, saying Congress was Dufferin's idea.
Mehta, Naoroji and Gokhale were Moderates, while Lajpat Rai was an Extremist (one of Lal-Bal-Pal), so he is the one not associated with the Moderates.
In 1920 Lajpat Rai started the Urdu daily Bande Mataram from Lahore, along with the English weekly The People.
Gokhale was a Moderate, whereas Pal, Tilak and Lajpat Rai were Extremist (militant nationalist) leaders, so Gokhale is the answer.
Lajpat Rai was lathi-charged at Lahore during the 'Go back Simon' protest and died on 17 November 1928.
The new view of development (Seers, 1969) targets poverty, unemployment and inequality, and does not stress the simple growth rate. So the simple growth rate alone is what it does not emphasise.

Amartya Sen is the Indian-born philosopher and economist (1998 Nobel laureate) for whom LSE created the position. The notes do not state this LSE fact, but Sen is the only option fitting the description.
The unlimited supplies of labour model of development was given by W. Arthur Lewis, not Rostow (stages of growth) or Solow. The notes do not cover it.
Development planning aims to remove obstacles and raise income and employment. The notes do not state this directly.
The Limits to Growth (Meadows and colleagues) models how interactions among population, resources and pollution would constrain growth. The notes list the book and its authors but not its argument.
The Limits to Growth (Meadows and colleagues) models how interactions among population, resources and pollution would constrain growth. The notes list the book and its authors but not its argument.
Amartya Sen won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economics for welfare economics and social choice theory. Solow, Marshall and Samuelson are not the 1998 laureate.
Colin Mackenzie surveyed and mapped Hampi in 1800 and later became India's first Surveyor General, so he brought the ruins to light. Prinsep is known for deciphering Brahmi, not Hampi.

Statement III is correct: the amara-nayakas were military commanders granted territories, later becoming hereditary Palegars. Statement I on the markets is a standard fact about Vijayanagara, while II is wrong because strain within the imperial structure marked the period after Krishnadeva Raya, not his own rule.
The notes do not mention a railway museum dedicated in August 2020 at Hubballi. Hubballi appears only as a zone HQ and for the longest platform.
RCF is at Kapurthala (A-3), the Wheel and Axle Plant is at Bengaluru (B-1), DLW is at Varanasi (C-4) and ICF is at Perambur (D-2). This gives code 3 1 4 2.
The notes say broad gauge covers over 95% of the network but do not give its width. Broad gauge is 1.676 m, about 5½ ft.
The first train ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder to Thane, so the first railway line started in 1853.
The notes give Hubballi (1,507 m) as the longest platform, not Gorakhpur. The keyed answer Gorakhpur reflects older data, when Gorakhpur held the record.
North Western Railway (HQ Jaipur) and East Central Railway (HQ Hajipur) were both created in 2002, so Jaipur and Hajipur is correct.
West Central Railway has its HQ at Jabalpur.
Konkan Railway (KRCL) has its HQ at Navi Mumbai.
East Central Railway has its HQ at Hajipur, formed in 2002.
The notes give only the zone HQs, not elevations. South Western Railway's HQ at Hubballi (about 650 m) is higher than Hajipur, Kolkata and Jabalpur.
Hajipur is the HQ of East Central Railway. Kanpur, Lucknow and New Jalpaiguri are not zone HQs.
South Eastern Railway has its HQ at Kolkata, not Bhubaneswar. Bhubaneswar is the HQ of East Coast Railway, so this pair is wrong.
Prakasam had the least gross irrigated area in 2015-16, as the notes state.
Surface lift schemes, deep tube wells and dug wells are all minor irrigation sources, so 'all of the above' is correct.
The notes say there are about 78,000 minor tanks serving about 46.5 lakh acres, which matches option 1. The other statements are not supported.
The Bhima lift irrigation project in AP draws on the Krishna river system, so the answer is Krishna.
Somasila dam is on the Pennar river, part of the Telugu Ganga chain.
Somasila dam is on the Pennar river, part of the Telugu Ganga chain.
Veligonda, Thotapalli and Pattiseema are all listed as the 2017 priority projects, so none of them is a non-priority project and option 4 is correct.
Nagarjuna Sagar was completed in 1967, as per the notes.
The notes identify the '100 km through West Godavari' canal statement as the false one. Pattiseema is a temporary lift scheme that benefits the Krishna delta.

Nagarjuna Sagar's foundation was laid on 10 Dec 1955, in the First Plan. Prakasam Barrage is a distractor because the notes link it to the First-Second Plan period, while Srisailam is Third and Telugu Ganga Sixth.

International liquidity means adequate availability of internationally acceptable reserve assets, chiefly dollars and other hard currencies, to settle external payments. A shortage of these, not of goods, gold/silver or exportable surplus, creates the problem.
Tiruttani lies on the Nandi river (Nandiyar), a small river in the Palar region. The notes do not state this, so no line is linked.
Pune lies on the Mula-Mutha river, as the city-river table shows; Nagpur, Dehradun and Bengaluru are not on it.
Cuttack is on the Mahanadi and Ujjain on the Kshipra. Ludhiana is on the Sutlej and Nashik is the source region of the Godavari, so the code is 3 4 1 2.
The Hizla fair at Dumka is held on the Mayurakshi river. The notes do not cover this, so no line is linked.
Pandharpur is on the Chandrabhaga and Tiruchirappalli (Srirangam) is on the Kaveri, so I and II are correct. Hampi is on the Tungabhadra, not the Malaprabha, so III is wrong.
Vijayawada lies on the Krishna river, as the city-river table shows; the Godavari is the tempting wrong option.

Kishanganga is in J&K, the Ganga is in the northern plains, and the Wainganga and Penganga are in central India. Penganga is a tributary of the Wardha, which joins the Wainganga downstream (Pranhita), so the Wainganga is placed north of the Penganga in the key's order. The notes do not state this, so no line is linked.

Early Sangam society had no fully developed rigid varna system, so options I and II are wrong; the one statement that fits is gradual Aryanisation (Brahmin and Vedic influence spreading). The notes only settle the caste point directly.
The Periplus calls Arikamedu (near Puducherry) Poduke. Korkai is a Pandya pearl port, not Poduke.
Yavanapriya ('beloved of the Yavanas') was black pepper, Rome's most prized Indian import, not muslin or ivory.

Muziris was a Chera port on the Malabar (west) coast, matching B-1. That eliminates options 1, 2 and 3 and leaves 4 1 2 3, where Barygaza lies north of the Narmada, Sopara is near Mumbai and Suvarnabhumi is to the east.
Arikamedu yielded Roman amphorae, Arretine ware and an intaglio of Augustus, showing a Roman trading settlement. The other sites are not linked to Rome.
Arikamedu (Poduke) is the foremost Indo-Roman trading station in eastern India, as its excavations show. Tamluk, Rajgir and Bhagrapir are not Indo-Roman stations.
An amphora is a tall, double-handled jar used for wine and oil, and examples were found at Arikamedu and other sites.

Soil erosion is linked to deforestation, which strips vegetation cover. Terracing is a conservation measure that checks erosion, so statement I is wrong; a tropical climate is not itself a cause, so only II is correct.
Lime is used to correct acidic soils, so mixing it in lowers the soil's acidity (it does not lower basicity). Gypsum, by contrast, is for alkaline soils.
Soil impoverishment means the soil has become very deficient in plant nutrients (loss of fertility). Erosion is a cause of loss, not the meaning of the term, and enrichment is its opposite.

Salts left behind by evaporating irrigation water can clog soil pores and make some soils impermeable. It does not raise yields; waterlogging, not salinisation itself, raises the water table and fills air spaces.
Gujarat has the largest area of salt-affected (saline) soil, mainly in coastal areas and the Rann of Kutch. Uttar Pradesh has the largest alkali area, which is a different question.
Buddha's mother Maya was a Koliya princess, not a Sakya; the Sakyas were his father's clan, so Koliyan is correct.
Mahapajapati Gautami raised the Buddha as his foster-mother; Maya was his birth mother.
The Buddha was born at Lumbini grove (Rumindei, Nepal); Kapilavastu was where the Renunciation took place, not his birth.
The Buddha's Mahaparinirvana took place at Kusinara in the Malla republic, so Mallas is correct.
Traditional dating places the Buddha's birth in 563 BC.
Buddhism as a teaching began with the first sermon (Dhammachakra Pravartana) at Sarnath, whereas Lumbini is only the Buddha's birthplace.
Lumbini is marked by an Ashokan inscribed pillar at Rumindei, which records the Buddha's birth there, so the king is Ashoka.
The Buddha's Mahaparinirvana (final nirvana) occurred at Kusinara (Kushinagar).
The Buddha gave his first sermon (Dhammachakra Pravartana) at Sarnath, not Mahavira, Sankaracharya or Guru Nanak.
The first sermon was delivered at Sarnath (Deer Park) after enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.
The first sermon was at Sarnath (Deer Park, Rishipatana); Bodh Gaya was the place of enlightenment.

Under the hybrid model announced in January 2025, insurance covers the first ₹2.5 lakh and the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust funds treatment up to ₹25 lakh per family for the poor. So the upper limit is ₹25 lakh, not ₹10, ₹15 or ₹20 lakh.
The notes list Mitra Mela (Nasik, 1899) as founded by V.D. Savarkar with his brother Ganesh; it was later merged into Abhinav Bharat.
Barindra Ghosh's activities gave rise to the Anushilan Samiti, so he is associated with it. Abhinav Bharat was Savarkar's society.
Pulin Behari Das led the Dhaka branch of the Anushilan Samiti. Sanyal's branch was at Patna, and Prafulla Chaki was a Muzaffarpur bomber.
The Kakori train action took place on 9 August 1925 and the case is dated 1925, so the answer is 1925.
Savarkar wrote The Indian War of Independence, 1857 (1909), so the answer is Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.
The notes confirm Savarkar founded Abhinav Bharat and wrote the Mazzini biography and the 1857 book. His failed escape at Marseilles also fits, so all four statements are true.
CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing) means using computers to assist in operating and controlling manufacturing plant operations, so option 1 is right.
Both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion. Traditional farming is labour-intensive whatever IoT offers, so R only states an alternative and is not the cause of A.
Wearables track health such as sleep and support identification/biometrics. Location tracking and hearing aids are also standard wearable uses, so all three are correct.

Statement I is wrong because passive tags have no internal battery and are powered by the reader's field. Statement III is wrong because active tags have their own battery. Statement II is correct, and RFID needs no line of sight (IV), so the answer is II and IV only.
Haptic technology gives tactile feedback, recreating the sense of touch through forces, vibrations or motions applied to the user. The other options describe unrelated technologies.

AR overlays digital content on the real world without blocking it, so I is wrong and III is correct. VR is fully immersive and replaces the real world, so IV is correct and II is wrong. Hence III and IV.
HRP-Choromet is a humanoid robot developed in Japan (an HRP-series humanoid), not a game, colouring system or dinosaur robot.
A semiconductor diode does not obey Ohm's law, since its current-voltage relationship is non-linear and it conducts in one direction only. Copper coils, heating coils and rheostats are ohmic.
Krypton is a noble gas and an insulator, not a semiconductor. Silicon, selenium and germanium are semiconductors.
Silicon is a semiconductor, which is why it is used to make IC chips.
In a p-type semiconductor, trivalent doping creates holes, which are the majority charge carriers. Electrons are the minority carriers.
The Shiwalik is the outermost, southernmost range forming the foothills of the Himalayas; the Trans-Himalayas and Great Himalayas lie to the north, and the Aravali is not a Himalayan range.
Lake Manasarovar lies in Tibet near Mount Kailash, in the Kailash range (the Ladakh Range's continuation), so Kailash range is correct; the Karakoram, Pir Panjal and Mahabharat ranges are elsewhere.
From north to south the order is Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar, Pir Panjal, then the outermost Shiwalik. Option 1 matches this sequence.
The Himadri (Greater Himalaya) is the oldest, loftiest and most continuous range; the Shiwalik is the youngest.
The Kashmir and Kullu valleys lie in the Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) range, which includes Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar. Himadri is the higher northern range and Shiwalik the outer foothills.
The Kashmir Valley lies between the Great Himalaya (Himadri) to the northeast and the Pir Panjal to the southwest, so Pir Panjal and Himadri is correct.
Markha Valley is in Ladakh (J&K), Dzukou Valley in Nagaland, Sangla Valley in Himachal Pradesh and Yumthang Valley in Sikkim, giving 3 4 2 1.
The French Open 2017 mixed doubles was won by Gabriela Dabrowski and Rohan Bopanna; this is a sports fact and the Carnatic Wars notes do not cover it.

The French company was state-controlled and dependent on the government, unlike the private, profit-driven English company, which hampered French success. The other options are not the reason given in the notes.

The First Carnatic War ended with Aix-la-Chapelle (4), the Third with the Treaty of Paris (1), and the Second was inconclusive/undecided (3). The First Mysore War is matched with the defeat of the British (2), giving 4 1 3 2.
The Gulf of Cambay (Khambhat) has no coral reefs because river sediment and freshwater inhibit coral growth. Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands all have reefs.
In coral bleaching the polyps expel their symbiotic algae, zooxanthellae, and lose pigment, turning white. Azotobacter, Paenibacillus and Rhizobia are soil bacteria unrelated to corals.
Frontal (cyclonic) rain occurs when warm air is lifted over cold air along fronts, i.e. through cyclonic activity. Convection currents cause convectional rain instead.
Convectional rain is typical of the equatorial belt, where the Amazon basin lies. The Ganga, Hwang Ho and Mississippi basins are in monsoon or temperate zones, where other rain types dominate.
Convectional rain comes from strong heating that makes air rise and form cumulonimbus, giving afternoon showers in the equatorial belt. These are short, so all three statements hold.
The equatorial belt gets rain almost daily all year through afternoon convectional showers. So A is true, and R explains A.
Inversion of rainfall means rainfall increases with height only up to a limit and then decreases above it. It is a feature of orographic rainfall on mountain slopes, but the notes do not state it.

A halo is refraction through hexagonal ice crystals, forming a ring of about 22°, so I and II are correct. III is wrong because cumulonimbus is a towering rain cloud, whereas the halo comes from thin high cirrus or cirrostratus.
A rainbow forms by refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection in raindrops.
Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight over the horizon, so the Sun is seen about two minutes before actual sunrise and after actual sunset. The notes do not cover this.

The sky's blue colour and the reddish Sun at sunrise are due to scattering, so I and III are true. The rainbow's seven colours are due to dispersion with refraction and internal reflection in raindrops, not scattering, so II is false.
Near the horizon sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so shorter blue wavelengths are scattered away and the Sun looks red. The notes do not cover this.
The change in direction of light on passing from one medium to another is refraction. Diffraction is bending around obstacles or edges.
Bending of light as it enters a different (denser) medium is refraction. Dispersion is splitting into colours, and reflection is bouncing back.
Light rays from the tank bottom bend away from the normal on leaving water, so the bottom appears raised and the tank shallower. This is refraction.
A rainbow arises from dispersion (together with refraction and internal reflection) of sunlight in raindrops. Interference, diffraction and dust scattering are not its cause.
In the primary rainbow red is outermost and violet innermost, so these are the terminal bands.
A byte is made up of 8 bits (a nibble is 4 bits), so the answer is 8.
One byte consists of 8 bits, so the answer is 8.

Cache is the fastest memory among the options, faster than hard disk and DVD-ROM. Registers are faster still, but they are not offered. Static RAM (SRAM) is what cache is built from, but cache is the answer expected here.
The order of storage units is bit < byte < KB < MB < GB < TB, which gives VI, II, I, III, V, IV. Option 1 matches this order.
Nalanda Mahavihara is located at Nalanda in Bihar (ancient Magadha), so Bihar is correct.
Vikramashila was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala; Gopala founded Odantapuri, and Devapala and Mahipala I did not found it.
Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur) was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala; Kumaragupta I is linked with Nalanda and Vijayasena was a Sena ruler.
Vikramashila was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala; the other options are not Pala founders of it.
Odantapuri was founded by Gopala, the first Pala king, not by Dharmapala (Vikramashila) or Ramapala (Jagaddala).
Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala, not Gopala (who founded Odantapuri), Devapala or Mahipala.
Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala, not Devapala, Ramapala or Gopala.
Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala; Gopala founded Odantapuri, and Devapala and Mahipala I did not establish it.
Vikramashila Mahavihara was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala, not by Kumaragupta I (Nalanda), Harsha or Lakshmanasena.
Nalanda, founded by Kumaragupta I in the 5th century, is the oldest of the listed monasteries; Odantapuri and Vikramashila were founded later by Palas.
Balaputradeva, the Shailendra ruler of Suvarnabhumi, built a monastery at Nalanda and his envoy obtained five villages from Devapala.
In the colour-revolution list, Silver Revolution stands for eggs/poultry, so Silver - Eggs is correct. Yellow is oilseeds, Golden is horticulture, and Grey (not Brown) is fertilisers.
MIDH is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme operating since 2014-15, so option 1 is correct.
Banganapalle mango received its GI tag in May 2017, so Baganapalle is the answer.
Alphonso is the most exported mango from India, so it is correct; Langra, Chausa and Gaurjeet are not the main export varieties.
The National Horticulture Mission began in 2005-06 (May 2005), later subsumed under MIDH, so May 2005 is correct.
Kanchan is an improved variety of amla (Indian gooseberry), not of grapes, guava or mango.
Artificial insemination lets semen of superior bulls be used widely, reduces the spread of contagious diseases and is economical, so all the statements hold.
Rashtriya Gokul Mission aims to conserve and develop indigenous bovine breeds, so option 1 is correct.
Milk and milk products are not a significant export of India, which consumes most of its milk domestically, whereas manufactured goods, handicrafts, textiles and gems are major exports.
Denmark has among the highest milk yields per cow, whereas India's per-cow yield is low despite being the largest producer overall.
The Tarapore Committee (I in 1997 and II in 2006) drew up the roadmap to capital account convertibility. The other committees named did not examine it.
Statement I is wrong because the World Bank does not determine a currency's price, which eliminates options 1 and 4. Of the remaining options, 'II and III' is the answer given.
Purchasing power parity links the long-run exchange rate to the inflation differential between two countries. So equality of purchasing power determines the rate of exchange.
SDRs, created by the IMF as an international reserve asset, are called 'paper gold'. The other options are not described by that term.
SDR stands for Special Drawing Rights, the reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969.

The RBI framework of July 2022, built into FTP 2023, allows invoicing and settlement in rupees. This encourages use of the Indian currency in cross-border trade and cuts dollar dependence, so it does not discourage rupee use or raise costs.
SWIFT is a Belgium-based cooperative (1973), not Switzerland or 1991. It is a messaging network that neither moves funds nor imposes sanctions, so all four statements are wrong.
Justin, the Roman historian, described the meeting of Sandrokottos (Chandragupta) with Alexander; Pliny, Strabo and Megasthenes are not credited with this.
Ashoka belonged to the Maurya dynasty, the grandson of its founder Chandragupta Maurya and son of Bindusara.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the first pan-Indian empire, the Maurya empire, so he is the answer rather than the later rulers.
Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was known by the name Vishnugupta, his childhood name; the other options are unrelated.
Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was known by the name Vishnugupta, his childhood name; the other options are unrelated.

The first lake in Girnar, Sudarshana, was built by Pushyagupta, governor of Chandragupta Maurya, so Chandragupta is the first ruler. Ashoka's governor only added canals, and Rudradaman and Skandagupta repaired it later.
Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya, so Seleucus is correct.
The Commission recommended a fixed Governor tenure of 5 years to shield the office from Central pressure, so option 4 is correct; 3 years or no fixed tenure is not what it proposed.
The Commission recommended amending Articles 355 and 356, not leaving them unchanged, so the statement that there is no need to amend them is wrong. The other statements match its recommendations.

The equatorial region is hot and wet all year (megathermal) with a multi-layered canopy, epiphytes and lianas, which fits statements I and IV. It is not a sclerophyll (Mediterranean hard-leaved) region, and it is not one of high development, so II and III are wrong.
The Mediterranean climate has hot dry summers and mild wet winters, so the dry summer is its defining feature. Dry winter is the opposite of the real pattern.
Mediterranean regions get their rain in winter from westerly depressions, while summers are dry under the subtropical high.
The Mediterranean region is known as the 'orchard lands', with citrus fruits and grapes as its main economy, so citrus production is best developed there.
Central Spain lies in the Mediterranean basin, with hot dry summers and mild wet winters, so the Mediterranean dry hot summer type is correct.
Bharatrabhatta I is not a Pratihara ruler, whereas Nagabhata I, Mahendrapala I and a later king Devapala (c. 948-954) are Pratihara rulers.
Rajashekhara was the Sanskrit poet and dramatist at the court of Mahendrapala I (and also Mahipala I). Among the options, Mahendrapala-I is the correct choice.
Rajashekhara was the poet and dramatist at the court of Mahendrapala I (also Mahipala I). Mahendrapala I is the correct option.
Phadke founded the Ramosi force in 1879, an armed struggle against the British in the 1870s; he was not a Congress leader and had nothing to do with 1857 or Gandhi.
Vasudev Balwant Phadke founded the Ramosi Krishak Jatha in Maharashtra in 1879.
The Phadke revolt was led by Vasudev Balwant Phadke, who built a Ramoshi combat force in 1879.
Petroleum is a non-renewable fossil resource and is the raw material for both plastics and gasoline. The notes do not state this use, so no line is linked.
Solar is the most important non-conventional source for India and has the greatest potential, so (1) is right.
A solar (photovoltaic) cell converts light directly into electricity, so photovoltaic cells relate to solar energy.
Hydel, solar and geothermal power are all renewable, so none of the listed options is non-renewable and (4) is correct.
Biomass is a renewable source. Coal and petroleum are non-renewable fossil fuels, and kerosene is a petroleum product.
15° of longitude equals 1 hour, and places to the east are ahead of Greenwich, so the 15°E meridian is 1 hour fast.
Local time depends on longitude, not distance north or south. Places on the same meridian have zero longitude gap, so they have the same time, 12:00 noon.
IST is based on 82.5°E, and 82.5 × 4 = 330 minutes, so IST is GMT + 5½ hours.
Noon at the IST meridian and 6 a.m. elsewhere is a 6-hour lag, which is 90° west of 82°30'E, i.e. 7°30'W. A place to the west is behind.
Local time is 5 hours ahead of Greenwich, so the place is 5 × 15° = 75° east of Greenwich, i.e. 75°E. East means ahead.
The standard meridian of India is 82°30'E, which is the IST meridian.
India's standard meridian is 82°30'E (82.5°E), from which IST is set.
Saddle Peak (732 m), near Diglipur in North Andaman, is the highest point of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; the other options are not the highest point of the territory.

Pulicat lagoon is shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, so only statement III is correct. The notes do not support the claims that the Himalayas and the Western Ghats each spread over only five states.
The Andhra Socialist Party (the Andhra unit of the Congress Socialist Party) was founded in 1934 at Vijayawada, so 1934 is correct; the other years are not supported.

Impatiens karuppusamyi is a new balsam species (genus Impatiens, Balsaminaceae) described by Botanical Survey of India researchers from Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve, so option 4 is right. The other options wrongly describe it as aquatic flora, a fungus or a bat.
The RBI was set up on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission (1926). The other bodies named are banking committees that came later or are unrelated.
The RBI Act was passed in 1934 and the RBI began functioning on 1 April 1935, so it was established in 1935.
The RBI's accounting year has been April-March since 2020-21, when it moved from July-June, so it now matches the banks' financial year.
The RBI started functioning on 1 April 1935, so it was established in 1935. Nationalisation came in 1949.
The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 under the 1948 Transfer to Public Ownership Act. 1935 is the year it was established.
The RBI's headquarters is in Mumbai (Mint Street). It was shifted there from Calcutta in 1937.
The RBI is the monetary authority, with price stability as its aim, and since 2016 the MPC works under an inflation-targeting framework. The other bodies listed do not carry out monetary policy.
Trishul is a short-range supersonic missile tested from Chandipur, so option 2 is right; it is neither subsonic like Nirbhay nor hypersonic.
Shaurya's range is about 700 km with a 1,000 kg payload (variants up to about 1,900 km), so the 900 km range claim is the incorrect statement.

Mission Shakti destroyed a live satellite in LEO and India became the 4th ASAT nation, so I and III are correct. II is wrong because the test was done in low LEO so debris decays quickly, not in the upper atmosphere.

Mission Shakti was a joint DRDO-ISRO test that destroyed a live satellite (Microsat-R) in Low Earth Orbit, so I and II are true. III is not supported: the notes give no such 50 km/s speed or 2000 km altitude capability.
India bought the Barak systems from Israel; Barak-1 was bought for the Navy and Barak-8 is an Indo-Israeli development.
The notes do not state this India-France 2013 deal; it concerned jointly developing a surface-to-air missile.
The notes list Abdali only as a Pakistani 450 km surface-to-surface missile, the same class as Prithvi, so it was the matching test.
Chandrasekhar won the 1983 Physics Nobel for the structure and evolution of stars, which is astrophysics (his white dwarf limit work). The other options do not match his work.
Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for the photoelectric effect, not for relativity. Relativity is the tempting wrong option.
Einstein's 1921 Nobel was for the photoelectric effect, not for special relativity, specific heat or Bose-Einstein statistics.
James D. Watson is listed in the notes as a Nobel laureate in genetics (DNA structure), so Genetics is correct.
The notes state the Forward Bloc was founded by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939 after he resigned the Congress presidency. Rash Behari Bose is linked to the IIL, not the Forward Bloc.
Azad Hind Radio was started in Germany and broadcast from Berlin, not from Japan.
The INA was formed in Singapore, then part of British Malaya, from Indian POWs after the fall of Singapore in 1942. It was not formed in India, Japan or Germany.
The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was an all-women combat unit under Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal. Usha Mehta ran the Congress secret radio, and Annie Besant belonged to an earlier period.

The notes credit the INA idea to Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon with Mohan Singh and Major Iwaichi Fujiwara. Of the options, the pair Pritam Singh and Fujiwara (I and IV) is correct, while Bose took over only in 1943.
Capt. Mohan Singh was the first commander and raised the first INA from Indian POWs in 1942. Bose only took over in 1943, and Rash Behari Bose headed the IIL.

The Kepler space telescope was launched by NASA in 2009 to find Earth-like planets (in the habitable zone of other stars) using the transit method, so option 4 is the most specific and correct answer.
NASA's Deep Space Atomic Clock was planned to be launched into space in 2019 to test precise timekeeping for deep-space navigation, so the answer is Space.

Lindeman's ten percent law says only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next, with about 90% lost. So it concerns energy transfer as food between trophic levels, not heat, birds or water.
Producers capture only about 1-2% of incoming solar energy, so 1% is the best option. The 10% figure is the share passed between trophic levels, not the share captured by plants.
Net primary productivity is lowest in deserts and the open ocean. Deep sea is the closest option, whereas prairie, deciduous forest and taiga are far more productive.
Ecological pyramids show the trophic levels, with producers at the base and top consumers at the apex. Maps, graphs and nets are not used for this.
Biomass is the total weight of organisms per unit area or volume. Standing crop is the living biomass of a trophic level at a given time, so it is not the best fit.
The biomass pyramid is inverted in pond and marine ecosystems, where the small, fast-turning phytoplankton crop supports a larger biomass of consumers. Forest and grassland pyramids are upright.

Charles Elton introduced the pyramid of numbers in 1927, so statement I is correct. Pyramids show producers and consumers in terms of numbers, biomass and energy, so II is correct too. Neither statement is incorrect.

Mycorrhiza is a fungus-root association in which the fungus helps absorb water and minerals and the plant feeds the fungus. Lichen is a fungus-alga association, and coralloid roots and biofertilizer are not fungus-root associations.
Mycorrhizae are mutualistic associations of fungi with the roots of higher plants. The fungus absorbs water and minerals for the plant, and the plant provides food to the fungus.
Commensalism is a +/0 interaction in which one organism benefits and the other is unaffected. Amensalism is −/0, so it harms one partner, and mutualism benefits both.
Lichen is a symbiotic association of a fungus with an alga or cyanobacteria. The alga supplies food and the fungus gives shelter and water.
Cuscuta, ticks and lice are parasites (+/−), so A is true. R gives the definition of a parasite, living on or in a host and feeding at its expense, so it correctly explains A.

rDNA technology moves genes between unrelated species, so a transgenic organism carries a foreign gene from another species: plant to plant, animal to plant and microbe to higher organism are all possible, so all three statements are correct.

Gene mapping helps trace livestock pedigree and breed disease-resistant animals, so I and III hold. II is wrong because knowing gene positions does not explain the causes of all human diseases (many are environmental or multifactorial).

Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall disease in plants through its Ti plasmid, which transfers T-DNA into plant cells. Bacillus thuringiensis is an insect pathogen (the source of the Bt toxin) and Pseudomonas fluorescens is a biocontrol agent, so neither causes crown gall.
Restriction enzymes (restriction endonucleases) are molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific recognition sequences. Joining fragments is the job of DNA ligase, which is the tempting wrong option.
Restriction endonucleases act as molecular scissors, cutting DNA at specific sites. Ligase is the glue that joins fragments, and a plasmid is a vector.
Bt cotton is insect-resistant because it carries the Bt (Cry toxin) gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis. So both A and R are true, and R explains A.

The 2020 three-capitals proposal was backed by the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development Bill, 2020 and the AP Capital Region Development Authority (Repeal) Bill, 2020, so 2020 is the correct year; the 2021, 2022 and 2023 options are wrong.

Statements I and II are confirmed (Visakhapatnam Top Impact Creator; Tirupati first in Safaimitra Suraksha), and Vijayawada was also among the awarded cleanest big cities in 2022, so I, II and V is the correct combination. The notes do not support III and IV, so options containing them are wrong.
Vipravinodins were Brahmin jugglers/magicians who performed only before Brahmins, so they belonged to the Brahmin group, not weavers, Kshatriyas or Vaisyas.
The notes state that first-year MeeSeva training through television was run by the IT&C Department with MANA TV, so option 2 is correct.

CARD (Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department) was one of ten finalists in the Commonwealth Association for Public Administration and Management's International Innovation awards, so option 4 is correct. MeeSeva is the tempting wrong option.
CARD, the Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department (1998), computerised registration and delivered registration services electronically, so option 1 is correct.

The Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 targets US$50 bn production, US$10 bn investment and 5 lakh first-time jobs. The '2 lakh first-time entrepreneurs' figure is not a target, so option 4 is the answer.
Fiber Grid Phase-I (24,000 km IP-MPLS ring) covers all 13 districts of the State, so option 1 is correct.
Mori in East Godavari is the pilot fibre-grid smart village, so option 2 is correct.
MEDHAS stands for Medical Education and Health Administrative System. It was built for Dr NTR University of Health Sciences, India's first health university, so option 3 is correct.
The IT/ITES SEZ is the Visakhapatnam SEZ, while Sri City and Kakinada are multi-product SEZs, so option 4 is correct.

LEDs have the highest efficacy and use less energy than CFLs, so urging people to replace bright and CFL bulbs with LEDs is justified by their energy efficiency. Both statements are true and R explains A.

LEDs have the highest efficacy and use less energy than CFLs, so urging people to replace bright and CFL bulbs with LEDs is justified by their energy efficiency. Both statements are true and R explains A.

A fluorescent tube is filled with low-pressure mercury vapour plus argon. Mercury is the characteristic active substance, since it emits the UV that the phosphor converts to visible light, while argon is only a buffer gas.
LED has the highest efficacy and longest life, and uses less energy than CFL, fluorescent tubes and incandescent bulbs (which lose most energy as heat). So LED bulb saves the most energy.

Statement I is correct: a CFL uses mercury vapour and phosphor, while an LED uses a semiconductor emitter. Statement III is correct since LEDs are more energy efficient. Statement II is wrong because LEDs, not CFLs, last longer.

Operation Polo was the 13–17 September 1948 police action in Hyderabad after which the Nizam surrendered and acceded to India. Blue Star and Meghdoot are unrelated, and Vijay was the 1961 Goa operation.
Hammir Mahakavya (Nayachandra Suri) traces the Chauhans to the solar line (Suryavanshi). The notes give the Agnikula theory but not this text's claim, so the answer rests on outside knowledge.
The Agnikula clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan (Chahamana) and Solanki. The Solankis are the Chalukyas of Gujarat, so all four listed clans are included.
The Kachwahas ruled Amber (Jaipur) in Rajasthan. The notes do not cover this fact.
Durgara is the medieval name for the Jammu region, so pair II is correct. Champaka is Chamba in Himachal, not Central India, and Kuluta is Kullu, not Malabar.
Jejakabhukti was the Chandela region, which is Bundelkhand, with Khajuraho and Mahoba as its centres.
Dhanga (Dhangdev) is listed among the Chandela rulers of Jejakabhukti, so option 1 is right.
The Tribhuvan Narayan temple at Chittor is linked to Bhoja, the Paramara king, though the notes do not mention this.
Bhoja was a Paramara ruler of Malwa, whose capitals were Ujjain and Dhara. Dhar is the city of Bhoja, with the Bhojshala there.
The Bhojshala at Dhar is a Saraswati (Vagdevi) temple, so the presiding deity is Goddess Saraswati.
Somnath was sacked in 1025 during Bhima I's reign and was rebuilt by Bhima I, so Bhimdev (Bhima I) is right. Mularaja was only the founder, and Jayasimha is not credited with the rebuilding.
Rani-ki-Vav, a UNESCO site, was built at Patan by the Solanki queen Udayamati, so it is in Gujarat.
The Khajuraho group of temples was built by the Chandelas between 950 and 1050 CE.
Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest Khajuraho temple and was built by the Chandela king Vidyadhara.
The Dilwara Jain temples (Vimal Vasahi and Luna Vasahi) are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.
A fathometer uses echoes of sound (sonar principle) to measure the depth of the sea, so option 3 is correct; it does not measure sound intensity or travel time as its purpose.
Hydraulic brakes work by transmitting pressure equally through a fluid, which is Pascal's law, not Bernoulli's theorem or Archimedes' principle.
In a stethoscope, sound from the chest is confined in the tube and reflected repeatedly off its walls, so it reaches the ears intensified; this is reflection of sound.
A lactometer measures the specific gravity of milk and so tests its purity, including water adulteration. A hygrometer measures humidity, so it is the tempting wrong option.
A bird on a live wire touches only one conductor and both its feet are at the same potential, so no current flows through it. Its body resistance or feathers are not the reason.
Kutch (Gujarat) is India's largest district by area, bigger than Leh, Jaisalmer and Barmer; the notes do not state this.
The listed answer is questionable: Sikkim is the least populous of these (6.08 lakh), while Meghalaya (about 29.7 lakh) has the largest population among the four options.
Rajasthan is the largest state by area, larger than Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Jaipur is the capital of Rajasthan; Udaipur, Jodhpur and Ajmer are other Rajasthan cities but not the capital.
By area, Chhattisgarh (about 1.35 lakh sq km) is larger than Jharkhand (about 79,700), then Himachal Pradesh (55,673), then Uttarakhand (53,483). The notes do not give these areas.
Uttarakhand (about 53,500 sq km) is far smaller than Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, so it is the smallest in area among the options.
Uttar Pradesh ranks 1st in population with 16.49% of India's population, ahead of Maharashtra and Bihar.
Jammu and Kashmir has a smaller population than Rajasthan, Haryana and Gujarat. The notes do not give these figures.
Punjab (about 2.77 crore) has a smaller population than Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha, so it is the least populated of the options. The notes do not give these figures.
The Kalahari lies in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa, so I and II are correct. Zaire (DR Congo) and Zambia are not part of it.
Many desert plants bloom at night because the insects that pollinate them are active in the cooler night hours.
Sonoran (USA), Takla Makan (China) and Karakum (Turkmenistan) are correctly matched. The Gibson Desert is in Australia, not Brazil.
Llanos (Illanos) are tropical grasslands of Venezuela and Colombia in South America, and the Campos are also in South America (Brazil). So South America is correct.
British Columbia in Canada, with its many mountain ranges, is called the 'Sea of Mountains'.
The Horn of Africa comprises Ethiopia, Eritrea, Somalia and Djibouti. Sudan is not included.
The Panjshir Valley is in northeastern Afghanistan, in the Hindu Kush north of Kabul.

Mauryan rule is credited with provincial division (provinces under Kumaras/governors) and a vast empire reaching the Hindukush, plus cultural patronage. Gold coins are not a Mauryan development, so only I, III and IV hold.
The Saptanga limbs are king, ministers, territory, fort, treasury, army and ally. Option 1 (king, territory, administration, treasury) is the closest match, while the others list unrelated groups.
Dandapala is the head of the army department among the 18 tirthas, so it is not treasury (Sannidhata) or judicial.
Among the options only Rajuka is a Mauryan district officer, with survey, assessment and judicial powers. Krori, Faujdar and Chirastadar are later titles, so Rajuka is the best fit.

Registration of births and deaths was the work of the third Mauryan city committee and remains municipal work today. Weights, prices and artisans' matters do not show unbroken continuity in the notes.
Megasthenes' Agronomoi were district officers responsible for roads, irrigation and land measurement. Roads is the matching option.
Pindakara was a tax on groups of villages, so the 'pin tax' is best read as a tax collected by a village unit.
Megasthenes records that evasion of the sales tax was punished with death, so Death is correct.
IC chips are made from silicon, a semiconductor. Silica is a compound (silicon dioxide), not the chip material.
A hybrid computer combines analog and digital features, so it handles conversion between analog and digital forms. A purely analog or purely digital computer does not.
ALU stands for Arithmetic Logic Unit, which performs arithmetic and logical operations inside the CPU.
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer where most processing happens. RAM, keyboard and hard disk are memory, input and storage devices.
Buses are the wire pathways connecting the parts of a computer. A modem links telephone lines and computers, and URLs and CPUs do not connect parts.
Statement I is correct: the CPU is the brain and most important part. Statement II is wrong because the CPU is hardware, not software.
Sufism, like Bhakti, stressed loving devotion to one God over formal ritual, so its philosophy parallels Bhakti rather than karma, kalpa or gyana.
Hath Yoga was the practice of the Nathpanthis (Gorakhnath, Matsyendranath) and was also adopted by the Sufis, so both statements are correct.

All Bhakti saints composed their verses in the language of the common people, which their followers understood. The other options are not common to all: idol worship was criticised by the Nirguna saints.
The Satnami sect in Chhattisgarh was founded by Guru Ghasidas. Ravidas, Ramdas and Tukaram are other Bhakti saints and not its founders.
Heat lost by the hot body equals heat gained by the cold body is the principle of calorimetry; thermal equilibrium only means equal temperatures.
Silver has the lowest resistivity of all metals, lower than aluminium, while nickel and nichrome (a heater alloy) have high resistivity.
A galvanometer becomes a voltmeter when a high resistance is connected in series, so most of the voltage drops across the resistance and little current flows through the galvanometer.
Electromagnetic induction is the production of an induced current/emf in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil (change in magnetic flux).
Photoelectric cells use alkali metals with low work function, such as rubidium or caesium, which emit electrons easily when light falls on them; tungsten is used for bulb filaments.
Iron is a solid with a high melting point of about 1538°C, so 1500°C is the only option close to it.
Zinc reacts with hot NaOH to give sodium zincate and hydrogen gas, which is combustible. NH4Cl would give ammonia, which is not combustible.
Xylem parenchyma is the only living cell type in xylem; tracheids, vessels (trachea) and fibres are dead at maturity.
Cardiac muscle is a muscular tissue. Adipose, bone and areolar tissues are connective tissues.
In a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration outside), water enters the cell by osmosis and the cell swells; in a hypertonic solution it shrinks.
Ethylene is the only plant hormone that is a gas (fruit ripening); abscisic acid, gibberellins and auxins are not gaseous.
Water is the most abundant component of the cell, making up more than 80% of it; protein, fat and minerals form much smaller fractions.
Electrostatic potential has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Velocity, force and angular momentum are vectors.
Momentum = mass × velocity, with unit kg m/s, which equals newton second (N·s), since 1 N = 1 kg m/s².
Stress is force per unit area, so it has the same unit as pressure (pascal, N/m²). Strain is dimensionless.
Joule, watt-hour and newton-metre are all units of energy. Kg·m/s² is the unit of force (newton), so it is not an energy unit.
Photovoltaic cells (solar cells) convert sunlight directly into electricity through the photovoltaic effect. Leclanche, dry and voltaic cells are chemical cells, not solar converters.
India has 250–300 clear sunny days and about 5,000 trillion kWh of solar energy incident a year, so both statements are true and Statement II explains the huge potential in Statement I.
As per the notes, India's cumulative solar capacity on 31 Dec 2022 was 63.30 GW. 100 GW was the 2022 target, not the achieved capacity.
Shakti Sthala is the Pavagada solar park in Karnataka, which was expected to be the world's largest solar park when complete. It is not a wind, geothermal or tidal project.
In Bihar the Civil Disobedience Movement took the form of a Chaukidari (Chowkidari) Tax agitation, e.g. in Begusarai, alongside salt-making. Haathi and Malba are not mentioned as the taxes opposed.
Gandhi was arrested on 5 May 1930 and held in Yerwada Jail, so he was in jail when Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid on 21 May 1930.
Chandra Singh Garhwali led the Garhwal Rifles who refused to fire on the Peshawar crowd in 1930, which is the Peshawar Incident.
The Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirts) was founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the Frontier Gandhi, among the Pathans of the NWFP.
The notes do not cover the Charan Paduka massacre of Madhya Pradesh, so no line is linked.

Kamaladevi led women into the Salt Satyagraha, Kasturba Gandhi joined protests and was imprisoned, Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman INC President, and Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag in Quit India. This gives A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

The notes do not cover Gandhi's 1916 Banaras Hindu University speech. In it he chided the elite for ignoring the labouring poor and said India's salvation lay with the farmers, so I and II are correct.
Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Gandhi's political guru, advised him to spend a year studying India before starting any movement.
Rabindranath Tagore gave Gandhi the title 'Mahatma' (about 1914). Bose is linked to 'Father of the Nation', not 'Mahatma'.
The Alluru inscription (Ikshvaka period) records multiple gifts to different communities and institutions; Karle, Veerapuram and Ramagiri are distractors.
Ship-motif coins prove maritime trade and are attributed to Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri; of the options, Yajna Sri Satakarni is the one listed, so option 3 is correct.
Vaishali, capital of the Vajji confederacy, was an early republic (gana-sangha) in the 6th century BC. Athens and Sparta are Greek city-states, and Pataliputra was a Magadhan monarchy capital.
Vaishali, capital of the Vajji confederacy led by the Lichchhavis, was an early republic in the 6th century BC. Athens and Sparta are Greek, and Pataliputra was a Magadhan capital under monarchy.
Ajatashatru belonged to the Haryanka dynasty, the dynasty of Bimbisara and Ajatashatru. Maurya, Nanda and Gupta came later or are unrelated.
Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE, helped by iron, elephants and fertile land. Kashi, Kuru and Matsya did not reach this dominance.
Parivrajaka means a wandering renunciant and Upasaka means a lay follower of Buddhism, so I and III are correct. Shramana means an ascetic or striver, not a high-status priest, so II is wrong.
Walter G. Rosen coined the term 'biodiversity' in 1985 (E.O. Wilson later popularised it), so option 3 is correct.

Alpha diversity measures species diversity within a single habitat or area at a local scale, so it is the index used for richness within a particular area. Beta compares between ecosystems and gamma covers the whole region.
Biodiversity follows the latitudinal gradient: it is richest in the tropics near the equator and falls towards the poles, so it increases towards the equator.

Ecosystem services of biodiversity include clean air and water, pollination and climate regulation, which underpin soil formation, erosion prevention, waste recycling and crop pollination, so all four are correct.
The Asiatic lion is found naturally only in Gir, India. The one-horned rhino also occurs in Nepal, and the double-humped camel is not exclusive to India, so only statement I is correct.

Marsupials are mammals whose young are born undeveloped and carried in a pouch, which is their distinctive feature. They do not lay eggs (as monotremes do) and are not defined by hibernation or migration.
The ruling party can misuse government servants, vehicles and discretionary grants to influence voters, but political parties are not a resource of government used this way, so (4) is the exception.
The party system is a sub-system of the political system, since parties operate within the political process of elections and government formation.
Chandrashekhar and A.B. Vajpayee are the pair who received the Outstanding Parliamentarian award; the other pairs include members who did not receive it as a pair.

In Kerala, the Congress-led UDF was the ruling coalition in 2004 when A.K. Antony resigned as CM, so it was the United Democratic Front government. The UPA was the Centre's coalition, not the state's.
India has identified 106 Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas, so option 3 is correct.
All three statements are correct: Svalbard is on Spitsbergen, Norway, and India's Chang La vault in Ladakh is a joint DRDO (DIHAR)-NBPGR facility. So none is incorrect.
The Svalbard Global Seed Vault is on Spitsbergen island in Norway, so Norway is correct.
Dhanush is the Bofors-based 155 mm gun made by OFB Jabalpur (Ordnance Factory Board); the other firms are not its manufacturer.

Statement I is false: the ships decommissioned were Cheetah, Guldar and Kumbhir (not Magar), at Port Blair, not Lakshadweep. Statement II is true: INS Imphal was commissioned at Mumbai on 26 Dec 2023, so only II is correct.
Admiral Gorshkov was a Soviet/Russian ship that India bought and refitted as the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya, so it is an aircraft carrier, not an organisation or a person.
INS Ranjit, a Rajput-class destroyer, was decommissioned in May 2019; INS Sindhurakshak is a submarine, not a destroyer.
INS Viraat was an Indian Navy aircraft carrier (ex-HMS Hermes); Talvar, Rajput and Mysore are destroyers or frigates.
The August 2016 leak concerned the Scorpene submarine data (Project 75), so the answer is submarines.
Varunastra is a ship-launched heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo developed by NSTL, so it is a torpedo and not a missile or minesweeper.
Vikram, Samarth, Vishwast and Rajshree are all Coast Guard surface vessels (offshore patrol vessel classes), not Navy submarines or research vessels.
INS/ICGS Sarthak is a Coast Guard offshore patrol vessel built by Goa Shipyard and launched in August 2020, so the answer is offshore patrol vessel.
Gun cotton is cellulose nitrated with nitric and sulphuric acids, i.e. cellulose nitrate; cellulose acetate is not an explosive.
Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in Hyderabad in 1901, so option 1 is correct; 1905 is the date of Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam and 1910 of Andhrula Charitramu.
The Nilayam was founded by Komarraju Lakshmana Rao in Hyderabad in 1901. Kovvur (1916) is a different institution, the Andhra Council of Research.

The first Telugu library, founded in Hyderabad in 1901 by Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, was Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam. Rajaraja Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was his later one at Hanamkonda (1904).
Vignana Chandrika Mandali (Hyderabad) was founded by Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, so option 3 is correct. The notes give the year as 1906, though the question says 1905.
Vignana Chandrika Mandali published Andhrula Charitramu in 1910, so option 2 is correct.
The Madras Public Libraries Bill of 1938 was drafted and moved in the Madras Assembly by Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya, so option 1 is correct. The 1948 Madras Act and 1960 AP Act came later.
Nitrochloroform (chloropicrin-like compound) is not an explosive, whereas TNG and TNT are explosives. The notes state explicitly that nitrochloroform is not an explosive.
Nitroglycerine is glyceryl trinitrate, i.e. the nitrate ester of glycerol, C3H5(ONO2)3, so it is an ester, not a salt or a nitro-hydrocarbon.
Nitro chloroform is not an explosive. Cyclotrimethylene trinitramine is RDX, and TNT and TNG are explosives too.
Dynamite is nitroglycerine absorbed in kieselguhr or sawdust, and nitroglycerine is glyceryl trinitrate (glycerol trinitrate).
Neither statement is correct. Bio-toilets use an anaerobic bacterial inoculum, not a fungal one, and the end products are methane, carbon dioxide and water, not just ammonia and water vapour.
Multi-brand retail FDI is capped at 51% under the Government route, so option 1 is correct; 100% applies to single-brand retail.
The Budget 2021-22 raised the insurance FDI limit from 49% to 74% (effective 19 May 2021). The 100% limit came later, in Budget 2025-26.

Post-2010 changes include 51% in multi-brand retail, single-brand policy changes, and foreign airline FDI up to 49%. 100% FDI in the automotive sector is not one of the listed post-2010 changes, so only I is 'not' a change.
Chit funds are on the list of sectors where FDI is prohibited (along with lottery, gambling, Nidhi companies). The other options allow FDI subject to conditions.
