Over the cumulative period, Mauritius was the top source of FDI into India, so option 1 is correct. Singapore only overtook it in recent years.
Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl: one Na+ ion combined with one Cl- ion, so the formula has no subscripts.
An amalgam is an alloy of a metal with mercury (Hg), the only common liquid metal.
In the reactivity series calcium lies far above zinc, iron and copper, so it is the most reactive of these.
Osmium is the densest naturally occurring metal, denser than iron, silver and nickel.
Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, so it is used in fireworks for brilliant white light. Sodium gives yellow.
Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron, so it corrodes in preference to iron and protects it (galvanisation, sacrificial protection).
Lead (lead-acid accumulators) is used in storage batteries, with lead plates in sulphuric acid.
Germanium is a metalloid (semiconductor) while zinc, silver and gold are true metals.
FeCl3 is a salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a weak base Fe(OH)3, so it hydrolyses to give an acidic solution (pH<7). NaCl and KCl are neutral and NaOH is basic.
Strain is a ratio of change in length to original length, so it has no dimensions. The other quantities have dimensions.
A blackboard appears black because it absorbs all colours and reflects none. Black is the absence of reflected light.
Solids have negligible compressibility because their particles are tightly packed, so high compressibility is not a characteristic of solids.
Wolffia (duckweed) is the smallest flowering plant known.
Male frogs have vocal sacs that act as resonating sound boxes that amplify the croak. Females lack these, though they do have a larynx.

In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the velocity direction keeps changing, so there is a centripetal acceleration of constant magnitude but changing direction. Hence it is non-zero and not constant as a vector.
In a wheelbarrow the load lies between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort, which is a class II lever.
Elasticity is the ability to resist deformation and regain shape. Steel needs a larger deforming force for the same strain (higher Young's modulus) than rubber, so it is more elastic.
Commercial banks are the largest source of institutional agricultural credit, with about three-fourths of the flow, well ahead of cooperatives and RRBs.
NABARD is the apex development finance institution for agriculture and rural development and the premier agricultural credit institution; SBI, RBI and RRBs are not the apex body in this sphere.
Land Development Banks are part of the long-term cooperative structure and give long-term loans for land development, wells and machinery. They do not give short-term loans or lend to industry.
NABARD is the apex institution whose primary role is refinance to banks such as SCBs, RRBs, State Cooperative Banks and Land Development Banks. RBI, LDB and SBI are not the apex refinance bank.
NABARD is the apex institution whose primary role is refinance for agriculture and rural development. RBI, SBI and the Imperial Bank do not hold this role.
NABARD refinances institutions for agriculture and rural development; it does not refinance export business (EXIM Bank) or industrial development, so the 'all the above' option is wrong.
NABARD is the apex development finance and refinance institution for agriculture and rural development, so it is the biggest compared with RRBs, central cooperative banks and Land Development Banks.
Land Development Banks provide long-term credit (land development, wells, machinery). State Cooperative Banks and PACS give short-term credit.
NABARD is the apex institution dedicated to agriculture and rural development finance. SBI and RBI are general banks, and IFC is not an agricultural bank.

The Anglo-Vedic (DAV) school at Lahore was opened in 1886 in Dayananda's memory with Lala Hansraj as headmaster, so Hansraj is credited with it. Dayananda had died in 1883 and did not found the college himself.
In recent years engineering goods have been India's largest export item by value, ahead of gems and jewellery, chemicals and mineral fuels.

For the question's period (2012), gems and jewellery was the single largest export item, ahead of readymade garments, leather and chemicals.
The USA has been India's largest trading partner and had the maximum trade volume, ahead of Japan, Germany and the UAE.

Tyagaraja created new ragas (II) and Annamacharya's sankirtanas praise Lord Venkateswara (IV) are correct. Most Tyagaraja kritis praise Rama, not Krishna (I), and Annamacharya and Tyagaraja were not contemporaries (III), so 'II and IV' is right.

Falls occur in the upper course, meanders in the middle course, and oxbow lakes and deltas in the lower course, with oxbow lakes forming before the river reaches its delta. The order is therefore II, I, IV, III.
A doab is the land between two confluent rivers (Persian do-ab, 'two waters'), such as the Ganga-Yamuna doab. It is not a region between mountains, lakes or river and sea.
An alluvial fan is a fan-shaped deposit of coarse load dropped where a stream meets a break of slope. A sand bar is only a channel feature and not a gently sloping fan.
The notes do not cover the moribund delta subdivision. It is a stage of the Bengal (Ganga-Brahmaputra) delta, where the distributaries have become inactive and are no longer renewed by flooding.
Sri Lanka's central highlands send rivers outward in all directions, which makes it a classic example of radial drainage. The other options are not standard radial examples.
Mangifera indica is the binomial name of the mango; guava, amla and jackfruit have different scientific names.
The genus names Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera are taxa, i.e. units of classification; the specific epithet is the second word (indica, tuberosum, leo).
A true fruit develops only from the ovary of the flower; fruits that develop from other parts such as the thalamus or receptacle are false fruits.
Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of incident light that can eject photoelectrons from a material. Option 3 describes the work function (an energy), not the frequency.
Iron exposed to air and moisture forms a brownish layer of hydrated iron oxide, called rust.
In prokaryotes the nuclear region without a membrane is the nucleoid. The nucleolus and nucleosome are structures in eukaryotic nuclei.
Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and promotes cell elongation there, so the plant bends towards light (phototropism).
Sycon, Spongilla and Euspongia are sponges, which belong to Phylum Porifera.
Copper is the best conductor of heat, aluminium is next, and stainless steel is a poor conductor. So the order is stainless steel < aluminium < copper.
Silk is a natural protein fibre from silkworms. Rayon is semi-synthetic, and nylon and polyester are synthetic.
For 4d, n=4 and l=2. Angular nodes = l = 2, and radial nodes = n-l-1 = 1.
Polyester is a synthetic fibre that resists wrinkling. Cotton, flax and silk crease easily.
Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals (solutes) upward, so blocking it affects the transport of both.
Cyanides, along with oxides of carbon, carbonates and carbides, are carbon compounds traditionally treated as inorganic. Methane, propane and nucleic acids are organic.
Centrifugation spins the liquid so that very fine insoluble particles settle out. Decantation works only for larger particles that settle on their own.
Gravitational force depends on the masses and the distance between the bodies (F = Gm1m2/r²), so it differs for different pairs of bodies.
The Indian peafowl (peacock) is Pavo cristatus. The other names refer to other birds.
Cutting a bar magnet perpendicular to its axis gives two smaller complete magnets, each with its own N and S poles. Poles cannot be isolated, and the two poles have equal strength.
Magnesium burns in air to form magnesium oxide, a white ash. It does not form baking soda, calcium carbonate or vinegar.
Asafoetida (heeng) is the dried latex (oleo-gum resin) exuded from the roots of Ferula plants.
The Salankayana capital was Vengi (Pedavegi, Eluru district). Vijayapuri is the tempting wrong option, as it was the Ikshvaku capital.
Salankayana is a gotra name meaning Nandi, the holy bull, which matches their bull emblem.
The Salankayanas were early Saiva kings (Parama Mahesvara, Nandi emblem), though later kings turned Vaishnava, so Saivism is the expected answer.
GST is a multi-stage, destination-based value-added consumption tax levied on every value addition, so it is not a gross value tax; ITC avoids tax-on-tax.

Only I is a likely advantage: GST replaces many taxes with one and creates one national market. Claims that it drastically cuts the current account deficit or makes India overtake China are unsupported.
GST was introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, so option 4 is correct.

Statement I is incorrect because the Council is constituted under Article 279A, not 269A (which deals with IGST). Statement III is also incorrect as stated: votes are weighted (Centre 1/3, States 2/3), and the question's answer treats it as incorrect. Statements II and IV are correct.
The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
GST replaced indirect taxes such as State VAT, whereas income, corporate and capital gains taxes are direct taxes and were not replaced.

GST subsumed both Central taxes (excise, service tax, CVD/SAD) and State taxes (VAT, entry tax, octroi), so option 2 is right. Alcohol is excluded, and petroleum is within GST but levied only from a date the Council recommends.
GST subsumed State VAT; property tax, corporation tax and income tax were not subsumed.

Bakelite, made from phenol and formaldehyde, is the first synthetic plastic and a poor conductor of heat and electricity. The notes list its monomers but do not say it was the first or a bad conductor, so this rests on prior knowledge.
Lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags' because their hydrolytic enzymes can digest the cell itself when the cell is damaged or dies.
Red, green and blue are the primary colours of light, and mixing all three gives white light.
Mixing red and green light gives yellow, as in additive colour mixing.
The primary colours of light, used in photography, are red, green and blue. Yellow and cyan are secondary colours.
Double fertilisation, in which one sperm fuses with the egg and the other with the polar nuclei, is unique to angiosperms.
Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruit. Parthenogenesis is the development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg, not of a fruit.
Parthenocarpy is fruit development without fertilisation. Apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, so it is not the answer.
In plant sexual reproduction, pollination is followed by fertilisation, then division of the zygote, embryo formation and finally the seedling.
Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryote, so it belongs to Kingdom Protista, not Monera, which holds prokaryotes.
Meristematic tissue is made of actively dividing cells, and its cell division drives plant growth. It is not dead and is not limited to bark.
Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are dead at maturity. Epidermis, parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues.
Lysosomes contain hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes that break down macromolecules and worn-out cell parts.
Ethyl acetate is an ester, and esters have sweet, fruity smells. Methyl chloride, methanoic acid and methanol do not smell fruity.
Fungal cell walls are made mainly of chitin, not purely cellulose, so the statement that all fungi have a purely cellulosic wall is wrong.
Abscisic acid is the stress hormone. It closes stomata and so helps the plant tolerate drought.
Lysosomes store digestive enzymes, and this is why they are called 'suicidal bags'. Ribosomes make proteins, and desmosomes are cell junctions.
Bacteria are prokaryotes and belong to Monera. Mushrooms and yeast are fungi, and moss is a bryophyte.
Seeds are dispersed by wind, water and animals. Fungi do not disperse seeds.

Copper in moist air slowly forms a green patina, which is basic copper carbonate. The notes mention the green patina on the Statue of Liberty but not its composition, so the compound comes from prior knowledge.
About 59% (58.6%) of India's landmass is prone to moderate-to-high earthquakes, so 58.6 is the right option.
About 5,700 km of the 7,516 km coastline is exposed to cyclones and tsunamis.
Tsunami is a natural disaster, not man-made; war, hazardous materials exposure and transport accidents are human-caused.
After the 1993 Killari quake, the 2002 revision merged old Zone I into Zone II.
Landslide zoning divides hilly areas into homogeneous units by degree of actual or potential landslide susceptibility, hazard or risk. Mapping is only the depiction.
The devastating Indian Ocean tsunami struck on 26 Dec 2004.
The devastating Indian Ocean tsunami struck on 26 Dec 2004.
India's tsunami warning centre (ITEWC) is at INCOIS, Hyderabad.
ITEWC was set up after the 26 Dec 2004 tsunami at INCOIS, Hyderabad.
The notes do not give 2006 as the adoption year; they only say the Indian Ocean warning system was set up after 2004 and ITEWC has operated since 2007. The answer is 2006 as keyed.

The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, prepares and presents the Budget. Revenue handles tax estimates and Expenditure and Financial Services do not prepare the Budget.
The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance) prepares and presents the Union Budget. The Department of Revenue only handles tax estimates.
Banking Division is not a Department of the Ministry of Finance, whereas Expenditure, Revenue and Economic Affairs are Departments.
R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first budget of independent India on 26 November 1947. James Wilson presented India's first budget in 1860.
R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first budget of independent India on 26 November 1947. James Wilson presented India's first budget in 1860.
The Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget in 2017 (Budget 2017-18), ending a 92-year practice.
Disinvestment is a capital receipt because it reduces government assets. Corporate tax, dividends and interest receipts are revenue receipts.
Din-i-Ilahi stayed a small voluntary circle of about 18 members, was never pushed on the masses, and ended with Akbar's death; orthodox critics also rejected it. So all the given reasons apply.

Akbar is credited with this social reform on marriage (he also acted against child marriage and Sati), whereas Alauddin and Sher Shah are not known for it. The notes do not state the one-wife rule directly.
Akbar had the Ibadat Khana built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575, and opened it to all religions in 1578; the other years are not associated with it.
Sulh-i-Kul (peace with all) was Akbar's guiding principle of religious policy. Nizamuddin Auliya, Zainul Abidin and Nasiruddin Chiragh were not Mughal emperors.

Akbar's popularity rested on the mansabdari system, his liberal religious policy (jizya abolished), the Dahsala land revenue system and social reforms like acting against child marriage and Sati. So all four apply.
The Mahzar of 1579, which made Akbar supreme arbiter in religious disputes, was issued by Akbar and drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.
Under Mahalwari the village community jointly owned the land and revenue was settled with the mahal, so the claim that the land belonged to the government is incorrect.
Under Ryotwari the ryot paid revenue directly to the Government, received pattas, and lands were surveyed and assessed before taxation, so all three statements are correct.
The Ryotwari experiment began in Baramahal in 1792 under Captain Alexander Read (assisted by Munro). Elphinstone only extended it to Bombay.
Thomas Munro crushed the Rayalaseema palegars with the officer Campbell, and then introduced Ryotwari there.
Holt Mackenzie designed the Mahalwari system in 1822, so he is regarded as its father. Bird only revised it in 1833, and Munro and Read are linked to Ryotwari.
The order is Guntur acquired (1788), Battle of Padmanabham (1794), Ryotwari in Madras (1802 onwards), then zamindari abolition (1948), which is B, C, A, D.
Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimes directly to gas without melting; it is not ice, salt mixture or sulfur.
In the visible spectrum violet has the shortest wavelength (about 400 nm), shorter than blue, yellow and red.
Red has the longest wavelength (about 700 nm) of the visible colours listed; green, yellow and blue are all shorter.
Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light most strongly, and of the options red is the one that drives photosynthesis most effectively; green is mostly reflected.
Ginger is a rhizome, an underground modified stem that stores food, so it is a tuberous stem and not a root.
Desert plants have long roots because roots grow towards water (positive hydrotropism) and the water lies deep in the soil.
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things; the nucleus, DNA and chromosomes are components within it.
ATP is the cell's primary energy currency, storing energy in its phosphate bonds and transferring it when converted to ADP; ADP is the lower-energy form, and RNA and DNA carry genetic information.
The notes do not mention the title 'Gunraj Khan'. Maladhar Basu, the Bengali poet of Shri Krishna Vijaya, received it from the Bengal Sultan.
The Atala Masjid at Jaunpur was built by the Sharqi ruler Ibrahim Shah Sharqi, who is the correct option; Lal Darwaza was built by Bibi Raje.
Hindola Mahal is at Mandu, so statement II is true. Mandu lies in Dhar district, so statement I is also true, and both are true.
Gujari Mahal at Gwalior Fort was built by Raja Man Singh Tomar for his queen Mrignayani, so the answer is Man Singh.
Jahaz Mahal at Mandu was built by Ghiyasuddin Khalji of Malwa, not Hoshang Shah.
Anantavarman Chodaganga was a Ganga king of Kalinga (Odisha) who built the Jagannath temple at Puri, so he belongs to Orissa.
The Sumerians of Mesopotamia developed cuneiform, the earliest proper writing system, before Egyptian hieroglyphs and the Indus script (which is undeciphered). The notes do not cover this fact.

The Industrial Revolution replaced cottage industry with the factory system and gave rise to working class movements (I and III). It caused overcrowding of towns through migration from villages, not overpopulation of villages, so II is wrong.

LTE is a 4G technology, not 3G, so statement I is wrong. VoLTE is voice carried over the LTE data network, so it is not voice-only versus data-only, which makes statement II wrong too.
An endoscope uses optical fibres that carry light by total internal reflection, so it can view inside body organs.
Optical fibres guide light pulses by total internal reflection, so it is the phenomenon used for transmission. Refraction alone would let light leak out of the fibre.
Optical fibres work on total internal reflection, which keeps the light pulses confined within the glass strand.

Light stays inside a bent fibre because it undergoes repeated total internal reflection at the boundary. Ductility has nothing to do with it, and light still travels in straight lines between reflections.
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, not by the pituitary, thyroid or adrenal glands.
Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin that is stored in the liver, so the liver is the correct answer.
Tejas is India's indigenous 4.5-generation light multirole fighter (LCA). Aakash is a missile, Vikrant a carrier and Arjun a tank.
Phalcon is the Israeli-origin AWACS system on the IL-76 platform in IAF service. The notes do not cover it.
Hansa-2 is a light trainer aircraft developed by NAL. The notes do not cover it.
The Ilyushin IL-78 is the mid-air refuelling tanker of the IAF (MARS). The IL-76 is a heavy transport, and the C-130J and C-17 are transports.
The C-5M Super Galaxy is a large US military transport aircraft (Lockheed Martin). It is neither a helicopter nor a galaxy of stars.
The AH-64E Apache Guardian is an attack helicopter made by Boeing in the USA. The notes do not cover it.
The Ilyushin IL-78 is the IAF's mid-air refuelling tanker (MARS), so it is the aircraft that refuels fighters in flight. Mirage-2000, Su-30MKI and Jaguar are fighters that receive fuel.

The first indigenously assembled T-90S, licence-built at HVF Avadi, is named Bhishma. Arjun is a different, DRDO-designed tank.
Mangdechhu hydropower plant in Bhutan was inaugurated by PM Modi in 2019, so option 4 is right.

Jute is grown in West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, Odisha and MP; Andhra Pradesh is not a significant jute state, so it is the answer.
The Tea Board of India is headquartered at Kolkata; Kottayam is the Rubber Board seat and Guntur the Tobacco Board seat.
Coffee Board is at Bengaluru, Rubber at Kottayam, Tobacco at Guntur and Spices at Kochi, giving 1-b, 2-c, 3-d, 4-a.
Egypt, with its Nile valley Giza cotton, is the leading producer of extra-long staple cotton; India grows mostly medium staple.
The Indian Institute of Skills foundation stone was laid in Kanpur, so option (4) is correct. The notes do not cover this fact.
The AP Employment of Local Candidates in Industries/Factories Act (July 2019) reserves 75% of private jobs for locals, so 75 is correct; the other percentages are not the figure in the Act.

The notes do not state Captain Lakshmi Sehgal's mother tongue, so no line can be linked.
Trayi (Vedatrayi) comprises the Rig, Yajur and Sama Vedas; the Atharvaveda is excluded.
The Rigveda is the oldest Veda; the Atharvaveda is the latest.
The Rigveda has 10 mandalas and 1,028 hymns (1,017 plus 11 Valakhilya); 1,017 is only the count without the Valakhilya hymns.
The Purusha Sukta, describing the four varnas, is in the 10th mandala of the Rigveda.
The Purusha Sukta in the Rigveda's 10th mandala mentions the four varnas, so the Rigveda is the first text to refer to varna.
The Rigveda is the oldest Veda; the Atharvaveda is the latest.
The Gayatri Mantra is in the III mandala of the Rigveda and is attributed to Vishvamitra.
The Surya Sukta of Rigveda Mandala X describes the marriage of Surya, and is used in marriage ceremonies; the Purusha Sukta concerns the varnas. The notes do not state this.
Purusha Medha is associated with the Panchavimsha Brahmana per the notes, so Shatapatha is not supported; the notes do not support the given answer.
Purusha Medha is associated with the Panchavimsha Brahmana per the notes, so Shatapatha is not supported; the notes do not support the given answer.
The Aitareya Brahmana belongs to the Rigveda; Gopatha is Atharvaveda, Shatapatha and Taittiriya are Yajurveda.
'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad and was adopted as the national motto in 1950.
Girivraj/Rajgriha (Rajgir) was Magadha's first capital; Pataliputra came later and Vaishali was never the first capital.
Rajgir (Girivraj/Rajgriha) was Magadha's earliest capital; Pataliputra was chosen later by Udayin.
The Vishwa Shanti Stupa is on the Ratnagiri hill at Rajgir; the notes do not cover this fact.

Ajatashatru (Kunika) killed his father Bimbisara; the other options are not described as parricides.
Bimbisara founded the Haryanka dynasty; Brihadratha belongs to the earlier dynasty of Magadha and Ajatashatru was Bimbisara's son.
Bimbisara was known as Seniya in Buddhist and Jain tradition; the notes do not mention this name.
Bimbisara was the founder and first ruler of the Haryanka dynasty; Ajatashatru came after him.
Jivaka was the son of the courtesan Salavati according to Buddhist tradition; the notes do not state this.
Jivaka (Jeevaka) was Bimbisara's royal physician.
Shishunaga destroyed Avanti (Malwa) and brought it under Magadha; Bimbisara and Ajatashatru are not credited with this.
Narrow money (M1) is currency with the public plus demand deposits (plus other deposits with RBI). Options 2-4 add post office or time deposits, which belong to M2, M3 and M4.
Liquidity falls in the order currency, demand deposits, savings deposits, time deposits, which is IV, I, III, II. Time deposits are locked, so they are the least liquid.
Broad money M3 is currency with the public plus demand deposits plus time deposits plus other deposits with RBI, so all four items are included.
When banks lend more than the deposits they hold, they are creating new money through lending, which is credit creation. The other options do not describe this.
With money supply fixed, a rise in money demand raises the interest rate. A fall in prices or a rise in income does not follow directly from this.
Money demand, mainly for transactions, rises as income and the value of transactions rise, so the relationship is positive.

Gandhi opposed the separate electorate for Dalits that the Communal Award gave, so he began his fast unto death on 20 Sept 1932 in protest against the Award. The Round Table Conference failure was only the background.

The Poona Pact dropped the separate electorate and gave a joint electorate with reserved seats for the depressed classes (Harijans). The other options are not what the Pact provided.
The All India Anti-Untouchability League was founded by Gandhi in 1932 with G.D. Birla as its first president. Gandhi was the founder, not the first president.
The League, later renamed Harijan Sevak Sangh, had G.D. Birla as its first president. Gandhi founded it but was not its first president.
Scheduled Castes are also commonly called Dalits. The notes do not state this equivalence.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Juna Khan) became Sultan in 1325, not 1300, so option 3 is false. Warangal (Orugallu) fell in 1323 and was renamed Sultanpur.
Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limited revenue increases to about one-tenth, raised slowly. Alauddin and Firoz are not credited with this rule.

Diwan-i-Kohi (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi) was the agriculture department of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
Ibn Battuta was in India in 1333-42 under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who made him Qazi of Delhi.
Ibn Battuta stayed in India from 1333 to 1342, during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign (1325-51), not Firoz's or Ghiyasuddin's.
Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and other weaker sections, so option 2 is correct.
Article 51 deals with promotion of international peace and security; 41, 43A and 48A cover other subjects.

Equal pay for equal work for men and women is Article 39(d), a DPSP. The other options are Fundamental Rights (Articles 20, 21, and minority protections).
The 86th Amendment (2002) substituted Article 45 to provide early childhood care and education until age six.

The 42nd Amendment added Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid). Minimising inequalities in income was added by the 44th, cooperatives by the 97th, and early childhood care by the 86th.
The 42nd Amendment added Article 43A, workers' participation in management of industries. The other options were in the original Constitution.
Bag filters, cyclone separators (also called cyclone collectors) are real pollution-control devices. 'Cyclone divider' is not a recognised device, so it is the odd one out.
Crop residue burning releases CO, methane, ozone and SO2, so all four listed gases are released. Hence option 4 (all of these) is correct.

Acid rain is caused by SO2 and NOx, i.e. oxides of sulphur and nitrogen. Oxides of carbon and phosphorus are not the cause.

Sulphur dioxide (with NOx) causes acid rain, and it is the main single factor. Ozone, ammonia and carbon monoxide are not causes.
Acid rain is caused by oxides of sulphur and nitrogen. Oxides of carbon are not a cause, so I and II is correct.
Baiju Bawra was a dhrupad singer at the court of Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior, so he is the musician linked with that court. Tansen is tied to Rewa and Akbar's court, not Man Singh Tomar.
The title 'Tansen' came from Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior, not Akbar; Akbar gave only the title 'Mian'. So the statement that Akbar gave the title 'Tansen' is incorrect.
Dhrupad traces its origin to Vedic chanting and began under Man Singh Tomar (1486-1516), making it the oldest vocal form listed. Ghazal and Thumri developed later.
Baiju Bawra was a dhrupad singer at the court of Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior, so he is the musician linked with that court. Tansen is tied to Rewa and Akbar's court.
Amjad Ali Khan is a famous sarod maestro. The notes do not cover this.
Todi is a morning raga, whereas Bhopali is an evening raga and Bhimpalasi an afternoon raga. Darbari is a late-night raga. The notes do not state this.
The Akbarnama has three volumes: Akbar's ancestors, Akbar's reign, and the Ain-i-Akbari. So the answer is three.
Humayun-nama is the history of Humayun written by Gulbadan Begum.
Humayun-nama was written by Gulbadan Begum, a woman of the Mughal royal house. Akbarnama was by Abul Fazl, Baburnama by Babur, and Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori.

The Malhotra Committee (set up 1993, reported 1994) recommended private entry into insurance and an insurance regulator, which became IRDAI. The other committees listed are not linked to this recommendation.
IRDAI was recommended by the Malhotra Committee, not the Gadgil Committee, so option 2 is the incorrect statement. The other statements (statutory body, Sec. 114A, Hyderabad HQ) are correct.
IRDA (IRDAI) is the apex regulator of insurance and reinsurance companies. SEBI regulates securities markets, not insurance.
The government set up IRDAI under the IRDA Act, 1999 as the insurance regulator. SEBI and RBI regulate other sectors, and GIC is an insurer, not a regulator.
The Gathasaptasati contains verses by women contributors such as Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva and Madhavi. Brihatkatha, Kamasutra and Lilavati are not noted for women's contributions.
Prajnaparamita is by Nagarjuna, Samayasara by Kundakundacharya, Lilavati Parinayam by Kutuhala and Katantra Vyakaranam by Sarvavarma, which gives a-III, b-I, c-IV, d-II.
The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea was written by an anonymous Greek sailor, not by Ctesias, Pliny or Ptolemy, so 'None of the above' is correct.
Robert Sewell's 'A Forgotten Empire' is about the Vijayanagara Empire, so option 3 is correct.
Ram Sharan Sharma is the noted historian of ancient India; Satish Chandra, Bipin Chandra and Amalesh Tripathi are known for medieval or modern history.
A lost city more than 7,000 years old was reported in Egypt in November 2016, so Egypt is the answer.
'The Wonder That Was India' was written by A. L. Basham, a historian of ancient India.
Bhilsa (Vidisha) is in Madhya Pradesh and Girinagar (Junagadh) is in Gujarat. Dwarasamudra (Halebid) is in Karnataka, and Sthaneshwar (Thanesar) is in Haryana, so only I and III are correct.
Chalk (organic sedimentary) and marble (its metamorphic form) are both made of calcium carbonate, CaCO3. The notes do not state the chemical composition, so this rests on general knowledge.
Gondwana rocks hold nearly 98% of India's coal, so Gondwana is correct. Dharwar is mineralised for metals, Vindhyan for building stone, and Tertiary mainly for petroleum and lignite.
The Chota Nagpur Plateau is made mainly of Archaean granite and gneiss, so option 3 is correct. The notes do not mention the plateau, though they list granite and gneiss as Archaean rocks.
The notes give the order Archaean, Dharwar, Cuddapah, Gondwana. Vindhyan is a Purana system listed after Cuddapah and before Gondwana, so the sequence Dharwar-Cuddapah-Vindhyan-Gondwana is correct.
Mission 41K aims to save ₹41,000 crore in energy costs over a decade, so option 2 is correct. It is not about train numbers, track upgrades or staff training.
The notes give the PYQ key of about 94% broad-gauge electrification as on 1 March 2024, so option 1 is correct.

Vande Bharat is a semi-high-speed, engine-less train built by ICF Chennai and earlier called Train 18, so I, II and IV are correct. Statement III is wrong because its maximum speed is not 250 kmph (it is about 160-180 kmph).
The notes do not cover this. Trivandrum Rajdhani (12431) runs about 3,000+ km from Delhi (Hazrat Nizamuddin), the longest among the options.
Train 18 was the indigenously built semi-high-speed, engine-less train later named Vande Bharat Express, so option 2 is correct.
The first Kisan Rail ran from Devlali (Maharashtra) to Danapur in Bihar in August 2020, so the Devlali-Nashik option is the one given as correct. The notes do not cover this.
India's first CNG-powered train was launched on the Rewari-Rohtak section in Haryana in January 2015. The notes do not cover this.
The Tejas Express was a semi-high-speed train launched on the Mumbai-Karmali (Goa) route on the Konkan line. The notes do not cover this.
The notes do not give the lengths of these tunnels. Pir Panjal (about 11 km) is the longest, followed by Karbude, Nathuwadi and Berdewadi on the Konkan line, matching option 1.
The Seikan Tunnel, a rail tunnel linking Honshu and Hokkaido, is in Japan, so option 3 is correct.
The notes do not cover this. GAIL's roughly 600 km pipeline was being built between Visakhapatnam and Secunderabad, so option 4 is correct.

The Fifth Schedule covers States other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, so it does not apply to Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya and Mizoram (II and III). Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha are Fifth Schedule States.
The Fifth Schedule covers States other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, so it does not apply to II and III. Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha are covered.
An autonomous region is a unit within an autonomous district, with its own Regional Council. It is not a federation or block of districts.
The Sixth Schedule covers only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, so option 2 is right. Nagaland, Manipur, Arunachal and Sikkim are not covered.
The Sixth Schedule covers only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, so option 2 is right. Nagaland, Manipur and Arunachal are not covered.
Tripura is one of the four Sixth Schedule States. Sikkim and Nagaland are excluded, so 'All of the above' is wrong.
PESA applies to the 10 Fifth Schedule States and not to Assam, Meghalaya or Tamil Nadu. So the group Assam-Meghalaya-Tamil Nadu is where it is not enforceable.

Pavuluri Mallana wrote the Sara Sangraha Ganitam (from Mahaviracharya) and Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kreedabhiramam, so a-II and b-I; Aryadeva-Chittasuddi Prakarana and Dignaga-Pramana Samucchaya are the correct Buddhist pairings, giving option 3.
Prataparudra Yashobhushanam (Prataparudriyam) is a Sanskrit alankara work by Vidyanatha, court poet of Prataparudra II; it is not by Ketana, Baddena or Tikkana.
Dhoni became the first IPL captain to win 100 matches, which is the fact needed here; the notes do not state it, so no line is linked.
Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS (2,560 MW) became the largest thermal station in AP as of April 2025, ahead of Krishnapatnam (2,400 MW), Simhadri (2,000 MW) and Rayalaseema (1,050 MW).
Nana Saheb was the leader at Kanpur, proclaimed Peshwa there on 5 June 1857. Tantia Tope was his commander, not the main leader, while Lakshmibai and Kunwar Singh led elsewhere (Jhansi, Bihar).
Scindia of Gwalior and the Nizam of Hyderabad stayed loyal to the British, whereas Kunwar Singh and Nana Saheb were rebel leaders. So III and IV did not participate.
Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah of Faizabad led the rebels who defeated the British at Chinhat near Lucknow. Shah Mal, Mangal Pandey and Kunwar Singh were active elsewhere or earlier.
Maniram Dewan (Dutt) was the leader of the 1857 revolt in Assam; the other names are not linked to it.
Lakshmibai was born at Kashi (Banaras/Varanasi), though she is famed for Jhansi, so Varanasi is correct.
Lakshmibai was killed in battle at Gwalior (17 June 1858) and her mausoleum is at Gwalior.
Liyaqat Ali led the revolt at Allahabad and Banaras, while Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal. So the Lucknow–Liaquat Ali pair is wrong.
Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah, known as Danka Shah, fought at Chinhat, so I and II are correct. He was not killed by troops under Henry Lawrence, who died defending the Lucknow Residency, so III is wrong.
Shah Mal of Pargana Baraut rallied the headmen and cultivators of the 84 villages (chaurasee des).
Fazil Muhammad Khan of Bhopal is remembered for leading the 1857 movement there and sacrificing his life. The notes only say that in Bhopal troops rebelled while the ruler stayed loyal.
JRY was launched in 1989 (merger of NREP and RLEGP), not April 1995, so the JRY pair is wrongly matched. The other pairs (TRYSEM 1979, NREP Oct 1980, SGSY April 1999) are correct.
MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas) is AP's agency for the urban poverty programme NULM, so it is a poverty alleviation scheme for the urban poor.
The June 2023 UNDP-DAY-NULM partnership aimed at helping women make well-informed career choices, so women is correct.
The June 2023 UNDP-DAY-NULM partnership aimed at helping women make well-informed career choices, so women is correct.
NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage pilot in 1992, not RBI, SBI or UNDP. RBI is only the regulator.
Swadhar is a scheme for women in difficult circumstances, so option 3 is correct.
Swawlamban provides training in traditional and non-traditional trades for women. Swayamsiddha is SHG-based empowerment and Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is micro-credit.
Janmabhoomi, the AP rural development programme, was launched in 1997, so option 4 is correct.

The 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 were at Harbin (not Beijing), so I is wrong; the slogan 'Dream of Winter, Love among Asia' is right (II). The mascots are Binbin and Nini, not Yingying, so III is wrong. The emblem announcement (IV) is correct, so II and IV.
Cricket, dropped from the Asian Games after 2014, was re-included for the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games by the OCA.
Kamaljit Sandhu won the 400 m at the 1970 Asian Games, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games athletics gold.
The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951, which the notes confirm as one of India's hosting occasions.
Haryana topped the 1st Khelo India Para Games held in December 2023.
The 3rd Khelo India Youth Games (2020) were hosted by Assam at Guwahati.
The 4th Khelo India Youth Games were announced to be hosted by Haryana (Panchkula), the state named by the Sports Minister.
Kabaddi and netball both field seven players per team. Volleyball has 6, basketball 5, water polo 7, and kho-kho 9 on the field.
Mohun Bagan became the first Indian football club to appear on NASDAQ billboards in Times Square on 29 July 2020, its foundation day.
Kabaddi lasts 40 minutes (two 20-minute halves), shorter than hockey (60), football (90) and cricket.
India beat Iran in the final of the 2016 Kabaddi World Cup at Ahmedabad.
Mission XI Million was the outreach programme for the FIFA U-17 World Cup 2017 to popularize football, as the notes state.
Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is located in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
The National Sports University was set up in Imphal, Manipur, under the 2018 ordinance.
The Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NIS) is located at Patiala, Punjab.
Captain Roop Singh Stadium in Gwalior is a cricket venue, though it is named after a hockey player.
Early Aryan administration was a kinship-based tribal polity, with no formal bureaucracy or fixed territory. It was neither a republic nor an autocracy.

The Rajan's office tended to be hereditary, though not strictly, with traces of election by the Samiti. This fits the key's 'descended (hereditary) monarchy', while the other options are not supported.
The Panchajana are Anu, Druhyu, Yadu, Turvasa and Puru. Kikat is not among them, so it is the unrelated tribe.
PIL and judicial activism originated in the USA (the term was coined there in 1947), and India adopted PIL in the late 1970s. England, Russia and China are therefore wrong.
The Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) were added by the 42nd Amendment and are in line with the UDHR, which speaks of duties to the community. The notes do not state this fact.

Olympe de Gouges wrote the 1791 Declaration of the Rights of Woman and the Female Citizen during the French Revolution; Wollstonecraft wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, and Robespierre was a revolutionary leader.
John Locke propounded the theory of natural rights (life, liberty and property). Hobbes, Bentham and Marx are associated with other theories.
Both acts violate human rights: detaining a person on the way to vote denies the right to political participation, and killing a civilian in a combing operation violates the right to life.
Human Rights Day 2016 had the theme 'Stand up for someone's rights today'; the other options are themes of other years or are not the 2016 theme.

Democracies accept equality as a legal norm, which makes it easier to guarantee women's freedom and dignity. The other options overstate: democracies do not ensure equal representation or always ensure respect.
Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the day the UDHR was adopted in 1948. 24 October is UN Day.
The UDHR covers civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights and guides the SDGs Agenda. The Paris Agreement, Magna Carta and NAFTA are not human rights guides for the SDGs.
On 28 July 2022 the UNGA recognised the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment as a universal human right.
Rajendra Prasad held the Food and Agriculture portfolio in the 1946 Interim Government; Defence went to Baldev Singh and Home to Patel.
The Bill was introduced in the Commons on 4 July 1947 and received royal assent on 18 July 1947, i.e. about 15 days, so 15 is correct.

The Assembly was indirectly elected by Provincial Assemblies on a restricted franchise, not adult franchise, so I is true and II false. It was multiparty and worked through committees, so III is false and IV true; answer I and IV.
PKVY is AP's initiative on sustainable and organic farming; PMFBY, NFSM and RKVY are not organic-farming schemes.
The National Centre of Organic Farming is located at Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh), under the Ministry of Agriculture; the notes do not state this.
Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by Subhash Palekar, so option 2 is correct.

Statement I is wrong: natural farming uses on-farm, cow-based inputs, not chemical fertilisers. Statement II, that the method evolved in Karnataka, is the accepted fact (Palekar's movement began there), though the notes do not state it.
APCNF stands for Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming, the state's natural farming initiative (formerly ZBNF).
The NHRC was set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (12 Oct 1993), so 1993 is correct; 1990 and 1992 relate to the NCW Act and its constitution.
The SHRC committee consists of the CM, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition, etc. The Governor only appoints on its recommendation and is not a member of the committee.
NCW members, including the Chairperson, are nominated by the Central Government for a term of 3 years, so 3 years is correct.
In January 2022 the Cabinet extended the NCSK by three years beyond 31 March 2022, to 31 March 2025. So the answer is three.
Rekha Sharma became NCW chairperson in July 2023, so she was the chair as of July 2023. Vijaya Rahatkar is the later chair.

National income is the value of final goods and services produced, i.e. income from productive activity (factor incomes for productive services). Transfer payments and mere money-making without production are excluded.
Output of normal residents inside and outside the country is the GNP (gross national) concept, so 'Gross National Income' fits; GDP and NDP are territory-based.
GDP equals GNP when net factor income from abroad is zero, so this is possible. FC=MP needs zero net indirect taxes, but the notes support only the GDP=GNP case directly.
GNP stands for Gross National Product.
National income is measured as NNP at factor cost, not GDP or GNP at market prices.
National Income is defined as NNP at factor cost, so NNP at FC equals National Income.
National Income = NNP at MP minus (indirect taxes minus subsidies), converting market price to factor cost.
National Income is NNP at factor cost, the standard measure; market-price and domestic versions are not it.
NNP at MP is GNP at MP minus depreciation, because net figures remove capital consumption.
Indra was the most prominent and most popular Rigvedic god, with about 250 hymns and first rank. Varuna ranks third, and Vishnu and Rudra rose only in the later Vedic period.
Varuna upheld Rita, the cosmic and moral order, so he is its guardian.
Jeremy Bentham is regarded as the founder of the utilitarian school; Hegel, James Mill and Locke are not. The notes do not cover this topic.
Rita is the cosmic and moral order, and the notes say the idea of dharma grew out of it. Dharma, as the obligation of duty, is therefore also correct, so both statements hold.
The whole of the 9th Mandala is devoted to Soma, the plant and ritual drink deified as a god.
Indra, god of lightning, storm and war, is the war-god. Varuna is the god of water and cosmic order, and Agni is the god of fire.
Indra has about 250 hymns, the most in the Rigveda, while Agni has about 200.
The whole of the 9th Mandala is devoted to Soma, the plant and ritual drink deified as a god.
Indra, with about 250 hymns, is the most prominent god of the Rigveda and is ranked first. Agni comes next with about 200 hymns.
Pushan is one of the aspects of Surya, the Sun, along with Savitri, Mitra and Vishnu. Indra is a storm god and Aranyani is a forest goddess.
Brihaspati was regarded as the priest of the gods. The notes do not state this fact.
The main theme of the Upanishads is philosophy, namely Brahman, Atman and moksha.
The Upanishads are mainly books of philosophy, dealing with Brahman, Atman and moksha.
Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) is attributed to Badarayana, the author of the Brahma Sutra, who is identified with Vyasa. Patanjali is Yoga, Gautama is Nyaya and Kapila is Samkhya.

The notes do not settle these statements: they give India's GII ranks only for 2022 (40), 2024 (39) and 2025 (38), and list patent filing as 6th (WIPO 2023) and NRI 2024 as 49th. They say nothing on GII 2023, the 2022 resident-filing rank, NRI 2023 or the IP Index 2024, so the answer 'None of the above' rests on knowledge outside the notes.

Only III is correct: plant varieties are excluded from patenting under Section 3(j) of the Patents Act, and biological processes for producing seeds are not patentable, so I is wrong. II is wrong because the IPAB was abolished in 2021 and its functions were moved to the High Courts, yet this does not make the statement 'correct' as framed in the answer key. The notes do not cover these points.

The capital market deals in long-term debt and equity instruments such as shares, debentures and bonds, so bonds and shares are traded in the capital market. The other options (imperfect, bullion, black markets) are not markets for securities.
Stars twinkle because their light travels a great distance and is refracted by fluctuating air density; planets do not twinkle. In space, stars do not twinkle, so air is the cause.
Apparent brightness depends on a star's size and temperature (colour) and its distance from Earth; the notes give colour as surface temperature and magnitude as brightness measured at distance.
A constellation is a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern; the Milky Way and Andromeda are galaxies and the Solar System is the Sun with its planets.
A black hole's gravity is so strong that no light escapes, so it cannot be seen directly; R correctly explains A.

Twinkling arises as starlight passes through the atmosphere, where varying temperature and density continually change the refractive index. The notes say stars do not twinkle in space, where there is no air.
Saptarishi (Ursa Major) points toward the pole star Polaris, so it indicates the direction of the pole.
The Sun emits all colours together, which combine to white light. It only looks yellow from Earth because of atmospheric scattering.
Sunlight takes about 8 min 19 s to reach Earth, i.e. nearly 8 minutes.
The photosphere (the Sun's visible surface) is at about 5,778 K, so 5778 K is correct.
The Sun's diameter is about 109 times Earth's.
By current notes Saturn has the most moons (285 vs Jupiter's 101), so Jupiter is not correct; the keyed answer follows older data when Jupiter led (79 moons in 2018).
Venus is called Earth's twin because it is close to Earth in size, mass and density.
The inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars; Jupiter is an outer planet (a gas giant), so it is not an inner planet.
A toggle key switches between two states each time it is pressed; Caps Lock alternates between capital and small letters, so its function goes back and forth.
OLEDs can be built on flexible plastic substrates, enabling roll-up displays in clothing and transparent displays, so all three statements are advantages over LCDs.
A webcam is an input device that captures video, whereas a projector and headphones are output devices; a sound card is not listed as a basic input device.
A joystick is an input device with a lever that moves in several directions to control an on-screen image or cursor.
Plotter, printer and monitor are all output devices, whereas the other groups include input devices such as scanner, keyboard or mouse.
Laser printers are non-impact printers, whereas line, drum and serial printers are impact printers.
The mouse is the standard pointing device in a GUI, used to select icons and windows; the other devices are less commonly used for pointing.
A trackball is a pointing device that sends input to the computer, so it is an input device, not an output device.
A digitizer converts analogue information such as drawings or pictures into digital form, while barcode readers and OMR read coded marks and a gamepad is a game controller.

The notes confirm PM-MKSSY is a Central Sector sub-scheme of PMMSY running 2023-24 to 2026-27, which settles statements I and II. Statement III (one-time incentive for aquaculture insurance) is not in the notes, so it rests on outside knowledge of the scheme; with all three correct, option 4 is right.
Russia is not a G7 member: it joined in 1997-98 to make the G8 and was suspended in 2014 after Crimea. France, Germany and Japan are G7 members.
The Halifax Summit (1995) was a meeting of the G7 countries.
India's G20 presidency theme was 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future', so statements II and III are wrong. Statements I and IV are correct, making I and IV only the answer.
The 2025 G20 Summit was held in Johannesburg, South Africa.
The question is dated. The 2019 G20 Summit was held at Osaka, Japan, so Osaka is the answer.
The 2020 BRICS Summit was chaired by Russia, held virtually, as Russia held the chair that year.
In August 2023 Argentina was named among the new BRICS members, though it later declined in December 2023. Portugal, France and Italy were not invited.
I2U2 comprises India, Israel, UAE and the US, which is the group in option 2.
The TPP was signed by 12 Pacific Rim nations in 2015 and covers about 40% of global GDP. India was not a founder member, so III is wrong.
The Commonwealth has no charter, treaty or constitution, so I is correct. Not every former British territory joined automatically, since membership is by application and consent, so II is wrong.
The Almaty Charter was signed at the 2002 CICA summit; Thailand did not sign it, so Thailand is the answer.

Coral reefs are called the "Rainforests of the Sea" because of their rich species diversity, so they are the marine counterpart of tropical rain forests, not of temperate forests, savannas or scrubland.
Phytoplankton (diatoms, dinoflagellates, cyanobacteria) are the main primary producers of the ocean. Seaweeds and marine angiosperms contribute far less.

Phytoplankton are the base of ocean food chains and take up CO2 through photosynthesis, so losing them harms the food chains and the carbon sink (I and II). Water density depends on temperature and salinity, not on phytoplankton, so III is wrong.
Upwelling brings cold, nutrient-rich water to the surface, which causes the plankton boom. It does not bring decomposers or bottom-dwelling organisms, so only II is correct.
Both statements are true, but the epithet comes from the reefs' species richness, not from their wave-breaking role. So II does not explain I.
Coral skeletons are made of calcium carbonate (aragonite), so calcium carbonate is the major chemical component of reefs.
Oyster shells, like coral skeletons, are made of calcium carbonate.
The notes do not mention IUCN/Mission Blue Hope Spots. Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands were named Hope Spots, so option 4 is correct.
Lakshadweep is formed entirely by coral and has India's only true atolls, so it is the coral island group. The Andaman & Nicobar Islands are not primarily coral islands.
Shivaji bought cannons and ammunition from the Portuguese, who supplied arms from their Goa settlements. The notes do not state this, so no line is linked.
Both statements are correct. Shivaji used guerrilla warfare (Ganimi Kava) in the Sahyadri terrain, and he held hill forts such as Raigad, Rajgad and Panhala.
After Shivaji's death in 1680, the succession dispute was between his sons Sambhaji and Rajaram. The notes do not state this dispute directly, so no line is linked.
The Treaty of Warna (1731) settled Tarabai's line at Kolhapur, so it was between Sambhaji of Kolhapur and Shahu of Satara.
The order of rule is Sambhaji, then Rajaram, then Shivaji II (Tarabai), then Shahu. This gives III, II, IV, I.
Balban was the first to use the term Zillillah, as part of his divine-right theory of kingship. Alauddin and Iltutmish did not coin it.
Diwan-i-Arz (the question's 'Arj') was the army/defence department headed by Ariz-i-Mumalik, so the answer is Defence. Royal correspondence belonged to Diwan-i-Insha and finance to Diwan-i-Wizarat.
Diwan-i-Arz handled the army (4), Diwan-i-Risalat religious affairs (1), Diwan-i-Insha royal correspondence (2), and Diwan-i-Wizarat finance (3), giving 4 1 2 3.
Iltutmish created the Forty, the Turkish slave-nobles known as Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Chalisa). The other options are not groups he founded.
Balban, though himself one of the Forty, destroyed the power of the Chahalgani nobles that Iltutmish had created.
Balban finally destroyed the power of the Turkan-i-Chihalgani, which Iltutmish had created. Iltutmish is the tempting option, but he founded the group rather than breaking it.
The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in the USA by Indians living in the US and Canada, so the USA is correct.
The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in the USA (San Francisco), by Indians living in the US and Canada, not in Europe.
The Ghadar Party's headquarters was Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco.
The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in the USA by Indians settled in the US and Canada, so U.S.A is correct.
India House in London (1905) was founded by Shyamji Krishnavarma, not by Rash Behari Bose or Taraknath Das.

The Preamble opens with 'We, the People of India', showing the Constitution derives its authority from the people, so it indicates the source of the Constitution. It is a part of the Constitution (Kesavananda Bharati), so the other options are wrong.
Liberty, Equality and Fraternity are the trinity drawn from the French Revolution; Fraternity is the third ideal in the Preamble.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949; 26 January 1950 is when it came into force, so option 1 is the tempting wrong choice.
The ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity come from the French Revolution (1789), not the Russian Revolution, which gave the idea of justice.
The Preamble secures justice in all three forms - social, economic and political - so 'all of the above' is correct.
The original 1949 Preamble described India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'; 'Socialist' was added only by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
Constitution Day is observed on 26 November (the adoption date of 1949), since 2015.
The Preamble as it now stands declares India a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic; option 1 is the original 1949 wording, before the 42nd Amendment.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950, which is the tempting wrong option.
On 26 January 1950 India was a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'; Socialist and Secular were added only in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment.
Th-232 is fertile; on absorbing a neutron it is converted into fissile U-233. Hard water, H2S and heavy water are not fuels.
Statement I is wrong: enrichment raises the share of U-235, not U-238 (U-238 is fertile). Statement II is wrong: weapons-grade uranium needs far more than 20% enrichment, so neither is correct.
Mass number is defined as the number of protons plus neutrons, i.e. the nucleon count, not the mass.
Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but different mass numbers (different neutrons).
India holds about 25% of the world's thorium, against only about 2% of uranium, so thorium is the element with large reserves.
Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers (neutron counts).
Graphite slows neutrons, so it serves as a moderator and not as a fuel.
Heavy water (D2O) is a moderator that slows neutrons. U2O, Na2O and Cl2O are not moderators.
YSR Jala Kala provides free borewells to single or group farmers with 2.5 acres, as a policy against irrigation water shortage; the other names are not AP schemes in the notes.
Zero poverty, delivered through P4 (Public-Private-People Partnership), is the first principle of Swarna Andhra @2047, so the Zero Poverty – P4 Policy is the cornerstone.
Real Time Governance, with its command centre at the Secretariat, is the e-governance initiative first launched in AP; the other options are not noted as AP firsts.
In 2017 the AP government and a Singapore consortium formed the partnership for the Amaravati Capital City Start-Up Area Project.
Bangaru Laxman was a senior BJP leader and former BJP national president; the notes do not state this fact.
The National Election Watch report of August 2010 named the Congress as the richest party, so Congress is correct. BSP, BJP and the Socialist Party were not reported as richest.
The notes state that Azad reorganised Sanyal's HRA and renamed it the HSRA. Bhagat Singh was a founder leader of the HSRA but did not rename the HRA.
The HSRA was reorganised and renamed under Chandrashekhar Azad's leadership after Bismil's death, so Azad is the answer. Bhagat Singh was a founder leader but not the one who formed it.
The HSRA was set up in September 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi, so the answer is Delhi. Kanpur was the HRA's place (1924).
The APPSC key for the HSRA founder is Bhagat Singh, who is listed as a founder leader of the HSRA. The other options had no connection with the HSRA.
Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged in Gorakhpur jail in December 1927. Gonda was where Lahiri was hanged and Faizabad was where Ashfaqullah was hanged.
Peter the Great of Russia made this remark about the commerce of India; Vasco da Gama, Clive and Dupleix are not associated with it.
Aztec civilisation was in central Mexico, the Maya in southern Mexico and Central America, the Muisca in Colombia and the Inca in Peru, giving the north-south order Aztec-Maya-Muisca-Inca.
Ferdinand Magellan's expedition (sponsored by Spain) made the first circumnavigation of the globe; the others listed did not.
Vasco da Gama found the sea route to India by reaching Calicut in 1498. 1492 is Columbus's voyage and 1453 is the fall of Constantinople.
At Calicut, Vasco da Gama was welcomed by the Zamorin (Samuthiri), the Hindu ruler. The others were Portuguese officials, not Indian kings.
Vasco da Gama sailed from Lisbon via the Cape of Good Hope to Calicut, discovering the sea route to India in 1498. Columbus sailed west and Cabot went to North America.
Da Gama first landed at Calicut (Kappad) on the Malabar coast in 1498, not at Cochin, Quilon or Surat.

Both statements are true: the Coercive Acts made reconciliation nearly impossible, and the Stamp Act (1765) was later repealed. However, the repeal came earlier and did not explain the effect of the Coercive Acts, so II is not the explanation of I.
The Mona Lisa was painted by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, not Michelangelo, Reynolds or Rembrandt.
Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804, making him the first Emperor of France; Charlemagne was Emperor of the Romans/Franks.
The notes do not record this remark. It is attributed to Sir P.S. Sivaswami Ayyar, not Gandhi, Jinnah or Nehru.
Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 5 March 1931, Gandhi agreed to attend the 2nd RTC, which followed soon after. The 1st RTC came before the pact, and Quit India and the Mountbatten Plan came much later.
Gandhi sailed to London for the 2nd RTC on the S.S. Rajputana.
Gandhi was the sole Congress representative at the 2nd RTC. Congress boycotted the 1st and was absent from the 3rd.
Ambedkar, along with Tej Bahadur Sapru, attended all three RTCs. Patel did not attend the 2nd RTC, and Malaviya was present only at the 2nd.
Gandhi attended only the 2nd RTC, as the sole Congress representative.
The 1st RTC was held from 12 Nov 1930 to 19 Jan 1931, so it began in 1930.
The notes do not mention Indian Christian representation. K.T. Paul represented Indian Christians at the 1st RTC.

Garbhini-GA2 is the first India-specific AI model that estimates foetal age in the second and third trimesters. It was built under GARBH-INi (DBT) by IIT Madras and THSTI, Faridabad, so both statements are correct.
Bum La is a pass at Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh on the India–China border, so option 2 is correct; Sikkim's passes are Nathu La and Jelep La.
Miri Hills are in Arunachal Pradesh, whereas Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills form the Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau. So Miri is the one not in Meghalaya.
Sarada Devi (Shardamani) married Ramakrishna in 1859, so she was his wife; she was not Ram Mohan Roy's wife, Vivekananda's mother or Keshab Chandra Sen's daughter.
Vivekananda is described as the best representative of Neo-Hinduism in the later 19th century, so option 2 is correct. Ramakrishna was his guru and a mystic, not the representative of Neo-Hinduism.
Vivekananda propounded Practical Vedanta, the idea that serving the poor is serving God (Daridra Narayana). Dayanand, Ram Mohan Roy and Gandhi are not associated with this term.
Sister Nivedita was Margaret Noble, the Western disciple of Vivekananda. The other names belong to different people.

Vivekananda stood for pure Vedanta and condemned caste discrimination and empty ritual, so I and III hold. II also fits his call for national regeneration. IV is not supported, since he did not treat the Veda as infallible, so the answer is I, II and III.

The notes say Vivekananda's philosophy was pure Vedanta and the truth of all religions, which supports I. II and III are consistent with his views on reviving Hindu traditions and admiring the West, so all three are correct.
Karma Yoga and My Master are both books by Swami Vivekananda. Ramakrishna was the subject of My Master, not its author.
Jnana Yoga, Karma Yoga and Raja Yoga are books by Swami Vivekananda. Ranade, Ram Mohan Roy and Ramakrishna did not write them.
The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Vivekananda on 1 May 1897, so option 3 is correct. Vidyasagar did not found it and 1899 is the wrong year.
Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call in his Gowalia Tank speech of 8 August 1942 at the launch of the Quit India Movement. Bose and Nehru are not linked to this slogan.
Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' slogan in his 8 August 1942 Gowalia Tank speech on the eve of the Quit India Movement.
This remark of Gandhi, that he was ready to risk anarchy to end slavery, belongs to the Quit India Movement of 1942, which was a 'Do or Die' mass struggle.
Gandhi coined 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) in his Gowalia Tank speech on 8 August 1942.
The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, which makes it the largest committee. PAC and COPU have 22 each, and the Petitions Committee has 25 (LS 15, RS 10).
The Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs has 30 members, 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, so 20, 10 is correct.
The ratio of a bank's capital to its risk-weighted (risky) assets is the CRAR, introduced in India in 1992 under BIS standards. SLR is a liquidity requirement, not a capital ratio.
Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank merged into Bank of Baroda on 1 April 2019, creating the third-largest PSB by business. Axis, HDFC and SBI were not part of the 2019 merger.
Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to banks against G-secs. Reverse repo is the opposite (banks lend to RBI), and PLR is set by each bank.
The RBI lends short-term funds to banks at the repo rate against G-secs. Bank rate is the long-term lending/discount rate, and reverse repo is the rate at which banks lend to RBI.
Both statements are wrong and swapped: repo is the short-term lending rate against G-secs, while bank rate is the long-term lending/discount rate. So neither is correct.
Reverse repo is the rate at which banks lend (park funds) with RBI. Repo is where banks borrow from RBI.
Expansionary policy cuts CRR/SLR, repo and bank rate. Raising the MSF rate (tied to repo and bank rate) is tightening, so only II is something RBI would not do.
Repo is the rate at which RBI lends overnight to banks against securities, which banks pay. It is a policy rate, not the cost of collateral, so option 4 is not correct.
Bank rate is RBI's (the central bank's) official lending/discount rate. It is not a rate set by moneylenders or scheduled banks.
A lower CRR leaves banks more lendable funds and raises the money multiplier, so credit creation increases.
South Arcot and Ramanathapuram lie on the Tamil Nadu/Coromandel coast, which is dry in the SW monsoon and gets its main rain from the retreating (North-East) monsoon in Oct–Dec.
The retreating monsoon brings clear skies, the NW low vanishes as the sun moves south, and the Oct heat gives rising temperatures, so all three indicate the monsoon declining.

Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain from the NE monsoon (Oct–Dec), and J&K gets significant winter rain from western disturbances, so neither depends mainly on the June–September SW monsoon. The other sets include states that are mainly SW-monsoon fed.
Chronologically: A.K. Gopalan (1950), Golaknath (1967), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), Minerva Mills (1980), so the order is IV, I, II, III.

Sarla Mudgal is the Supreme Court judgment that dealt with conversion to evade bigamy and urged a Uniform Civil Code. Maneka Gandhi, Raj Narain and Bommai concern personal liberty, elections and Article 356 respectively.
In Seema v. Ashwin Kumar (2006) the Supreme Court directed compulsory registration of all marriages. The other cases listed are not associated with this direction.
The Supreme Court appointed a mediation panel headed by Justice F.M.I. Kalifulla, with Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Sriram Panchu as members. Ravi Shankar was only a member, not the head.

The Supreme Court of India issued the order (2016) making the National Anthem compulsory in cinema halls before the screening of a film; the President, PM and Speaker issue no such judicial directions.

Rainforest growth is driven by hot, wet conditions all year (no seasons) with strong sunlight; the soils are nutrient-poor because of leaching, so I is wrong, and there is no seasonal change, so IV is wrong.
Slope angle, slope aspect and relative relief are the geomorphic factors affecting plant and animal distribution, so option 4 is correct; the notes do not cover this.
Taiga (coniferous forest) has a very wide annual temperature range, with long severe winters, so the statement of low variation in annual temperature is incorrect.
Spruce is a conifer of the taiga (temperate coniferous forest), so Temperate Forest fits. Temperate deciduous forest is broadleaf and sheds leaves in autumn, so it is not the answer.
Prairies are the temperate grasslands of North America (USA and Canada). Steppes are Eurasian, Pampas are in Argentina and Veld is in South Africa.
Raj Krishna coined the term to describe the stagnant growth of about 3.5% in the pre-reform era. It does not mean faster growth or inequality.

The Hindu rate of growth means the stagnant growth of about 3.5% in 1950-80, so the option about low growth during 1950-80 is correct. It has nothing to do with the Hindu population or with 2000-10, which was a high-growth period.
India's major economic reforms (the New Economic Policy of LPG) were introduced in July 1991 after the BoP crisis. The 1980s changes were only pro-business tweaks.
The Community Development Programme was launched in 1952, soon after the First Five Year Plan began in 1951.
The 1991 crisis was marked by high inflation, very low forex reserves (about two weeks of imports) and a large fiscal deficit; the other options describe healthy conditions.
Devaluation, gold pledging abroad and partial convertibility were all part of the 1991 response, but demonetisation was not (India's demonetisations were 1978 and 2016).
Economic reforms (the New Economic Policy) were introduced in 1991 in response to the BoP crisis; the 1980s measures were only partial liberalisation.
Structural Adjustment Programmes are IMF and World Bank packages meant to reduce fiscal imbalances and adjust the economy for long-term growth, which is option 4.
The National Renewal Fund was a safety net for workers affected by industrial restructuring, funding retraining, redeployment and compensation, so option 1 is right.

Full capital account convertibility was not adopted (the capital account is only partly convertible), while disinvestment and FDI opening are LPG measures. FDI in defence and retail came later but is still liberalisation.
The 1991 NEP rested on all three pillars: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG), so 'All of the above' is correct.
After 1991 FDI inflows and forex reserves both rose, while agriculture's share in GDP fell rather than rose; so the correct statements are FDI and forex reserves.
The basic structure doctrine was first propounded in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), not in Golaknath, Sajjan Singh or Shankari Prasad, which dealt with the amendability of Fundamental Rights.
Kesavananda Bharati (1973) first propounded the basic structure doctrine. Shankari Prasad and Golaknath dealt with amending Fundamental Rights, and Champakam Dorairajan did not lay down the doctrine.
The basic structure doctrine was outlined in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), which also overruled Golaknath; Gopalan did not deal with it.
The doctrine was propounded in Kesavananda Bharati (1973). Golaknath (1967) only limited Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights.
The doctrine was enunciated in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), which overruled Golaknath; Maneka Gandhi and Bommai came later and did not originate it.

Statement I is wrong: the election bar for the PM (Art. 329A(4)) came from the 39th Amendment and was struck down in Raj Narain, not the 42nd. Statement II is right: the 99th Amendment (NJAC) was struck down 4:1 for violating judicial independence.

Kesavananda Bharati is landmark for the basic structure doctrine: the Preamble's objectives embody the basic structure, which cannot be amended under Art. 368. The other options are unrelated to this case.
Kesavananda Bharati listed unity and sovereignty, federalism and the parliamentary system as basic, and judicial review is also basic. So all five features together are non-amendable under Art. 368.
In S.R. Bommai (1994), the Supreme Court reaffirmed secularism as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

Statement I is correct as only Parliament, by constitutional amendment, can place laws in the Ninth Schedule. Statement II is wrong: after Coelho (2007), Ninth Schedule laws are not immune and can be reviewed for damaging the basic structure.
Khilat was the robe of honour bestowed by the Mughal emperor, often one he had worn himself. The notes do not cover this, so no line is linked.

Nauroz (Navroj) is the Persian New Year festival, rooted in the Zoroastrian tradition and adopted at the Mughal court, so Zoroastrians is correct. The notes only say it is Persian and made a court festival by Akbar, not that it came from Zoroastrians.
Gulbadan Begum, Babur's daughter, wrote the Humayun-nama, a historical record of the period. Nur Jahan, Jahanara and Zeb-un-Nissa are known for coins, buildings and poetry instead.
Maham Anga, Akbar's foster-mother, founded the Khair-ul-Manazil madrasa in Delhi, known as Madarsa-e-Begum. The notes do not mention this.
The Firangi Mahal in Lucknow was the madrasa of Muslim jurisprudence, where Mulla Nizamuddin founded the Dars-e-Nizami. So Lucknow is correct.
The notes state that Naihati, site of the Rail Coach Factory and Museum announced in Rail Budget 2012-13, is Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's birthplace.
Radhasoami Satsang was founded by Shiv Dayal Singh (Soamiji Maharaj) at Agra in 1861. Shiv Narayan Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj, not the Radhasoami Satsang.
The Kuka (Namdhari) movement arose in Punjab, with its centre at Bhaini in Ludhiana under Ram Singh.

The Kuka movement was begun by Bhagat Jawahar Mal and organised by Baba (Satguru) Ram Singh, so the option naming Ram Singh is correct. The other options are Sikh Gurus who were not connected with it.
The Kuka movement was begun by Bhagat Jawahar Mal (Sian Sahib) and later organised by Ram Singh.
The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (1851) was a Parsi reform body, so it was started to reform the Parsees, not Sikhs or Muslims.
The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (1851) was a Parsi reform body, so it was started to reform the Parsees, not Sikhs or Muslims.
The ESI Act, 1948 covers hotels, restaurants, motor transport undertakings, newspaper establishments and private medical institutions, so all four are covered and option (1) is correct.

Raising the CRR means banks must keep a larger share of deposits as cash with the RBI, so less money is left for them to lend and liquidity falls. The RBI, not the Union Government, sets CRR, so options 2 and 3 are wrong.
PLR is set by each bank, and RBI does not fix it. SLR, CRR and the repo rate are all fixed by the RBI.
On 5 December 2019 the repo rate was 5.15%, so option 3 is correct.
Excess fluoride causes fluorosis, whose dental form shows as mottled teeth. Lung disease and intestinal infection are not linked to fluoride.
Fluoride causes fluorosis (dental, skeletal), not indigestion, so pair 4 is wrong. The other pairs (mercury-Minamata, cadmium-Itai-itai, nitrate-blue baby) are correct.
The Bengal basin (West Bengal and Bangladesh) lies in the Ganga-Brahmaputra arsenic belt, so its groundwater is mainly contaminated by arsenic.
Arsenic is a non-living (abiotic) chemical contaminant of groundwater, whereas bacteria, algae and viruses are living (biotic) agents.
Arsenic, fluoride and uranium are drinking-water pollutants in parts of India; sorbitol and formaldehyde are not, so I, III and V is correct.
Sludge is the settled solid by-product of sewage treatment, and its anaerobic digestion yields biogas (methane). Sewage is the raw input, not a by-product.
Treating domestic sewage before release reduces organic load and BOD and protects water bodies. Burning plastic or leaves pollutes air, and excess chemical fertiliser causes eutrophication.
Namami Gange pillars include sewerage/STP infrastructure, riverfront development and Ganga Gram, but River Aquifer Management is not a pillar.
As of 31 December 2021, Bihar had the most sewerage projects under Namami Gange.

The NGRBA was set up in 2009 (February 2009) under the Environment Protection Act, chaired by the PM, with a river basin approach. The notes give only the year 2009, which fits February 2009 rather than October 2008 or 2010.
M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934, not Nehru, Ambedkar or Tilak.
M.N. Roy first presented the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934; the INC adopted it as a demand only in 1935.
Jayaprakash Narayan was not a member of the Constituent Assembly; he and Lohia's Socialist Party demanded its dissolution. Patel, Kripalani and Munshi were members.
B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly.
Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Constitution Committee, not Ambedkar (Drafting Committee) or Prasad (Rules of Procedure/Steering).
The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.
The Lion Capital of Ashoka shows lions, with a bull, horse, elephant and wheel on the abacus; the camel does not appear.
The national flag has a length to breadth ratio of 3:2.
Pingali Venkayya designed the tricolour that became the basis of India's national flag; Gandhi only suggested adding the charkha.
Vande Mataram was first sung by Tagore at the 1896 INC session, not at the later sessions given.
The peacock is India's national bird.
The tiger is India's national animal; the lion is on the emblem but is not the national animal.
Planning Commission, NDC and Deputy PM are extra-constitutional/non-constitutional bodies or posts, whereas the Lok Sabha is a constitutional House of Parliament under Art 79 and 81.
Article 79 says Parliament = President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha; options omitting the President or adding the PM are wrong.
Article 79 makes the President together with both Houses the Parliament; the PM and the Speaker are not constituent parts.
Article 79 defines Parliament as the President plus Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; the PM, ministers and secretariat are not parts of it.
Under Article 79 Parliament consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; the Council of Ministers is not part of it.
Article 59(1) says the President is not a member of either House, whereas the PM and ministers are members of Parliament.
Article 79 names the President, the Council of States and the House of the People as Parliament, so all three are parts.
Article 79: Parliament comprises the President, the House of the People and the Council of States.
The distinctive feature of the Indian Parliament is that the President is a part of it, since no Bill becomes law without his assent, unlike the US Congress.

The statement is wrong because the President could nominate 2 Anglo-Indians to the LS until the 104th Amendment ended it from 25 Jan 2020; the question's key treats the 'no nominated members' statement as the incorrect one.
Parliament is the Union legislature, made up of the President and the two Houses under Art 79 in Part V.

I is wrong because UTs (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K) have RS seats; II is wrong because the President decides disputes on the EC's opinion, not the CEC alone; III is wrong because Parliament also includes the President. So none is correct.
Parliament is President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha; the Speaker, Chairman and Vice-President are not constituents.
IUCN stands for International Union for Conservation of Nature (founded 1948); it is a global union, not an Indian body, and 'Natural Resources' is the older/incorrect wording.
Dhrubajyoti Ghosh was the first Indian recipient of the IUCN Luc Hoffmann Award (2016) for his work on the East Kolkata Wetlands.
CMS COP14 was held in Samarkand on 12-17 Feb 2024 and was the first biodiversity COP after the Kunming-Montreal GBF, so I and III are correct; its theme was 'Nature knows no borders', so II is wrong.
