Nagaland recorded the highest decadal growth in 1991-2001 (64.41%), ahead of Sikkim, Manipur and Meghalaya, so it beats Bihar, Sikkim and UP.
Goa is the most urbanised State (about 62%), so it is the answer; Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Mizoram are less urbanised.

Socialism is associated with a state-controlled economy, in which the State owns and runs production. The other options (liquidating the bourgeoisie, removing the peasantry, military dictatorship) are not definitions of socialism.
Oxidation is the loss of electrons (it occurs at the anode), so option 2 is right; gain of electrons is reduction.
An electric cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy through redox reactions; a heater, fan and hair dryer consume electrical energy.
A car battery is lead-acid with sulphuric acid (not hydrochloric) and lead/PbO2 electrodes (not copper), so II and III are wrong; 12 V and ampere-hour capacity are correct, giving I and IV.
The dry (zinc-carbon) cell uses a paste of NH4Cl and ZnCl2 as electrolyte, so option 1 is correct.
A battery is a combination of two or more cells connected together, so the answer is battery; a bulb, switch and current are not cell combinations.
A dry cell is a galvanic cell whose working relies on a spontaneous redox reaction that produces electricity; electrolysis needs external energy.
The traditional lead-acid battery uses lead and PbO2 electrodes with sulphuric acid as electrolyte, so sulphuric acid is correct.
Mobile phone batteries are Li-ion batteries, so lithium is the prominent metal; zinc, nickel and copper are not the main ones.
A capacitor stores electric charge and energy in an electric field between its plates. It does not step voltage up or down, nor does it generate electricity.
A step-up transformer has more turns in the secondary than the primary, so it raises voltage (while lowering current). It does not increase power, since power is conserved apart from losses.

The notes list below-cost sales, poor cost recovery, rising commercial losses and project delays as causes of SEB trouble, but state autonomy over generation and distribution was not a cause. So option 3 is the one that is not a problem.

Power from central generating stations is allocated to states in proportion to their average actual energy consumption, not their aid, production or tax revenue. The notes do not state this allocation rule.
Gastrin is a hormone secreted by the stomach lining, not a gland. Thyroid, liver (the largest gland) and pancreas are all glands.
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, so pancreas is correct.
Insulin comes from the Islets of Langerhans (beta cells) of the pancreas, not the spleen, gonads or liver.
The adrenal glands secrete adrenaline and cortisol, which regulate blood pressure; parathyroid, thyroid and thymus do not primarily do so.
The pituitary is a single gland at the base of the brain, while the adrenals, testes and ovaries occur in pairs.
In diabetes mellitus blood glucose is high and excess glucose is excreted in urine, carrying water with it, so the person drinks more water to eliminate glucose.
Sodium ions (Na+), with potassium, create the ion movements across nerve cell membranes that carry electrical signals. Lithium, rubidium and caesium are not needed for this.
Neurons are specialised for excitability (responding to stimuli) and conductivity (transmitting impulses). Elasticity and flexibility are not their properties.
Hypermetropia is corrected by a convex (converging) lens, while concave lenses correct myopia.
The eye lens acts like a convex lens in a camera and forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.
Human blood is slightly alkaline, with a normal pH of about 7.35-7.45, so 7.5-8.0 is the closest option. Ranges below 7 would be acidic.
The cerebrum is the seat of memory, thinking and intelligence. The medulla and cerebellum control involuntary functions and balance.
Tachycardia means an abnormally fast heart rate (above normal), whereas a slow rate is bradycardia.
The brain handles thinking (cerebrum), heartbeat regulation (medulla) and body balance (cerebellum), so all of the above is correct.
The pinna is the external part of the ear, not of the brain. Medulla, thalamus and pons are brain parts.
The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain, much larger than the cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
The eye lens forms images on the retina about 2.5 cm behind it, so the focal length of a normal eye is about 2.5 cm.

The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens, which alters its focal length (accommodation). The pupil and iris control only the amount of light entering, and the retina receives the image.
Smooth (involuntary) muscle is found in the walls of internal organs like the stomach. Leg and arm muscles are skeletal, and the heart has cardiac muscle.
Human sperms remain viable and capable of fertilising in the female genital tract for about one to two days.
The MFN clause requires that an advantage given to one WTO partner be extended to all partners, which is non-discrimination among nations. Option 3 describes national treatment, not MFN.
The WTO is a rules-based body that promotes multilateral trade, with rules applying to all members on a non-discriminatory basis. It is not a lender, a peace body, or a promoter of unilateral trade.

Rayon is artificial silk made from wood pulp, which is why it counts as a forest-based product. Polymer, glass wool and allotropy are not artificial silk.
The notes do not cover the location of the Uttar Pradesh State Leather Development and Marketing Corporation, so no line is linked. The answer given is Agra.

Rabindranath Tagore criticised the burning of foreign cloth as a wasteful act and preferred the constructive programme. Jinnah did not even support the movement.

The Government of India Act 1935 provided for an All-India Federation of provinces and princely states. The 1909 and 1919 Acts had no federal scheme.

The Indian Councils Act 1861 saw Indians nominated as non-officials to the Viceroy's council. This was the beginning of representative institutions. Indirect election came only in 1892.

Godavari surplus water is used through the Polavaram project, which diverts 80 TMC to the Krishna basin and so helps drought-prone areas. The other rivers (Indus, Yamuna, Ganges) are not in Andhra Pradesh.

The notes state that Fundamental Rights are granted by the Constitution (Part III). They are not absolute (they are qualified by reasonable restrictions) and can be amended, so options 2 and 3 are wrong.

Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Constitution.

Amino acids in a protein are joined by peptide bonds (amide linkages formed between the carboxyl group of one and the amino group of the next); ester, glycosidic and phosphodiester bonds occur in lipids, carbohydrates and nucleic acids.

Fast-moving air near the train has lower pressure (Bernoulli's principle), so the higher pressure of the still air behind the man pushes him towards the train.

Polarisation occurs only for transverse waves; radio, UV and infrared are electromagnetic (transverse), while ultrasonic sound waves are longitudinal and cannot be polarised.

A horse pushes the ground backward and the ground pushes it forward with an equal and opposite reaction, which is Newton's third law.
By the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse (force x time) equals the change in momentum of the particle.
Refractive index = speed of light in air/speed in medium, and light is slower in any material medium than in air, so it is always greater than one.
Nuclear sizes are of the order of 10^-15 m, which is called a fermi (femtometre); angstrom is 10^-10 m, and newton and tesla are units of force and magnetic field.
A conductor that offers appreciable resistance to current is called a resistor, used to limit current in circuits.
Liquid pressure at depth is P = h·rho·g, so it depends on the height of the liquid column (and density), not on the base area.
Gravity is always attractive, whereas electric and magnetic forces can attract or repel; gravity is actually the weakest, and all are long range.
By the law of conservation of energy, energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.

Passing current through a conducting liquid (electrolyte) causes electrolysis, which is a chemical reaction decomposing the substance at the electrodes.

Fundamental Duties were added in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment.

Mexico lies in North America, south of the USA. The notes do not state this directly, so no line is linked.

Condition 1 for national party status is recognition as a State party in four or more States, so four is correct. Three is a distractor, since the 3-State rule applies only to the 2% Lok Sabha seats route.
DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party are all not national parties, so none of the listed parties qualifies and 'None of these' is correct.

The State Finance Commission, constituted by the Governor under Art. 243I, advises the Governor on sharing and assignment of State taxes and duties to local bodies. District planning bodies and State ministries do not have this role.
The 14th Finance Commission fixed the basic:performance grant ratio at 90:10 for gram panchayats. The 80:20 ratio is the tempting wrong option because it applies to municipalities.
The Constituent Assembly was constituted in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. The Cripps Mission (1942) only proposed an elected Constituent Assembly; it did not create one.

Members were indirectly elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies (set up under the 1935 Act), not directly by the public. Princely state representatives were nominated by rulers, but the question concerns elected members.

The Rummindei (Lumbini) pillar inscription records Ashoka's visit and marks Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace. The other pillars listed do not serve as this confirmation.
Kalsi in Dehradun district, Uttarakhand, has a set of the 14 Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka.
The Mauryan emperor Ashoka's Rummindei pillar inscription identifies Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace. So the Mauryan dynasty is the answer.
Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga War, with its casualties and Ashoka's remorse. The Rummindei pillar and Minor Rock Edict I do not give this account.
Rock Edict I bans animal sacrifice and festive gatherings (samaja) and reduces killing in the royal kitchen.

Ashoka's inscriptions record his own life events such as the Kalinga War, his internal administration such as the Mahamattas and rajukas, and foreign relations such as the Greek kings and southern kingdoms. So all the options are correct.
The Bhabru (Bairat) minor rock edict states his faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha, which proves he was Buddhist. The listed Major Rock Edicts and Pillar Edict IV do not state this.

The environment fails to sustain life when extraction exceeds regeneration and waste exceeds absorptive capacity. Option 1 describes extraction above regeneration, while the other options describe sustainable or healthy conditions.

Nyaya school was founded by Gautama (Akshapada), author of the Nyaya Sutra; Kapila is Samkhya, Kanada Vaisheshika and Jaimini Purva Mimamsa.
Purva Mimamsa (Mimamsa Sutras) was founded by Jaimini; Kanada is Vaisheshika, and the others are not founders of a darshana.

The Constitution does not mention a no-confidence motion; it flows from Art 75(3). It can be moved in the Lok Sabha only, so both statements are correct.

In the Kanpur Bolshevik case of 1924, Muzaffar Ahmad, Dange, Shaukat Usmani and Nalini Gupta were jailed. The other options name people who were not jailed in this case.

The Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929) against 31 labour and communist leaders drew worldwide publicity and sympathy from figures such as Einstein and Laski. The notes only say the long trial made the accused martyrs.

The CSP was founded in 1934 by Narendra Dev, JP and Lohia and others, with Narendra Dev as President and JP as General Secretary. Nehru and Bose were not its organisers, and Nehru did not formally join.
Acharya Narendra Dev was the President and a founder of the Congress Socialist Party. M.N. Roy, Vidyarthi and Pattom Thanu Pillai were not CSP leaders.
Pratishthana (Paithan) on the Godavari was the principal Satavahana capital. Nagarjunakonda was an Ikshvaku centre, and Pataliputra was the Magadhan capital.

The 'Test and Treat' policy was launched for HIV, under which every person found HIV-positive is offered free ART regardless of CD4 count. The notes mention free lifelong ART but do not state this policy.

HIV spreads through sexual contact, infected blood or transfusion, and from mother to child across the placenta. Mosquitoes and other blood-sucking insects do not transmit it, so statement III is wrong.
HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) causes AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome). The other diseases listed are not caused by HIV.

Both statements are true: the mission targets elimination by 2047, and sickle cell is inherited, with misshapen red cells that cannot carry oxygen properly. The disease's nature is the reason why a long-term elimination mission with screening and counselling is needed, so R explains A.
Kovvada, proposed for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, is at Ranastalam in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh, so Srikakulam is correct.
Kakrapar in Gujarat lies near Surat; the notes do not state this, but it is the correct location rather than Kota (Rawatbhata), Kalpakkam or Mumbai.
SODAR (sonic detection and ranging) is used for weather and atmospheric monitoring at the nuclear sites Kaiga and Kalpakkam, so option 4 is correct.
The notes give 8,780 MW (2026), not 6,780 MW. The answer 6,780 MW reflects the capacity at the time the question was set, so the notes do not confirm it.
The Manuguru heavy water plant, India's largest, was commissioned in 1991 in then-undivided Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana), so 1991 is correct.
The Manuguru heavy water plant, India's largest, was commissioned in 1991 in then-undivided Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana), so 1991 is correct.
Nangal in Punjab, on National Fertilisers premises, hosted India's first heavy water plant (1962), so Nangal is correct.
Kudankulam was delayed by the USSR's disintegration and civil-society protests; the 1991 economic crisis is not cited, so I and III only is correct.
India ranked 78th of 180 countries in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2018, so option (2) is correct.

In Swachh Survekshan 2023, Mhow was the cleanest cantonment and Navi Mumbai was 3rd, so III and IV are correct pairs. Varanasi was the best Ganga town (not rank 2), so II is wrong. Prayagraj was not the Safaimitra Surakshit Shehar winner, so I is wrong. Hence I and II are incorrectly paired.

The notes do not say India was a major producer of cotton yarn and wheat in the late 19th century. They state only that India shifted from exporting manufactures to supplying raw materials such as raw cotton. Iron and steel, sugar and alcohol and rice are not supported as major Indian exports.
Laissez-faire and one-way free trade flooded India with British goods and left no independent industrial development. They did not promote indigenous capitalism, so statement 2 is the incorrect one.
British rule ruined Indian industries and trade and left agriculture stagnant. The notes do not list the ruin of feudalism as a result, so it is the option that was not a result.
Gahira Guru was a Kanwar tribal leader from Chhattisgarh. The notes do not mention him, so no line settles it.

Statement I is right: PVTGs are in 18 States and 1 UT. Statement IV is right: Konda Reddi is on the AP PVTG list. Statement III is wrong because the count is 75, not 95. Statement II (a stagnant or declining population is a PVTG criterion) is a standard criterion, though the notes do not state it.
The Widal test is used to diagnose typhoid, which is caused by Salmonella Typhi.
Salmonella Typhi is the bacterium that causes typhoid. Varicella zoster is a virus, while Trypanosoma and Plasmodium are protozoa.
Chickenpox is a viral disease caused by the varicella zoster virus. Rabies and polio are also viral, but they are caused by different viruses, and cholera is bacterial.
The common cold is caused by a virus, the rhinovirus.
Measles is a viral disease, caused by the rubeola virus.
Rabies is a viral disease. Cholera, typhoid and whooping cough are bacterial.
Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium M. tuberculosis. The common cold, AIDS and dengue are viral.
Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Cholera is a faeco-oral, water-borne disease and does not spread through the air. The other options spread through the respiratory route.
Pneumonia is commonly caused by spherical bacteria (cocci), such as Streptococcus pneumoniae. The notes do not state this.
Cirrhosis is a liver disease and is not infectious. AIDS, hepatitis B and syphilis are transmitted between people.

Set II is wrong because AIDS is viral, not bacterial. Set IV is wrong because plague is bacterial. Set I is wrong because these diseases are infectious, not hereditary. Set III is wrong because colour blindness is genetic, but sickle cell anaemia is not sex-linked. So none is correct.
Rheumatic fever is an autoimmune reaction that follows a Streptococcus pyogenes infection. Type I diabetes is also autoimmune. The other options pair in infectious diseases.
Botulism is caused by the toxin of Clostridium botulinum.
Measles is a viral disease, so antibiotics cannot cure it.
Plague is spread by rat fleas, filariasis by Culex mosquitoes, and typhoid affects the intestine. Beri-beri is due to vitamin B1 deficiency. This gives the code 2 3 4 1.
Hepatitis B and HIV spread through blood, so contaminated tattoo needles can transmit them. Chikungunya is spread by Aedes mosquitoes, not by blood contact.
Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
AIDS is caused by HIV, a retrovirus that kills helper T cells.
Samudragupta was the first Gupta ruler to take the title Param Bhagavata, as shown by the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates. Chandragupta II came later.
V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' because of his extensive military conquests. Chandragupta Maurya, Pushyamitra and Kanishka did not get this epithet.
Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to take the title Maharajadhiraja. Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were only Maharaja.
Samudragupta was called Kaviraja (king of poets), and his lyrist coins show him playing the veena. Chandragupta I and II do not bear this title.
A stack is an erosional feature, left when a sea arch collapses. Tombolo, bar and spit are depositional ridges of sand or shingle.

Cliffs and arches are erosional features in the sequence cliff, cave, arch, stack. A notch is also cut by waves at the cliff base. A hook is a depositional spit feature, so options including IV are wrong.

Stalactites, stalagmites and pillars form when groundwater dissolves limestone and redeposits calcium carbonate in caves. They are therefore karst (underground water) features, not running water, wind or glacial ones.

Rebel proclamations appealed to all sections irrespective of caste and creed; the notes do not state this, so no line is linked. The other options are wrong because the revolt was not carefully planned by the rulers, rumours and prophecies did play a role, and the British did not control it quickly.
'In Memoriam' (1858) is a painting by Joseph Noel Paton, depicting British women and children awaiting death during the 1857 revolt. The notes do not cover it.
Sir James Outram and W. Taylor viewed the revolt as a conspiracy, with Muslims exploiting Hindu grievances. Lawrence saw it as a mere sepoy mutiny and Holmes as civilisation versus barbarism.
The Last Mughal (2006) was written by William Dalrymple, the historian of Delhi and the 1857 revolt. The notes do not mention this book.

Narmada and Son rise at Amarkantak, and Mahanadi rises in the nearby Sihawa hills. Among the options, Amarkantak is the best match; the notes do not place any of the three in the Eastern Ghats, Aravalli or Pulamu hills.
Narmada and Son rise at Amarkantak, and Mahanadi is linked to this region by the question's premise. Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri, Chambal, Betwa and Luni have different sources, so option 2 is right.
Narmada rises at Amarkantak in the Maikal range (Anuppur, MP). Bhedaghat is only a place on its course near Jabalpur.
Narmada and Son rise at Amarkantak. Damodar is a rift-valley river of Chota Nagpur, not an Amarkantak river, so it is the answer.
The notes do not give the length or catchment area of the Sabarmati, Mahi or Pennar, so they cannot confirm which basin is smallest. Sabarmati is the smallest of the listed basins.
Indravati and Pranhita are Godavari tributaries. Vamsadhara and Pennar are not, so only II and III are correct.
Penganga joins the Godavari, via the Pranhita, not the Ganga. So Ganga–Penganga is the wrong pair.
Pravara, Purna and Manair are Godavari tributaries. Koyna is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna, so it is the odd one out.
The notes list Suravaram Pratapa Reddy as the first president of the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha (Jogipet, 1930), so option 4 is correct.
The 2nd Rayalaseema Mahasabha met at Kadapa in September 1935 and opposed a separate Andhra state, which led to the Sri Bagh Pact.
At the Nandyal session (1928), on Gadicherla's proposal, the Ceded districts were renamed Rayalaseema, so Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao is correct.
B.N. Sarma moved the linguistic provinces resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 Feb 1918, so 1918 is correct. The 1917 date is for his separate-province resolution at Congress.
Nyapati Subba Rao was the first president of the Andhra Congress Committee formed in 1918, with Konda Venkatappayya as secretary.
Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati was established in 1954 after Rayalaseema's colleges were separated from Andhra University, so 1954 is correct.

Toothpaste is sold by many firms with differentiated brands (Colgate, Pepsodent, etc.), which is the hallmark of monopolistic competition. It is not perfect competition (products are not identical), nor monopoly or duopoly (many sellers).

FSSAI, set up under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, is the statutory authority that regulates food safety and standards in India. FDA is a US body, while WHO and FAO are international organisations.
TRAI stands for Telecom Regulatory Authority of India, the telecom regulator set up under the TRAI Act, 1997. The other options are invented expansions.
The Dobson Unit measures the thickness of ozone in a column of air from the ground to the top of the atmosphere. The other options are not ozone-measuring units.
The Dobson Unit measures the thickness or concentration of the ozone layer (1 DU = 0.01 mm of pure ozone at STP).
The Dobson unit measures the thickness of the ozone column from the ground to the top of the atmosphere. Decibel measures sound, and angstrom measures length.
Ozone column thickness from the ground to the top of the atmosphere is expressed in Dobson Units (DU).
CFCs release chlorine under UV in the stratosphere, and this chlorine breaks down ozone. CO₂ and CO are not the main ozone depleters, and nitrous oxide is less important.
CFCs are the main cause of ozone depletion because they release chlorine that destroys ozone. CO₂ and hydrocarbons are not the main depleters.
CFCs release chlorine in the stratosphere under UV, and this chlorine destroys ozone. SO₂, smog and photochemical oxidants are not the main cause.
CFCs are the main cause of ozone depletion, releasing chlorine in the stratosphere that breaks ozone down. CO₂, methane and N₂ are not the main depleters.
Freon, a CFC, is the gas used in domestic refrigerators. Radon, sodium and fluorine are not refrigerants.
The Junnar (Manmodi) inscription was issued by Ayama, Nahapana's minister; Ushavadatta's records are at Nasik and Karle, so he is the tempting wrong option.
The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman records that Sudarshana lake was built by Pushyagupta, governor of Chandragupta Maurya, which shows Gujarat was within his kingdom.
The Saka era began in 78 AD and the exam key credits it to Kanishka. Vikramaditya and 58 BC relate to the Vikrama era, and Rudradaman did not found it.
Vikram Samvat began in 57 BC (often written 58 BC), so 57 BC is the matching option; 78 AD is the Saka era.
Vikram Samvat began in 57/58 BC, Saka in 78 AD, Gupta in 319/320 AD, and Muslim rule era in 1192 AD, so all four statements are correct.
The Saka era began in 78 AD; 58 is Vikrama (BC), 320 is Gupta and 606 is Harsha.
Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights by special majority under Art. 368 (Kesavananda), provided the basic structure is not altered. The Supreme Court only reviews, it does not amend.
Article 368 in Part XX lays down Parliament's power and procedure to amend the Constitution. The other Articles are not about amendment.
Article 368 deals with Parliament's power to amend the Constitution and its procedure. The other options concern different subjects.
Article 368 gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution. Arts 352, 356 and 360 deal with emergencies.

Statement I is true: Art. 368 gives the amendment procedure. Statement II is false: only federal provisions need ratification by half the States, and most amendments need only a special majority in Parliament.
The amendment procedure is in Article 368, the sole Article of Part XX.
The Constitution is amended under Article 368, which gives Parliament its power and procedure to amend. The other Articles concern emergencies.

Only Parliament can alter State boundaries under Art. 3, but option 4 is the wrong statement here. The notes only state that Parliament alone has the power, and do not mention any intimation to the States.
Statement I is false because an amendment Bill can be introduced in either House. Statement II is false because ratification is needed from only half the States, not all.
Railways, post and telegraph were introduced under Dalhousie (1848–56). Wellesley, Cornwallis and Canning are not linked with introducing railways.
Sati was declared illegal in 1829 under Governor-General William Bentinck, so option 1 is correct.
Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta (Kolkata) Madrasa in 1781. The notes do not state this fact.
Bentinck's key reforms were the abolition of Sati, suppression of infanticide and of Thuggee. Slavery was made illegal in 1843 under Ellenborough, not Bentinck, so it is the odd one out.
Dalhousie's measures included railways, post and telegraph, and the PWD. A Factories Act for Indian labour is not among them, so option 4 is not his scheme.
Marquess Hastings (1813–23) pursued intervention and wars, including humiliating treaties on the Peshwa. This led to the end of the Peshwa's position in the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
For January-December 2021, AP's FDI rank was 13th (the 12th and 14th ranks belong to other periods). The quoted US$ 178.09 billion figure is misprinted, so the rank is the fact to learn.

Protein digestion begins in the stomach with pepsin, which acts on proteins; among the options, pepsin is the only protein-digesting enzyme (lactase acts on lactose, urease on urea, zymase on sugar fermentation).
Parietal cells secrete HCl, which activates pepsinogen into pepsin; damaging them mainly impairs protein digestion, not carbohydrate or lipid digestion.
Salivary amylase in the mouth starts the digestion of carbohydrates (starch); protein digestion begins in the stomach and fat digestion in the small intestine.
The eye lens acts as a convex lens and forms a real, inverted image on the retina; the brain interprets it as upright.
Blood is a fluid connective tissue, consisting of cells suspended in plasma matrix.
The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain, being the seat of intelligence, memory and voluntary action.
A person who cannot see near objects distinctly (nearest clear distance greater than normal 25 cm) has hypermetropia; myopia is the opposite defect, where distant objects are blurred.
The Rampa rebellion, led by Tammandora in the East Godavari Agency, took place in 1879; the 1922-24 revolt was Alluri's later Rampa rebellion.
The notes do not mention the Kallar; they were a community of the Madurai region in Tamil Nadu, who revolted against British rule.
Velu Thampi Dalawa was the Diwan of Travancore and revolted against the British in 1808-09, issuing the Kundara Proclamation.
CFCs, halons and carbon tetrachloride are all listed as ozone-depleting substances, so all three statements are correct and the answer is I, II and III.
A ball balanced on top of a vertical rod is in unstable equilibrium: a small displacement lowers its potential energy, so it moves further away from its position instead of returning.
When the string snaps, the centripetal force vanishes, so by Newton's first law the stone continues in the direction of its velocity at that instant, which is tangential to the circle.
Trees are very tall plants with a hard, thick, brown woody stem (trunk). Herbs have soft green stems and shrubs are shorter and bushy.
Specific gravity (relative density) is the density of a substance divided by the density of water at 4°C, where water's density is maximum (1 g/cm³).
Water expands by about 9% on freezing. In a tightly sealed, full glass vessel it cannot expand, so the pressure breaks the vessel.
Glycol (ethylene glycol type) is an anti-freeze additive. It lowers the freezing point of aviation fuel at high altitude, so the petrol does not freeze.
Sodium acetate is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (acetic acid). Its acetate ion hydrolyses to give OH-, so the solution is basic. NaCl is neutral; CuSO4 and FeCl3 are acidic.
Salt (sodium chloride) was the symbol of the freedom struggle through Gandhi's Dandi March and Salt Satyagraha (1930) against the salt tax.
Magnesium sulphate is used as a mordant in the dyeing and tanning industry. The other magnesium compounds are not used for this purpose.
Phenolphthalein turns pink in basic (alkaline) solution. Tube B has an alkali, while water, acid and NaCl solution are neutral or acidic and leave it colourless.
Salts are ionic compounds with strong ionic bonds, so they have high melting and high boiling points. The statement that they have low melting points is false.

Chromatography separates mixture components because they move at different rates through a medium (stationary phase) carried by a solvent. Filtration, distillation and evaporation do not work this way.
The wavelength is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs. A crest and the adjacent trough are half a wavelength apart.
Electromagnetic waves are transverse, with electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel. So the claim that they are longitudinal is not true.
From Hooke's law F = kx, k = F/x, so its unit is newton per metre (N/m).
Charles Darwin propounded the theory of evolution by natural selection (On the Origin of Species, 1859). Wallace independently proposed a similar idea, but Darwin is credited.
Constant velocity means constant speed and direction, so motion is in a straight line, acceleration is zero and displacement grows linearly. Speed changing with time is therefore not correct.
The flying fish is a true fish (class Pisces) with gills and fins. Silverfish is an insect, jellyfish is a cnidarian and cuttlefish is a mollusc.
Speed of light in a medium is v = c/n. Quartz has the lower refractive index (1.46 vs 1.77), so light travels faster in quartz: vq > vs.
Bee-keeping is a primary-sector activity (direct use of nature, a genetic/agricultural activity), whereas call-centre work, tuition and banking are services, i.e. tertiary.
Dairy is animal husbandry, a genetic primary activity that breeds and rears livestock, so it belongs to the primary sector, not to processing or services.

Trade is a service (tertiary) activity and fisheries are primary. Water supply is grouped under the industrial sector (the revised IIP added water supply and waste management), and GDP is compiled by the Central Statistical Organisation, giving a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III.
Agriculture is a primary activity (direct use of nature), while services such as transport, trade and banking are tertiary, so the answer is primary and tertiary respectively.
Farming depends most directly on climate (rainfall, temperature, seasons) for crop growth. Fishing and mining are less climate-dependent and manufacturing least of all.
Gandhi had full trust in the Swarajists' bona fides and valued them as respected leaders; the notes do not state this attitude.
Rajendra Prasad was a No-Changer and not a Swaraj Party founder or member, whereas Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das founded it.

The Swaraj Party was formed after the NCM was suspended (I) and aimed at council entry to end or mend the councils and obstruct the 1919 Act's working (II). Repression and the wish to gain administrative experience were not its stated reasons.
C.R. Das was the Gaya Congress president whose council-entry resolution was defeated; he then formed the Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru and became its president.
Tarun Ram Phukan led the Swaraj Party in Assam; the notes do not cover this.
Madan Mohan Malaviya and Motilal Nehru decided to launch the Independent Party on 16 Dec 1922; the notes do not state this.
Only Motilal Nehru was a Swaraj Party founder. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was a No-Changer, and Gokhale died in 1915 before the party existed.
Shri Krishna Singh established the Swaraj Dal in Bihar; the notes do not cover this.
Belgaum (1924) was the only INC session presided over by Gandhi.
Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session in 1924, his only INC presidency.
Belgaum (1924) was the only session presided over by Gandhi.
Vithalbhai Patel, a Swarajist, was elected Assembly President in 1925. Vallabhbhai Patel was a No-Changer.
The Sarkaria Commission (R.S. Sarkaria, set up 1983, report 1988) was the Centre-appointed commission on Centre-State relations. The other options are not Centre-State bodies.
The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with electoral reform (State funding of elections), not Centre-State relations; Sarkaria, Rajamannar and Punchhi all did.
The NCRWC, also called the Constitutional Review Commission (Feb 2000), was chaired by M.N. Venkatachaliah.
The National Integration Council is headed by the Prime Minister, and Dr. Manmohan Singh was the PM at the time of this question, so he was its chairman.
The 6th BIMSTEC Summit (Bangkok, April 2025, Thailand in the chair) was held under the theme "Prosperous, Resilient and Open", so option 2 is correct. The other options are invented themes.
The IRDA Act 1999 set up IRDAI as the statutory regulator of insurance. SEBI regulates securities and RBI regulates banks, while GIC is only an insurer.
The notes do not cover Rashtriya Krishi Bima Yojana or its implementing agency.
Insurance penetration is total premium as a percentage of GDP, not the number of insured persons per 100 population. So none of the given definitions is correct.

The notes confirm that insurance is a para-banking activity (banks sell it as corporate agent or via joint venture). They do not mention credit cards or factoring, so only the insurance link is supported.
In e-banking, 'e' stands for electronic, meaning banking services delivered through electronic channels such as the internet and mobile. The other options are not real terms.

UDAN is the Ministry of Civil Aviation's Regional Connectivity Scheme aimed at tier II and III cities, so statements I and III are correct. Statement II is wrong because the first flight was in April 2017, not 2015.
UDAN stands for Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik, so 'A' stands for 'Aam' (common).
In a pocket veto the President neither assents, rejects nor returns the Bill, and Art. 111 prescribes no time limit, so he can hold it for an indefinite period.
The Indian President has absolute, suspensive and pocket vetoes, so the answer is Yes; he lacks only the qualified veto.
Art. 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session; the Speaker, Chairman and Attorney-General have no such power.
Art. 123 is the ordinance-making provision for the President. Art. 360 deals with financial emergency, Art. 200 with the Governor's assent to Bills and Art. 356 with President's Rule.
The maximum gap between sessions is six months and the ordinance lapses six weeks after reassembly, so its maximum life is six months plus six weeks.
Commutation substitutes a lighter form of punishment (e.g. death to rigorous life imprisonment). Remission only reduces the period.
Remission reduces the duration of the sentence while keeping its character (2 years RI to 1 year RI). Commutation changes the form of punishment.
The President (Art. 72) and the Governor (Art. 161) both have pardoning powers, though the Governor's are narrower, as he cannot pardon a death sentence.

All four statements match the succession: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangamas (1485), Vira Narasimha deposed Immadi Narasimha (1505), Krishnadevaraya followed his brother Vira Narasimha, and Achyutaraya succeeded his half-brother Krishnadevaraya. So all are correct.
Annamacharya (1408-1503) is listed as a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha, so option 4 is right.
Saluva Narasimha of Chandragiri expelled Praudha Raya in 1485 and began the Saluva dynasty. Immadi Narasimha was the last Saluva, and Vira Narasimha founded the Tuluva dynasty.
Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty, which began in 1505 under Vira Narasimha, and he succeeded Vira Narasimha in 1509.
The notes do not mention any battle of Golconda or Quli Qutb Shah.
Geomorphic processes (weathering, erosion, mass wasting, deposition) are the processes that shape the Earth's surface; the notes do not state this term directly, so no line is linked.
Chemical weathering is fastest in hot and wet (humid) climates, since higher temperature and more rain speed up chemical reactions. Cold or dry climates slow it.
Clay particles are finer than 0.002 mm, whereas silt is 0.002-0.05 mm and fine sand is 0.05-2 mm.
Water-holding capacity rises as particles get smaller, so clay holds the most, then silt, then sand, which drains easily.

Lithosol is an azonal soil (a young, shallow soil on rock without a developed profile), while sierozem, podzol and solanchak are zonal/intrazonal types. The notes do not cover this, so no line is linked.
National income is compiled officially by the CSO (now NSO) under MoSPI; ISI, NCAER and the Indian Standards Institution do not compute it.
IIP is a monthly index, released on the 28th of each month, not quarterly or yearly.
The 2015 revision replaced the 2004-05 base with 2011-12 (2009-10 was never a base year), so 2011-12 is correct.
In 2015 the national accounts base was revised from 2004-05 to 2011-12, so 2011-12 was the base then in use.
The new GDP series released in 2015 moved the base from 2004-05 to 2011-12.
The CSO's 2015 revision changed the base year from 2004-05 to 2011-12.
Bakhtiyar Khalji, Ghori's slave/general, conquered Bihar and Bengal (1193-1203). Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate, and Iltutmish and Yaldauz did not conquer these regions.
Bakhtiyar Khalji, Ghori's general, sacked Nalanda, Vikramashila and Odantapuri during his conquest of Bihar. It was not destroyed by Mahmud or by later Sultans.
The Lakshmana Era (Lakshmana Samvat, from AD 1119) is linked to the Sena dynasty of Bengal, whose king Lakshmanasena gave it its name. The Pratiharas, Palas and Chauhans did not start this era.
Article 224 provides for additional judges (224(1)) and acting judges (224(2)) in High Courts; Art. 220 restricts post-retirement practice and Art. 231 concerns a common HC.
Under Article 231, Parliament by law establishes a common High Court for two or more States (or States and a UT); neither the SC nor the President can do so by order.
Delhi High Court was the first to announce dedicated commercial benches in March 2015, so it is the correct option.
Andaman and Nicobar Islands fall under the Calcutta High Court, which is in West Bengal, so West Bengal is correct.
Statement II is correct as Calcutta, Bombay and Madras HCs were set up in 1862. Statement I is wrong because India now has 25 High Courts, not 24, after Andhra Pradesh HC began in 2019.
V. Gopala Gowda was sworn in as Chief Justice of the Orissa High Court on 25 March 2010, before becoming an SC judge.
Under Art. 224A the HC Chief Justice requests a retired judge to sit only with the President's prior consent (and the judge's consent), so the President is correct.
Minamata disease was caused by methyl mercury in industrial wastewater that biomagnified in fish, so mercury-polluted water is correct; chromium, cadmium and lead are not the cause.
Minamata disease resulted from eating fish contaminated with methyl mercury, so mercury is correct, not lead or cadmium. The notes date its discovery to 1956, but the agent is mercury regardless.
The International Tropical Timber Organization has its headquarters in Yokohama, Japan. The notes do not cover this.
Greenpeace International is headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The notes do not cover this.
The Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM) is in Bhopal, not Kolkata, so the pair in option 3 is wrongly matched.
NEERI, the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute, is a CSIR laboratory located in Nagpur.
The Forest Research Institute (FRI) is located in Dehradun, which has its roots in the Imperial Forest Research Institute of 1906.
The 104th Indian Science Congress was held in January 2017 at Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati, so option 2 is correct.
The 98th Indian Science Congress (2011) was held in Chennai, so option 1 is correct.
Part IX-A (74th Amendment) is the constitutional base for urban local government only; rural Panchayats are under Part IX.
The 74th Amendment Act gave constitutional status to urban local governments; the 73rd dealt with rural Panchayats.
The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA 'The Municipalities' (Articles 243P-243ZG).
Electoral rolls and elections to municipalities are conducted by the State Election Commission (Art. 243ZA), not the State Government or the municipal bodies.
Municipalities have a fixed five-year term under Art. 243U, and the Mayor's tenure is taken to match this five-year term.
Under Art. 243R, municipality members are directly elected from the wards; only a few additional persons may be added by State law, without a vote.
Under Art. 243V, qualification follows the law for State Legislature elections, and being a registered voter is a basic condition; permission from the Principal or party membership is not required.
Article 243ZA vests superintendence, direction and control of municipal elections in the State Election Commission.
Under Art. 243Q, a Nagar Panchayat is constituted for a transitional area, i.e. one changing from rural to urban.
The notes give the MSP of common paddy for 2016-17 as ₹1,470 per quintal, so option 1 is correct.

Statement I is treated as correct: the notes say the SMP was replaced by FRP from 2009-10, and the question's wording reflects the earlier statutory price. Statement II is correct because the Sugarcane (Control) Order operates under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. So both statements are correct.

Statement I is wrong: only wheat and paddy are procured effectively open-ended, while pulses and oilseeds are limited to a 25% cap and coarse grains need prior approval. Statement II is wrong: MSP is a floor price, not a ceiling that the market never exceeds. So neither statement is correct.
The notes list the price-support phase (MSP, FCI buffer stocks, PDS) after the Green Revolution phase. So the phase characterised by MSP and procurement-based price policy is option 3.
Areca nut, coffee and turmeric have no MSP, which eliminates every option containing 1, 3 or 7. Barley, finger millet (ragi), groundnut and sesamum are all covered by MSP, so option 2 is correct.
The Sea of Tranquility (Mare Tranquillitatis) is a lunar mare, a dark plain on the Moon where Apollo 11 landed in 1969.
The Moon's surface gravity is about 1/6th of Earth's, so option 1 is right; the other options give wrong ratios or compare with Mars.
Moon's gravity is only about 1/6th of Earth's, so the same jump effort carries a person higher; roughness, temperature or lack of atmosphere are not the cause.
On Apollo 11 (20 July 1969) Neil Armstrong was the first to step on the Moon, followed by Aldrin; Collins stayed in orbit.
Earth's escape velocity is about 11.2 km/s, the minimum speed needed to leave Earth's gravity without further propulsion.
The Moon's mean distance is about 384,400 km; 364 thousand km is the closest option offered (near perigee distance), so the key is the best match.
Moonlight travels about 384,400 km at the speed of light (300,000 km/s), so it takes roughly 1.3 seconds, i.e. about one second.
Rotation and revolution of the Moon both take about 27 d 7 h 43 min (tidal locking), so the same face always points to Earth.
The Moon's rotation and revolution periods are equal (27 d 7 h 43 min), so the same face always faces Earth; the opposite-direction option is wrong.
The notes state the 2021-22 health budget was Rs 13,830.44 crore, a rise of 21.1%, so option 1 is correct.
Seven new ESI hospitals were approved in February 2021, including a 100-bed hospital at Vizianagaram due by March 2023, so the answer is Seven.
The September 2023 colleges were Vizianagaram, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Rajamahendravaram and Nandyal. Pulivendula and Adoni came later, so only I, II and IV are correct.

The notes do not state the administrative motive behind spreading modern education, so no line settles it. The answer rests on the colonial need for a class of educated Indians to fill minor posts, not on promoting Indian culture.
The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded in 1784 by Sir William Jones to promote Oriental studies. The other names were not its founders.
The notes do not say who identified Sandrokottos with Chandragupta Maurya. Sir William Jones made this identification, which was a key step in fixing the chronology of ancient India.
The notes do not mention Colebrooke's post. He taught Sanskrit at Fort William College in Calcutta, which was set up to train Company civil servants in Indian languages.
The notes do not cover this. Madan Mohan Malaviya, founder of Banaras Hindu University, pressed for religious education in Indian universities.
The Calcutta Madrasa, set up in 1781 by Warren Hastings, was the first Madrasa established by the British. Madras and Aligarh are only name-alikes or later institutions.

The Asiatic Society of Bengal, founded in 1784 by Sir William Jones, was meant for Oriental studies, meaning research into India's past and antiquities. It was not set up for English education or social reform.
The Calcutta Madrasa, set up in 1781 by Warren Hastings, was the first Madrasa established by the British. Madras and Aligarh are only name-alikes or later institutions.
Finland joined NATO on 4 April 2023 as the 31st member, not in February 2023. So statement I is not true while statement II is true, making 'Only I' correct.
India is not an APEC member, and Russia is not a NATO member, since NATO is a Western alliance founded in 1949. Both statements are false, so 'Neither I nor II' is correct.
The Nordic Council comprises Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden. The United Kingdom is not a member, so it is the correct answer.
Russia has not joined NATO. The recent entrants were Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024), while France, Germany and Britain were already members, so the stated answer does not fit the notes.

IORA dates from 1997, so it was not set up recently in response to piracy or oil spills. It covers many areas such as trade, fisheries, disaster management and tourism, not maritime security alone, so both statements are false.
Anantapur was the headquarters of the single Ceded Districts collectorate under Munro (1800–1807/08). Bellary and Cuddapah became seats only after the 1808 split.
Peddapuram was ruled by the Vatsavayi (Vatsavai) dynasty for about three centuries, so option 3 is correct.
Chittoor was formed as a district in 1911, the year it gave Kadapa its present area. 1858 is Kurnool and 1882 is Anantapur.
Moturpha was a tax on looms, a trade/profession tax on weavers and artisans. It was not a toddy, sugar or salt tax.

Land-tax management in Andhra had three methods (zamindari, ryotwari, mahalwari), so A is true. Zamindari was imposed in the Northern Circars and ryotwari was introduced first in the Ceded Districts (Datta mandals) in 1802, so B is true. Hence both are correct.
The notes give no 2001 census literacy rate for Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh, so no line settles it. The answer, 53.5 percent, comes from the 2001 census data.
As per Census 2011, Scheduled Castes make up 17.08% of Andhra Pradesh's population, so option (2) is correct. The other figures are not the SC share.
Surya Sen ('Masterda') led the Chittagong Armoury Raid of 18 April 1930 and planned it. Ganesh Ghosh was only an associate, while Azad belonged to the HRA/HSRA in north India.

Statement III is not true: the Assembly bombs of 8 April 1929 were non-lethal smoke bombs meant to make the deaf hear, not to kill people. Statements I and II are true, since Bhagat Singh was a founder leader of the socialist HSRA.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931 in the Lahore Conspiracy Case. Bismil and Roshan Singh were hanged in the Kakori case.

The message describes the Maratha disaster at Panipat (1761), where Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao's forces lost Vishwas Rao and Sadashiv Rao Bhau. The power that suffered the defeat was the Maratha power under the Peshwa, not the Mughal emperor or Shuja-ud-Daula, who sided with Abdali.
Panipat III (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali. It was not Mughals vs Abdali, and Nadir Shah's invasion was in 1739.
The Treaty of Purandar (1776) was concluded between the Marathas and the English (the Calcutta council), annulling the earlier Treaty of Surat. The other options name parties that were not involved.
VCIC is the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC), a gateway to ASEAN markets, and covers nine coastal districts of AP, so all the statements hold and 'All of these' is correct.

Machilipatnam is the imitation jewellery cluster and Makavarapalem is the alumina and aluminium park, matching d-IV and c-III. This fits option 1, which also pairs Gandrajupalle with Silk and Garments and Kopparthi with Engineering.
The notes do not mention the Kadapa-Renigunta four-lane highway announcement, so no line can be linked.
Golden Rice is engineered to produce beta carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A, so vitamin A is the answer.
Golden Rice is a transgenic crop made to contain beta carotene, the precursor of vitamin A, to fight vitamin A deficiency.
Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting (its deficiency causes slow clotting), so it is the vitamin responsible for coagulation.
Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting and its deficiency causes slow clotting; vitamins A, B and C do not have this role.
Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin when exposed to sunlight (UV), which is why it is called the sunshine vitamin; vitamins A, K and E are not made this way.
Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, while vitamin C and B-group vitamins (such as B12) are water-soluble, so 'A and D' is the correct pair.
In Andhra the Swadeshi Movement was popularly called the Vandemataram Movement; the other options are unrelated movements.
Mark Hunter was the principal of the Government Arts and Teachers' Training College, Rajahmundry, who banned Vandemataram badges in 1907; the other names are distractors.
The Rajahmundry College incident of 1907 (badge ban and punishment of students) marked the beginning of student participation in Andhra's freedom struggle.

Konda Venkatappayya is named as the president of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam (1910); Nyapati Subbarao is the tempting alternative given in one key but he is not the one named in the table.
The Andhra Jateeya (National) Kalasala at Machilipatnam was founded in 1910, so 1910 is correct.
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham founded Ram Mohan School in 1909 giving free education to depressed communities; Veeresalingam is a different reformer.
Ghazi Malik was the name of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq before accession, and he founded the Tughlaq dynasty in 1320.
The Slave dynasty was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak, not Balban (a later ruler), so pair 1 is wrong; the other pairs are correct.
The Delhi Sultanate began in 1206 with Aibak and lasted until 1526.
The Khaljis were of Turkish (Khalji) origin; the first Afghan Sultan was Bahlol Lodi.
Bahlol Lodi was the first Afghan Sultan, so the Lodis were the Afghan dynasty; all earlier ones were Turks or claimed Prophet's descent.
The order is Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi, so IV, I, III, II is correct.
Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty in 1206.
Amir Khusrau lived in the reign of Alauddin Khalji.
Alauddin Khalji is known for market control and military reforms; the other Sultans are not associated with them.
India is 2nd, not 1st, in vegetable production (China is 1st), so statement (2) is incorrect. India is 1st in milk and rice and among the top sugarcane producers.

Sea buckthorn is a cold-desert, high-altitude shrub that checks soil erosion and desertification and has nutritional value (I and III). It is not a notable biodiesel source and its timber has no major commercial value, so II and IV are wrong.
Cloves are the dried, unopened flower buds of the clove tree (Syzygium aromaticum), not seeds, fruits or leaves.

Maharashtra is not the largest banana producer; that is Tamil Nadu or Andhra Pradesh, depending on the year's data (the notes do not cover this). The other pairs are correct, so Banana - Maharashtra is the wrongly matched pair.
Nagpur is famous for its oranges (the Nagpur orange). Ratnagiri is known for Alphonso mango, Darjeeling for tea, and Lucknow for mango (Dasheri).
Uttar Pradesh is the largest mango producer, so a mango export zone was set up there. The notes confirm only UP's leadership in mango, not the export zone itself.

Banana (the Cavendish) has a very narrow genetic base because it is propagated vegetatively, so it is at risk from diseases such as Panama wilt. Apple, mango and cherry have broader genetic diversity.
The 1922 Rampa revolt (Alluri Sitarama Raju, 1922-24) was provoked by the Madras Forest Act, 1882. The Santhal revolt was 1855-56 and the Sepoy revolt 1857, so neither fits.
Birsa Munda was captured in the Jamkopai forest, Chakradharpur, on 3 February 1900, so option 3 is correct.
Uttar Pradesh has the largest long-run share (35%) of sugar capacity, so it has the most sugar factories. Maharashtra leads only in the latest season's output.
Southern tropical cane gives higher sucrose content and yield than northern subtropical cane, which drives the shift south. Power, labour cost and rail are not the stated reasons.
Southern cane has higher yield and sucrose and a longer crushing season (200–250 days vs 150–180 days). Cheap labour is not the reason, so I, II and III are correct.
Both statements are correct: the government's partial decontrol freed millers from the levy sugar obligation, and the Rangarajan Committee also recommended decontrolling the sugar industry.
Cement is made from limestone (main), silica/alumina (clay) and gypsum. Option 2 includes all three, while the others omit one.
Dalmianagar (Rohtas, Bihar) is known for its cement factory, so cement is correct.
Chunar (UP) is a cement cluster, so the Cement Industry is correct.
The notes do not give mill counts by state, so no line supports this answer.
Bhopal is known for its pesticide industry (the Union Carbide pesticide plant), which is why option 1 is correct.
Secular stagnation was put forward by Alvin Hansen. The notes do not cover it; Solow and Harrod-Domar are different growth models.
Differential savings propensities (different saving rates for wage and profit earners) are a feature of Kaldor's distribution-based growth theory. The notes do not cover Kaldor.
The Second Plan (1956-61) was based on the Mahalanobis model. Harrod-Domar was the First Plan's basis; Manne-Rudra was the Fourth Plan's and Sandy-Chakravarty the Third Plan's.
The First Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model. Mahalanobis was the basis of the Second Plan, and the Gandhian and Sarvodaya plans were non-official.
The Second Plan followed the Mahalanobis model. Solow was never used for an Indian plan, and Harrod-Domar (Domar) was the First Plan's model.
The Second Plan was built on the Mahalanobis model with its heavy-industry priority. Harrod-Domar was the First Plan's model, and Solow was never used.
The capital-output ratio is the amount of capital needed per unit of output, as the notes' definition of COR states. The other ratios are not defined that way.
The 2015 amendment merged the PIO card into OCI, creating the 'OCI Cardholder' with a lifelong visa. It did not give voting rights to NRIs, so option 2 is the change that was not made.
The NRC draft was published for Assam, so option 1 is correct. The other States listed had no NRC draft published.
The pituitary lies at the base of the brain and secretes growth hormone (GH). Over-secretion of GH increases growth in length, so all three statements are true.
The adult human skull has 22 bones (8 cranial and 14 facial), or 28 if the ear ossicles and hyoid are counted. The notes do not state this, so the answer rests on that standard count.
The liver has a role in fat digestion because it makes bile, which emulsifies fats. Bile contains no enzymes, so the Reason is false. The fat-digesting enzyme lipase comes from the pancreas.
Arthroplasty is surgical replacement or reconstruction of a joint, such as hip-joint replacement. It is not heart surgery, a kidney transplant or a transfusion.
The pituitary is the master endocrine gland. It controls other glands through its hormones such as TSH and ACTH.
Fertilization normally occurs in the oviduct (fallopian tube), where the sperm meets the ovum. The uterus is where the embryo implants afterwards.
BMD (bone mineral density) testing measures bone density. It is used to diagnose osteoporosis, not infections such as dengue, malaria or AIDS.
Fertilization normally takes place in the fallopian tube (oviduct). The cervix and uterus are not the usual site.
Bulimia is an eating disorder with compulsive overeating, so the person cannot stop eating. Anorexia nervosa is the opposite, a refusal to eat.
Long bones such as the leg bones are hollow, with a marrow cavity. This gives strength with less weight.
A normal adult has about 5-6 litres of blood, roughly 7-8% of body weight.
Haemoglobin is an iron-containing pigment that carries oxygen and gives blood its red colour. It does not provide immunity; antibodies and WBCs do, so statement III is false.

Trypsin digests protein after pepsin in the stomach. Protease is a general term for protein-digesting enzymes, but trypsin is the specific enzyme named for protein digestion. Urease and sulfatase act on other substrates.
The hypothalamus contains the centres for hunger, satiety, thirst and temperature regulation.
Most kidney stones are made of calcium oxalate crystals. Acetates and sodium benzoate are not the cause.
Typical signs of a heart attack are severe chest pain, nausea and heavy sweating. Headache is not a typical sign.
Insulin is a hormone made by the beta cells of the pancreatic Islets of Langerhans. It lowers blood sugar.

Platelets number about 1.5-4 lakh per microlitre, far more than WBCs at about 4,000-11,000. Blood cells are only about 45% of blood volume. Veins hold most of the blood. WBCs are also made in bone marrow.
The Golden Hour is the first hour after a heart attack or trauma. Prompt treatment in it greatly improves survival.
The kidneys receive about 1200 cc of blood per minute, roughly 20-25% of cardiac output.
The Andes (~7,000 km) are the longest mountain range, longer than the Rockies and Himalayas; the Himalayas are only the highest.
German silver is an alloy of copper, zinc and nickel and contains no silver, so none of the listed percentages is right and 'None of these' is correct.
Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3. Na2CO3 is washing soda, which is the tempting wrong option.
Teflon (PTFE) is the non-stick coating used on frying pans.
Azimullah Khan was Nana Saheb's adviser and secretary (he even went to London to plead Nana's pension case), so he was not an adviser of Tatya Tope, Lakshmibai or Kunwar Singh.
Tatya Tope's real name was Ramachandra Pandurang; the other leaders listed had different names.
Bahadur Shah II (Zafar) was the last Mughal emperor; the rebels proclaimed him Shahenshah-e-Hindustan at Delhi in 1857, after which he was exiled.
Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon and died there in 1862. Lakshmibai was killed in battle, Tatya Tope was hanged, and Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal.

Henry Lawrence died defending the Lucknow Residency and Havelock died at Lucknow in Nov 1857; Neil is also traditionally counted among those killed there. Nicholson died at Delhi, so statement I is wrong.
Danapur, Patna and Ara (Arrah) were involved in the revolt, with Danapur sepoys and Kunwar Singh at Arrah, while Munger was not a centre of the rising. So only V was unaffected.
Scindia of Gwalior stayed loyal to the British, although his troops joined the Rani; Holkar is listed as loyal too, but Scindia is the clear answer.

The Nizam of Hyderabad was pro-British and kept the Deccan quiet, so he did not support the revolt. The Scindia statement is wrong because Scindia stayed loyal and fled to Agra, and Mangal Pandey did not lead the march to Delhi.
The notes list Phulhar only as the source of the Gomati, without naming its state. Fulhar (Phulhar) lake is in Uttar Pradesh, which is why option 3 is correct.

Sudarshan Lake was an artificial reservoir at Girnar (Junagadh), Gujarat, built in Mauryan times under Chandragupta's governor Pushyagupta and later repaired by Rudradaman. Lonar is a meteorite crater, Loktak is in Manipur and Pushkar is in Rajasthan.
The first estimate on the new 2011-12 series put real GDP growth in 2014-15 at about 7.3%, so option (1) is correct.
India's GDP growth in 1950-51 was 3.6%, so option (4) is correct.
India's GDP growth in 1950-51 was 3.6%, so option (4) is correct.

Among the options, a strong state (strong crisis response, uniform policy and quick decisions) is a listed merit of unitary government. Adaptability and participation relate to regional diversity, which is a federal trait.
A federal policy covers Union-State relations, inter-State relations, and mechanisms for cooperation and for resolving disputes, so all four statements hold.

Power sharing is justified because it reduces conflict, prevents majority imposition and consults all affected groups. It does not speed up decision-making; it often slows it, so option 4 is the exception.
States have no right to secede, so I is correct. The notes do not say that advocacy of secession is protected, so II is not supported.
Sales tax is an indirect tax because its burden is shifted to consumers through prices. Income, corporation and wealth taxes are all direct taxes.
Income tax is a direct tax. Sales tax, excise and octroi (entry-type tax) are indirect taxes, so income tax is the one that is not indirect.
Income tax is a direct tax and does not directly raise the price of a commodity. Business, import and manufacturing levies such as customs and excise are indirect and enter prices.
Corporation tax is a direct tax levied on the net profit or income of companies, not on production, sales or stock.
A regressive tax makes the poor pay a higher share of their income than the rich. A progressive tax does the opposite.

A progressive tax has an average burden that rises with income, with higher marginal rates on higher slabs. So the tax rate increasing with income is progressive; a same rate is proportional and a falling rate is regressive.
In the first four decades of planning the Centre's main revenue came from indirect taxes such as excise, customs and sales tax, not direct taxes.
AIMIM (All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen) is led by Asaduddin Owaisi, its president and Hyderabad MP. The other names are not its leader.
Praja Shanti Party was founded by K.A. Paul; Y.S. Sharmila founded the YSR Telangana Party. So pair (4) is the incorrect one, while the other three pairs are correct.
On 30 April 2002 the TDP, backing the NDA from outside, abstained on the opposition censure motion on the Gujarat riots. So TDP is the party that did not vote.
In the 8th Lok Sabha (1984) the TDP won 30 seats and became the main opposition, the first regional party to do so. The other options did not achieve this.

The President appoints the Central Information Commissioner and the Governor appoints the State Information Commissioner, so A and B are correct. PIOs are designated by each public authority, not by the Supreme Court, so C is wrong. D is wrong too, as Parliament does not elect appellate authorities.

The Corruption Perceptions Index, published by Transparency International, scores the perceived level of public-sector corruption from 0 to 100. It does not measure actual unethical practices or black money.
The UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection were first adopted in 1985 (widened in 1999, revised in 2015), so 1985 is correct; 1986 is the year of India's own Consumer Protection Act.
National Consumer Day in India is observed on 24 December. World Consumer Rights Day is the different one, on 15 March.

Art. 324(1) vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President in the ECI, so the ECI conducts the Presidential election, not the Lok Sabha Speaker or ministries.

Under Arts. 243K(1) the State Election Commission holds superintendence, direction and control of panchayat elections and rolls, not the ECI, which handles Parliament, State Legislatures, President and VP.
The ECI was set up on 25 January 1950, so its Golden Jubilee (50 years) fell in 2001. The nearby year 1999 or 2000 is a common trap.
Lancashire (Manchester) is in the UK, the Ruhr is in Germany, and Keihin (Tokyo–Yokohama) is in Japan. Southern Appalachian is the remaining US region, so the code is 3 2 4 1, which is option (4).

The Arjuna 2022 list pairs Sushila Devi with judo, Om Prakash Mitharwal with shooting, Vikas Thakur with weightlifting, Tarun Dhillon with para badminton and Jerlin Anika with deaf badminton, which is option 1.
Arjuna 2023: Ritu Negi is kabaddi, Sheetal Devi para archery, Roshibina Devi wushu, Diksha Dagar golf and H.P.S. Sandhu squash. This gives a-II, b-IV, c-V, d-I, e-III.
Raga Kameshwari was composed by Pandit Ravi Shankar, the sitar maestro. The other options are not credited with it.
Lyricist Sameer is credited with writing 3524 songs in 650 films, which earned him a Guinness World Records entry. Gulzar and Javed Akhtar are not associated with that record.

SNA Awards 2023 included Jagdish Gangani (Kathak) and Helen Giri (Khasi folk music), so those pairs hold. The pair Parikshit Mahato-Tribal Dance is the one that does not fit, making it the incorrect pair.
The civilian award in Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's name recognises contribution to the unity and integrity of India, reflecting his role in integrating the princely states.
Kalli Purie (India Today Group) was honoured with India's Most Powerful Women in Media Award at the Confluence Excellence Award ceremony in the British Parliament in 2019.
Shaurya Chakra is a peacetime gallantry award. Vir Chakra and Param Vir Chakra are wartime gallantry awards, and Yudh Seva Medal is a wartime distinguished service medal.
Medha Patkar was not among the 2019 Mother Teresa Memorial Award for Social Justice recipients, while the other three named were recipients.
Raghu Rai is a renowned Indian photographer, known especially as a photojournalist.

Stree Shakti Puraskar is given to women for courage and enterprise for the betterment of women and for contribution to the nation and people. It is not an award for athletics or games, so III and IV are correct.

The Rajiv Gandhi Environment Award is for clean technology and development, so option 2 (a typo of 'clean') is the intended answer. Afforestation, wildlife and Hindi books relate to other environmental awards.
The Gujarat Police was honoured with the President's Colours Award in December 2019.
The Indira Gandhi Paryavaran Puraskar is awarded for significant contribution in the field of environment in general. The narrower options describe other specific awards.
Krishna Yadav won the Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Antyodaya Krishi Puraskar 2016 in the innovative farmers category.
The Rajiv Gandhi Environment Award is given for contributions to clean technology and development, not for afforestation, wildlife or Hindi books.
Ratan Tata was selected for the 2010 CIF Chenchlani Global Indian Award.

The notes do not state the composition of the Union Executive. Constitutionally it consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Council of Ministers and the Attorney-General, so option (1) is the closest. The Speaker and the Deputy Chairman are not part of it.

Members of Legislative Councils (elected or nominated) do not vote in the Presidential election. Elected MPs of both Houses and elected MLAs of the Assemblies do vote, so option (4) is the one not included.
The electoral college comprises the elected MPs of both Houses and the elected MLAs of the States, including Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members are excluded, so option (3) is correct.

The President is chosen indirectly by a college of elected MPs and elected MLAs, so A is true. R correctly describes that college and explains why the election is indirect, so R is the correct explanation.
Repo is the rate at which RBI lends to banks against securities, and it is used to inject liquidity and so regulate money supply in the economy. The other options describe things repo does not do.

To control rising inflation the central bank tightens policy by raising the repo rate. This makes credit costlier, lowers demand and cools inflation; cutting rates is expansionary and would worsen inflation.
Bank Rate and open market operations are monetary policy instruments. Public debt and public revenue belong to fiscal policy, so only I and II are correct.
Bank rate, variable reserve ratios and OMO are quantitative tools. Rationing of credit is a qualitative (selective) tool, so it is the odd one out.
Open market operations are a quantitative (general) credit control tool, since they affect the total volume of credit. They are not qualitative, fiscal or labour policy tools.
Variable reserve ratios are a quantitative tool, whereas rationing of credit, consumer credit regulation and margin requirements are qualitative. So variation of the reserve ratio is not qualitative.
Open Market Operations means RBI buying and selling G-secs to adjust liquidity and money supply. Rationing of credit and variable reserve ratios are different tools.
OMO means RBI buying or selling government securities, which is trading of securities. It does not involve forex auctions or gold.
Margin requirements and moral suasion are qualitative (selective) controls. CRR and SLR are variable reserve ratios, which are quantitative.
The Jungle Book was written by Rudyard Kipling, not R.K. Narayan; Malgudi Days, The Guide and Swami and Friends are Narayan's works.
'Adhe-Adhure' is a Hindi play by Mohan Rakesh.
'A Corner of a Foreign Field: The Indian History of a British Sport' was written by historian Ramachandra Guha.
'Andhayug' is a Hindi verse play by Dharmveer Bharti; Mohan Rakesh is known for 'Adhe-Adhure'.
'India Shastra: Reflections on the Nation in Our Time' is by Shashi Tharoor.
'Ashtaraj Ambhoj' was written by Dhanulal Shrivastava, a Chhattisgarhi writer.
'Rashmirekha' is a poetry collection by Bal Krishna Sharma 'Naveen'.
'Ignited Minds' was written by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
'Nineteen Eighty-Four' is the dystopian novel by George Orwell.
Arunachal Pradesh's Legislative Assembly adopted a logo with the National Emblem and the Foxtail Orchid, the state flower, in January 2020.
'Cry, the Peacock' is the 1963 novel by Anita Desai.
'A Brief History of Time' was written by the physicist Stephen Hawking.
'A Gallery of Rascals' is a story collection by Ruskin Bond.
Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier system (Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat), replacing the three-tier BRM model.
The Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, G.V.K. Rao and L.M. Singhvi committees all dealt with Panchayati Raj institutions, so 'All of the above' is correct.
Ashok Mehta recommended a two-tier system, not a three-tier one; party participation, taxation powers and SC/ST reservation were all among its recommendations.
The Ashok Mehta Committee made the district the first point of decentralisation, with the Zila Parishad as the executive body for district planning, so it emphasised the Zila Parishad.

Balwant Rai Mehta proposed three tiers and Ashok Mehta two tiers. Singhvi's focus was on constitutional recognition of local self-government, while G.V.K. Rao's was on improving the representative character through regular elections.

The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) first suggested constitutional recognition of PRIs in a new chapter of the Constitution. Ashok Mehta had also urged it, but the notes credit Singhvi as the first to suggest it.
The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended a Local Body Ombudsman, not the Balwant Rai Mehta or Ashok Mehta committees.
The chronological order is B.R. Mehta (1957), Ashok Mehta (1977-78), G.V.K. Rao (1985), then L.M. Singhvi (1986), i.e. III, IV, I, II.
Thungon was 1988, Ashok Mehta 1977, Balwant Rai Mehta 1957 and Singhvi 1986, which gives the code 4 3 1 2.

Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology working in the 2.4 GHz licence-free ISM band, i.e. it uses radio waves, so statement II is correct; it forms short-range personal area networks, so statement I is also taken as correct.
The notes do not cover the venue of the 77th Indian History Congress, so no line is linked. The correct answer is Thiruvananthapuram.
ISRO's 100th space mission was launched from Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh) in September 2012. Mahendragiri, Thumba and Bengaluru are not launch sites for it.
The notes say the Launch View Gallery opened in 2019 but give no capacity. The correct answer is 5,000.
NARL is at Gadanki, Tirupati district (AP), so Tirupati is correct.
IIRS trains in remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography and GIS, but not angiography, which is a medical imaging technique.
IIRS field equipment does not include a LINAC (Linear Accelerator), so option 4 is the one not included.
IIRS was founded in 1966 as the Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI).
IIRS is located at Dehradun.
IIRS is located at Dehradun.
IIRS was founded in 1966 as the Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI).
IIRS is situated at Dehradun.
SPARK is ISRO's virtual space museum, launched on 10 Aug 2022.
The Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate Muslim electorates, the communal electorate. The 1919 and 1935 Acts only extended it.
The Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909) gave Muslims separate electorates, which was communal representation. The 1892 Act only introduced indirect elections.
1916-1922 was the period of Congress-League agreement after the Lucknow Pact, the high point of unity. The 1906-1911 period saw the League founded to keep Muslims away from Congress.
Separate electorates divided voters on religious lines and fed later separatism that ended in partition. The League's founding and the Bengal partition were not the root communal mechanism.
Both the Congress session (president A.C. Majumdar) and the League session (president Jinnah) were held at Lucknow in December 1916.
At Lucknow in 1916 Congress accepted the League's demand for separate electorates. There was no merger, since they still held separate sessions, and the Congress president was not a Muslim.
The Lucknow Pact between Congress and the League was made in December 1916.
The Lahore session of the League in March 1940 was presided over by Jinnah. Others such as Fazlul Haq and Khaliquzzaman only moved or approved the resolution.

The TFA was part of the Bali Package (MC9, 2013) and India ratified it in 2016, so statements I and II are correct. Statement III is wrong because the TFA did not come into force in January 2016; the notes link 2016 only to India's ratification.
The Kailasa temple (Ellora Cave 16) was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, so Rashtrakuta is correct; Satavahana, Maurya and Pallava are not linked to it.
Kailasa at Ellora was carved under Krishna I of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, not by the Chalukyas, Cholas or Pallavas.
The monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I, so the Rashtrakutas are correct.
Kailasa is Cave 16 of the Ellora group, so Ellora is correct; Ajanta, Elephanta and Kanheri are different cave sites.
Kailasa was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, so the Rashtrakutas are correct, not the Chalukyas of Vatapi or the Gangas.
Ellora lies about 30 km from Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad district), Maharashtra, and most of its caves were built by the Rashtrakutas.
Ellora has Buddhist (caves 1-12), Hindu (13-29) and Jain (30-34) caves together, so Ellora is correct.
The notes do not mention the Pashupata sect at Elephanta, so no line settles this.
The Trimurti or Maheshamurti, a three-headed Shiva, is the masterpiece of Elephanta, not Ellora, whose highlight is Kailasa.
Directive Principles of State Policy are in Part IV, Articles 36 to 51 (16 articles), so option 3 is correct.
Under the 1954 Application to Jammu and Kashmir Order, Part IV (DPSP) did not apply to J&K, so option 2 is correct. The 2019 order later applied all provisions.
DPSPs aim at social and economic democracy and a welfare state, not at making India an advanced capitalist country, so statement 4 is incorrect. Statements 1-3 reflect Article 37.
DPSPs aim at social and economic democracy (statement I), and Article 37 makes them non-enforceable by courts (statement II). Both are correct.
The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in 1961 and came into force on 1 July 1961, so option 4 is correct.
In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) the Supreme Court laid down guidelines on sexual harassment of women at the workplace, which later led to the POSH Act, 2013.
The 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave for the first two children from 12 to 26 weeks, so 26 weeks is correct.

Only III is correct: the notes say leave is 26 weeks for the first two children and 12 weeks from the third child, so women with two children do not get reduced entitlements. Statement I is wrong because leave is 26 weeks, not 3+3 months. Statement II is not supported by the notes.

The anti-partition (Swadeshi) movement was formally launched on 7 August 1905 with the boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall. 20 July was the partition announcement and 16 October the day it took effect.
The immediate cause of the Swadeshi Movement was Curzon's partition of Bengal. The other options are unrelated events.
