The partition of Bengal by Curzon was the immediate cause that spread Swadeshi and boycott. The other Curzon measures were not the direct trigger.
The Swadeshi Movement arose as a reaction to the partition of Bengal. Non-Cooperation was not a programme against the partition.
Vande Mataram became the slogan and theme song of the Swadeshi agitation against the 1905 partition of Bengal. It was not the slogan of the 1857 revolt, Non-Cooperation or Quit India.
Aurobindo Ghosh was the first principal of the Bengal National College in Calcutta, founded during the Swadeshi Movement.
Both statements are correct. The Swadeshi Movement revived Indian industry, and the National Council of Education (1906) was set up as part of its national education programme.
Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is used for plaster, and heating it gives Plaster of Paris; marble and limestone are calcium carbonate, and cement is a different product.
Andhra Pradesh (Nellore) ranks first in mica in India, so it is the biggest producer. Bihar and Jharkhand are famous belts but not the top producer here.
Rajasthan is the main gypsum-producing state, as listed for gypsum in the notes.
The 2021-22 value shares are Odisha 44.11%, Karnataka 17.34%, Jharkhand 4.36% and MP 2.96%, which gives A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.
Odisha led with a 44.11% share of the value of mineral production in 2021-22, well ahead of the other states.
The 2021-22 value shares are Odisha 44.11%, Karnataka 17.34%, Jharkhand 4.36% and MP 2.96%, which gives A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.

Odisha is a leading bauxite producer, and Gujarat is the other leading producer according to the keyed answer. The notes name Maharashtra as the second leading producer, so they conflict with this key.
Rajasthan is the sole producer of lead-zinc ores, so it has a near monopoly in zinc. It is not the sole producer of copper, and mica is led by AP.
Nickel is about 93% in Odisha, so pair 2 is correct. Copper is mainly in Rajasthan (~52%), not Jharkhand, and tungsten is mainly in Karnataka, not Kerala.

The Narmada flows in a rift valley between the Vindhya (north) and Satpura (south) ranges, so it separates the Deccan Tableland from northern India. Krishna and Godavari lie wholly within the peninsula.
Mahanadi is an east-flowing river that forms a large delta near Paradeep, not an estuary. Narmada, Tapi and Mandovi are west-flowing rivers that end in estuaries.
Betwa is not a west-flowing river; it is a Yamuna tributary that flows north-east. Periyar and Sabarmati are west-flowing rivers, and the Bharathpuzha is also a west-flowing river of Kerala.

Statements III and IV are correct: the duties were added on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation and apply only to citizens. I is wrong because duties are non-justiciable and cannot be enforced by writs, and II is wrong because they were added in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment, not at adoption.

Both statements are judged false by the answer key. Statement I fails because the Constitution itself provides no legislative enforcement process, even though Parliament may legislate. Statement II fails because duties correlate with rights, not with 'legal duties' as stated, so neither statement is true.
Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable in courts, whereas Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable. The Preamble is also not enforceable in court.
The Rajya/Mandala (province) was the largest unit of Vijayanagara provincial administration, above Nadu, Sthala and Grama, so Mandalam is correct.

Nayakas (Amaranayakas) were military chiefs who held land (amaram) in lieu of salary, and administered it, so they were military chiefs controlling territories, not ministers, priests or ordinary cavalry.

Palegars (Poligars) were the amara-nayakas who administered territories and held military obligations, so they were territorial administrative and military governors, not ordinary zamindars (they were only forerunners of zamindars).
Land revenue (share of produce, usually 1/6, and higher on fertile land) was the mainstay of Vijayanagara finance, so Land Revenue is correct.

Navidadere is the barbers' tax (II), and the notes also list the house tax (Maneyanna) and the marriage tax (Kalyana Kanika). That fits option 2, with Melivamsam as the plough tax (III) and Tudimeya as the marriage tax (I).
Convection is one of the three modes of heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation); evaporation, revolution and thermal expansion are not modes of heat transfer.
A thermometer measures temperature, the degree of hotness; heat is energy and is measured by a calorimeter.
Lateral inversion is caused by reflection in a plane mirror, not refraction. Twinkling, mirages and bending of light in a medium are refraction effects.
Water pressure increases with depth, so a deep-sea diver's ear drum can be hurt by the high water pressure.
By Bernoulli's principle, fast-moving air between the cars lowers the pressure there. The higher outside pressure pushes the cars together.
A real gas behaves ideally at low pressure and high temperature, where molecules are far apart and intermolecular forces are negligible.
Weight is a force, so its SI unit is the newton. The kg and gram are units of mass, and the dyne is a CGS unit.
Water has a high specific heat, so it stores a large amount of heat and releases it slowly, which makes it suitable for a hot water bag.
Liquid pressure P = hρg depends on the height of the liquid column and the density, not on the base area.
Floating ice displaces water equal to its own weight, so the melted ice exactly fills the displaced volume and the level does not change.
Water expands on freezing, so ice has greater volume for the same mass and lower density, which is why ice floats.
During melting, the heat supplied goes into latent heat to change the state, so the temperature stays constant at the melting point.
Electromagnetic induction: a faster-moving magnet changes flux faster, which induces a larger emf and so a larger current.
Water's high dielectric constant reduces the attraction between ions, so it dissolves ionic substances well.
Stomata carry out transpiration, xylem transports water, root hairs absorb water, and phloem transports food, which gives 2 4 1 3.
By the work-energy theorem, net work done equals the change in kinetic energy, so positive work increases kinetic energy.
Detergent molecules lower the surface tension of water, which helps it wet fabric and remove dirt.
Spherical rain drops, capillary rise and detergent cleaning are surface tension effects. The flow of a liquid is related to viscosity, not surface tension.
Heat flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature, so the direction depends only on their temperatures.
Bahadur Shah I, Jahandar Shah, Farrukhsiyar, Muhammad Shah and Shah Alam II is the order of reigns (1707-1712, 1712-13, 1713-19, 1719-48, 1759-1806), which is option 3.
Aurangzeb died in 1707 and was succeeded by Muazzam, who took the title Bahadur Shah I (reign 1707-1712). Jahandar Shah came after him, and Muhammad Shah and Akbar II were much later.
Roshan Akhtar was the personal name of Muhammad Shah, who was later nicknamed 'Rangeela'.
Muhammad Shah ruled 1719-1748, about 29 years. Bahadur Shah I ruled about 5 years, Jahandar Shah about 1 year and Farrukhsiyar about 6 years, so Muhammad Shah had the longest reign.
Nadir Shah invaded in 1739 and defeated Muhammad Shah at Karnal, so Muhammad Shah was the emperor at that time. The other options ruled at different times.
The notes tie the control of eunuchs and ladies to Muhammad Shah's reign, not Ahmad Shah's. The keyed answer, Ahmad Shah, conflicts with the notes, though Ahmad Shah's rule passed to Udham Bai.
Plassey was fought in 1757, which falls in Alamgir II's reign (1754-1759). Ahmad Shah ended in 1754 and Shah Alam II began in 1759.
Shah Alam II was blinded by the Rohilla Ghulam Qadir. The notes give the year as 1788, not 1780, but the person is the same.
Bahadur Shah Zafar (Bahadur Shah II) was the last Mughal emperor, exiled to Rangoon after 1857. He was not a Lodi, was not a successor of Sher Shah, and was not a successor of Shivaji.
The order is Jahandar Shah (1712-13), Muhammad Shah (1719-48), Ahmad Shah (1748-54), then Alamgir II (1754-59), which is option 2.
Bora is a cold, dry wind of the NE Adriatic (eastern shore). Mistral is also cold and dry but belongs to the Rhone valley in France.
Chinook is a warm, dry 'snow eater' wind of the Rockies, so it does not bring lots of rain; the statement that it does is incorrect.
Shamal is a hot, dusty wind of Iraq and the Persian Gulf, i.e. Mesopotamia, not East Asia or the Sahara.
Purga is the cold, snowy wind of Siberia (tundra). Bora is Adriatic and Mistral is French, and a blizzard is a general snowstorm, not a specific Siberian wind.
Mistral is a cold, dry wind of the Rhone valley. Santa Ana, Chinook and Loo are warm or hot winds.
Mistral is a cold, dry wind of the Rhone valley in France, not Australia, so the pair is wrong. Santa Ana is correctly matched with California.
The Stamp Act Congress met in New York City in 1765 to protest the Stamp Act passed by the British Parliament. The notes cover only the Age of Discovery, so this is not stated there.
The Treaty of Schonbrunn (1809) ended the war between Austria and France after Napoleon's victory at Wagram. Austerlitz led to the Treaty of Pressburg, and Tilsit was a treaty (1807), not a battle.

Olympe de Gouges, author of the Declaration of the Rights of Woman, held that the nation is the union of woman and man. She was guillotined under the Jacobin government, so she was no supporter of it.
Kerensky headed the Russian Provisional Government from July 1917 until the Bolsheviks took power in the October Revolution. He was an opponent of Lenin, not his confidant.
The Tennis Court Oath (June 1789) was taken by the Third Estate deputies of the National Assembly at Versailles, so it belongs to the French Revolution.
The National Convention met in 1792 and abolished the monarchy and declared France a republic. The Tennis Court Oath was in 1789, and the Napoleonic Code was 1804.
V.I. Lenin led the Bolsheviks in the 1917 Russian Revolution and is regarded as its father. The others were later Soviet leaders.
The 1911 Xinhai Revolution overthrew the Qing dynasty and established the Republic of China in 1912.
The Crimean War (1853-56) was fought between Russia and the Ottoman Empire (Turkey). Britain and France joined on the Turkish side, so they were not opponents of each other.
The Stamp Act Congress met in New York City in October 1765. Philadelphia hosted the later Continental Congresses.
The first Marxist (socialist) revolution was the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 in Russia.

All four factors contributed to Britain being first: scientific inventions, favourable social and political structures, navigable rivers for transport, and the rise of capitalism. So all four statements are correct.
The order is Kay's Flying Shuttle (1733), Hargreaves's Spinning Jenny (1764), Arkwright's Water Frame (1769) and Crompton's Mule (1779).

The factory system brought production under one roof, which undermined the guilds, and merchant capitalists gained a growing role. Statement I is wrong because production moved from the countryside to factories in towns.

Olympe de Gouges was a politically active woman of the Revolution and wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and Citizen (1791). She was not on the committee that drafted the Declaration of the Rights of Man, so II is wrong.
The Boxer Rebellion, an anti-foreign uprising in China, took place in 1899-1901 and peaked in 1900.

The First Continental Congress (1774) rejected Galloway's plan for a colonial union under British authority. It also drew up a statement of grievances and agreed a non-importation scheme to stop trade with England. All three statements are correct.
The American Revolution was a conflict between the colonists and Britain over taxation without representation, not between settlers and native Americans. So only II is correct.
The Bolsheviks under Lenin wanted a disciplined, restricted party, while the Mensheviks wanted a party open to all members. Both statements are correct.
The colonists' slogan was 'No taxation without representation', and American merchants boycotted British goods. Both statements are correct.

Sustainable development aims at intergenerational equity and balancing economy, society and environment; prioritising individual wealth accumulation is listed as not a goal. Economic growth, environmental protection and social inclusion are the three pillars.

Sustainable development aims at intergenerational equity and balancing economy, society and environment; prioritising individual wealth accumulation is listed as not a goal. Economic growth, environmental protection and social inclusion are the three pillars.
Using resources to meet present needs while leaving options and stock for future generations is the definition of sustainable development, not mere economic or social development.

The notes do not cover the negative aspects of development discussed in the mid-1980s. Resource degradation, pollution and displacement were prominent concerns, whereas 'politics and development' was not a major one.
Rio+20 was the 2012 UN Conference on Sustainable Development, held twenty years after the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. It is not the Earth Summit itself, which was Rio 1992.
The notes give no poverty-percentage data for India under the MDG programme. The answer is 21.9%, the figure reported for the poverty headcount ratio in 2011-12.
SDG 13 is Climate action, which covers urgent action against climate change. SDG 6 is water, SDG 7 is energy and SDG 14 is life below water.
Agenda 2030 specifically focuses on ending all discrimination and violence against women and girls.

The Contingency Fund of India is an imprest placed at the President's disposal, so advances can be made for unforeseen expenses and Parliament approves them later. Withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund need an Appropriation Act first.
Andhra Pradesh presents a separate agriculture budget, as in the AP Budget 2026-27, where K. Atchannaidu presented it. So 'Agriculture budget' is correct.
The notes do not give the year the Budget presentation time moved from 5 pm to 11 am. It was shifted in 2001, when Yashwant Sinha presented the Budget at 11 a.m.
The notes state that the Union Budget 2023-24 was presented in the Lok Sabha by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
The stages run: presentation, scrutiny by standing committees, then the Appropriation Bill, then the Finance Bill. So the order is I, II, IV, III.
Estimates are submitted as demands; once the Lok Sabha votes and passes a demand it becomes a grant, so a demand becomes a grant after it is granted.
The notes do not cover this fact. Statement 3 is the incorrect one, since the Finance Bill is the vehicle for tax changes, though rate changes to existing taxes are also usually made via it.
The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784 (the question's 'Royal Asiatic Society' refers to this body). The other options are not linked with its founding.
Charles Wilkins made the first English translation of the Bhagavad Gita (1785). The notes do not cover this fact.
James Mill wrote 'The History of British India' (1817). John Stuart Mill was his son and wrote on other subjects. The notes do not cover this.
Sir William Jones first translated Kalidasa's Shakuntala into English (1789). Wilkins is linked with the Gita, not Shakuntala. The notes do not cover this.
Downward Filtration Theory is an education theory: learning was to flow from the higher classes to the masses. It has nothing to do with railways, irrigation or poverty alleviation.

Macaulay's Minute of 1835 is called the foundation of modern education in India. It made English-medium Western science and literature the focus of education funds. Wood's Despatch is the 'Magna Carta', but the notes name the Minute as the foundation.

The 1835 Act, on Macaulay's Minute, directed funds exclusively to English-medium Western education and made English the medium of higher education. So continued stipends and publication of classical texts for oriental institutions is not correct.
Wood's Despatch is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India' and is the most important education document. Macaulay's Minute is the foundation, but not the most important document.
Wood's Despatch of 1854 recommended universities in the presidency towns, and Calcutta University was set up in 1857 as a result. Macaulay's Minute and the Hunter Commission did not create it.
The Despatch introduced grants-in-aid and recommended universities, so I and II are true. It recommended English only for higher education and vernacular for lower levels, so III is false.
A Joint SPSC's chairman and members are appointed by the President, not by Governors or a committee of them. Only the State PSC is appointed by the Governor.
A JSPSC is created by an Act of Parliament when the Legislatures of two or more States pass resolutions requesting it (Art. 315(2)). Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha or UPSC alone cannot create it.
APPSC came into existence on 1 November 1956 with the formation of Andhra Pradesh, so 1956 is correct.
SHE stands for Scholarship for Higher Education, not 'Support for Her Education'; it is not a women's scheme. The other expansions (SEATS, AORC) match the notes.
VAJRA, the Ramanujan Fellowship and INSPIRE are the brain-drain-to-brain-gain schemes. The ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship is not one of them, so only I, II and III are correct.
WIDUSHI under DST's WISE-KIRAN targets senior women scientists in interdisciplinary S&T. GATI targets institutions, and SERB-POWER is a SERB scheme for women researchers.
JIGYASA is a partnership of CSIR and Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (2017), bringing KV students into CSIR labs. It is not linked with CBSE or Navodaya.
The Atal Innovation Mission is NITI Aayog's flagship initiative, set up in 2016 to build innovation and start-up culture. The other options are not real NITI Aayog initiatives.
The notes do not give the year APIS was set up. The answer, 2015, is not stated in the notes, so no line is linked.

The notes do not mention anyone named Hasan Suhrawardi presiding. They show that the League called Direct Action, that it was observed in Calcutta (not Delhi), and that the Congress did not endorse it. The riots spread to Bihar. The keyed answer rests on a fact the notes do not state.
The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946. The call was made on 29 July 1946, and 3 September is not the date.
At Noakhali Gandhi failed to stop the enmity and violence, so option 3 is correct.
Mountbatten's instructions were to keep India united if possible. Partition was only accepted later, once unity proved unachievable.
The 3 June Plan set out how power would be transferred: partition, dominion status, and an advanced date of 15 August 1947. It was not a constitution-making guideline or a federal scheme.
A Bill originating in the Council and rejected by the Assembly ends, since the Council has no second chance and there is no joint sitting in States.
Article 169 deals with the creation and abolition of Legislative Councils; Art. 368 is constitutional amendment, so it is not the answer.
The Legislative Council is a permanent body that cannot be dissolved but can be abolished under Art. 169, whereas the Assembly can be dissolved.
Rajasthan is not among the six States with a Legislative Council (AP, Telangana, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP), while Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka have one.
The 2015 Amendment raised the AP Council from 50 to 58 members, which is one-third of the 175-seat Assembly.
The AP Reorganisation Act 2014 originally provided a Council of not more than 50 members; it was later raised to 58.
Both are correct: on dissolution the Speaker continues until just before the first meeting of the new Assembly, and under Art. 179 the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker.

Statement I is wrong because the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution but continues until the new Assembly meets. Statement II (legislative immunity for speech and votes) is correct, so only II is right.

Statement II is wrong because the Speaker continues in office after dissolution until just before the new Assembly's first meeting. Statement I is correct, as ceasing to be a member ends the Speaker's office, so only I is right.

Disqualification questions of State legislators are decided by the Governor under Art. 192, acting on the binding opinion of the Election Commission. The ECI only advises; the decision is the Governor's.
The parsec is a unit of astronomical distance, equal to 3.26 light years, so it measures distance and not density, brightness or velocity.
Sunlight takes about 8 min 19 s to reach Earth, so about 8 minutes is correct.
There are 8 planets in the solar system, since Pluto was dropped and the earlier count of 9 no longer applies.
The notes do not give the number of constellations. The IAU recognises 88 constellations.
The notes do not state the Sun's galactic orbital period. It is about 225-250 million years, i.e. about 25 crore years.
The Steady State theory was proposed by Hoyle, Bondi and Gold in 1948, so Gold and Bondi is correct. Lemaitre proposed the Big Bang, not Steady State.
The Big Bang (expanding universe) theory, proposed by Lemaitre, explains the origin of the universe. It has nothing to do with continental drift, the Himalayas or volcanoes.
Otto Schmidt's interstellar dust hypothesis derives the Earth's origin from gas and dust. Jeans is linked to the tidal hypothesis and Hoyle to the Nova hypothesis.

These terms (event horizon, singularity, string theory, standard model) belong to cosmology and physics, i.e. the observation and understanding of the Universe. They have nothing to do with eclipses, satellites or biological evolution.

All three pairs match the master table: Krishna Patrika was founded by Konda Venkatappayya, Andhra Patrika was edited by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, and Swarajya (1907) was edited by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao. So A, B and C are all correct.
Mutnuri Krishna Rao, editor of Krishna Patrika, invited Bipin Chandra Pal to Andhra in April 1907. Gadicherla (Hari Sarvottama Rao) is the tempting wrong option.
The CEC and ECs have equal powers, equal salaries and allowances, so the statement that members lack equal powers is the incorrect one, which makes (1) the answer to the 'except' question.
On 16 October 1989 two Election Commissioners were added, creating the first three-member Commission. It reverted to a single member in 1990, so 1989 is the answer.

The ECI settles symbol disputes (such as splits and mergers of parties), so III is correct. It is a three-member body, not five, and the ECI itself, not the Home Ministry, announces election schedules, so I and II are wrong.
The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge, by a special majority in both Houses of Parliament on proven misbehaviour or incapacity, so option 4 is the closest to this rule.
Under Art. 324(5) the CEC is removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge, so the answer is the option stating the same procedure.
Saksham-ECI is the app for registration and polling help for persons with disabilities, so Saksham is correct.

Speaker and Deputy Speaker are chosen by their own Houses and municipal polls belong to the State Election Commission, so I and II are wrong. Election petitions go to the High Court and the ECI does not hear them, so III is wrong. The answer is none of these.

The notes give only the SC/ST seat counts for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, not a state-wise ranking. Madhya Pradesh has the most ST-reserved Lok Sabha seats (6) among the options, but the notes do not establish this.
Article 330 provides for SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha in proportion to population, so the option '330 (A)' is the closest match. Articles 331 and 332 deal with Anglo-Indians and State Assemblies.
Article 330 reserves seats for SC/ST in the House of the People (Lok Sabha). Article 325 deals with electoral rolls.
The notification is issued by the President (Lok Sabha) or the Governor (Assembly) under Sections 14 and 15, not by the ECI. The ECI only fixes the schedule.
The notification is issued by the President (Lok Sabha) or the Governor (Assembly) under Sections 14 and 15, not by the ECI. The ECI only fixes the schedule.
The MCC consists of ECI guidelines that are not enacted by Parliament and are not statutory, so the Constitution, IPC and RPA are not its source. Option 3, voluntary compliance, is the closest fit.
The Supreme Court's PUCL judgment of 27 September 2013 introduced the NOTA button on EVMs. It was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014, which is the tempting wrong option.
National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January.

Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state, so Andhra Pradesh is not correct by the usual facts. The notes place AP third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, so the listed answer is not supported by them, and among the options AP (1,053 km revised) is the longest.
The 2023-24 remeasurement by the MHA revised India's coastline to 11,098.81 km, up from 7,516.6 km.
India has 9 coastal states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal.
Excluding island UTs, India has 9 coastal states and 2 coastal UTs (Puducherry, Daman & Diu), so Nine States and two UTs is correct.

The notes confirm only that NAYAN is a C-DAC software against cyber attacks and data theft. They do not mention USB Pratirodh or Malware Resist, so those are not covered. All three are C-DAC tools, which is why option 1 is correct.

Haidar Ali (with Tipu) defeated Col. Baillie's British force at Pollilur in 1780, and he had already come out on top near Madras in the First War, so he is the first South Indian ruler to defeat British armies; Tipu came later and the Nizam was a British ally.
Tipu was killed defending Srirangapatna on 4 May 1799 in the Fourth War; 1797 is the Jacobin Club date and 1769 the Treaty of Madras.
Tipu Sultan became a member of the Jacobin Club at Seringapatam as 'Citizen Tipu' and planted a Tree of Liberty there; it was not Haidar Ali.
Sir Eyre Coote beat Haidar Ali at Porto Novo in July 1781 during the Second War, reversing the Pollilur defeat.
At Pollilur on 10 Sep 1780 Haidar and Tipu defeated Col. Baillie's British force in the Second War.
The Treaty of Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) of March 1792 ended the Third War and was made with Tipu Sultan; Haidar's treaty was that of Madras (1769).
Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide) with the molecular formula C6H12O6; the other formulas given are not glucose.
Speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Velocity, torque and displacement all have both magnitude and direction, so they are vectors.
The giant panda belongs to the bear family (Ursidae), not the cat, dog or rabbit families.
Strain is the ratio of change in length to original length, so it is dimensionless and has no unit. Stress, force and pressure all have units.
Dead fish smell is due to amines such as trimethylamine, formed when bacteria break down the fish, so the answer is amino compounds.
Chlorophyll, the green pigment of leaves, has magnesium at the centre of its porphyrin ring.
Sound travels fastest in solids such as steel because they are the most elastic and rigid, and it cannot travel through a vacuum at all.
Acceleration is measured in metre per second squared, force in newton, work in joule and impulse in newton second. This gives the code 4 3 1 2.
By Newton's law of cooling, the rate of cooling falls as the body gets closer to the surroundings' temperature. The same 15°C drop therefore takes more than 25 s.
Transformer heating comes from I²R (copper) losses from the current and from hysteresis (core) losses. Coolant liquid heating is an effect, not a cause, so statement III is wrong.
The electron is lightest, then the proton, then the neutron (slightly heavier than the proton), and the alpha particle (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is heaviest: III-II-IV-I.
Watt is the unit of power, knot is the speed of a ship, nautical mile is used in navigation and calorie is a unit of heat, giving 4 3 2 1.
Apoptosis is genetically controlled programmed cell death. Necrosis is uncontrolled death caused by injury.
The world's first camel hospital is in Dubai, UAE.
Reactivity of halogens decreases down the group, so fluorine, the most electronegative element, is the most reactive.
Sound travels fastest in solids, which are the most elastic and dense in particle packing, slower in liquids and gases, and not at all in a vacuum.
The positron is the antiparticle of the electron, with the same mass and opposite charge. The other pairs are not particle-antiparticle pairs.
The cockroach has colourless (whitish) haemolymph because it lacks haemoglobin, so its blood does not look red.
The primary colours of light are red, green and blue, and of pigments are red, yellow and blue. Black is not a primary colour.
The functions to be devolved on Panchayats are listed in the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects, Article 243G); the Twelfth Schedule is for Municipalities.
The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats under Article 243G.
Panchayati Raj is in Part IX of the Constitution 'The Panchayats' (Articles 243-243O); Part IXA is for Municipalities.
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 deals with rural Panchayats (Part IX); the 74th deals with urban Municipalities (Nagar Palika).
The third tier (local government) was added by the 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts of 1992, which came into force in 1993. The Act year is 1992, so (3) is the keyed answer.
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions; the 42nd, 44th and 86th Amendments deal with other matters.
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 inserted Part IX on Panchayats, so it relates to the Panchayati Raj system.
The 73rd Amendment concerns rural Panchayats (Part IX), so statement 1 is correct. Urban local bodies were recognised by the 74th Amendment, so statement 2 is wrong.
Hind Swaraj (1909) was written by Gandhi in Gujarati aboard the Kildonan Castle, so Mahatma Gandhi is the author; Tilak, Gokhale and Ranade did not write it.
'Conquest of Self' is a compilation of Mahatma Gandhi's writings and thoughts (edited by Raghavan Iyer), so Gandhi is the correct author; the other options are not associated with it.

This statement on a sound body serving the spirit is attributed to Mahatma Gandhi, who stressed physical fitness and discipline as instruments of the spirit; it is not associated with the other options.
The Srikakulam Girijan struggle ran from 1968 to 1970, so option 4 is correct. 1967 was Naxalbari, and the other periods are not linked to the movement.

Kishanji was the Maoist leader killed by security forces; the notes date this to 2011 (the question says 2012), but he is the only option that fits. Veerappan was a forest brigand, and Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal were Naxalite founders who were not killed by security forces in that year.

The view that the Mughal state was itself the principal instrument of exploitation of the peasantry comes from Irfan Habib's The Agrarian System of Mughal India, which stresses the agrarian crisis caused by over-exploitation. Satish Chandra is linked with the jagirdari crisis instead.
IMF stands for International Monetary Fund; the option 'International Monetary Funds' is the closest match to the correct expansion.
The IBRD is the original institution of the World Bank, so it is also called the World Bank. The other options are not the IBRD.
The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C., not in New York, Manila or Geneva.
The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C., not in New York, Vienna or Brussels.
IDA is part of the World Bank Group and is run by the IBRD, giving soft loans to the poorest countries. So it is an affiliate of the World Bank.

Christine Lagarde was IMF Managing Director in the period the question refers to, so she is the keyed answer. The notes list Kristalina Georgieva as the current head, which would be the tempting choice for a present-day question.
As of January 2020 the IMF had 189 members. The notes give only the current figure of 191, so 189 is the earlier count.
The IMF lends only to its member countries; project financing is the World Bank's job. So it cannot lend to any country or only to developed ones.
IDA is run by the IBRD, part of the World Bank Group, and gives soft loans to the poorest countries.
The Indian Development Forum was earlier known as the Aid India Consortium, the donor group for aid to India. It is not the World Bank itself.
Ajay Banga became World Bank President in June 2023. Georgieva heads the IMF, not the World Bank.
Ajay Banga became World Bank President in June 2023. Georgieva heads the IMF, not the World Bank.
The Andhra Communist Party was formed in January 1936 at Kakinada, where its 1st Maha Sabha was held on 29 January 1936. The other towns are not associated with this founding conference.
Na2X means X carries a 2- charge. Al is 3+, so the formula is criss-crossed to Al2X3.

Colour blindness is X-linked recessive. A colour-blind mother (XcXc) passes Xc to all children. The son gets Xc from her and Y from the father, so he is affected. The daughter gets a normal X from the father, so she is a carrier but not affected.
Robert Hooke first observed and named cells in 1665 in cork slices under a microscope. Leeuwenhoek saw living cells later.
Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes says gases react in volumes that bear a simple whole-number ratio.
Bat is a mammal and so is warm-blooded. Shark, snake and lizard are cold-blooded.
Mammals are the most advanced class of these. Bat is a mammal, while Aves and Pisces rank lower.
The apical meristem is responsible for growth in length. Damage to it stops the plant from growing taller.
Birds are studied in ornithology, inheritance in genetics, environment in ecology and fossils in palaeobiology. This gives 3 4 2 1.
Kirchhoff's first (current) law states that the current entering a junction equals the current leaving it, which follows from conservation of charge.
Boyle's, Charles's and Avogadro's laws are gas laws. Joule's law concerns the heating effect of current.
1 calorie = 4.18 J, so 1 J = about 0.24 calorie.
A freely falling body has a constant acceleration g, so its motion is uniformly accelerated.
A suspension has visible particles that are not uniformly distributed, so it is heterogeneous. A solution is homogeneous.
Water boils at 100°C, which is 212°F.
0 K equals -273.15°C.
In Fleming's left-hand rule the thumb shows force, the forefinger shows the field and the middle finger shows the current direction.
Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide in the air to form black silver sulphide.
In the reactivity series Zn is more reactive than Cu, which is more reactive than Ag. So the electron-releasing tendency is Zn > Cu > Ag.
Bat and bird wings have the same function but different structure and origin, so they are analogous organs.
Relative density is the ratio of two densities (substance to water), so the units cancel and it has no unit, whereas speed, density and acceleration all have units.
An electromagnet needs a core that magnetises strongly and loses magnetism quickly when current stops; soft iron does this, while steel retains magnetism.
Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, a chemical compound with fixed composition formed by a chemical reaction, not a mixture.
Constantan is an alloy of about 60% copper and 40% nickel, used in resistance wires and thermocouples.
In Fe2O3 iron is +3 throughout. Pb3O4 (Pb +2/+4), Fe3O4 (Fe +2/+3) and Mn3O4 (Mn +2/+3) each have the same element in two oxidation states.
Atomic weight = equivalent weight × valency, which is the standard relation.
Rusting is oxidation of iron, which combines with oxygen and water to form hydrated oxide, so the nail's weight increases.

All three statements are correct: a changing magnetic field induces current (Faraday), a current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field (Oersted), and relative motion between conductor and coil changes the flux and so produces induction.
On heating, a plate expands uniformly, including the hole, which behaves as if it were made of the same material, so the hole's area increases.
Integrated circuits are fabricated on silicon, a semiconductor, wafers.
Limestone, chalk and marble are all calcium carbonate, which releases CO2 with HCl. Quicklime (CaO) is an oxide and gives only CaCl2 and water.
Inert (noble) gases have complete outer electron shells, so they are chemically unreactive and stable.
Silicon, germanium and gallium arsenide are semiconductors; quartz (SiO2) is an insulator.
Aluminium is trivalent, an acceptor impurity in tetravalent silicon, which creates holes and makes it p-type.
Upthrust (buoyancy) arises from pressure differences caused by the fluid's weight under gravity, so it disappears without gravity. Viscosity and surface tension are molecular forces and remain.
Surface tension makes a liquid surface contract to minimum area, and a sphere has the least surface area for a given volume, so a soap bubble is spherical.
Human ear sensitivity varies strongly with frequency (most sensitive about 2-5 kHz), so statement 2 is incorrect.
By Newton's third law, action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, acting on different bodies.
In uniform circular motion speed is constant but the velocity direction changes. The acceleration is centripetal with constant magnitude but changing direction, so only II and IV are true.
The National MPI is built by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI, so NITI Aayog is the responsible body. The Planning Commission no longer exists, and the RBI and Finance Ministry do not estimate it.

The Gram Sabha's role in the notes is holding social audits, along with recommending works and monitoring them. Receiving applications for work and issuing dated receipts is done by the Gram Panchayat (programme officer), not the Gram Sabha, so option 2 is the answer.
The notes list M.C. Setalvad, B.N. Rao and Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer as members of the Servants of India Society, which Gokhale founded.
After the 1919 reforms failed, Swaraj was sought under Gandhi's leadership. Gokhale had died in 1915 and Tilak was an Extremist who died in 1920.
Only pair I (Sapru as President of the Liberal Federation) is settled by the notes. The notes do not cover pairs II and III, so the answer rests on outside knowledge that all three pairs are correct.
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar in 1929. The other options were not its founders.
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan led the Khudai Khidmatgar, known as the Red Shirts, so he is the leader of the Red Shirts movement.

Velu Nachiyar was the first queen to wage war against the British in 1780, so statement I is correct. The notes do not mention an alliance with Tipu Sultan, and the answer treats statement II as incorrect.
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati led the Bihar Kisan Sabha and was first president of the All India Kisan Sabha. He was therefore associated with the farmers' movement in Bihar.
In the Social Progress Index (Dec 2022) Andhra Pradesh ranked 23rd among States/UTs, so option 4 is correct; 9th is the SDG India Index/MPI rank, not SPI.
A letter of credit is produced by the importer, whose issuing bank promises payment to the exporter (the beneficiary). The exporter does not produce it.
The import process begins with the indent, which is the importer's order to buy goods. The other options are not the starting step (the shipping bill is an export customs document).
The first Deendayal Handicraft Sankul (Hastkala Sankul) trade facilitation centre is in Varanasi. The notes do not cover this fact.
Gandhi, Sarojini Naidu and Madan Mohan Malaviya all attended the Second RTC (1931), but Rajendra Prasad is not listed among the participants, so he is the one who did not attend.
The remark is attributed to Lord Willingdon (Viceroy 1931-36), who was hostile to Gandhi and repressed the second phase of the CDM; the notes do not state the quote itself.
The CDM was formally withdrawn in April 1934, after the mass movement was suspended on 14 July 1933; so April 1934 is correct and 1932/1933 are not the withdrawal date.
After the CDM failed, Gandhi turned to constructive work, especially service to Harijans, which was his top priority.
UNIX is a multi-user OS used on servers, workstations and, in Unix-like forms, mobile devices, so all the options are correct. The notes do not state these applications.
Linux is an operating system (its kernel was written by Torvalds), not a language or an interpreter.
Linux, Windows and macOS are operating systems, whereas Mozilla Firefox is a web browser, an application program.
Windows lets several programs run at once, so it is a multi-tasking OS. The notes do not state this.
Running two or more programs at the same time on a single processor is called multi-tasking. Multiprocessing needs more than one processor.
UNIX is a multi-user, time-sharing OS, and the notes support statement I. The claim in statement II that it is coded in C is accepted as correct, so both statements hold.
A soft or warm reboot restarts the computer under software control without cutting power, so both statements are correct. The notes do not state this.
Booting is the start-up process that checks that the hardware components are working and connected, then loads the OS. The notes do not state this.
MS-Word is application software, part of the Microsoft Office suite, and not an OS. Mac, Linux and Windows are operating systems.

Qutub Minar (c. 1200), Tughluqabad (14th century), Lodi Garden (15th–16th century) and Fatehpur Sikri (1571–85) give the order III, I, II, IV. The notes only date Fatehpur Sikri, so no line is linked.

Qutub Minar (c. 1200), Tughlaqabad (14th century), Lodi Garden (15th–16th century) and Fatehpur Sikri (1571–85) give the order III, I, II, IV. The notes only date Fatehpur Sikri, so no line is linked.
Bibi ka Maqbara, the tomb of Rabia-ud-Daurani (Aurangzeb's wife), is called the 'Second Taj'. Itimad-ud-Daula is the 'Baby Taj'.
Babur is buried in Kabul, Akbar at Sikandara, Jahangir at Shahdara (Lahore) and Shah Jahan in the Taj Mahal at Agra, giving 3 4 1 2.
Panch Mahal is the five-storey pillared building at Akbar's Fatehpur Sikri. Moti Mahal, Rang Mahal and Hira Mahal are not Fatehpur Sikri buildings in the notes.
The Taj Mahal is traditionally said to have a square-like plan with equal length and breadth. The notes do not state this fact, so no line is linked.

All four statements are true: Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha (1815), wrote Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin (Gift to Monotheists), published Precepts of Jesus (1820) and founded the Brahmo Sabha (1828). So 'All of these' is correct.

The Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019 established the Central University of AP (Anantapuramu) and the Central Tribal University of AP (Vizianagaram). The other options name institutions in different states.
The Thirteenth Schedule says GoI 'shall develop' a new major port at Duggirajupatnam, the only item with 'shall develop'. Ramayapatnam was only the substitute the State built itself.
The notes give 2010–11 small and marginal holdings as about 85% of holdings, covering about 44% of the area. This matches 44.58.
AP's crop insurance covered 22 crops in 2022, so the answer is 22.
Low yield from poor seed quality is not a ground for a claim. Cover is for natural calamities, pests and diseases, so option 4 is the exception.
Varsha Bima was run by AICIL and introduced in 2004, not 2007. Statement I is correct and statement II is wrong, so only I is correct.

The notes do not state which crop insurance schemes run in AP. PMFBY and the weather-based scheme are in use, while a special cover for GM crops is not a known scheme, so option 4 is the one not implemented.

MLAs (elected members of the Legislative Assembly) and MPs vote in the Presidential election. A member of the Legislative Council is not part of the electoral college, so a CM who is only an MLC cannot vote.
Article 170 provides that a State Legislative Assembly has not more than 500 and not fewer than 60 members, so the maximum is 500.

Karnataka was the first State to provide 1% reservation for transgender persons in all government services (July 2021). Kerala is known for the first State transgender policy (2015), not the job quota.
The Lok Sabha presently has 543 members (524 from States and 19 from UTs); 550 is only the constitutional maximum.
The Lok Sabha is called the Popular Chamber because its members are directly elected by the people on adult suffrage; Rajya Sabha members are indirectly elected.
Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012 by the President; notes list nominees under literature, science, art and social service, and sport is not a category, so he came under Art.
The Rajya Sabha's maximum strength is 250 (238 from States/UTs plus 12 nominated); 245 is only the present strength.
Rajya Sabha seats are allotted by population under the Fourth Schedule, not equally like the US Senate.
The 250 maximum is up to 238 representatives of States and UTs plus 12 nominated members.
Rukmini Devi Arundale was the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha, in 1952.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is never dissolved, so the statement that the President can dissolve it is wrong; the other statements are correct.

Statements I and II are correct: the maximum is 250 and 238 members are indirectly elected from States/UTs. III is wrong because creating All-India Services (Art 312) is a special power of the Rajya Sabha, not a power shared equally with the Lok Sabha.
Production of goods is not a function of money; the primary functions are medium of exchange and unit of account, and store of value is a secondary function.
Plastic money means cards such as credit and debit cards, mainly issued by banks, used in place of notes. It is not paper or plastic-coated currency.
Money supply is currency plus deposit money, which commercial banks create by lending. Hoarded, black or debt money are not components.
Near money covers liquid assets like time deposits, T-bills and bills of exchange. Bills of exchange are listed as near money, while coins are legal tender.
Decimal coinage began on 1 April 1957 under the Indian Coinage (Amendment) Act 1955, so 1957 is correct; 1955 was only the year of the Act.
The demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes was announced on 8 November 2016, effective midnight.
Venezuela's President Maduro ordered the 100-bolivar note out of circulation in December 2016, then put off the deadline after protests and cash shortages, so it backtracked.
Reserve money consists of currency, bankers' deposits with RBI and other deposits with RBI. Foreign exchange held by individuals is not a component.
The Gandhian Plan (1944) was formulated by Shriman Narayan Agarwal, not by Gandhi himself, M.N. Roy (People's Plan) or Mahalanobis (Second Plan model).
The Gandhian Plan of 1944 was authored by Shriman Narayan Agarwal. The Bombay Plan (also 1944) was by industrialists and the Visvesvaraya Plan was 1934.
The Bombay Plan wanted a big State role with public-sector dominance, so public-sector investment in infrastructure and heavy industry fits. It did not leave the economy to private investment alone.
The Sargent Plan of education (post-war educational development) was presented in 1944; the notes do not cover it.

The Janata alternative strategy emphasised agriculture, rural development, employment, and small and cottage industries, in line with Gandhian ideals. Special Economic Zones are a later concept and were not part of it.
Guru Nanak chose Bhai Lehna, who became Guru Angad, as his successor before his death. Amar Das and Ram Das came later.

Kabir's work Bijak is linked to his followers, and the Adi Granth/Guru Granth Sahib contains his verses. The Kabir Granthavali tradition in Rajasthan is not in the notes, but all three options are accepted as correct, so 'All of these' is right.
Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 and made the Sikhs a military order. The other Gurus did not found it.
Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi, 13 April 1699, at Anandpur.
Guru Gobind Singh made the Sikhs a military order through the Khalsa (Singh/Kaur surnames, Five Ks). He did not found the Sikh state (that was Banda Bahadur) and did not make Sikhs peaceful.
The Khalsa was founded by the tenth Guru, Gobind Singh, in 1699. Har Rai, Har Kishan and Tegh Bahadur preceded him.
Guru Gobind Singh instituted the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur.
Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir.
Aurangzeb executed Guru Tegh Bahadur at Delhi in 1675.
Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir instead.
Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev died under Jahangir in 1606.
Arjan Dev was executed by Jahangir (1606) and Tegh Bahadur by Aurangzeb (1675). Hargobind was only imprisoned and freed, and Angad was not executed.
Akbar granted 500 bighas of land to the fourth Guru, Ram Das, where Ramdaspur (Amritsar) was founded.
Coronary artery disease results from plaque buildup in the arteries supplying the heart. The other options are not real or do not describe plaque in arteries.
HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over about 2-3 months, so it is used to diagnose and monitor diabetes. It is not a marker for anemia, haemophilia or hypertension.
Oncogenes are genes that, when mutated or overexpressed, drive uncontrolled cell growth and cause cancer. They are not linked to infectious diseases like tuberculosis, hepatitis or typhoid.
The Quit India (August) Resolution was ratified by the AICC at Bombay (Gowalia Tank Maidan) on 8 August 1942; Wardha was only the CWC meeting in July.
The AICC session that ratified the resolution met at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay, on 8 August 1942.
The Quit India resolution was ratified at Gowalia Tank Maidan, now called August Kranti Ground (Maidan), in Bombay; the other options are unrelated places.

Gandhi told government servants to stay in service but pledge loyalty to Congress, and soldiers not to fire on Indians, so statements I and II are wrong. Only III (princes accepting sovereignty of their people) remains correct.
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was Congress President from 1940 to 1946, so he presided over the CWC in July 1942; the notes do not state this.
Gandhi said "We shall either free India or die in the attempt" in his Gowalia Tank speech of 8 August 1942 at the Quit India launch.

NITI Aayog (2015) was the body that put cooperative federalism into practice, with a bottom-up approach where Centre and States work together; so its thrust is promoting cooperative federalism. It is only an advisory think-tank, not a body for planning-failure correction.
The 2021 World Air Quality Report found that 63 of the 100 most polluted cities in the world are in India, so 63 is correct.
The 2021 World Air Quality Report found that 63 of the 100 most polluted cities are in India, so option 4 is correct.
Germany's national highway network is known as the Autobahn; Autoroute is the French term, and Autostride and Autoway are not real names.
The notes give Kolkata-Chennai (~1,649 km) as the longest arm of the Golden Quadrilateral.

Statement I is wrong because the Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, not Bengaluru. Statement II is accepted as correct per the key: the N-S corridor runs through Hyderabad on NH-44.
The N-S and E-W corridors meet at Jhansi, not Nagpur.
Passenger coaches are made at ICF Perambur (Tamil Nadu) and RCF Kapurthala (Punjab), so Punjab and Tamil Nadu is correct.
Konkan Railway runs through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka and links to Kerala. The notes name Madgaon, Ratnagiri and Udupi, which fall in Goa, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Ghum station on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway in West Bengal is the highest-altitude railway station in India.
The Konkan Railway runs from Roha in Maharashtra to Mangalore in Karnataka. The notes mention Udupi, Madgaon and Ratnagiri, which lie along that route.
Viscosity is the internal friction of a fluid that opposes relative motion between its layers, so a stirred liquid gradually comes to rest.
Water has its maximum density of 1 g/cc at 4°C; at other temperatures such as 0°C or 100°C it is slightly lower.
Neon, helium and argon are Group 18 noble gases; hydrogen is a reactive Group 1 element, so it is not a noble gas.
In temperate regions seasons alternate, so distinct annual rings form, each made of spring (early) wood and autumn (late) wood. Both statements are correct.
Venus flytrap traps and digests insects, so it is carnivorous; the other plants are not insectivorous.
Magnetic field lines are continuous closed curves (they continue inside the magnet), so saying they are open curves is incorrect.
Luminous objects emit their own light; the Moon only reflects sunlight, so it is not luminous.
By Fleming's left-hand rule, F = qv × B. With v toward West and force toward North, B must point upward.
The region around a magnet where its influence can be detected is called its magnetic field.
The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called its pole; the centre of curvature and focus lie off the surface.
A spring's constant depends on its material, wire thickness, coil diameter and length, so option 4 is the best answer, not a single factor.
Between two parallel plane mirrors, images keep reflecting back and forth, producing an infinite number of images.
In uniform motion, velocity is constant, so the change in velocity over any time interval is zero.
A curved distance-time graph has a changing slope, meaning the speed changes, which is non-uniform speed.
When the lift accelerates downward, apparent weight is m(g-a), which is less than mg. At uniform speed apparent weight equals real weight.
For the same mass and radius, a solid disc has I = ½MR², while a solid sphere has I = 2/5MR². ½ is larger than 2/5, so the disc has the higher moment of inertia.
The period T = 2π√(L/g) is independent of mass and proportional to √L, so making the length four times doubles the period.
Gravitational force acts at a distance without contact, whereas push, friction and strain forces need contact.
The updated NDC of August 2022 raised the emissions-intensity cut of GDP from 33-35% to 45% by 2030 (base year 2005), so 45 is correct.

An INDC is each country's own pledged post-2020 climate action plan submitted before COP21 (Paris), so it is the world's climate-change action plan. The other options (refugees, AIIB shares, SDGs) are unrelated.

Emotional intelligence is the ability to perceive and monitor one's own and others' feelings and use that to guide thinking and actions. It is not about IQ scores, avoiding emotions or manipulating others.
Malta became the 119th member of the International Solar Alliance in February 2024, so Malta is correct.
Per Census 2011, Bihar is the densest State (1,106 per sq km), ahead of Kerala (860) and UP (829); Haryana is far lower.
Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest density among States in Census 2011 (17 per sq km); Mizoram (52) is the next lowest among the options, while Himachal and West Bengal are much denser.
Sikkim is the least populous State (also in 2001), so it has a smaller population than Mizoram, Chandigarh and Puducherry.
Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest density among all States (17 per sq km in 2011, 13 in 2001), lower than Sikkim, Meghalaya and Himachal Pradesh.
Bihar has the highest density (1,106 per sq km) in Census 2011, above West Bengal (1,028), Kerala (860) and UP (829).
The Kaladan Multimodal project links Kolkata to Sittwe port in Myanmar and then by river and road to Mizoram, so the partner country is Myanmar.

India imports power from Bhutan, supplied by hydro projects such as Mangdechhu. Nepal and Bangladesh are not India's power suppliers in this sense, so the statement that India does not import power is wrong.
The earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism is the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, set up by Heliodorus. The Prayaga Prashasti and the other inscriptions are later.
The Garuda pillar at Besnagar, erected by the Greek envoy Heliodorus, is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. Samudragupta's Prayag Prashasti is much later.
Kalika Purana is an upapurana belonging to the Shaktism tradition (goddess worship), so it is not Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain.
Ardhanarishvara is the union of Shiva and Parvati, i.e. the God with his Shakti, joining Shaivism and Shaktism. Option 3 is the most specific of the overlapping choices.
Nandi is Shiva's bull, Kalpavriksha is the divine tree, Airavata is the divine white elephant and Kamadhenu is the holy cow, giving 3-4-1-2.
Disputes between States fall under the Supreme Court's original (and exclusive) jurisdiction under Art. 131; inherent, plenary and advisory do not describe this power.

Under Art. 143(1) only the President can seek the Court's opinion; the Court cannot advise on its own initiative, and the reference is not limited to Fundamental Rights. So only statement II is correct.
Writ jurisdiction under Art. 32 is original but not exclusive, since High Courts can also issue writs under Art. 226. So the claim of exclusive power to issue writs is false.
Art. 131 covers Centre-State and State-State disputes (I and IV). Election disputes go to High Courts and Centre-UT disputes are excluded, so II and III are wrong.
India's Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Art. 143, whereas the US Supreme Court has none. The other options are roles that both courts share.
Election of Rajya Sabha members was borrowed from South Africa; Ireland is the source only for nomination to the Rajya Sabha and the President's election.
Election of Rajya Sabha members was borrowed from South Africa; Ireland is the source only for nomination to the Rajya Sabha and the President's election.
The Directive Principles (Part IV) were borrowed from Ireland, which itself took them from Spain. South Africa is the source of the amendment procedure, not of the DPSP.
The Directive Principles (Part IV) were borrowed from Ireland, which itself took them from Spain.
The Directive Principles (Part IV) were borrowed from Ireland, which itself took them from Spain.
The idea of the Directive Principles came from Ireland, which took it from Spain. South Africa is the source of the amendment procedure, not of the DPSP.
When the options do not include the 1935 Act, the Emergency provisions are matched with Weimar Germany. The notes list suspension of FRs during Emergency as Weimar Germany.
Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A) were borrowed from the USSR constitution. They were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
The amendment procedure (Art. 368) was borrowed from South Africa, not from Britain, America or Germany.
Single citizenship was borrowed from Britain (England). The USA has dual citizenship.
The Concurrent List was borrowed from Australia. Canada is the source of the strong-Centre scheme and residuary powers, though the makers added a third list to the Canadian division.
India was the first country in the world to set up a ministry for non-conventional energy sources in the early 1980s (CASE 1981, DNES 1982), so Australia, the US and Russia are wrong.
IREDA signed an MoU with IIT Bhubaneswar for innovation and research in renewable energy at the 100 Cube Start-up Conclave (Feb 2024); the other IITs are not the signatories.
The NCEF, funded by the coal cess, finances research and innovative clean energy projects to promote renewable energy and reduce carbon emissions, not fossil fuel use or forest conservation.
Cochin (Kochi) International Airport is the first fully solar-powered airport, so Kochi is correct and the other cities' airports are not.
Nishka (nikkha) was originally a gold ornament or unit of value and only later became a coin, so 'Gold Ornament' is correct; the coin options reflect its later usage.

Guilds fixed prices and wages, controlled quality and had their own rules (shreni-dharma), which supports statement II and the guilds' internal authority over members in III. Statement I, that every guild was registered with the state and the King was its chief authority, is not supported, so II and III only is correct.
India is the world's largest remittance recipient (also in 2015), so India is correct.
Forex reserves comprise foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position in the IMF, so all four are included.

Avoiding reliance on short-term foreign borrowing is a safeguard against external shocks. Full capital account convertibility would increase vulnerability, and the notes do not support opening to more foreign banks as a safeguard.
SDRs exist only as book-keeping entries, a reserve asset and not a currency in circulation, so they are not paper currency, gold or silver.
The IMF's main purpose is to help solve members' balance of payments problems; it is not a deposit arranger or a development lender.
The FEMA preamble states the objective of facilitating external trade and payments. Control of imports or outflow belongs to the restrictive FERA approach.
India accepted Article VIII and introduced full current account convertibility in 1994, while the capital account remains only partially convertible.

Tropical cyclones form over warm oceans, need the Coriolis force, and have a calm, clear, sinking-air eye (I, II, IV correct). Statement III is wrong because they form at about 5°-30° latitude, not in mid-latitudes.
Warm sea surface above 26.5°C, moist air and an unstable atmosphere are the pre-conditions for cyclone genesis, so they belong to the formative/initial stage rather than maturity or decay.
Tropical cyclones are confined to the belt between 30°N and 30°S, so option 2 is correct.
The eye is calm and clear with sinking air, the lowest pressure and a higher temperature, so option 1 is right. Dense cloud belongs to the eyewall, not the eye.

Temperate cyclones move west to east with the westerlies, while tropical cyclones are steered east to west by the trade winds. The other options are wrong: the eye is the calm centre, cyclones have a low-pressure centre, and hurricanes are tropical.
In the Northern Hemisphere cyclonic winds blow anticlockwise, so II is true. A cyclone is a low-pressure system, so its approach brings falling, not rising, pressure; I is false.
In a Northern Hemisphere cyclone, air spirals inward and rotates anticlockwise because of the Coriolis effect.
A cyclone has a low-pressure centre surrounded by higher pressure, and an anticyclone has a high-pressure centre surrounded by lower pressure. So I and III are correct.
A low-pressure centre (cyclone) in the Northern Hemisphere has air moving inward and rotating anticlockwise (counter-clockwise), so option 3 is right.
Rising pressure indicates a high-pressure/anticyclonic condition, which brings clear, dry, calm and settled weather. Cloudy, stormy weather goes with low pressure.
A tornado is a land-based storm, whereas hurricanes, typhoons and willy-willies are ocean-born tropical cyclones.
A galvanometer detects small electric currents in a circuit; refractometer, viscometer and diffractometer measure refractive index, viscosity and diffraction, so they cannot detect current.
A fuse works on the heating effect of current: the low-melting wire heats up and melts when current is excessive, breaking the circuit.

Cutting a magnet always produces two complete magnets, each with north and south poles, because poles cannot be isolated. Each piece keeps the same pole strength, though its magnetic moment is halved.
Bose-Einstein condensate is the 5th and most recently discovered state of matter, after solid, liquid, gas and plasma.
Melting requires overcoming the attractive forces holding particles together, so a higher melting point means stronger intermolecular forces of attraction.
Henry's law says gas solubility in a liquid increases with the pressure of the gas, so CO2 is dissolved in soft drinks under high pressure.
Pressure lowers the melting point of ice, so ice at the contact surfaces melts under pressure and refreezes when pressure is released, joining the blocks (regelation).
Crookes glass contains cerium oxide and absorbs ultraviolet rays, so it is used in protective spectacles. Soda, Pyrex and Jena glass transmit UV.
A telescope uses a convex lens or mirror to form images of distant objects; a microscope is for tiny nearby objects.
Two electrons in the same orbital have the same n, l and m values and differ only in spin quantum number (+1/2 and -1/2), per the Pauli exclusion principle.
The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, which makes the beam's path visible.
Cosmic rays have the shortest wavelength and so the highest frequency among the options, higher than X-rays, microwaves and radio waves.
Nuclear radii are of the order of 10^-15 m, which is one fermi (femtometre), so fermi is the suitable unit.
Smooth ER synthesises lipids and steroid hormones and transports materials, but protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes of rough ER.
Darwin's theory of natural selection includes overproduction, struggle for existence, variation and survival of the fittest, so all of these are correct.

A Bragg spectrometer uses X-ray diffraction from crystal planes (nλ = 2d sinθ) to measure X-ray wavelength. A GM counter only detects radiation, a cyclotron accelerates particles, and a mass spectrometer measures mass.
A candle produces light by burning, i.e. chemical energy. LED (electroluminescence), laser and TV convert electrical energy to light.
The speed of sound in air at 0°C is about 331 m/s, written 331 ms⁻¹ with the correct unit.
Coulomb's law says force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, so doubling the distance reduces the force to one quarter.
A step-down transformer lowers voltage and, since power is nearly conserved, raises current, so output current is greater than input current. It works only on AC.

Geography (Sahyadri forts), Bhakti saints giving religious and regional unity, and Deccan Sultanate service giving political and administrative experience all contributed, so all of the above is correct.

Shahaji served the Bijapur (Adil Shahi) sultanate, and the notes do not state which kingdom granted the Pune jagir. The linked lines only show Pune was a jagir kept by Dadaji Kondadev; Adil Shahi is the answer by general knowledge.
Shivaji was born at Shivneri fort in 1630. Purandar was the treaty fort and Raigad the coronation site.
Raigad was Shivaji's capital and coronation site, taken from the Mores of Javli in 1656.
The Treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665 with the Mughals under Raja Jai Singh, not with Afzal Khan or Shaista Khan.
Afzal Khan was a Bijapur general, so the contingent was sent by the ruler of Bijapur.
In 1663 Shaista Khan, Aurangzeb's maternal uncle, was the Mughal noble who fought Shivaji and was attacked in the night raid at Pune.
The notes do not say which forts were recaptured; Shivneri, Shivaji's birthplace, was never recaptured by him, while Purandar, Mahuli and Lohagarh were.
Sar-i-Naubat was the Persian title of the Senapati, the military commander, not a finance or revenue post.

In Census 2011 the UA ranking was Greater Mumbai (18.4 million), Delhi (16.3), Kolkata (14.1), Chennai (8.7), so Mumbai-Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai is right. Delhi-first or Kolkata-before-Delhi orders reflect the earlier 2001 position.
Goa is the most urbanised State (62.17%), followed by Mizoram, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Maharashtra ranks lowest of the four listed, so the ascending order is Maharashtra-Kerala-Mizoram-Goa.
Mining = Ankleshwar, Industrial = Jamshedpur, Administrative = Gandhinagar, Garrison = Udhampur. This gives a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III.

The answer key links Lutyens with Chandigarh, though he is actually best known as chief architect of New Delhi. Chandigarh was planned by Le Corbusier, so (1) is the key's answer, not a historically accurate one.

The notes do not cover town planning in early 19th-century British India, so no line settles it. Both statements are historically accurate: epidemic fears and public lotteries funded town improvement.
Asia's largest wholesale spice market is Khari Baoli in Old Delhi, so Delhi is correct.
Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar, Hubli-Dharwad and Cuttack-Bhubaneswar are recognised twin cities. Thrissur and Thiruvalla are not a twin-city pair.
Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam), founded in 1605, was the first Dutch factory in India. Pulicat came later (1610), and Surat was set up in 1616.

Bheemili (Bheemunipatnam) had a Dutch settlement and cemetery, so it was a Dutch colony. Mahe was French, and Yanam was also not Dutch. Karaikal was Dutch-held in the notes' list (1645), but it later became French, so Bheemili is the intended answer.
The notes do not give a date for the Dutch factory at Patna. It is only named as a Dutch factory, and 1632 is the date that is accepted for it.
Mattancherry Palace in Kochi was built by the Portuguese and gifted to the Raja of Cochin in 1555. It was later renovated by the Dutch, and so it is popularly called the Dutch Palace.
English rivalry, together with the Dutch defeat at Bedara (1759), made the Dutch withdraw from India. The other options are not supported, since the Portuguese were not what ended Dutch influence.
The notes state that the projected revenue deficit for 2022-23 was about ₹17,000 crore, although the actual figure turned out to be ₹43,487 crore. So 17,000 is correct.
In February 2021 Andhra Pradesh became the second State to complete the power-sector reforms set by the Department of Expenditure, not the first.
Unnava Lakshminarayana was the leader who went to Palnadu in July 1921 to study the forest-law agitation; the other options are not linked with it.
The Rampa Rebellion of Alluri was fought against the Madras Forest Act of 1882, so 1882 is correct; the other years are not the date of that Act.
Alluri's samadhi is at Krishnadevipeta near the Tandava river; Mogallu is only his ancestral village and Chintapalli was the first police station attacked.
The notes give AP's share of India's marine product exports as 40% (March 2022, APPSC 2021 key), and AP ranks 1st. So 40 is correct.
The notes do not cover this fact. Apache, a Taiwanese-origin footwear maker, set up its SEZ at Nellore (Sri Venkateswara SEZ, Ramapuram) to make shoes, so Apache is the answer.
The epithet "Light of Asia" belongs to the Buddha, from Edwin Arnold's 1879 poem on his life, so Lord Buddha is correct.

Kanthaka (horse), Channa (charioteer) and Alara Kalama (teacher) belong to the Buddha's life. Makkhali Gosala (Goshala Maskariputra) was an Ajivika teacher and a contemporary, not part of his life, so only IV is correct.
The Buddha's other names are Tathagata, Shakyamuni and Siddhartha Gautama. Parth, Prachhanna and Mihir are not among them, so none of these is correct.
The Buddha taught karma, rebirth until nirvana, and nirvana as the goal. He neither affirmed nor denied God, so belief in the power of God (IV) is not a Buddhist tenet; I, II and III are correct.
Impermanence (anicca) is one of the three marks of Buddhism, so the idea that the world is unstable and transient is Buddhist.
The Four Noble Truths run in the order suffering, cause, cessation, path. That is I, IV, II, III.
The Middle Path rejects both extreme asceticism (self-mortification) and sensual indulgence. This matches option 3.
The Buddha named no successor; the Dhamma and Vinaya were to be the teacher. So none of these is correct.
The order of tenure was Warren Hastings (1773-85), Cornwallis (1786-93), Wellesley (1798-1805), then William Bentinck (1828-35), which is option 3.
Bentinck's measures included Sati abolition and suppression of female infanticide, so he is the correct choice. Minto, Shore and Lytton are not linked with this measure.
Charles Metcalfe liberated the press in 1835, so he is credited with removing restrictions on newspapers. Bentinck is the tempting wrong option.
The notes do not state this fact. Bentinck met Ranjit Singh at Ropar in 1831, around the time of the treaty of perpetual friendship.
Sati was declared illegal in 1829 under Governor-General William Bentinck, by Regulation XVII.
Sati was declared illegal in 1829 during William Bentinck's governor-generalship.
Notes do not give inflation rates for the Ninth and Tenth Plans; the answer (about 4% and 5%) is the recalled average annual inflation.
The Eleventh Plan achieved 8.0% growth, the highest among plans, above the Ninth (5.4%), Tenth (7.6%) and Twelfth (about 6.7%).

Notes do not state the KN Raj claim or the public-sector industries list or the difficulty of balancing industry and agriculture; the Second Plan drafters found the balance difficult, so III is correct and IV is wrong, and II is correct about public sector industry.
The Nehru-Mahalanobis model was the basis of the Second Plan (1956-61), which stressed heavy and basic industries.
The Second Plan gave maximum emphasis to heavy industry under the Mahalanobis model, whereas the First Plan focused on agriculture.
The Second Plan was pruned because of the 1957-58 foreign-exchange crisis, along with food and capital shortages and inflation, so foreign exchange is the best answer.
The Twelfth Plan's theme was Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth; the Eleventh lacked 'sustainable'.
The Eleventh Plan's theme was Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth.
The Eleventh Plan ran from 2007 to 2012.

The NGT Act's preamble links the Act to the right to a healthy environment as part of the right to life under Article 21, so only statement I is correct. Article 275(1) grants and Gram Sabha powers under Article 243A are not the constitutional basis of the Act.
Muhammad bin Qasim removed Raja Dahir, ruler of Sindh with his capital at Alor, so Dahir is the answer.
The notes do not mention Arab traders on the Malabar Coast. The notes link Islam's first arrival to Sindh in 712, but the answer keyed here is the Arab traders' contact.
Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab invasion of Sindh in 712, so he was an Arab, not a Turk or Mongol.
The Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim (712) were the first Muslim invaders of India, before the Ghaznavids and Ghurids.
Mahmud raided for plunder and temple wealth and did not seek a permanent empire, so plunder was his main motive.
The notes do not cover the Battle of Waihind (1009). Historically Anandapala of the Hindu Shahis fought Mahmud of Ghazni there.
The notes do not mention Farista. The Shahnama was written by Firdausi at Mahmud of Ghazni's court, so the answer is Mahmud Ghazanavi.
Al-Biruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni, who raided India in 1000-1027, so he came in the 11th century AD.
Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) was written by Al-Biruni, who was in Mahmud's court.

The Indigo Revolt (1859-60) and the Deccan Riots (1875) both came after 1857, as did the Birsa Munda uprising (c. 1899-1900). The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) came before 1857, so options with I are wrong.
Nil Darpan (Neel Darpan), written by Dinabandhu Mitra, depicted the plight of indigo cultivators. Dinbandhu is the author, not the book.
The Indigo Revolt was supported by the Bengal intelligentsia (e.g. Hindu Patriot, Nil Darpan). Poona-Ahmednagar and moneylenders refer to the Deccan Riots, so options 1 and 2 are wrong.
Harish Chandra Mukherjee, editor of the Hindu Patriot, championed the cause of indigo cultivators and supported the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 in Bengal.
Planters forced peasants to grow indigo under the Tinkathia system on 3/20 of their land at poor prices. So the grievance was being forced to grow it at an unacceptable price.
The Indigo Revolt (1859-60) came right after 1857. The Sanyasi revolt (1763-1800) was earlier, the Santhal rebellion was in 1855-56, and Pabna was in 1873-76, which came later.
The Eka movement began among farmers of Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur in UP, against excessive rent by zamindars and taluqdars.
Eka aimed at conversion of rent into cash and opposed rent 50% above the recorded rate. It was not about stopping rent to the government.
The Moplah revolt of 1921 took place in Malabar (Kerala). Telangana was the Hyderabad State struggle.
The Moplah revolt of 1921 broke out in Malabar, in Kerala.
The CAG serves 6 years or until 65, whereas the President, VP and Lok Sabha member serve 5 years, so the CAG's term is the longest.
The CAG is an independent constitutional authority created by Article 148 of the Constitution, not by an Act or a Cabinet resolution.
The CAG is an independent constitutional authority created by Article 148, so it was created by the Constitution rather than an Act or a Cabinet resolution.
The CAG's term is 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier.
The CAG is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge (Art. 148(1) with Art. 124(4)), by an address of both Houses.

Statements I, II and IV are correct: 6 years or 65, constitutional powers, and removal like an SC judge on an address by both Houses. III is wrong because the CAG is a single appointee named by the President by warrant, not a multi-member body.
Article 148 provides for the appointment, oath, term and removal of the CAG; Article 149 deals with duties and powers.
The CAG holds office for 6 years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.
On 6 April 1930 Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi after the march that ended on 5 April, which marked the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The other options are not linked to this date.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed on 23 March 1931, and the Karachi session was held on 29-31 March 1931. So the order is 3, 2, 1.
Mercosur comprises Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, all in South America, so it is a Latin American group.

Rising incomes change consumption patterns (demand side) and structural supply-chain constraints (storage, distribution) drive food inflation, so I and II are correct. Statement III's claim of a 30% fall in foodgrain area is not supported.
Inflation lets debtors repay loans in money of lower real value, so they gain. Pensioners (fixed income) and consumers lose.
CPI-IW, CPI-AL and CPI-RL are compiled by the Labour Bureau, while CPI-UNME is not a Labour Bureau series. So only IV is the one not from the Labour Bureau, which matches the answer.
Since April 2014 headline inflation is measured by CPI-Combined, replacing WPI as the headline index.
In the WPI, manufactured products carry the largest weight (about 64%), more than food articles or fuel.
DA is based on the Consumer Price Index, specifically CPI-IW. National income, per capita income or living standard are not used.
Silicon Valley, the US high-tech and aerospace region, is in California.
Sun City is a resort city in South Africa; the notes do not cover it.
Baku (Azerbaijan) is a centre of the oil/petroleum industry, not iron, aircraft or shipbuilding.
Santos in Brazil is the world's chief coffee-exporting port; São Paulo and Rio are not known by this name.
London was historically called the 'City of Smoke' because of its heavy coal smoke and smog.
Wuppertal is a German textile and wool centre. Bradford is in England, Prato in Italy and St Petersburg in Russia.
Venice, built on lagoon islands linked by canals, is known as the city of canals. Amsterdam is also canal-rich but Venice is the standard answer.
