Guyana is in northern South America, while Gabon, Guinea and Guinea-Bissau are all African countries.
Ghana was called the Gold Coast under British rule and became independent in 1957 as Ghana. Tanganyika is the former name of mainland Tanzania.
Catalonia is a region of Spain and Mindanao is in the Philippines. Crimea is tied to Ukraine/Russia, not Hungary, and Oromia is in Ethiopia, not Nigeria.
Benelux is the economic union of Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg, whose names form the acronym.
Chad is a landlocked country in Africa. Angola, Kenya and Senegal all have coastlines.
Denmark is known as the country of winds because of its extensive wind energy and windy climate.
Norway, Sweden, Iceland, Denmark and Finland together are known as the Nordic countries.
Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun, as its name Nippon means 'origin of the sun'.
Devaraya II hired 10,000 Muslim soldiers and improved cavalry and archery. Devaraya I only first appointed Muslims; the 10,000 figure belongs to Devaraya II.
Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was a title of Devaraya II. The other options are not titles noted for him.
Abdur Razzaq, the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh, visited Vijayanagara in 1443 during Devaraya II's reign.
Ashoka built the original brick core of the Sanchi Stupa. The Sungas later added the stone casing and the Satavahanas the toranas, but Ashoka is credited with constructing it.

Statement I is wrong because the Barabar caves (3rd c. BCE), not Badami, are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves. Statement II is wrong because the caves were given by Ashoka and his grandson Dasaratha, not Chandragupta. Statement III, that Ellora has caves for different faiths, is the only correct one, so the answer is Only III.
The Ramsar Convention (1971) deals with conservation and wise use of wetlands, so wetlands is correct; the other options are unrelated.
The Ramsar Convention (1971) deals with conservation and wise use of wetlands, so wetlands is correct; the other options are unrelated.
In 2022, 28 new Indian wetlands were declared Ramsar sites, so 28 is correct.

Satkosia is a tiger reserve in Odisha on the Mahanadi gorge, so statements I and III are correct. The notes do not support statement II (the two adjoining sanctuaries), which is the one that makes the answer exclude it.
Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 with 9 reserves, so 1973 is correct.
Periyar is in Kerala, Sariska in Rajasthan, Buxa in West Bengal and Indravati in Chhattisgarh, which gives a-IV, b-II, c-III, d-I.
Pitti is a seabird islet sanctuary in Lakshadweep, so option 3 is correct.

Global warming is the rise in global surface temperature, and it is driven mainly by higher greenhouse gas concentrations (CO2 causes about three-quarters of it), so Statement II correctly explains Statement I.
China is the largest CO2 emitter among developing countries, ahead of India; the notes do not cover this fact.

IPCC says warming raises the frequency and severity of storms, floods, droughts and similar events, so cyclones, storms and hurricanes are all affected; hence 'All of these' is correct, not any single one.
The notes state that the first-ever national meet of DLSAs was held on 30-31 July 2022 in New Delhi.
Seshachalam is AP's first and only biosphere reserve, notified in 2010; the other options are wildlife sanctuaries.
AP had 13 wildlife sanctuaries in 2019, and the number is still 13.
Sri Venkateswara NP is noted for protecting spotted deer; the golden gecko and slender loris are species found there, but spotted deer is the protection answer in the notes.
Sri Venkateswara NP is noted for protecting spotted deer; the golden gecko and slender loris are species found there, but spotted deer is the protection answer in the notes.

The notes place Sri Venkateswara NP in Annamayya and Tirupati districts (Seshachalam-Tirumala hills), which were part of old Chittoor, but they do not name Chittoor itself. Chittoor is the expected answer among the options.
Kandaleru Deer Park is in SPS Nellore district; the notes do not mention it.
Chinnar WLS is in Kerala, not AP. Kambalakonda, Pulicat and Sri Venkateswara are AP sanctuaries.
By notification year: Nelapattu (1976), Rollapadu (1988), Koundinya (1990), Kolleru (1999), i.e. C, A, B, D.
Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam is India's largest tiger reserve by area and by core/critical tiger habitat.
The Rayala Elephant Reserve is linked with Koundinya WLS, AP's only elephant sanctuary. Coringa, Papikonda and Nelapattu are not elephant habitats.
The Rayala Elephant Reserve is linked with Koundinya WLS, AP's only elephant sanctuary. Coringa, Papikonda and Nelapattu are not elephant habitats.
The notes do not mention rosewood. They give red sanders as the Seshachalam hills speciality, so Seshachalam is the expected answer among the options.
The Telineelapuram mass deaths involved the spot-billed pelican, Pelecanus philippensis, not P. onocrotalus, the stork or the crane.
Pulicat is the brackish lagoon with a bird sanctuary, in Tirupati district (earlier Nellore). Kolleru is freshwater and Chilika is in Odisha.
Koundinya WLS is the only Asian elephant habitat of AP, so it is famous for Asiatic elephants.
The notes do not state which wife of Jahangir committed suicide.
The notes do not mention Sawai Jai Singh as an amir of Jahangir, but the other pairings are not contradicted; the notes give no line settling it.
Khusrau (1606), Khurram (1622-26) and Mahabat Khan (1626 coup) all rebelled against Jahangir. Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and a junta member, not a rebel.
The junta consisted of Nur Jahan, Asmat Begum, Ghiyas Beg (Itimad-ud-Daulah), Asaf Khan and Prince Khurram. Mahabat Khan was not a member (he later seized Jahangir in a coup).
Mehrunnisa married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Nur Jahan, so Jahangir is correct.
Jahangir himself was not a member of the junta, which was made up of Nur Jahan, her parents, Asaf Khan and Khurram. Ghiyas Beg, Asaf Khan and Khurram were members.
Sir Thomas Roe, James I's ambassador, came to Jahangir's court in 1615 (stayed 1615-19), so 1615 is correct.

Francois Bernier, the French physician linked with Dara Shikoh, was in India during the succession war and witnessed Dara's humiliation. Hawkins came in Jahangir's time, and Manucci was Dara's artilleryman.
Dara Shikoh, the eldest son, bore the titles Shah-i-Iqbal and Shah Buland Iqbal.
Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir, bore the titles Shah-i-Iqbal and Shah Buland Iqbal.
Stone Age phases are defined by tool type and technology (statement i is true), but tools varied regionally and cultures did not evolve in a uniform unilinear way, so statements ii and iii are false.
Cro-Magnons were anatomically modern humans of the Upper Palaeolithic, later than Neanderthals and Heidelberg humans; 'Pilt magnon' is not a real group.
The Three-Age system (Stone, Bronze, Iron) was devised by the Danish scholar C. J. Thomsen while arranging the Copenhagen museum collection.
The Levallois prepared-core technique was used at Sembur in Tamil Nadu; the other options are not real techniques.
Bone implements are reported from the Mesolithic sites of Mahadaha and Sarai Nahar Rai; of the options, Mahadaha is the one listed as correct.
Adamgarh (MP) gives the earliest evidence of animal domestication in the Mesolithic; Langhnaj, Birbhanpur and Chopani Mando are not known for this.
Early farming began in the Neolithic, with Lehuradeva rice at c. 6500 BCE and Mehrgarh wheat and barley; 7000 BC is the closest option.
Navdatoli is a Malwa-culture settlement on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh, not in Gujarat or Maharashtra.
The Chalcolithic cultures were the first to use painted pottery, such as Ahar-Banas white-painted ware and Jorwe painted red ware.
Dr. V. S. Wakankar discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters in 1957-58.
ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969, superseding INCOSPAR (1962); 1967 and 1974 are not its founding year.
SITE (Satellite Instructional Television Experiment), 1975-76 with NASA's ATS-6, was the first use of space technology for education.
APPLE, India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, was launched on 19 June 1981 on Ariane-1 from Kourou.
Aryabhata (19 Apr 1975) was India's first satellite, with which India entered the space age; Bhaskara and APPLE came later and Agni is a missile.
Aryabhata, launched 19 April 1975, was India's first satellite; Bhaskara and Rohini came later (Rohini was the first on an Indian rocket).
SpaDeX (launched on PSLV-C60, docking done January 2025) was a space docking demonstrator, making India the 4th country to achieve docking.
Property tax is the major own revenue source of Panchayats, as the notes state; the other options are not stated as the major source.
Panchayats may levy only State-authorised taxes such as those on local fairs, house tax, fees and tolls. Sales tax and land revenue are State levies, so they are not levied by Gram Panchayats.
The notes state that the 2022-23 plan raised agricultural credit by 10%, so 10 is correct.
Indira Prabha is the AP land development programme supported by NABARD, which fits the land development package for land given to the poor. The other names are not listed as such schemes.
Indira Prabha is the AP land development programme with NABARD support. Indira Kranti is a different (SHG/poverty) programme.
Lakshmidhara, the Gahadavala minister of Govindachandra, compiled the Krityakalpataru, the earliest Nibandha digest. The notes do not state this, so Harsha and Kalidasa are wrong on date and context.
Muni Jin Vijay Suri was not a scholar at Kumbha's court, unlike the others listed. The notes do not cover Kumbha's court scholars.
The Lingaraj Temple at Bhubaneswar is the largest and tallest surviving temple in Odisha, which makes it the right answer. The notes do not mention Odisha temples.
The Bhubaneswar and Puri temples belong to the Odisha (Kalinga) school of the Nagara style, with a curvilinear shikhara. The notes do not cover Odisha temples.
Dahsala (1580) assessed revenue on the average produce and prices of the previous ten years (1571-80), converted into cash. It was not a fixed ten-year rate, a decennial survey or crop-sharing.

Dahsala (Ain-i-Dahsala) is the system called Bandobast, also known as Zabti or Bandobast and associated with Todar Mal. Nasaq and Kankut are different methods (past records and standing-crop estimate).

The Amalguzar was the sarkar-level revenue collector, responsible for assessing and collecting land revenue and extending cultivation. Law and order was the faujdar's task, and the treasury was kept by the potdar.
Madad-i-maash was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy, so option 2 is correct. It was not a tax or a military pension.

The amalguzar was the revenue collector, the qanungo kept revenue records, and the bitikchi kept records on land and produce, with the karkun preparing crop statistics. The option a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III matches this pattern.

Statement I is taken as correct in the key, and statement II (PSLV launched IRS satellites) and statement IV (GSAT launched in 2001 with digital broadcast and internet payloads) are also correct. Statement III is wrong because the cryogenic engine was not used on the SLV third stage; it was used on the GSLV. So I, II and IV are correct.
APPLE (Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment), the first experimental comsat, was launched on an Ariane rocket in 1981. Ariane launches take place from Kourou, French Guiana, not from Sriharikota.
The Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) was set up under the Regulating Act 1773. Pitt's Act 1784 created the Board of Control, and the 1861 and 1892 Acts dealt with councils.
The Charter Act of 1833 created the Governor-General of India, with William Bentinck as first holder. The 1773 Act created only the GG of Bengal, and 1858 created the Viceroy.
The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly, except for tea and the China trade. The 1833 Act ended all trade activity.
The office of Governor-General of India was created by the Charter Act of 1833, with Bentinck as the first holder. 1774 relates to the Supreme Court and 1858 to the Viceroy.
The 1858 Act did transfer rule from the Company to the Crown, so A is true. The transfer was Parliament's decision, not because the Company was unwilling to rule, so R is false.
The Indian Councils Act 1892 allowed discussion of the annual budget, though with no vote. Under the 1861 Act there was no budget discussion.
Natural gas is a fossil fuel and therefore non-renewable, whereas sunlight, tides and geothermal heat are renewable sources.
Earth's resources include water, minerals, fish stocks and fossil fuels, so option 1 is correct.
Syngas is the mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen (CO + H2), which is the same as water gas. The other options are not this mixture.
Thermal power has the highest share of installed capacity (48.07%), and coal supplies over 70% of electricity, so thermal power is India's main source of energy.
A mixture of CO and H2 is called water gas. Producer gas is different, being CO + H2 + N2.
World Humanitarian Day is observed on 19 August, so option 3 is correct. The other dates are not the notes' date for this day.
The State Emergency Operations Centre of APSDMA is at Kunchanapalli (Guntur district). The notes mention the SEOC but do not give its location.
Delta is formed by running water, cirque by glaciers, cliffs by waves and currents, and sand dunes by wind, which gives a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II.
Exfoliation is physical (mechanical) weathering with no chemical change, whereas hydration, oxidation and solution are chemical weathering processes.
Weathering is in-situ breakdown, so A is true, and R is also true as physical weathering is driven by temperature changes. But R does not explain A, which defines weathering in general, so (2).
Patland in central India consists of lava-capped mesas, not buttes, fans or oxbow lakes.
Borra Caves are limestone karst caves in the Ananthagiri hills near Araku, so Ananthagiri Hills is correct.
Stalactites and stalagmites form when groundwater dissolves and redeposits calcium carbonate in limestone caves, so they are karst features.
The U.S.A. passed the landmark Affordable Care Act (ObamaCare) health care reform in 2010. The notes do not cover this.
ObamaCare is the U.S. Affordable Care Act, a law to make health insurance and care affordable. The other options describe unrelated areas.
The Varishtha Bima Yojana was an insurance/pension scheme for senior citizens (60+), so option 2 is right. The notes do not cover this scheme.
Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched on 1 April 2017 at Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, so Nellore is correct.

The 2015 amendment made witchcraft accusations an atrocity; the notes do not give the penalty, but the option stating a minimum of six months extending to five years with fine is the statutory punishment.
The 1995 Rules require investigation by an officer not below the rank of DSP, so an Inspector is not enough.
The PCR Act 1955 proved inadequate to check atrocities against SCs/STs, which is why Parliament enacted the PoA Act in 1989.
The Act's preamble provides for relief and rehabilitation of victims of atrocities, so rehabilitation is correct. The notes do not state the preamble.
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v State of Maharashtra (2018) was seen as diluting the Act by allowing preliminary enquiry, anticipatory bail and prior approval for arrest. The other cases are unrelated.
The PoA Act was enacted in 1989 (in force from 30 January 1990), so 1989 is the enactment year; 1990 is the trap.
Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria, so Syria is correct; it is not in Israel, Ukraine or Palestine.
The 15th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (2019) was held in Varanasi, so option 4 is correct; Gandhinagar hosted the 13th in 2015 and New Delhi the 12th in 2014.
Jeffrey Armstrong was named the ICCR Distinguished Indologist for 2021, so option 1 is correct. The other names are historical Indologists, not the 2021 awardee.
Ishwar Sharma, a young yoga practitioner, received the Global Child Prodigy Award 2020 for yoga, so the answer is Yoga.
Carbon monoxide, from incomplete combustion such as vehicle exhaust, is a pollutant even under normal conditions. N2 and O2 are normal air constituents, and CO2 is not the pollutant meant here.
Particulate matter (PM2.5/PM10) is an air pollutant arising from combustion, construction and road dust. It is not a water or soil pollutant.

Diesel engines give more CO at low temperatures because combustion is incomplete, and more NOx at high temperatures because nitrogen and oxygen combine in the hot cylinder. The notes do not state this temperature dependence.
Carbon monoxide has an affinity for haemoglobin 200-250 times that of oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin. Methane, NO2 and SO2 do not combine with haemoglobin in this way.
Tropospheric ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from NOx, VOCs (including methane) and CO in sunlight. Water vapour is not a precursor, so it does not cause ozone pollution.
Tetraethyl lead was added to petrol as an antiknock agent to prevent engine knocking. The notes do not mention this use.
Asthma is aggravated by air pollution; ground-level ozone is listed in the notes as causing asthma. It is not caused by water, soil or noise pollution.
Lichens are the bioindicator of SO2; they disappear where SO2 is high. Mosses indicate heavy metals instead.
Statement II is supported by the notes: lichens are SO2-sensitive indicators. Statement I is also true, since a lichen is a symbiotic association of algae and fungi, so both are correct.
Lichens indicate air pollution, especially SO2, and fail to grow where SO2 is high.

Constitutional government is limited government bound by the Constitution and rule of law, so it is run by fixed rules rather than the will of individuals. A republic, monarchy or socialist system does not carry this meaning.

Thomas Hobbes, in Leviathan, argued for the absolute sovereign power of the monarch, since people surrender all rights to the sovereign. Locke favoured limited government and Rousseau popular sovereignty.
The Social Contract (1762) was written by Jean-Jacques Rousseau. Hobbes wrote Leviathan and Locke wrote Two Treatises of Government.
Individualists see the state as a necessary evil, to be kept minimal because it restricts individual liberty but is needed to maintain order. Anarchists want it abolished, so they are not the answer.
A constitutional government is limited by the terms of the Constitution, which defines and restrains power to prevent tyranny. So it is a limited government.

The presidential system is based on separation of powers between the executive and legislature, unlike the parliamentary system, which is based on fusion. Division of powers between Centre and States is federalism.
The legislature (Parliament and State Legislatures) consists of the people's elected representatives. The media is not a government organ, and judges are appointed rather than elected.

Sultan Qaboos bin Said ruled Oman from 1970 until his death in January 2020, making him the Arab world's longest-serving ruler. Abu Dhabi and Dubai are emirates of the UAE, and Kuwait is ruled by an emir, so they are wrong.
Anuradha Sawhney is known for her work in animal rights and animal welfare, not in micro finance, environment protection or rainwater harvesting.
Savitribai Phule worked with Jyotiba Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, where she taught at the girls' school opened in 1848 and later headed the Samaj's women's section. So Maharashtra is correct.
The Satyashodhak Samaj, founded by Phule at Pune in 1873, was an anti-caste movement in Maharashtra. The other options name regions and movements unrelated to it.

All four statements hold: Art. 21 is available to citizens and foreigners, courts have read dignity into it, and it can be curtailed only by procedure established by law (also covering arbitrary action). So I, II, III and IV is correct.
Art. 21A makes education for ages 6-14 both a human right and a fundamental right. Right to information is statutory, and housing and the right to die are not fundamental rights.
Art. 21A makes education for ages 6-14 both a human right and a fundamental right. Right to information, work and housing are not fundamental rights.
Article 43 (DPSP) deals with a living wage and decent standard of life for workers. Art. 42 covers only humane conditions and maternity relief, and Art. 39 covers livelihood and equal pay.
Section 2(1)(m) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 defines 'public servant', so Section 2(M) is correct.
Musiri (Muziris) and Tondi were western-coast Chera ports. Korkai is Pandyan and Puhar is Chola, so I, III are wrong; Saliyur is not listed as a Chera place, so option (2) is correct.
The NDC secures states' cooperation, promotes common economic policies and works for balanced development of all regions, so all the listed functions are correct.
The Finance Commission (Article 280) handles tax devolution and decides the formula for sharing tax proceeds between Centre and States; the Planning Commission and NDC dealt with plans.
The Finance Commission decides the method and formula for sharing tax proceeds between Centre and States, so it lays down the basic principles; the Planning Commission and NDC do not.
The Finance Commission is the constitutional body (Article 280) dealing with tax devolution; the Planning Commission is non-constitutional and the NDC is neither constitutional nor statutory.

The Finance Ministry controls budgetary allocation for spending, including plan spending, making it the controlling authority of government expenditure; the Finance Commission only recommends tax devolution.
Article 40 of the DPSP deals with village panchayats, making the village a primary unit of self-government; Article 39 is the source of plan objectives.

In the planning flow the Commission drafts, the NDC approves, then the Cabinet and Parliament take it up. So the NDC and Parliament are associated with planning; the Finance Commission and the ministries are not part of this flow.
The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA dealing with municipalities; it does not cover the NDC, State Finance Commission functions or the Kaveri authority.
Infrared radiation is used in heat therapy and imaging; it is the radiation that can bring out faded or hard-to-read writing, unlike gamma rays, X-rays or radio waves, which are not used for this.
Unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole of a magnet, so a non-magnet iron piece is attracted to the north pole, whereas like poles repel and charged rods are not affected by magnets.
X-ray emission converts electron kinetic energy into photons, while the photoelectric effect is the reverse: photons falling on a metal eject electrons.
The pencil 'lead' is actually graphite, a form of carbon, not the metal lead or its compounds.
The banyan is a flowering plant that bears seeds enclosed in fruits (figs), so it is an angiosperm, not a gymnosperm, pteridophyte or alga.
SBI was formed in 1955 from the Imperial Bank of India (itself the 1921 merger of the three Presidency banks) under the SBI Act 1955.
SBI is the largest commercial bank and its headquarters is at Mumbai.
The notes do not cover this award; HDFC Bank was named Best Retail Bank in India by The Asian Banker.
Large commercial banks were nationalised on 19 July 1969 (14 banks) and 15 April 1980 (6 banks), so 1969 and 1980 is correct.
The first round of bank nationalisation took place on 19 July 1969, covering 14 banks; the second round was in 1980.
In the second round on 15 April 1980, six banks were nationalised; 14 was the 1969 figure.
Nationalisation aimed at social control of credit and shifting credit to agriculture and small industry, i.e. improving credit facilities for neglected sectors.
In 1969, 14 banks were nationalised.
The 1969 round covered banks with deposits of Rs 50 crore and above (the 1980 round was Rs 200 crore).
SBI is the largest commercial bank in India; RBI is the central bank, not a commercial bank.
Nationalisation of banks, formation of RRBs (1975-76) and the Lead Bank Scheme under which banks adopt districts are all features of the Indian banking system, so all three are correct.
Atomic weight is the average mass of an element's isotopes, so it can be fractional, whereas mass number (protons + neutrons) is always a whole number.
Mass number minus atomic number equals the number of neutrons, and atoms with the same neutron number are isotones.
Isobars share the same mass number but have different atomic numbers (e.g. 3H and 3He).
In beta (negative) emission a neutron changes into a proton and an electron, which is emitted, so the number of protons increases by one.
U-235 is the fissile isotope of natural uranium and is used as fuel in reactors; U-334 and U-239 are not usable fuel isotopes, and U-233 is bred from thorium for later stages.
Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed most alpha particles passed through while a few were deflected sharply, indicating a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at the atom's centre.
The nucleus contains the protons and neutrons, which account for nearly all of the atom's mass; electrons are negligible in mass.
7 electrons in the M-shell means 2+8+7 = 17 electrons, so 17 protons. Mass number = 17 + 18 = 35.
The force between the negatively charged electron and the positively charged nucleus is the electrostatic (electric) force; gravity is negligible at this scale.
A positron carries a +1 charge, equal in magnitude and sign to the proton's charge; the electron is negative, and the neutron has no charge. The alpha particle has +2.
Isotopes have the same atomic number (same number of protons and electrons), so their chemical properties are the same.
Isotopes share the atomic number but differ in mass number, while isobars share the mass number but differ in atomic number. Both statements are reversed, so neither is correct.
Neutrons = mass number − protons = 12 − 6 = 6.
Stars generate energy by nuclear fusion, mainly hydrogen fusing into helium, not by fission.
Brahmani is listed among the east-flowing rivers draining to the Bay of Bengal. Sharavati, Mahi and Sabarmati are west-flowing rivers.
Periyar is west-flowing and reaches the Arabian Sea via Vembanad. Godavari, Tungabhadra (a Krishna tributary) and Kaveri flow east to the Bay of Bengal.
Tamraparni flows east into the Gulf of Mannar, so it is not west-flowing, while Periyar, Bharathapuzha and Pamba are Kerala rivers that flow west.
The north-to-south order of east-flowing rivers is Godavari, Krishna, Pennar, Cauvery. Periyar in Kerala lies furthest south of the four, so the order is Godavari, Pennar, Kaveri, Periyar.
Damodar is called the 'biological desert' because it is heavily polluted by industrial effluents. The notes do not cover this fact.
Narmada and Sabarmati are west-flowing and drain into the Arabian Sea. Krishna and Mahanadi flow east to the Bay of Bengal.
Tapi is west-flowing and drains into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat. Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi flow into the Bay of Bengal.

Most east-flowing peninsular rivers form deltas, so A is true. Reason R is false because the deltas are built by river sediment, not because the Deccan rocks are soft; peninsular rivers flow over hard rock.
Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats, not at Kodagu or Trimbakeshwar.
The Gandhi Solar Park is a solar installation at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, gifted by India. The notes do not cover this fact, so no line is linked.
Nannaya and Tikkana translated the Mahabharata into Telugu (with Errana) as the Kavitrayam. Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana and Kuttan is not a Telugu translator, so I and II are wrong.
Andhra Shabda Chintamani, a Sanskrit grammar of Telugu, is traditionally attributed to Nannaya. Tikkana, Errana and Peddana are known for other works.
The Faraizi movement was founded by Haji Shariatullah (1818, Faridpur), so the Faraizis were his followers. Dudu Miyan was only his son and successor who made it a peasant movement.
Dadu (Dudu) Miyan, son of founder Haji Shariatullah, succeeded him and made the Faraizi movement a peasant movement against zamindars and planters. The other names are not Faraizi leaders.
Khusrau served several Sultans and is linked with Alauddin's court, which gave him the title Tuti-i-Hind. Alauddin is the best match among the options; Ibrahim Lodi is outside his period.
Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India) was the title of Amir Khusrau. Sadi-i-Hind is Amir Hasan's title, so Amir Hasan is the tempting wrong option.
Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh (Khazain-ul-Futuh-i-Alai) describes Alauddin's conquests, so he is the contemporary author. Barani and Afif wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
The statement is attributed to Amir Khusrau, who criticised the burden on the peasants. The notes do not state this fact.
Khusrau was born at Patiyali, which lies in the Etah district, so Etah is correct.
Barani was a companion of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, so II and III are correct. The notes do not say he was born in Golconda, so statement I is not supported.
Apabhramsa denotes the early forms of the modern Indian languages, which grew out of Prakrit. The notes do not cover this.
Persian was the elite language of administration in the Sultanate. Urdu grew in camps and bazaars and was not the official language.

Statement I is correct: the Second Plan gave maximum emphasis to heavy industry. Statement II is wrong because the Third Plan's focus was self-reliance with priority to agriculture, not import substitution.
The Eighth Plan ran from April 1992 to March 1997, so option 3 is correct.
The Eleventh Plan covered 2007-12.
The Twelfth Plan (2012-17) was the last plan, so it ended in 2017.
'Food, Work and Productivity' was the tagline of the Seventh Plan (1985-90).
The Plan Holiday was 1 April 1966 to 31 March 1969, when three Annual Plans were run.
The Janata government ended the Fifth Plan a year early, in 1978, so it is the plan terminated before schedule.
The Twelfth Plan was launched on 1 April 2012 and ran 2012-17, the last of the Five Year Plans. 2007-12 was the Eleventh Plan.
The notes do not state the agriculture share of GDP given in the Tenth Plan Approach Paper, so no line is linked.
The notes give no sector-wise outlay for Andhra Pradesh's Second Plan, so no line is linked.

The Janata government's Rolling Plan (1978-80) is called its Sixth Plan, but it never became an official plan because Congress introduced a new Sixth Plan in 1980. Of the options, the Sixth Plan is the one that fits. The notes do not mention Panchayati Raj.
A seismograph records ground vibration using a vibrating rod (a suspended mass/pendulum-type sensor), so option 1 is correct. The notes only say seismographs record waves, not how they are built.
The lithosphere is the rigid outer shell made of the crust plus the uppermost mantle (~100 km), so option 3 is correct. The other options include the whole mantle or the core, which is wrong.
Besides iron and nickel, the core's lighter elements are silicon, sulphur and oxygen, so silicon is correct. Magnesium, calcium and cobalt are not the listed light elements.
Oxygen is highest in the crust at 46.60%. Among the listed elements, magnesium is lowest at 2.09%, below calcium, sodium and silicon, so option 4 is right.
Oxygen makes up 46.60% of the crust by weight, the highest of any element. Silicon is second at 27.72%, so it is the tempting wrong option.
NIFE stands for nickel plus ferrum (iron) and forms the core, so Nife is correct. Sial is silica-aluminium and Sima is silica-magnesium.
At the magnetic equator the field lines run parallel to the Earth's surface, so the dip angle is zero and the field is horizontal. At the poles the field is vertical.

Statement I is false because the magnetic axis is inclined about 11.5°, not 23.5°, to the geographic axis. Statements II and III are true: the north magnetic pole is in northern Canada and the magnetic equator passes near Thumba.
Magnetic field direction at a place is given by the declination (angle from geographic north) and the inclination or dip (angle from horizontal). Both are needed, so option 3 is correct.
Carbon-14 dates once-living remains such as wood, bones and shells (up to ~50,000 years). Uranium-238 is used for very ancient rocks, not organic remains.
Carbon-14 dating is used for once-living organic remains such as fossils, wood and bones. It is not suited to dating rocks, which need uranium-lead or potassium-argon methods.
Radiocarbon, uranium-lead and potassium-argon are all radiometric dating methods. Mining is just extraction of minerals and not a dating technique.
Article 51A(k) makes it a parent/guardian's fundamental duty to educate a child aged 6–14. It became enforceable as a statutory right when the RTE Act came into force on 1 April 2010.
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for ages 6–14 a Fundamental Right. The other amendments listed do not deal with this.
Kailash Satyarthi founded Bachpan Bachao Andolan. Shantha Sinha is known as the first NCPCR chairperson, not the founder of this movement.
The RTE Act 2009 is a Parliamentary Act and the States frame rules under it, so Andhra Pradesh issuing its RTE Rules in 2010 is true and the Act is the reason it did so. Hence R correctly explains A.
The NPE priority areas are universal elementary education, adult literacy and women's educational equality. Compulsory nutrition education for all is not a priority area.
e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR portal for online complaints about child-rights violations, launched in 2015 and updated in September 2022.
Banjaras were the traders who carried bulk goods like grain and salt over long distances in bullock caravans. Baniks and Beoparis are local retail traders, and Sarrafs are bankers.
A hundi was a letter of credit issued by shroffs against deposited cash, encashable later or at another place. Farman is a royal order and Rokad means cash.
The notes do not mention Akbar's gold coins like the Sihinsah; the Sihinsah was Akbar's largest gold coin, while Dam was copper and Illahi was a smaller gold coin.
The Dam was the Mughal copper coin (40 dams = 1 rupee). The rupee was silver.
Lahari Bandar was the port of Thatta in the Indus delta, so Thatta itself was the town and not the port named among the options, while Cambay and Surat were ports. Hence Thatta is the answer.

Moreland wrote India at the Death of Akbar, Irfan Habib wrote The Agrarian System, Bernier wrote Travels in the Mogul Empire, and Foster edited Early Travels in India. This gives a-IV, b-I, c-II, d-III.
The NRF (1992) funded VRS, retraining and redeployment of workers displaced by restructuring, so retraining of labour is correct. It was not meant for roads, railways or bank refinancing.
'Golden Handshake' is the term for the Voluntary Retirement Scheme, used by public and private firms to reduce staff. It has nothing to do with gold dealing or gold trade.

The NRF was a social safety net that funded VRS, retraining and redeployment for displaced workers, so 'social security' fits. It was not for industrial restructuring or modernization capital, which is the tempting wrong option.

Statements I and III are supported by the notes: the ED Director can attach "proceeds of crime" under PMLA, and PMLA 2002 came into force on 1 July 2005. Statement IV (Appellate Tribunal and Special Court) is also part of the Act, so the answer is I, III and IV only. Statement II is the tempting wrong one: it is incorrect as framed, because Part A of the Schedule is not described as the trans-border crimes part.

The notes say DPE was earlier under the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises, so that ministry comprised the Department of Heavy Industry and the Department of Public Enterprises. The DPIIT and DSIR belong to other ministries.

QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and Indian industry associations, and its Chairman is appointed by the Prime Minister on the industry's recommendation, so both statements are correct. The notes do not cover this.
The Krishnapatnam port region is a cluster for heavy industries, so Heavy Industries is correct; textiles, tourism and IT are not its focus.
Undivided Andhra Pradesh ranked 5th in population in Census 2011 (7.00% of India); residual AP is 10th only after the 2014 bifurcation.
Visakhapatnam is the most urban district (47.45% urban), so it has the lowest rural share of population among the options.
East Godavari was the most populous district in 2011 (about 51.5 lakh), so it likely had the largest rural population, but the notes do not state rural population by district.
Kurnool had the highest share of 0–6 child population among districts in 2011, so it is correct; East Godavari is only the most populous.

The President is only the nominal head (de jure); the real executive is the PM and Council of Ministers, so statement 2 is wrong. The other statements correctly describe collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha, individual responsibility to the President and dependence on legislative confidence.
Under Art. 75 the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (the popular House), not to both Houses, the President or the ruling party.

The Council of Ministers is answerable to the legislature; specifically the Lok Sabha, the popular House, under Art. 75. Among the options, Parliament is the correct one, as the President receives only individual responsibility and the PM and Speaker are not the bodies it answers to.
A non-member can be a minister but must become an MP within six months, otherwise he ceases to be a minister.
The notes describe CRIIIO 4 GOOD as an ICC–UNICEF cricket animation series on life skills and gender equality, so the statements are consistent with it and none is incorrect.
The notes do not cover the 2002 ICC Champions Trophy; Sri Lanka hosted it in September 2002.
The notes give the 2025 order as 20th National Youth (Patna), then 28th National Federation Senior (Kochi), then Indian Grand Prix 2 (Trivandrum), which is 2-3-1.

Statement II is right, as Hardik Singh was FIH men's Player of the Year 2023. Statement III is wrong because Savita Punia, not Sushila Chanu, was Goalkeeper of the Year. Statement IV is also wrong (the ICC Emerging Cricketer 2023 was Rachin Ravindra, per the notes), so III and IV are incorrect.
Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics; Los Angeles is the 2028 host. The notes do not state this.
Bilateral monopoly is a market with a single seller (monopolist) facing a single buyer (monopsonist), so option 4 is right; the other options list multiple sellers or buyers.
Zero price elasticity means perfectly inelastic demand: quantity demanded stays unchanged whatever the price change, so option 1 is right.

Neither statement is correct: disinvestment means reducing government equity while control may stay with the government, so II is wrong. Proceeds are not mainly used to repay external debt (they were channelled to the NIF and used for fiscal needs), so I is wrong.

In a monopoly there is a single firm, so the firm is the industry and the market demand curve is the firm's demand curve. In oligopoly, duopoly or perfect competition there are several firms sharing the market demand.
Many sellers selling differentiated but close substitute products is monopolistic competition. Perfect competition has homogeneous products, and oligopoly has few sellers.
A market with a few large firms is an oligopoly. Duopoly is specifically two sellers, and monopoly is one seller.
Red is the colour for 'take action', which also marks the post-landfall outlook stage of cyclone warnings. Yellow, orange and green denote 'be aware', 'be prepared' and 'no warning'.
Geo-informatics helps predict track and intensity and plan evacuations, but it cannot predict every impact such as the death count. So option 4 is not a valid role.
The 2019 Arabian Sea storms were Vayu, Hikka, Kyarr, Maha and Pavan. Pabuk, Bulbul and Fani were Bay of Bengal systems, so the other options are wrong.

The exosphere is the outermost layer and merges into space, so the atmosphere has no sharp upper limit but gets progressively thinner until it becomes imperceptible. It does not thicken with height, which rules out options 3 and 4.
The troposphere begins at the surface (0 km) and is the lowest layer, where weather occurs. The exosphere, thermosphere and mesosphere lie far above it.
The ozone layer lies mainly in the lower stratosphere, about 15-30 km up, where ozone absorbs UV. The troposphere holds only about 10% of ozone.
The mesosphere is the coldest layer, with temperature falling to about -100°C. The stratosphere and thermosphere are warmer because temperature rises in them.

The troposphere extends only to about 8-18 km (average 13 km). The stratosphere reaches 50 km, the mesosphere 50-80 km, and the thermosphere begins at 80 km and extends far higher, so the troposphere is the thinnest.
The upward order is troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, i.e. II, III, I, IV.
The layers are defined by how temperature changes with height: it falls, rises, falls and rises again. It is not defined by wind, humidity or pressure.

AABY covers the head or one earning member of a rural landless household, so statement I is correct. The notes give the age band as 18-59, so the 30-65 in statement II is wrong. Statement III on scholarships for children is correct but is not covered in the notes, so the answer is I and III.
Uttar Pradesh borders Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand but not Punjab, so II, III and IV are correct.
Puducherry has units on both coasts: Mahe lies on the Arabian Sea coast in Kerala, while Puducherry, Karaikal and Yanam lie on the Bay of Bengal coast.
Puducherry's four districts (Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam) are separated, lying within Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh, so they do not touch each other.
Among the options, Delhi (about 1,483 sq km) is larger than Puducherry (490), Chandigarh (114) and Daman and Diu (111), so it is the largest.
Puducherry's units lie within Tamil Nadu, Kerala (Mahe) and Andhra Pradesh (Yanam); none touches Karnataka.
Uttar Pradesh borders about nine states/UTs (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar), more than the other options.
Karnataka borders six states (Goa, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala), more than any other southern state.
Latur is a district city in Maharashtra, not in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat or Madhya Pradesh.
India's mean sea level is determined from tide-gauge observations at Chennai, which is the reference datum for national heights.
Jahanpanah, the fourth medieval city of Delhi, was built by Muhammad bin Tughluq, so option 3 is right; the notes do not state this fact.
Alauddin Masud Shah is the Slave ruler whose coins carried the name of the last Abbasid caliph of Baghdad. The notes do not mention this fact.
Balban took the title Zil-i-Ilahi (Shadow of God) to assert divine kingship. Din-i-Ilahi was Akbar's creed, and the other titles do not belong to Balban.
Sikandar-i-Sani (Second Alexander) was the title of Alauddin Khalji. Sikandar Lodi is the tempting wrong option, since he is known by the pen name Gulrukhi.
Qutbuddin Aibak was Muhammad Ghori's slave and commander, and he took over Ghori's Indian territories and became the first Sultan. The other options were rival governors, not heirs.
The last Tughlaq ruler was Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah (1394-1412). Firoz and Ghiyasuddin were earlier rulers.
Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in 1221 during Iltutmish's reign, chasing Jalaluddin Mangbarni, and Iltutmish refused the prince shelter.
Iltutmish was the first Sultan to shift his capital to Delhi; Aibak ruled from Lahore.
Pataliputra was the Magadha capital, not a Harappan site, whereas Kalibangan, Ropar and Lothal are all Harappan sites.
Kalibangan yielded a ploughed field. Great Bath-type finds belong to Mohenjodaro and the dockyard to Lothal, so those are not the answer.
An ivory scale was found at Lothal, so Lothal is the correct answer.
Rakhigarhi is the largest Harappan site in India; Dholavira is only the second largest.
Kalibangan is on the Ghaggar in Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan, not Fatehabad (Banawali), Kutch or Ahmedabad.
Notes give India's current-price PCI growth from 2016-17 to 2017-18 as 8.6%, so option (1) is right.
AP's per capita income in 1960 was ₹7,781, which is option (1).
Mehrgarh (c. 7000 BCE, Baluchistan) shows the first farming and domestication in the subcontinent, so it gives the earliest evidence of agriculture.
Dantidurga, the Rashtrakuta founder, performed the Hiranyagarbha ritual at Ujjain. Mayurasharma, Harishchandra and Harsha are not linked to it in these notes.
The monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora (Cave 16) was built by Krishna I. Amoghavarsha and Indra III are known for other achievements.
Krishna I built the rock-cut Shiva (Kailasa) temple at Ellora. It was not Krishna III, nor Dantidurga or Govinda III.
The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I, not Krishna III or the others.
At Takkolam (949) the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III with his allies defeated the Cholas under Parantaka I. So it was Cholas versus Rashtrakutas.
Madrid lies on the Meseta, the plateau of the Iberian Peninsula (Spain). Bucharest, Jamnagar and Singapore are not plateau cities.
The Brazilian Plateau is rich in minerals and is called the storehouse of minerals of South America. The notes give that title to Patagonia, so they do not support this answer and no line is linked.
The Sonoran Desert is a hot desert lying in the USA and Mexico. The other options pair countries that do not contain it.

Sustainable development aims to balance economic, social and environmental goals, so its basic goal is equality and inclusive growth, not growth, environmental protection or industrial development alone.

The Green Revolution package (HYV seeds, fertiliser) depended on assured water, so its gains stayed confined to irrigated areas such as Punjab. Seeds and fertiliser were available more widely, so irrigation was the limiting factor.
Norman E. Borlaug, who developed Mexican dwarf wheats and won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize, is the father of the Green Revolution in the world.
Norman E. Borlaug is the father of the Green Revolution in the world (Nobel Peace Prize 1970); Swaminathan is the father of it in India.

M.S. Swaminathan coined the term 'Evergreen Revolution', meaning productivity gains in perpetuity without ecological harm. Borlaug is the world father of the Green Revolution, not the author of this term.
Subramaniam, Swaminathan and Borlaug are all linked with the Green Revolution, whereas Sardar Swaran Singh is not.
Urea is the most subsidised fertiliser, kept under statutory price control, whereas P and K come under NBS with fixed subsidy.
The notes do not state this fact. Balanced fertiliser use supplies nutrients in correct proportion and so corrects all deficiencies, rather than merely adding NPK.
Urea contains about 46% nitrogen; among the options 47% is the closest, and the others are far off.
The notes do not state this fact. Efficient fertiliser use means higher nutrient use efficiency, i.e. more crop produced per kg of fertiliser applied.
Urea dissolves easily and loses nitrogen through volatilisation and leaching, so slow-release forms such as briquettes are used. All the stated reasons apply.
Cotton fibres are seed hairs (trichomes) growing from the seed coat of the cotton boll, so the answer is seed.
Prakasam started the English daily Swarajya in 1921; Kesari is not his paper (Andhra Kesari is only his title), and the other options are unrelated.
Andhra Bank was founded in 1923 at Machilipatnam by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya (B.P. Sitaramayya), so option 2 is right; Prakasam and Konda were other Andhra leaders but not its founders.
Andhra Bank was founded in 1923 at Machilipatnam by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya (B.P. Sitaramayya), so option 2 is right; Prakasam and Konda were other Andhra leaders but not its founders.

Reform movements began in Bengal, with Rammohan Roy's Brahmo Samaj and later Derozio's Young Bengal, so Bengal is correct. The notes mention Bengal bodies but never state that reform movements started there.
Akbar was unlettered, though a great patron of learning; the other three emperors were literate.
Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur (Gurdaspur, Punjab) on 14 February 1556 after Humayun's death.
Bairam Khan's regency lasted 1556-60; 1560-64 was the petticoat government of Maham Anaga and Adham Khan.
Bengal (with Bihar merged) was annexed in 1576 after Daud Khan Karrani was defeated.
Akbar's empire extended from Bengal to Afghanistan and Kashmir to the Godavari; Khandesh, Kabul and Kashmir were conquered, but Bijapur was not annexed until Aurangzeb.
Rani Durgavati of Gondwana resisted Akbar's conquest in 1564, so she was his contemporary; the others belong to later centuries.
Jaswant Singh of Marwar belonged to Shah Jahan's reign, whereas Man Singh, Amar Singh and Udai Singh were Akbar's contemporaries.
The first Rajput marriage alliance of Akbar (1562) was with the Kachhwaha house of Amber, through Raja Bharmal's daughter.
Satyamev Jayate is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad (Mundakopanishad), not the Rig Veda, Gita or Matsya Purana. The notes do not cover this fact.
Resistivity (ρ = RA/l) is a property of the material, not of the wire's length or cross-section area, so statement 3 is incorrect. The other statements are standard facts.
A bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria (phage = 'eater' of bacteria). The option describing a bacterium-infecting virus is the right one; the others wrongly call it a bacterium.
The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is about 25 cm, so 25 cm is correct.
Geitonogamy is pollen transfer from the anther to the stigma of a different flower on the same plant. Autogamy occurs within the same flower and xenogamy between flowers of different plants.
Calorie, erg and joule are units of heat/energy, whereas centigrade is a temperature scale, not a unit of heat.
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis, and the rough endoplasmic reticulum, which carries ribosomes, helps synthesise and process proteins. So ER and ribosome is correct.

All three statements are correct definitions: homologous organs share origin but may differ in function, analogous organs differ in origin but are similar in function, and vestigial organs are reduced, non-functional remnants.
As temperature rises, molecules of a liquid gain kinetic energy and intermolecular cohesive forces weaken, so viscosity decreases. (In gases viscosity increases.)
The amnion encloses the embryo in amniotic fluid, protecting it from desiccation and shock. Allantois handles excretion/respiration, chorion is the outer membrane, and the yolk sac holds nutrients.
The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad, flat, green part of the leaf where photosynthesis mainly occurs; the midrib is the central vein and the petiole is the stalk.
The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad, flat, green part of the leaf; the petiole is the stalk and the midrib and veins are the supporting and conducting structures.
Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms (adults show pentamerous radial symmetry) are radially symmetrical, and sponges are mostly asymmetrical, so both statements are correct.
A cross symbol is the standard sign for first aid, not for a hospital, crossroad or no parking.
Ants are social insects because they live in organised colonies with division of labour (queen, workers, soldiers).
Pure gold is 24 carat, so 14 carat gold has 14/24 ≈ 58.3% gold. This is consistent with 22 carat = 91.6% and 18 carat = 75%.
Lake Gatun is part of the Panama Canal, not the Suez Canal. The Suez Canal passes through Lake Timsah and the Great and Little Bitter Lakes.
The Ludwigs Canal is an inland waterway in southern Germany. The Volga-Don is in Russia and the Sault-Sainte Marie is in Canada.
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) first proposed the three-tier structure of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad. Ashok Mehta later proposed a two-tier system.
The Gram Panchayat is a PRI, and the Gram Sabha is part of the village-level set-up. A Gram Cooperative Society is a cooperative body, not a Panchayati Raj institution.
The Panchayati Raj system has three tiers: village (Gram Panchayat), block (Panchayat Samiti) and district (Zila Parishad).
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee first used the term democratic decentralisation, later known as Panchayati Raj. Ashok Mehta came later and is not the source of the decentralisation idea.
The BRM Committee recommended three tiers at village, block and district levels. The two-tier model with a Mandal level is Ashok Mehta's.
BRM recommended a three-tier system, while Ashok Mehta recommended two tiers.

The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee report of 1957 recommended democratic decentralisation, which became Panchayati Raj. The other options are colonial-era Acts or missions, not the source of Panchayati Raj.
Balwantrai G. Mehta chaired the committee that proposed democratic decentralisation, later known as Panchayati Raj.
Democratic decentralisation was first recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee. Ashok Mehta recommended a later two-tier model.
Rajasthan was the first State to introduce Panchayati Raj, on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur. The other States listed were not first.
The name Panchayati Raj is credited to M.K. Gandhi, linked to his idea of Gram Swaraj. Nehru inaugurated the system, but the name is Gandhi's.
Panchayati Raj was first introduced on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur, Rajasthan, and inaugurated by Nehru. The other dates and places are incorrect.
Nehru inaugurated the first Panchayati Raj at Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959. Sikar, Sabarmati and Wardha were not the venue.
The Fifth Schedule (Art. 244(1)) covers Scheduled Areas and the Scheduled Tribes living in them, so STs reside in 'Scheduled areas'. The other options are not constitutional terms.
Article 244(1) makes the Fifth Schedule applicable to Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. Article 244(2) relates to the Sixth Schedule (Tribal Areas), so it is the tempting wrong option.

Under Para 5 the Governor may direct that any Act of Parliament or the State Legislature does not apply to a Scheduled Area, or applies with modifications. So the statement that the Governor is not authorised to do so is the incorrect one.
The Tribes Advisory Council under Para 4 of the Fifth Schedule has not more than 20 members, so 'Upto 20' is correct.
The President declares Scheduled Areas by Order and can increase, decrease, alter boundaries or rescind them. The Governor only advises and reports; he does not alter boundaries.
Under Para 5 of the Fifth Schedule the Governor makes regulations for the peace and good government of a Scheduled Area, after consulting the TAC and with the President's assent.
After consulting the Tribes Advisory Council, the Governor can direct that Acts do not apply or apply with modifications in Scheduled Areas. So the Governor is the authority.
Shivanasamudra is a hydel project on the Cauvery in Karnataka, not Kerala, so this pair is wrong. The other pairs (Jawahar Sagar–Rajasthan, Nagarjuna Sagar–AP, Gandhi Sagar–MP) are correct.
Bhakra-Nangal is a joint project of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, which receive its water (HP also benefits as the dam site, but the option with HP, Punjab, Haryana omits Rajasthan). Hence option 3.
Hirakud on the Mahanadi has a main dam of 4,801 m, making it the longest dam in India; Bhakra and Nagarjuna Sagar are much shorter in length.
Sardar Sarovar has four partner states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. Hence option 1.
DVC is a statutory corporation set up in 1948 and jointly run by the Central Government and the governments of West Bengal and Jharkhand (formerly Bihar), so option 3 is right.
Malampuzha dam is in Palakkad, Kerala, and is built on the Malampuzha river, a tributary of the Bharathapuzha. Hence option 3.
Aliyar (Tamil Nadu), Isapur (Maharashtra) and Kangsabati (West Bengal) are all water reservoirs/dams, not uranium sites, forests or caves.
The Kukadi irrigation project is on the Kukadi river, a tributary of the Ghod/Bhima, in Maharashtra (Pune and Ahmednagar districts).
The nucleolus is the site where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosomes are assembled; the Golgi bodies, ER and plasma membrane do not form ribosomes.
By the OIL RIG rule oxidation is loss (of electrons, and of hydrogen), so loss of hydrogen is oxidation, not reduction.
By OIL RIG, oxidation is electron loss, so gain of electrons is reduction.
Loss of oxygen from a substance is reduction, the opposite of oxidation (gain of oxygen); corrosion is a different process.
In electroplating the object to be plated (the spoon) is made the cathode and the plating metal (pure nickel) is the anode, so nickel dissolves from the anode and deposits on the spoon.
The energy needed to remove the electron from hydrogen's ground state is 13.6 eV (electron-volts), not MeV or J.
Creating something from nothing would violate the law of conservation of mass-energy, which says mass-energy can be neither created nor destroyed.
Kirchhoff's loop rule says the net energy gained and lost by a charge around a closed loop is zero, which is conservation of energy.
Violet light has the shortest wavelength and highest refractive index in glass, so it bends (deviates) the most in a prism; red deviates the least.
Syngamy is the fusion of gametes, a feature of sexual reproduction; budding, gemmulation and fragmentation are asexual methods.
Paramecium is a unicellular protozoan; fungi (mostly), Spirogyra and Hydra are multicellular.
Collenchyma has cell corners thickened with cellulose and pectin, giving flexible support; lignin is characteristic of sclerenchyma.
n-Butane and isobutane share the formula C4H10 but differ in carbon chain (straight vs branched), so they are chain isomers.
Active transport moves a substance against its concentration gradient using energy (ATP) from respiration; movement along the gradient or without energy is diffusion or passive transport.
Plants prepare their food by photosynthesis, using light, CO2 and water in chlorophyll-containing cells.
Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll; mitochondria are for respiration.
A grasshopper's hearing organs (tympanum) are on the sides of the first abdominal segment, i.e. the abdomen, which fits 'stomach' among the options.
Apical meristems at the tips of stems and roots cause increase in length (primary growth); lateral meristem increases girth.
The first law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, which is the law of conservation of energy applied to heat and work.
The Kelvin-Clausius statement that heat cannot flow spontaneously from cold to hot body is the Second Law of Thermodynamics.
Al-Biruni, scholar at Mahmud of Ghazni's court, wrote Kitab-ul-Hind. Hasan Nizami and Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote other chronicles (Taj-ul-Maasir, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri).
Al-Biruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni and described 11th-century India, so he came in the 11th century CE (Mahmud's raids were 1000-1027).
Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Ghori at the First Battle of Tarain (1191). Chandawar (1194) was Ghori's victory over Jaichand.
At Chandawar in 1194 Ghori defeated Jaichand (Jayachandra) of Kannauj, the Gahadavala king.
Chandawar (1194) was Ghori's victory over Jayachandra (Jaichand) of Kannauj; Prithviraj was defeated at Tarain II, not Chandawar.
Prithviraj Chauhan is Prithviraja III, the Chahamana ruler of Ajmer who fought at Tarain.
Ghori's first defeat (1178) was at the hands of the Gujarat Chaulukya/Solanki ruler Mularaja II (Bhimdev II), the 'Baghel Bhim' of the options, not Prithviraj, who beat him in 1191 but lost in 1192.
Prithviraj won the First Battle of Tarain (1191); Ghori won the second (1192) and Chandawar (1194).
The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191, with Prithviraj winning; the second was in 1192.
The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was fought between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan; Ghori won.
Muhammad Ghori won the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, which opened North India. Mahmud of Ghazni only raided.
The Second Battle of Tarain (1192) was the turning point: Ghori's victory opened North India to Turkish rule.
Ghori's first defeat came in 1178 in Gujarat at the hands of Mularaja II (Bhimdev II), a Chaulukya/Solanki ruler, near Mount Abu, before his Tarain battles with Prithviraj.

The notes do not discuss the constraints on raising Seed Replacement Rates. Only statement III is correct: there is a demand-supply gap in quality seed for low-value, high-volume crops. Statements I and II are wrong because a National Seed Policy exists and private companies do supply vegetable and horticultural seed.
The notes do not mention the Indian Seed Congress 2017. The theme of that event was 'Seed of Joy'.

A seed village gives farmers foundation seed so they produce certified seed locally, making quality seed available to others at the right time and an affordable cost. It does not reserve villages exclusively for certified seed or discourage buying seed from others.
Labour-saving mechanisation is a rational response to rising wages and a tighter labour market, since machines replace costlier, scarcer labour. The notes do not state this link.
The notes do not mention the Zero Till Seed-cum-Fertiliser Drill. It was developed at GB Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar.
The National Academy of Agricultural Research Management (NAARM), established in 1976, is located in Hyderabad.

Public investment means capital formation such as cold storage and PACS computerisation, together with education and training, which covers social capital. MSP is price support, and free electricity and loan waivers are subsidies, so none of these is public investment. Hence II, III and VI are correct.
The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier if necessary (Art. 280(1)), so the answer is 5 years.

Only (i) is true: the FC has 5 members. A High Court judge is only one possible qualification, not mandatory; members are eligible for reappointment; and the first Chairman was K.C. Neogy, not K. Santhanam.
The main function of the Finance Commission is to decide the share of States in central taxes. It exercises no financial control over the Centre or States.
The FC is constituted about every fifth year to recommend distribution of net tax proceeds between the Centre and States, so option 4 is right.
Options 1-3 are the functions under Art. 280(3). Maintaining income and expenditure details of governments is not an FC function; it only recommends.

The Finance Commission recommends distribution of tax proceeds between the Centre and States, which is why it is the body linked to sharing of taxes with States. The other bodies do not have this function.
10th FC was chaired by K.C. Pant, 11th by A.M. Khusro, 12th by C. Rangarajan and 13th by Vijay Kelkar, giving a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III.
Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th Finance Commission (2015-20). C. Rangarajan chaired the 12th.

A digital signature shows the content is unaltered (statement III is correct). A record naming the issuing CA is a digital certificate, not a signature, so I is wrong. Statement II is wrong because proof of identity is not what the signature note describes.
The IT Act, 2000 gave legal recognition to e-commerce transactions and electronic records, making it India's first cyber law. The other years listed are not the year of enactment.
Sanauli (Baghpat, UP) is known for a large cemetery of human burials, so option 1 is correct; it did not yield animal burials or a residential building.

Harappan burials were extended with the head generally north, and grave goods such as pottery and ornaments were buried with the dead. Both a and b are therefore correct; sitting-posture burial is not attested.
Harshacharita was written by Banabhatta, not Harshavardhana. The notes confirm that Brihatkatha is by Gunadhya and the Gathasaptasati is by Hala, so those pairs are right.
The notes state that the Satavahanas made the first tax-free land grants (agraharas) to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks. The Parthians, Kushanas and Shakas are not credited with this.
The Nasik inscription of Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta) records 2,000 karshapanas deposited with the Govardhana weavers' guild. The Sopara, Kanheri and Pratishthana records are not the source for this.

Socialism aims at reducing inequalities of income and wealth and ensuring a fair distribution of resources, i.e. distributive justice (Art. 38 and 39(b),(c)); the other options are not types of justice linked to socialism.
The 11th Plan's theme was 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth', making inclusive growth its core concept.
The 11th Plan was the first to make inclusive growth its objective, so inclusive growth is the answer.
The 11th Plan's theme was 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'; the other options are not its theme.
The 12th Plan's theme was 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth', which is option 4.
The 12th Plan's theme was 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'; the other options give incomplete or altered versions.
The 11th Plan's theme was 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth', which matches option 3.

The 11th Plan's inclusive growth components were agricultural growth, employment and poverty reduction, reducing regional disparities and equitable growth. Strengthening the capital market is not among them.
The 12th Plan's theme was 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth', which best states its vision.

The LPG (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) model stresses opening up to the private sector, de-licensing and abolishing MRTP controls. Employment growth for the poorest is not its emphasis.
Perth has a Mediterranean climate (warm dry summer, mild wet winter), not a steppe climate. Pretoria (veld), Saskatchewan (prairie) and Buenos Aires (pampas) lie in temperate grassland regions.
Vertisols (black cotton soils) form in tropical grasslands/savanna-type regions with seasonal rain, not in temperate grasslands, tundra or deserts.
Steppes of Eurasia separate Cold Asia from Dry Asia; Pampas, Veld and Prairie are in other continents.
Verkhoyansk (Siberia) recorded -67.8°C in 1892 and is known as the Cold Pole of the inhabited world; Antarctica is the coldest place overall but is not called the Cold Pole in this sense.
Death Valley (Furnace Creek) lies in California, USA, and is the lowest point in North America.
Eskimos (Inuit) are a Mongoloid people of the Arctic tundra. Bantu is an African language group, while Nordic and Alpine are European (Caucasoid) sub-races.
The Masai are cattle pastoralists of the Kenya and Tanzania savanna, not of steppes, veld or downs.
The amendment procedure (Art. 368) comes from South Africa, not France, so the statement is incorrect.
The USA has the world's first written Constitution, which is why the written Constitution is linked to the US.
The GoI Act 1935 is the single largest textual source of the Constitution, supplying its structure and administrative details, so it is the answer here rather than the British Constitution.
The cabinet system comes from Britain. The President's election is from Ireland and the DPSP from Ireland, so those options are wrong.
The cabinet system comes from Britain. The President's election is from Ireland and the DPSP from Ireland, so those options are wrong.
Prerogative writs (petitions) and bicameralism both come from Britain (the United Kingdom).
Fundamental Rights (Part III) were borrowed from the USA.
Fundamental Rights (Part III) were borrowed from the USA (America).
Judicial review is a US feature adopted by India, so the USA is its origin.
The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from the USA. Only the language of the Preamble is from Australia.
Indian federalism is based on the Canadian pattern, a Union of States with a strong Centre.
A federation with a strong Centre was borrowed from Canada.
The Concurrent List was borrowed from Australia. The makers followed the Canadian division of powers but added this third list.
Residuary powers with the Centre come from Canada. In the USA they lie with the States, so the USA is wrong.
The Jhelum (Vitasta) rises from a spring at Verinag at the foot of the Pir Panjal. The Chenab, Beas and Sutlej have different sources.
Mahanadi is a peninsular river that drains to the Bay of Bengal and is not an Indus tributary. Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi are Indus system rivers.
The Indus flows through north-western India and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea near Karachi. The other rivers do not flow through Pakistan.
From north to south the order is Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej. So among the four given, II, I, III, IV is correct.
The Indus river dolphin survives in the Beas (Punjab) in India, and the notes do not cover this.
Beas, Ravi and Chenab are Indus system tributaries. Tawi is not among the Indus tributaries listed in the notes, so it is the answer.
The notes do not give the positions of Shyok, Zaskar and Spiti. Shyok is the northernmost, then Zaskar, then Spiti, and the Sutlej is the southernmost.
Y.B. Chavan was the first LoP under the 1977 statute, and the APPSC key gave him as the answer. Ram Subhag Singh was recognised earlier, in 1969, but he is not among the options.
Surface tension explains the meniscus shape, capillary rise and spherical mercury drops. Vapour formation is evaporation, which is a separate process and not a result of surface tension.
Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy as heat and ATP, so it is an exothermic process.
Mass measures inertia, which is a property of the body that does not change with place. Weight varies with location but mass does not.
SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. It uses ultrasound echoes to detect and locate objects underwater.
Shortest wavelength means the largest energy gap. The n=2 to n=1 transition has the biggest gap among the options, so it emits the shortest wavelength.
Ultraviolet has a shorter wavelength than visible light, so its photon energy is higher. Statement 4 says it is lower, so it is the incorrect one.
The Lyman series involves transitions to n=1, which emit high-energy photons in the ultraviolet region.
All photons travel at the speed of light in vacuum, whatever their energy. So the claim that the two speeds differ is wrong.
Weight is the gravitational force with which the earth attracts a body towards its centre. It varies with location and can be measured in ways other than a spring balance.
At the centre of the Earth, g is zero because the attractions cancel out, so the weight is zero.
The moon's gravity is about one sixth of the earth's, so weight on the moon is 1/6th of that on earth.
A Barr body is an inactivated X chromosome. Turner syndrome (XO) has only one X, so it has no Barr body.
The king cobra is ophiophagous, feeding mainly on other snakes.
The king cobra is the only snake that builds a nest for its eggs.
Candela is the unit of luminous intensity, so it is not related to sound. Hertz (frequency), decibel (loudness) and Mach (speed relative to sound) are all linked to sound.
Mach number is the ratio of a body's speed to the speed of sound. A value above 1 means the speed is supersonic.
Hydrofluoric acid reacts with the silica in glass to form silicon tetrafluoride, so it dissolves glass. The other acids do not.
Frequency is set by the source and does not change on entering a new medium. Velocity and wavelength change instead.
Work and energy both have the dimensions ML²T⁻². Power has different dimensions.
A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom, so the molecule is the same as the atom, as in noble gases.
Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from Penicillium notatum. Streptomycin was found by Waksman, so option 3 is wrong.
Antibiotics act only on bacteria; viral infections such as measles cannot be cured by antibiotics.
Penicillin comes from the fungus Penicillium notatum, so the agent group is fungi.

Antibiotics work by targeting bacterial metabolic pathways and structures, which viruses lack, so they cannot act on viruses. Option 4 is wrong since viruses are not resistant, they are simply not targeted.
The DPT (triple antigen) vaccine protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus. Polio and smallpox are not part of it.
BCG vaccine prevents tuberculosis (TB).
The triple antigen (DPT) covers diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus; polio and smallpox are not included.
Triple antigen is the DPT vaccine, which prevents diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus. It is not a mixture of live disease-causing viruses.
Leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is spread by the sandfly, not a mosquito. Chikungunya, dengue and malaria are all mosquito-borne.
The listed stages are energy source, interaction with target, recording, transmission/processing, interpretation and application. 'Interaction of Energy with Minimisation' is not a component.
Remote sensing supports glacial lake monitoring, forest fire (wildfire) response and wind/cyclone tracking. 'Hills management' is not a listed disaster application.
Within visible light, violet has the shortest wavelength and red the longest, so violet is correct.
Wavelength falls in the order radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays. Infrared therefore has a longer wavelength than red, violet and X-rays.
Volcanic heat is emitted thermal infrared radiation, so infrared-sensitive sensors capture it. Visible or UV sensors do not record heat.
The official key gave Visible for this question, so follow it. In principle microwave SAR penetrates cloud, but the key answer is Visible.

NDVI from red and near-infrared reflectance gives vegetation health (chlorophyll), and thermal infrared gives land surface temperature. Remote-sensing data is also used to estimate paddy greenhouse-gas emissions, so all three are correct.
IRS satellites are used for crop productivity, groundwater and mineral exploration, not telecommunications or traffic studies. So I, II and III is correct.
EOS-03 was the earlier GISAT-1, the geo-imaging satellite. EOS-04 is RISAT-1A, EOS-05 is GISAT-1A and EOS-06 is Oceansat-3.
Cartosat-1 (2005) was India's first mapping satellite, giving stereo images for 3D maps.
SCATSAT-1 is a scatterometer satellite giving ocean wind vectors and cyclone tracking, which is weather monitoring. It is not for communication, navigation or crop monitoring.
Modhera Sun temple, built by Bhima I of the Solankis, is in Mehsana district, Gujarat. Dakshinark and Konark are in Odisha and Martand is in Kashmir.
The Khajuraho group (950-1050 CE) was built by the Chandelas, not the Paramaras or the others listed.
The Konark Sun temple in Odisha was built by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. The Pulakeshins were Chalukyas of Badami, so they are wrong.
The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandelas of Bundelkhand, not by the Holkars, Scindias or Bundelas.
The Khajuraho group was built by the Chandelas in 950-1050 CE.
Konark temple in Odisha is the Sun temple. Lingaraj and Rajarani are Shaiva temples in Bhubaneswar and Jagannath is a Vishnu temple.
The Dilwara temples (Vimal Vasahi and Luna Vasahi) are Jain temples at Mount Abu in the Aravalli hills, Rajasthan.
The Chandelas built the Khajuraho temples. Sanchi, Ujjain and Gwalior are not Chandela works.
Vijaya Stambha at Chittor was built by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
The notes do not cover Nahargarh Fort. It was built by Sawai Jai Singh II in 1734.
The Kirti-Stambha Prashasti was composed by the praise-poets Atri and Mahesh (Atri Kavi). Jaita only oversaw the work.
Alha Khand was composed by Jagnik at the court of Chandela Paramardi. Parmardidev was the king it celebrates, not its author.
Prithviraj Raso was written by Chand Bardai about Prithviraj Chauhan. Jayanaka wrote Prithviraja Vijaya.
The notes do not mention MODVAT. MODVAT (modified value added tax on inputs) was introduced in the 1986 budget following the long-term fiscal policy, so it is the correct option over CENVAT or VAT.

Fiscal policy objectives are growth, equitable (distributive) distribution, full employment and price stability. Of the options, price stability is the one that completes the list; reduction of inequalities duplicates distributive justice.
The notes do not list exchange stabilisation as an objective. Fiscal policy objectives are employment, price stability, growth and equity, while exchange stabilisation points to monetary policy.
Price stability (controlling inflation) is a stated objective of fiscal policy and its stabilisation function. Debt, tax and trade policy are not listed as having this aim.
Zero-based budgeting means every item is justified afresh with no base from last year, which is the critical review stated in R. It has been introduced in India, so both are true and R explains A.

Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts, so it is the excess of total expenditure over receipts. Revenue deficit compares only revenue expenditure with revenue receipts.
Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus all receipts other than borrowings, so it equals borrowings and other liabilities. Gross primary deficit further subtracts interest payments.
Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments, so option 3 is correct. The other options describe different measures.
Isotopes share the same atomic number (protons) but differ in mass number because their neutron counts differ.
Lead is not a nuclear fuel, whereas uranium and plutonium are fissile and thorium is fertile and can be bred into U-233.
Alpha particles are helium nuclei made of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, so a helium nucleus has two protons and two neutrons.
In heavy water (D2O) deuterium, an isotope of hydrogen, takes the place of ordinary hydrogen.
Pulakesin II of the Badami Chalukyas stopped Harsha on the Narmada (618 CE) and took the title Paramesvara. Pulakesin I is the tempting wrong option, as he was not the victor over Harsha.
The Simon Commission came to India in 1928 (arriving at Bombay on 3 Feb 1928), so 1928 is correct.
The Simon Commission came to India in 1928 (arriving at Bombay on 3 Feb 1928), so 1928 is correct.
Tanguturi Prakasam led the anti-Simon procession at Madras in 1928, so 1928 is correct.
The Nehru Report committee was chaired by Motilal Nehru (Jawaharlal was secretary), and its subject was constitutional arrangements for India.
The Nehru Report recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates, so option 2 was not its recommendation.
The Nehru Report, India's reply to the Simon Commission, was the first Indian effort at drafting a constitution on dominion status, so the Simon Commission is the answer.
The Nehru Report (1928) recommended fundamental rights, which makes option 1 correct.
The Report sought dominion status, not complete independence, so I is wrong. It recommended joint electorates with reserved seats and fundamental rights, so II and III are correct.
Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (ECCE) falls under Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, so its Union Minister launched it.
Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (ECCE) falls under Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, so its Union Minister launched it.
