BBBP aims to arrest the decline in Child Sex Ratio and ensure girls' survival, protection and education, which covers empowerment and reducing gender inequality. It does not provide legal aid, so statement I is wrong and the answer is II, III and IV.
BBBP is a PM flagship along with Make in India and Digital India, whereas Antyodaya Yojana is not one of them.
Ujjwala Yojana gives free LPG connections in women's names to BPL households. The other options are unrelated to it.
Ujjwala Yojana provides free LPG connections to BPL households, in women's names, which ends indoor smoke and improves health.
Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was set up in 1993 as a registered society under MWCD. It lends to NGOs/MFIs that on-lend micro-credit to poor women.
Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was set up in 1993 as a registered society under MWCD. It lends to NGOs/MFIs that on-lend micro-credit to poor women.
Mahila e-Haat is the 2016 online marketing platform of MWCD for women entrepreneurs and SHGs, run by RMK.
CBSE Udaan is not a scheme for girls' entry into medical colleges, so that pairing is wrong. The other pairings are correct.
The Aravalli is India's oldest range, about 570 million years old, so 570 million years is correct.
An anticline is an up-arch fold, whereas a syncline is a down-trough; a graben is a faulted block, not a fold.
With rising pressure, folds progress from overturned to recumbent, where the limbs lie horizontal and parallel. An overturned fold is still tilted.
The Narmada flows in a rift valley formed by faulting between the Vindhyas and Satpuras, so its valley is structural in origin, not volcanic, glacial or aeolian.
The Narmada flows west because it occupies a rift valley (a fault trough), so only I is the cause. Flowing between the Vindhyas and Satpuras describes the rift's location, not the reason.

Namdev (1270) came first, then Kabir, then Nanak (1469) and Mirabai (1498). The code II, I, III, IV is the option that places Namdev first, then Kabir, then Mirabai and Nanak as the given order of the list, which is the best match.
Mirabai was a contemporary of Guru Nanak, and Ramdas lived in Shivaji's age as his guru, so both statements are correct.
The notes do not state where Malukdas lived. He was a Bhakti saint poet of Kada (near Prayagraj), which is why (4) is correct.
Mirabai was married to Rajkumar Bhojraj, the Mewar prince and son of Rana Sanga. Rana Sanga was his father, so he is not the husband.
Tulsidas (1532-1623) lived in the reigns of Akbar and Jahangir, so (1) is correct. Babur and Humayun were too early, and Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb too late for most of his career.
Vallabhacharya = Gujarat, Tulsidas = Uttar Pradesh, Chaitanya = Bengal, Tukaram = Maharashtra, matching A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.
The Bijak, a collection of dohas and sakhis, is the main text of the Kabirpanthis and was composed by Kabir. Surdas wrote the Sursagar.
Kabir condemned rituals and idol worship of both Hindus and Muslims, so the statement that he was not against idol worship is incorrect and is the answer.
Guru Nanak founded the Sikh religion in the time of Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517), so he was his contemporary.
The Sikh religion was founded in the time of Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517), during Guru Nanak's lifetime.
The quote 'God knows man's virtues and inquires not his caste' is attributed to Guru Nanak, who also started the caste-free Guru Ka Langar.
Rajasthani is not among the 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule (English and Bhojpuri are also excluded), while Gujarati, Kashmiri and Dogri are included.
The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages and now has 22, so option 1 is correct.
Demands to include a language in the list of scheduled languages concern the Eighth Schedule, which lists the recognised languages (14 originally, now 22).
Demands to include a language in the list of scheduled languages concern the Eighth Schedule, which lists the recognised languages (14 originally, now 22).
Article 324 provides for the Election Commission (Part XV); Arts. 320-321 and 326 deal with other matters (PSC functions, adult suffrage).
Article 371 and the series 371A-371J in Part XXI make special provisions for particular States; Art. 370 dealt with J&K and is now abrogated.
Article 371J (98th Amendment, 2012) gives special provisions to the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka.
Article 371B makes a special provision for Assam (an Assembly committee of members from tribal areas); Nagaland is 371A and Manipur is 371C.
Article 371 provides development boards for Maharashtra and Gujarat (Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra, Kutch).
Urea, the nitrogenous fertiliser, promotes vegetative growth in wheat and most crops, so nitrogen is the fertiliser used for wheat.

The notes do not say which form of nitrogen is preferred for paddy and potato. Ammoniacal nitrogen is preferred because it is retained in the soil, and nitrate is easily leached and lost in flooded paddy.
Urea, CO(NH2)2, supplies nitrogen in the amide form. It is converted to ammoniacal and then nitrate nitrogen in the soil.
Urea has about 46% N, which is higher than DAP at 18% N. Ammonium nitrate (about 34%) and potassium nitrate (about 13%) are also lower.
Biochar is part of the growing medium in vertical farming and helps nitrogen-fixing microorganisms. It also retains water and nutrients, so all three statements are correct.
The notes give no NPK ratio for legumes. Legumes fix their own nitrogen, so they need less N and more P and K, which fits the 1:2:2 ratio.
Balanced fertiliser use raises production, improves fertiliser use efficiency and maintains soil productivity, so all the options are correct.
Green manure is a green, undecomposed crop, preferably a legume, that is ploughed in. Of the options, decomposing green legume plants fits best.
Magnesium is a macronutrient (secondary nutrient) needed in larger amounts. Iron, manganese and copper are micronutrients.
A lichen is a symbiotic association of an alga (chlorophyll-containing, photosynthetic partner) and a fungus.

Azotobacter is a nitrogen-fixing biofertiliser (I is correct), and biofertilisers are used alongside organic manures (IV is correct). They are applied to seed or soil, not only to leaves, and they do not alter the soil's chemical composition.
Rhizobium, Azolla and blue-green algae are all listed as biofertilisers, so all of the above is correct.
Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen in root nodules through symbiotic Rhizobium. Wheat, coffee and rubber do not.
Blue-green algae fix nitrogen in paddy fields, so paddy is the crop they supply with nitrogen.
Azolla is a water fern that works with the cyanobacterium Anabaena and is used as a biofertiliser.
Subhas Chandra Bose published "The Indian Struggle" in 1935, his account of the national movement, so (3) is correct. The other options are not its author.
The Proclamation aimed to disclaim annexation of Indian States and to place the administration under the Crown. Regulating the Company's trade was not an object, so statement III is wrong.

The 1858 announcement (Queen's Proclamation) restored the right of childless rulers to adopt heirs, with Canning withdrawing the Doctrine of Lapse. The 1858 Act only transferred power to the Crown, so option 1 is wrong.
After 1857 recruitment shifted to Gurkhas, Sikhs and Pathans (Punjab, NWFP), who had stayed loyal, rather than Awadh and Bihar.
Article 37 says DPSPs are not enforceable by any court, yet the State has a duty to apply them in making laws. So statements II and III are correct and I is wrong.

DPSPs are guidelines for the State in making laws and are not enforceable. They impose no legal duty and so are not limitations on the legislative or executive function, so neither statement is correct.

DPSPs are guidelines for the State in making laws and are not enforceable. They impose no legal duty and so are not limitations on the legislative or executive function, so neither statement is correct.
Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government. Article 38 is about social order and Article 39 about principles of policy.
Free legal aid (39A), maternity relief (42), living wage (43), safeguarding forests (48A) and protection of monuments (49) are all DPSPs, so all five are correct.

Promoting international trade is not a directive; Art. 51 covers international peace and security and respect for international law. Equal pay (39(d)), cow slaughter ban (48) and separation of judiciary (50) are DPSPs.
Plassey (Palashi) lies on the Bhagirathi in Nadia district of West Bengal, so Bengal is correct.
At Plassey (1757) Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah; Mir Jafar was a conspirator on Clive's side, not an opponent.
The Treaty of Alinagar (Feb 1757) was concluded by Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab then, who restored the Company's 1717 farman privileges.
Mir Qasim abolished all internal trade duties, putting Indian merchants on equal terms with the English; the other Nawabs did not.
Buxar was an open military victory over Bengal, Awadh and the Mughal emperor, and it confirmed Plassey; it is regarded as the most decisive battle, whereas Plassey was won by treachery.
The Company received the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1765 (order of 12 August 1765), so 1765 is correct.
Sufism originated in the Persia/Iran region of the Islamic world and later spread to India; the notes do not state this origin.
Ulema are scholars of Islamic religious law and not part of Sufism, whereas khanqah, shaikh and sama are all Sufi terms.
Pir (Murshid/Shaikh) means master or authorised guide, i.e. the teacher of Sufis, not God.
Silsila means order or chain of spiritual descent among Sufis. Chishti is one particular silsila and Auliya is only a title.
The successor nominated by a pir to carry on the order is called Khalifah (caliph). Pir is the master, murid the disciple and khanqah the hospice.
Pir/Sheikh is the teacher or guide (2), Murid is the disciple/student (1), Khalifa is the follower or successor (4), and Khanqah is the hospice (3), giving 2 1 4 3.
The ternary operator (?:) in C++ is the conditional operator, as it takes three operands and selects one of two expressions based on a condition.
Function overloading is resolved at compile time (static/early binding), because the compiler picks the function by its signature. Run-time resolution applies to virtual functions.
An assembler translates assembly language into machine code. A compiler translates high-level languages and an interpreter runs them line by line.
BASIC was developed in 1964 at Dartmouth College by John G. Kemeny and Thomas E. Kurtz. Ritchie created C and Grace Hopper worked on COBOL.
C is commonly used in embedded systems because it is efficient, close to the hardware and gives direct memory control. FORTRAN and COBOL target scientific and business use.
JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich at Netscape in 1995.

FORTRAN is used for scientific computation (physics and chemistry), COBOL for business and finance, C for system software and portable applications, and BASIC for education and non-science students. This gives A-4, B-1, C-3, D-2.
A 16-bit signed integer (as in classic C/C++ compilers) ranges from -32768 to +32767, i.e. -2^15 to 2^15-1.
Both statements are true: FORTRAN is an imperative language suited to numeric and scientific computing, and it is widely used in high-performance computing and supercomputers.
Both statements are false. COBOL is a procedural language for business use, not object-oriented. Numerical weather prediction and fluid dynamics are FORTRAN domains.
A bug is an error or flaw in a program that makes it produce wrong or unexpected results. A byte is a unit of data, not an error.

The notes say the aim of the three London conferences was to discuss the Simon report and a federal constitution, so option 1 is correct. The other options are outcomes or sub-issues, not the stated agenda.
The Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference (1930) because of the Civil Disobedience Movement. It attended only the 2nd RTC, so the statement that it attended the First is untrue.
Muhammad Iqbal is listed among those who attended the 2nd RTC, so he is the Urdu poet invited. The other poets are not mentioned as attendees.
Gandhi stayed at Kingsley Hall in London during the Second Round Table Conference, so option 2 is correct.
The notes say it was strictly one conference held in three sessions (1930-32), not three separate conferences, so option 4 is correct.
The Communal Award came in August 1932, not 1933, so option 4 is wrongly matched. The Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) and the Second RTC (1931) are correctly matched.
Under the 44th Amendment the President may return the Council of Ministers' advice once for reconsideration, after which he must act on it. So he can seek reconsideration before giving approval.
The notes say 'His Excellency' was dropped in 2012 and the form is now 'Rashtrapati ji' / 'Hon'ble President'. They do not support the keyed answer, so no line is linked.
K.R. Narayanan (1997) won about 95% of electoral-college votes, the record majority, against T.N. Seshan.
N. Sanjiva Reddy is the only President elected unopposed. Rajendra Prasad was elected twice, but with a contest.
M. Hidayatullah is the only CJI to have acted as President (20 July-24 August 1969). The other judges listed never did.
Zakir Husain was President from 1967 and was the first to die in office, in 1969, which gave him a very short tenure. The others served full 5-year terms.
V.V. Giri's trade union association is not stated in the notes, so no line is linked. He was the 4th President and a former AITUC chairman.
N. Sanjiva Reddy is the only President elected unopposed (unanimously). The others won contested elections.
The 1st session was at Bombay (1885), the 2nd at Calcutta (1886) and the 3rd at Madras (1887). The 4th was at Allahabad (1888), so the code is 4 3 2 1.
The 1905 Benares session of the INC was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, in the Swadeshi context.
The Lahore session of 1929, under Jawaharlal Nehru, declared Purna Swaraj as the goal. Karachi 1931 dealt with Fundamental Rights instead.
The Karachi session of 1931 (president Vallabhbhai Patel) adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.
Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'. Bonnerjee was the first president, not the GOM.
Gandhi presided in 1924 (Belgaum), Sarojini Naidu in 1925 (Kanpur), Nehru in 1929 (Lahore) and Patel in 1931 (Karachi). The order is I, IV, II, III.
Lord Dufferin described the Congress as representing only a "microscopic minority". The "tottering to its fall" remark is Curzon's, so Curzon is the tempting wrong option.
Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu upgrades government school infrastructure. Amma Vodi is a cash support to mothers, not an infrastructure programme.
Vidya Deevena is the fee reimbursement (RTF) scheme for post-matric students, so it covers college fees. Vidya Kanuka gives student kits and Nadu-Nedu upgrades school infrastructure.
Jagananna Amma Vodi (Jan 2020) gives ₹15,000 a year to the mother or guardian of a poor child. The other amounts match other schemes, such as ₹20,000 for Annadata Sukhibhava.

The APPSC key defines demographic dividend as a rise in economic growth due to a rise in the share of working people in the population, which is option 1. The other options describe different things, such as female work participation or a rising child population.
In the Quality of Life for Elderly Index released in August 2021 by Bibek Debroy, Rajasthan ranked first among the aged states. The other listed states did not rank first.
The 4th character of a PAN denotes the holder type, and P stands for an individual (C for a company). In AFZPK7190K the 4th character is P, so it is an individual.
DNA fingerprinting is based on inherited DNA polymorphism and is used for identity and paternity testing. Gene therapy, gene cloning and rDNA technology are not used to establish parentage.

Triticale is the first man-made cereal, produced by crossing wheat and rye. Dwarf wheat, hybrid maize and soybean are breeding products or not cereals, and none is a new cereal made by crossing two genera.
Dolly the sheep was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell (1996), so sheep is the answer. The other animals were cloned later.
Dolly the sheep (born 1996) was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, so sheep is correct.
Dolly was produced by SCNT, in which a somatic cell nucleus is transferred into an enucleated egg, so this is nuclear transfer. It was not IVF.
Dolly is listed as the first living cloned genetically engineered organism, so Dolly is the answer.
The first heart transplant was performed by Christian Barnard in South Africa.
Christian Barnard of South Africa performed the first heart transplant. William Harvey is known for blood circulation.
Sir Muhammad Iqbal is the one credited with this remark comparing Nehru and Jinnah; the notes do not state this fact.
This is Gandhi's well-known 'India of my dreams' passage, in which he describes an India where the poorest have an effective voice and all communities live in harmony.
The Swaraj Party (Swaraj Dal) was founded in 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru. Tilak and Gandhi were not its founders.

Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirts) in 1929, so option 1 is correct. The Ali Brothers and Ansari were associated with the Khilafat movement and the Congress, not this organisation.
The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1932. Gokhale died in 1915 and Ambedkar did not found it.
The Satya Shodhak Sabha was founded by Jyotiba Phule, not Tilak, so pair 4 is wrongly matched. Tilak was an Extremist leader associated with Swaraj and the Home Rule League.
AP ranked 1st in egg production in 2018-19, and its egg rank has stayed 1st in later years too. The 2nd rank in eggs came from the 2018 White Paper, which is the tempting wrong option.
Krishna topped milk production by district in September 2016 according to the key. Chittoor is the tempting option, but it is noted as the top dairy district in the Amul tie-up context.

AP partnered ICRISAT to transform agriculture, so option 1 is correct. The 25 growth engines claim is wrong, since the notes mention 17 growth engines, and the space sector mission is not an agriculture initiative.
AP contributed 36% of India's seafood export value by the end of 2018-19. The 31% and 75% figures relate to shrimp exports and cultured-shrimp exports respectively.
Jhum (Jhumming) is the shifting cultivation name in the North-East, including Assam. Podu is used in Andhra Pradesh and Bewar in Madhya Pradesh.
The notes list no 'Mashan' as a Himachal Pradesh shifting-cultivation name, so this match is wrong. Podu (Pondu) is Andhra/Odisha-type and Jhoom is Assam.
Ladang is Indonesia/Malaysia, Milpa is Mexico/Central America, Roca is Brazil and Masole is Central Africa. This gives A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.
Mixed farming combines crops and livestock on the same farm with equal weight. The other options describe shifting, subsistence and intensive farming.
Plantations are mostly in the humid tropics, so Statement I is true. Humid tropical soils are generally leached and not highly fertile, so Statement II is false.
Intensive subsistence farming is small-plot family farming for own consumption, so it is subsistence, not commercial. Dairy, grain and ranching are commercial types.
Large coffee plantations in Brazil are called fazendas, the Portuguese term for estates. Estancias are Argentine ranches and kolkhozes are Soviet collective farms.
Jupiter's faint ring system is made of fine dust particles, mainly silicates, not gases like oxygen, xenon or ozone. The notes only say Jupiter has rings, not their composition.

Mercury has the fastest orbit (88 days), so Mars is not the slowest-moving planet; the slowest are the outer planets like Neptune (164.9 years). The other pairs are correct: Jupiter is largest, Mercury smallest, Venus brightest.
The Blue Marble is the famous photograph of the whole Earth taken during Apollo 17, so it is an image of Earth, not of the Moon.
A total lunar eclipse turns the Moon reddish, so it is called a blood moon (as in July 2018). A blue moon is the second full moon in a month, a different thing.
Ibrahim Lodi (1517-26) was the last Lodi ruler and last Delhi Sultan; he was killed at Panipat in 1526.
Timur invaded India and sacked Delhi in December 1398, so 1398 AD is correct.

Khizr Khan, Timur's viceroy, ruled Delhi as Timur's deputy without the title of Sultan, so he accepted Timurid suzerainty (Shah Rukh being Timur's successor). The other Sultans listed were not Timur's deputies.
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and shifted the capital there from Delhi.
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and made it his capital, shifting it from Delhi.
Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504, not by Bahlul Lodi or earlier Sultans.
Gulrukhi was the pen name under which Sikandar Lodi wrote Persian poetry.
After winning at Panipat in 1526, Babur captured Delhi and Agra along with the Lodi treasure.
Autotrophs such as green plants get both their carbon (from CO2) and their energy (from sunlight) through photosynthesis. Transpiration, ingestion and osmosis do not supply carbon and energy.
Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, using sunlight to build organic matter. Osmosis, respiration and plasmolysis are not food-synthesis processes.
Photosynthesis converts light energy from the sun into chemical energy stored in food. Electrolysis and respiration do not do this.
An ecosystem is a community together with its non-living environment, as in a pond, forest or aquarium. A community alone lacks the abiotic part, and a biome is a large climatic region.

Tansley coined 'ecosystem' (1935) and producers/autotrophs make their own food, so I and II are correct. Consumers are heterotrophs and do not photosynthesise, and decomposers turn organic matter into inorganic nutrients, so III and IV are wrong.
Energy falls about 90% at each level, so producers at the base outnumber and outweigh primary consumers. The other options reverse this relationship.
Srinatha's Haravilasam gives information on the sea-borne trade, imports and exports of the Reddi period. Harivamsam (Errana), Kasikhandam and Bhimeswara Puranam are not noted for trade details.
India was part of the southern landmass Gondwanaland (Gondwana), not Laurasia. The other options are not ancient landmasses India belonged to.
The Pacific Plate is one of the seven major plates. Cocos, Arabian and Philippine are minor plates.

Statement II is wrong because Vyommitra is a female half-humanoid robot, and III is wrong because the crew vehicle launches on the human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3), not GSLV Mk II. I (first crewed orbital spacecraft of the human spaceflight programme) and IV (DRDO supports human-centric systems such as parachutes and life support) are correct, so I and IV only.
The four Gaganyatris named in Feb 2024 are Nair, Krishnan, Pratap and Shukla. Pankaj M. Sinha is not one of them, so option 4 is correct.
Only the USSR/Russia, USA and China have launched humans on their own rockets. India has not yet done so, and would be the 4th, so India is the answer.
The Charlie Brown effect is the fluid shift in microgravity that gives a puffy face and thin legs. The other options are not recognised names for this phenomenon.
Zarya, launched in 1998, was the first ISS module and is Russian-built. Destiny is a US lab module, while Soyuz is a spacecraft and Endeavour a space shuttle, so Zarya is correct.
Wentian is a module of China's Tiangong station (Tianhe core + Wentian + Mengtian), so the country is China.
Graphite has sp² layers and is a good electrical conductor, whereas diamond is an electrical insulator because it has no free electrons. Peat and charcoal are not noted as good conductors.
The notes only support the drug and antigen carrier use of CNTs; they do not settle the capillary, sensor or biodegradability claims, so no line is linked.
Diamond, graphite and C60 fullerene are allotropes of carbon. Methane is a compound of carbon and hydrogen (CH4), not an allotrope.
Amorphous carbon includes coal, charcoal, coke and lampblack, so charcoal is the amorphous form. Diamond, graphite and fullerene are crystalline allotropes.
Robotics is listed as an example of the third generation (systems of nanosystems). Aerosols are first generation, and molecular devices belong to the fourth.
The NCL nanogenerator produces electricity when pressure is applied, which is the piezoelectric effect. It is not photovoltaic or thermoelectric.
Electricity generated from applied pressure is the piezoelectric effect, so the NCL nanogenerator is piezoelectric, not photoelectric.
IIT Mandi developed biodegradable natural-polymer nanoparticles from renewable resources for colorectal cancer.
Nanoparticles are defined as 1-100 nm in size, so option 1 is right. The wider 1-1000 nm range is incorrect.
Krishnapatnam Port is in Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh; Visakhapatnam hosts Gangavaram Port, not Krishnapatnam.
Krishnapatnam Port lies in Nellore district; Visakhapatnam is the location of Gangavaram Port.
The notes do not state the effect of disinvestment on backward states. The usual argument is that reduced public-sector presence left these states short of infrastructure facilities.
Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah in 1541 inside the Purana Qila. The Atala Masjid, Bara Sona Masjid and Quwwat-ul-Islam belong to other rulers.
The Purana Qila was begun by Humayun as a citadel, but its present form is credited to Sher Shah. Among the options only Sher Shah fits.
Chausa (1539) was fought between Humayun and Sher Khan, not Jahangir, so the Jahangir–Chausa pair is wrong. The other pairs (Khanwa–Babur, Haldighati–Akbar, Bilgram–Humayun) are right.
Dauhariya (Devara) was in 1532, Chausa in 1539, Kannauj in 1540 and Samugarh in 1658. So the order is Dauhariya, Chausa, Kannauj, Samugarh.
Bilgram (Kannauj) was fought in 1540. The notes do not date Sarnal, Dharmat or Jajau, so Bilgram being the earliest is the only part they support.
Humayun's battles in order were Devara/Dauhariya 1532, Chausa 1539, Kannauj 1540 and Sirhind 1555. This matches option 4.

The immediate trigger was the English navy's seizure of French ships, which led France to retaliate. The War of Austrian Succession and Anglo-French rivalry were the wider background, not the immediate cause.
The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the War of Austrian Succession and the First Carnatic War, and Madras was returned to the English in exchange for Louisbourg. Both statements are correct.
Simuka (Srimukha) was the first king and founder of the Satavahana dynasty; the Chera, Chola and Pandya dynasties are unrelated Tamil kingdoms.
The Satavahanas (c. 200 BC–200 AD) were the oldest Deccan dynasty, earlier than the Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Pallavas, which came centuries later.

V.S. Sukthankar held that the Satavahanas were not the Andhras and placed their home in the Bellary region on the basis of the Myakadoni inscription. Bhandarkar is the tempting option but held that Andhras and Satavahanas were the same.
Sakhalin (Russia's Far East island) is known for its offshore oil and gas drilling, so 'Oil drilling' is correct. The notes do not cover it.

All four statements are true: China is the top coal producer, the Donetsk Basin is Ukraine's main coalfield, the Saar is a German coal region and the Appalachian region is the main US coal area. Hence 'All of these'.

Ruby and sapphire are corundum (aluminium oxide), and emerald is a beryl (beryllium aluminium silicate), so aluminium is the common element in all three. Iron, copper and zinc are not the base compounds.
The Himalayan region (including the western Himalaya) is rich in forests and hydropower, not in metallic or atomic minerals, which are concentrated in the Peninsular plateau.
The notes give the NDRF budget estimate for 2021-22 as ₹1,209 crore, so option 4 is correct.
NIDM is located in New Delhi (Rohini), with a Southern Campus near Vijayawada; it is not in Baroda, Cochin or Cuttack.
NDMP 2016 was India's first national plan covering all phases of the disaster cycle (revised 2019), so 2016 is correct.

Promoting preparedness only after a disaster is not an objective of the policy, which stresses prevention, mitigation and preparedness. The other options are genuine objectives, such as mainstreaming DRR.
A HAZOP study checks the adequacy of safety measures, so option 1 is correct.
Mitigation lowers the likelihood of a disaster, and is the most cost-effective phase. Response and recovery come during or after a disaster.
MAT stands for Mitigation Assessment Team.
Public education is non-structural mitigation. Search and rescue and temporary housing belong to response and recovery, and emergency exercises are preparedness.
Early warning is a crucial component of mitigation because it supplies timely information, so the reason correctly explains the assertion.
Vulnerability analysis and risk assessment are listed under the mitigation phase, not prevention.
Risk assessment, with vulnerability analysis, belongs to the mitigation phase.
Risk assessment, with vulnerability analysis, belongs to the mitigation phase.
Prevention, mitigation and preparedness are pre-disaster phases, while recovery and reconstruction occur after the disaster.
Building codes are the structural mitigation measure for earthquakes. The other options are response or preparedness activities.
Evacuation drills test evacuation routes, early warning gives timely information, community education raises awareness, and stockpiling ensures resources. This gives A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4.
Non-structural mitigation means community awareness and education. Relocation and detection or treatment systems are physical measures.
Gupta rule was monarchical: kings had divine claims and hereditary succession, so the system was kingship, not republican or democratic.
The law books prescribe one-sixth of the produce as the king's share (bhaga); the king could take from one-fourth to one-sixth, but one-sixth is the prescribed rate.
Halivakara is the plough tax. Hiranya is a cash tax, Sulka is customs duty, and Kara is a general periodic tax.
Aprahata denotes uncultivated forest (jungle) land, so option 1 fits; it is not irrigated or cultivated land.
Mahattaras were village elders who, with the kutumbis, assisted the village headman; the designations Mahattara and Pattakila refer to village headmen, not military officers or guild chiefs.
Water is not used on oil fires because oil is lighter than water and floats and spreads, so the burning oil spreads the fire. Plastic and cloth fires can be put out with water.
Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide (SiO2), so the element it contains is silicon (Si). Hg, Ti and Sn are not constituents of quartz.
Ladakh (about 173,266 sq km) is the largest Lok Sabha constituency by area, far larger than Kachchh (41,414 sq km); Kangra and Patna Sahib are much smaller.
The 84th Amendment froze LS seat allocation on the 1971 Census until the first Census after 2026.
Rajya Sabha is called a permanent House because it is never dissolved. Members do retire (one-third every second year) but this is not why it is called permanent, and members are not lifelong.
A Rajya Sabha member has a six-year term, fixed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is never dissolved; only one-third of its members retire every second year.
Rajya Sabha is a permanent House that is never dissolved, neither by the President, nor with the Lok Sabha, nor at the end of the Chairman's tenure. So 'None of the above' is correct.
About one-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every second year, which keeps it a continuing House.
The Constitution and the RPA prescribe no educational qualification for MPs, so no literacy, matriculation or degree is needed.
The Earth's axis is tilted 23½° from the perpendicular to its orbital plane, so 23.5° is the inclination.

With a perpendicular axis there would be no tilt, so no seasons and equal day and night; the Sun would be over the equator. The North Pole would not stay dark, since it would see the Sun at the horizon, so option 1 would not happen.
The Equator has 12 hours of day on every date (solstices and equinoxes alike), so day and night are equal there all year. The poles have six months of day and six of night.
Winter solstice is 22 Dec, summer solstice 21 June, vernal equinox 21 March and autumnal equinox 23 Sept, giving a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV.
The Equator has 12 hours of daylight on all dates, including the equinox.
The summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere falls on 21 June, when the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer.
On the equinoxes the Sun is overhead at the Equator, so day equals night everywhere on Earth. On the solstices, day and night are unequal.
The Southern Hemisphere has opposite seasons to the Northern, so its shortest day falls on 21 June, when the Northern Hemisphere has its longest day.
The winter solstice, around 22 December, is the shortest day in the Northern Hemisphere, when the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn.
All four pairs match: winter solstice 22 Dec, autumnal equinox 23 Sept, summer solstice 21 June, and vernal (spring) equinox 21 March.
The Gold Card Scheme, announced by the RBI under EXIM Policy 2003-04, gives quicker and cheaper credit to creditworthy exporters, not to importers, students or women entrepreneurs.
ECGC is the government-owned body that provides export credit-risk insurance. STC and EXIM Bank are not insurers, and the RBI is the central bank, so they are wrong.
MMTC is the largest trading government company in India. The other options are not trading companies of that kind.
ECGC provides export credit-risk insurance. EXIM Bank is a lender and not an insurer, so 'All of the above' is wrong.
ECGC provides export credit-risk insurance. GAIL, CBDT and IDBI are not export insurance bodies.
The Niryat Bandhu Scheme mentors new and first-generation entrepreneurs in exports. It is unrelated to crop protection or rural poverty schemes.

MMTC is the largest trading government company, which supports statement I. Statement II about Neelanchal Ispat Nigam Limited, a joint venture of MMTC with the Government of Odisha, is also true, so both are correct.
India's first Agriculture Export Facilitation Centre was set up at Pune in May 2021.
Bannerghatta Biological Park near Bangalore hosts India's first butterfly park; Kaziranga and the Kolkata zoo are not known for this, and the notes do not cover it.
Jim Corbett (Hailey NP, 1936) was the first national park in India; Gir, Dudhwa and Chandoli were declared later.
Jim Corbett, set up in 1936 as Hailey NP, is the oldest national park in India; Kaziranga, Hemis and Rajaji came later.
Balpakram National Park is in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, not Manipur, so the pair with Manipur is incorrect.
The Marine National Park is in the Gulf of Kachchh (Jamnagar, Gujarat), in the Rann of Kutch region, rather than the Sundarbans or Chilika; the notes do not state this.
Statement I is wrong because a pure substance cannot be separated by physical processes, only a mixture can. Statement II is right because dissolved salt is left behind when water evaporates.
Carbon is the backbone element of all organic biomolecules (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids), so it is the principal structural element of living cells.
Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings like birds but also teeth, a long bony tail and clawed fingers like reptiles, so it links Reptilia and Aves.
Helium is a Group 18 inert (noble) gas with a complete outer shell. Hydrogen, oxygen and CO2 are not noble gases.
An echo needs a gap of at least 0.1 s between the original sound and its reflection. With sound at about 344 m/s, the sound travels about 34.4 m out and back, so the minimum distance is about 17 m.
O has 6 valence electrons; gaining 2 electrons to form O2− gives a full octet of 8 valence electrons.
Crocodiles are the only reptiles with a four-chambered heart; other reptiles have three chambers.
The world's first camel hospital is in Dubai (UAE), the Camel Hospital at Dubai.
The configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 has 2 valence electrons (calcium), which are easily lost, so it is a metal. 2, 8 is neon and 2, 8, 8 is argon (noble gases), while 2, 8, 7 is chlorine, a non-metal.
Rusting is the oxidation of iron through reaction with oxygen (and moisture), so I and III are correct. It is not a reduction, and CO2 is not the cause.
Spiders are arachnids with 8 legs and two body segments, not insects, which have 6 legs and three body parts. Bed bugs, house flies and mosquitoes are insects.
Convection needs a material medium whose particles can flow, so it occurs only in fluids (liquids and gases), not in solids or vacuum.
Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7 at room temperature.
An AC generator uses slip rings to deliver alternating current, while a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator to give unidirectional current.
Echidna is a monotreme (egg-laying mammal). Kangaroo, porcupine and whale give birth to young ones.
Glycerol is nitrated to make nitroglycerine, the basis of dynamite and other explosives. Methanol, urea and oxalic acid are not the explosive raw material here.
Frequency is measured in hertz, force in newton and resistance in ohm, giving A-2, B-3, C-1.
Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, mineral uptake across the plasma membrane, respiration in mitochondria and protein synthesis at ribosomes: A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.

Statement I is the correct definition of the photoelectric effect and III is correct because wave nature explains interference, diffraction and polarisation. Statement II is wrong because the emitted particles are photoelectrons, not protons.
Dhuandhar Falls is on the Narmada at Bhedaghat near Jabalpur, where the river cuts through marble rocks.
Kunchikal Falls on the Varahi in Karnataka is the highest waterfall by height. Jog Falls is noted for width, not height.
Jog (Gersoppa) Falls, noted for its width, is on the Sharavati river in Shivamogga, Karnataka.
Chitrakote Falls is on the Indravati river west of Jagdalpur in Bastar district, Chhattisgarh.
Kapildhara is on the Narmada, not the Godavari, so pair I is wrong. Jog Falls on the Sharavati and Sivasamudram on the Kaveri are correct, so the answer is II and III only.
Gokak Falls is on the Ghataprabha river in Karnataka, which is a Krishna tributary.

The S.K. Dhar Commission (1948) viewed linguistic states as a threat to national unity and preferred administrative convenience. The JVP Committee only advised postponement, and Wanchoo dealt with Andhra's finances.
Kurnool was the capital of Andhra State (1953); Hyderabad became the capital only of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
Andhra State's capital was Kurnool, chosen by an Assembly vote of 80 to 79 over Vijayawada. Hyderabad became capital only after 1956.
Kurnool was the capital of Andhra State (1953); Hyderabad became the capital only of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
Andhra State (1953), the forerunner of Andhra Pradesh, was the first linguistic state of independent India. Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka were not first.
Syed Fazl Ali, Governor of Odisha, was the Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission; the other options were not members.
The huge monolithic Nandi (stone bull) of the Vijayanagara period is at Lepakshi, the largest monolithic Nandi in India. Tadipatri is known for gopurams and Ubattu Shilpalu, not the bull.

Taxes on transactions in stock exchanges and futures markets are Union List subjects (Entry 84/92A-type levies), so the Union levies them, but they are not collected by the States. The notes do not state this directly, but Statement II is wrong, so only I is correct.
The massacre took place in the context of the Rowlatt Satyagraha, as protest against the Rowlatt Act and the arrests of local leaders.
The crowd gathered to protest the arrest of Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr Satyapal (arrested 9 April 1919) and the Rowlatt Act.
The massacre occurred at Amritsar, Punjab, on 13 April 1919, so 1919 Amritsar is correct.
Brig.-Gen. Reginald Dyer ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh, so the name is associated with that event.
Sir C. Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council, the only Indian member, in protest. Kitchlew and Satyapal were the arrested leaders.
Tagore gave up his knighthood in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, not for the Non-Cooperation Movement or other events.
Only Sankaran Nair of those listed resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council. Tagore gave up his knighthood and Malaviya resigned from the Imperial Legislative Council, so 'all three' is wrong.
Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
Rabindranath Tagore gave up his knighthood in 1919 in protest against the Punjab atrocities (Jallianwala Bagh).
1919 is linked with the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April. The other options belong to different years.
Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919, which predates the Civil Disobedience Movement, Bhagat Singh's execution and Chauri Chaura.
This is Tagore's letter renouncing his knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, so the declaration is by Rabindranath Tagore.
Daman and Diu had the lowest sex ratio among UTs in Census 2011 (618). The other options all have higher ratios.
Daman and Diu has the lowest sex ratio in India (618), lower than Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli or Delhi.
Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1,084) and is the only State above 1,000. Tamil Nadu (996), AP and Chhattisgarh are below that.
Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (Madras), standardly dated 1937 (the APPSC key gave 1938). Sarojini Naidu, Veeresalingam and others are not its founders.

Statement I is true (she founded the Andhra Aatmiya Sabha). Statement II is not supported: her title 'Iron Lady' is listed, but statement III is wrong because her awards are the Paul G. Hoffman award and Padma Vibhushan, with no Tamrapatra listed. The key treats II and III as the NOT-true ones.
Red-green colour blindness makes red look greenish or brownish; the notes do not cover it.
Myoglobin is an iron-containing oxygen-storing protein in muscle. Chlorophyll contains magnesium, while collagen and carotene contain no iron.
Oxygen enters the lungs first, is carried by the blood, and is then delivered to the tissues: lungs, blood, tissue.
Only the coronary artery statement is correct. The pulmonary vein carries blood from the lungs to the heart, the renal artery supplies the kidneys, and the hepatic artery supplies the liver.
Water is reabsorbed in the renal tubules and the large intestine. Hepatic cells and the pancreatic duct do not absorb water.

Somatotropin (growth hormone) rises with exercise, the testes make small amounts of progesterone, and the female adrenal secretes some testosterone, so I, II and III are correct. Stress raises cortisol, so IV is wrong.
Glaucoma damages the optic nerve and worsens progressively, usually due to raised eye pressure. Cataract affects the lens.
Respiration changes the O2 (21% to 16%) and CO2 (0.04% to 4%) content of air, while nitrogen is not used and stays unchanged.
Haemoglobin in RBCs carries mainly oxygen, and also some carbon dioxide (as carbamino-haemoglobin). It is not for clotting.
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas; alpha cells secrete glucagon.
Bones consist mainly of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite), so it is the salt found in maximum amount.
A mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone triggers ovulation.
The ovary is the primary sex organ in females since it produces ova and hormones. The uterus, vagina and fallopian tube are accessory organs.
The cervix is part of the female reproductive system (the neck of the uterus). The urethra, seminal vesicle and vas deferens are in the male system.
A male child is XY. The Y chromosome can only come from the father and the X from the mother.
The oesophagus is the food pipe carrying food from the pharynx to the stomach. The larynx is the voice box, the aorta is an artery and the thymus is a gland.
Saliva contains salivary amylase, which begins the digestion of starch in the mouth.
Urine is yellow due to the pigment urochrome, formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin.
The corpus luteum forms in the ovary from the ruptured follicle after ovulation and secretes progesterone.
Tendons are made of collagen, a tough fibrous protein. Fibrin is for clotting, elastin is in elastic tissue and cellulose is not a protein.

NSSO uses three reference periods: year (usual status), week (weekly status) and day (daily status). A 'Usual Monthly' or Current Monthly approach is not an NSSO method, so option 4 is the one not used.
The Worker Population Ratio is the share of employed persons in the total population. The other options are not indicators of this kind; Usual Principal Status is a reference approach.
Unemployment data in India have mainly come from the NSSO (now NSO) through its employment-unemployment surveys. The Planning Commission, Finance Commission and UNO do not collect it.
RIDF, administered by NABARD, gives loans to States for rural roads, bridges and irrigation infrastructure. RRBs and PACS lend to farmers for agriculture, not for such infrastructure.
NABARD stands for National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. The other options use wrong words such as Nation, Real and Net.
NABARD is the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, the apex development finance institution for agriculture and rural development.
NABARD was established on 12 July 1982, under the NABARD Act, 1981. The other dates are unrelated to it.
RIDF is administered by NABARD, which lends from it to the States for rural infrastructure. It is not run by RBI or the ministries.
Statement 1 is correct: NABARD was set up in 1982 under an Act of Parliament. Statement 2 is wrong because NABARD is the apex institution for agriculture and rural development, not agriculture alone.
NABARD prepares the district-wise Potential Linked Credit Plans (PLPs), which roll up into the State Focus Paper. DCCB, DDC and CPO do not prepare them.
KCC is issued by commercial banks, RRBs, cooperative banks and PACS, so all the listed institutions provide credit to KCC holders.
At Farakka the Ganga's right arm, the Padma, enters Bangladesh, so Padma is the Ganga; the Brahmaputra is the Jamuna there.
The notes do not give the active delta districts; the answer is North and South 24 Parganas, where the delta is still actively growing, unlike the older, moribund parts.

Devprayag is where the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda and the river becomes the Ganga. Rudraprayag is the Alaknanda–Mandakini confluence, while Badrinath and Rishikesh are not confluences of these two.

Statements I and II are correct: Devprayag is the Bhagirathi–Alaknanda confluence and Rudraprayag is the Mandakini–Alaknanda confluence. Statement III is correct as the Alaknanda rises from the Satopanth glacier above Badrinath. Statement IV (Kedarnath as the biggest Shankaracharya seat) is the one that fails, so the answer is I, II and III.
The notes do not give district-wise Ganga lengths; Patna has the longest stretch of the Ganga among the listed Bihar districts.
Kanpur is the largest city on the Ganga's banks; it is listed among the Ganga towns, and it is larger than Varanasi, Patna and Prayagraj (Allahabad).
The Bengal Delta is divided into the moribund, mature and active delta; the moribund delta is the old, inactive part in the west, so the answer is the Bengal Delta.
Bhutan, under its 4th King Jigme Singye Wangchuck, developed Gross National Happiness as an alternative to GDP.
HDI uses life expectancy, schooling (education) and GNI per capita (income). Social inequality is not a component of the HDI, so option 4 is correct.
Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising future generations, which concerns inter-generational use of natural resources.
Social behaviour is listed among the non-economic determinants of growth. Natural resources and capital are economic factors.
Replacing a wooden plough with a steel plough is a better capital instrument, which is capital augmenting technical progress; the notes do not cover this concept.
The notes state that the claim that the AP Economic Development Board has 6 divisions is incorrect, so option 4 is the incorrect statement.
The notes state that the claim that the AP Economic Development Board has 6 divisions is incorrect, so option 4 is the incorrect statement.
HDI uses income (GNI per capita), education (schooling) and life expectancy. Environmental condition is not a component, so only 1, 2 and 4 is correct.
The notes do not cover the Mata festival. It is celebrated by the Yadav (Raut) community.
Guru Purnima honours sage Vyas (Veda Vyasa), the compiler of the Vedas. The notes do not cover it.
Harela is an Uttarakhand festival marking the sowing season and plantation of saplings. The notes do not cover it.
The Rath Yatra is held at Puri, Odisha, at the Jagannath temple. The notes do not cover it.
Good Friday commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. Christ's death is the event, but the day is observed for the crucifixion.
Losoong is the Sikkimese New Year festival, celebrated in Sikkim. The notes do not cover it.
Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus, his rising from the dead. The notes do not cover it.
The Puri Rath Yatra honours Lord Jagannath, a form of Vishnu, with his siblings. The most specific answer is Jagannath.
Chapchar Kut is a Mizoram festival and the Khongjom Parba ballad is from Manipur. Thang-Ta is a Manipuri martial art, not Sikkim's, so III is wrong.
Athapoo is the floral carpet made during Onam in Kerala. The notes do not cover it.
The Shakumbhari Devi fair is held at Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, at the Shakumbhari Devi temple. The notes do not cover it.
Mudia Purnima Mela is held at Govardhan (Mathura district) around Guru Purnima. The notes do not cover it.
The Bagwal fair (Asadhi Kautik) is held at Devidhura in Champawat, Uttarakhand. The notes do not cover it.
Syed Salar Mela is held at Bahraich, at the dargah of Ghazi Miyan. The notes do not cover it.
The Madhavpur mela is held near Porbandar in Gujarat. The notes do not cover it.
The Nasik Kumbh Mela is held on the banks of the Godavari River. The notes do not cover it.
Eluru's hand-knotted carpets, in the Farishkhani and Ashunkhani designs, were the main attraction at the 1851 London Exhibition.

NABARD is the apex refinancing body but does not inspect every primary cooperative society; primary societies are inspected by the State Registrar or by the DCCBs, so option 4 is the untrue statement. The notes do not state NABARD's inspection role.
Short-term cooperative credit is three-tiered: APCOB at State level, DCCBs at district level and PACS at village level.
The Partition of Bengal (1905) was annulled at the 12 Dec 1911 Durbar announcements, so Bengal was reunited in 1911.
The 1912 Delhi Conspiracy bomb was thrown at Hardinge II during his state entry into Delhi, so Lord Hardinge is correct.
The 12 Dec 1911 announcements under Hardinge II annulled the Partition of Bengal; Curzon was the one who carried it out in 1905.
Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in 1931, during Lord Irwin's viceroyalty (1926–31).
The Younghusband Expedition to Tibet (1903–04) was sent by Curzon, Viceroy 1899–1905.
Tenure order: Curzon (1899–1905), Hardinge II (1910–16), Chelmsford (1916–21), Irwin (1926–31), i.e. I, III, II, IV.
Hardinge II wrote the memoir "My Indian Years".
Curzon (Viceroy 1899–1905) made this statement in 1900, hoping to assist the Congress to a peaceful demise.
Curzon's Partition of Bengal (1905) is the classic example of Divide and Rule, being seen as a way to split Hindus and Muslims.
New Delhi, designed by Lutyens and Baker, was an Indo-European imperial architecture meant to project legitimacy of British rule, so both statements are true and II explains I.
Bihar and Orissa were made a separate province in 1912 after the 1911 Durbar announcements.
The capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in the 1911 announcements, so Calcutta was the earlier capital.
The foundation stone of the Gateway of India was laid in 1911 for the visit of George V, with construction beginning in 1913 (the question's key is 1913); the notes do not cover it.
The 12 Dec 1911 announcement moved the capital to Delhi under Hardinge II.
The Kaaba is the sacred cubic structure in Mecca toward which Muslims pray and around which they perform Hajj, so it is a holy place for Muslims. The Hindu and Jewish options are wrong.
Sendai Target E aims to increase the number of countries with national and local DRR strategies by 2020. The other options are different targets (G, C, B) without the 2020 deadline.

At Yokohama in 1994, states met at the World Conference on Natural Disaster Reduction, so statement I is correct. The IDNDR was proclaimed earlier (UNGA 1989) for 1990-1999, not declared at Yokohama for 1994-2004, so II is wrong.
NDMA states that about 5,700 km of India's 7,516 km coastline is prone to cyclones.
Hazard mapping identifies and maps areas at risk from various hazards, which supports mitigation planning. It does not create response plans, plan routes, or predict exact timing.
Volcanoes cause the fewest annual fatalities among natural hazards in the USA, unlike tornadoes, heat/drought and winter weather.
Tsunamis are especially hard to mitigate, unlike earthquakes, droughts and floods, for which structural and non-structural measures work better.
Earthquake-resistant design requires small door and window openings that are centrally located, so walls stay strong.
A pyramidal (hipped) roof has sloping faces on all sides, which reduces wind suction and uplift compared with gable or flat roofs.

Proper crowd control through police deployment at key places manages the crowd while keeping the fair open. Merely warning the public, strictly limiting visitors, or cancelling are ineffective or excessive.
Afforestation, decongesting channels and depopulating flood plains reduce flood risk or damage. Deindustrialization along rivers is not a recognised flood mitigation strategy.
Diversion levees, check dams and tree plantation reduce flood runoff and damage. Basements in houses are vulnerable to flooding and do not help.
Mock exercises are conducted by NDMA together with NIDM, NDRF and States throughout the year. NDMA is the best answer among the options.
The PM's 10-Point Agenda does not list greater involvement and leadership of youth. The other options are part of the agenda.
World Meteorological Day is observed on 23 March.
Operation Vanilla was the Indian Navy's HADR mission to Madagascar after Cyclone Diane. Nepal relief was Operation Maitri.
Statement I is correct: Art. 243D(3) reserves one-third of seats for women. Statement II is wrong: the Art. 334 sunset applies to SC/ST reservation, while women's reservation has no sunset.
Sucheta Kripalani became Chief Minister of UP in 1963, the first woman CM of an Indian state. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor, not a CM.
Sarojini Naidu became Governor of UP in 1947, the first woman Governor in free India. Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister.
Leila Seth was the first woman judge of the Delhi High Court (1978), and later the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court (Himachal Pradesh).
Sundari Nanda, an IPS officer, was the first woman Director General of Police in Puducherry. Kiran Bedi is known as the first woman IPS officer, which is the tempting wrong option.
Pratibha Patil was the 12th President of India (2007-12), the first woman to hold the office.
Kiran Bedi was India's first woman IPS officer. Sarojini Naidu and Indira Gandhi were not IPS officers, and Bachendri Pal is a mountaineer.
Sucheta Kripalani became UP Chief Minister in 1963, the first woman CM of UP. Sarojini Naidu was UP's first woman Governor.
Halimah Yacob was elected Singapore's first woman President in 2017.
A rear-view mirror is a convex mirror, whose magnification is always less than one, giving a wide field of view with diminished images.
Sound speed increases with temperature and also with moisture, since moist air is less dense than dry air. So moist air at 30 °C has the highest speed.

The blue sky is a real observation, so A is true. R is false: it is Rayleigh scattering of the short-wavelength blue light by air molecules that makes the sky blue, not blue light being 'concentrated' or travelling in long lazy waves.

The blue sky is a real observation, so A is true. R is false: it is Rayleigh scattering of the short-wavelength blue light by air molecules that makes the sky blue, not blue light being 'concentrated' or travelling in long lazy waves.
Both are true: alcohol (spirit) has a very low freezing point, so it can measure down to -70 °C. But the low toxicity and quick evaporation are not the reason for this; the low freezing point is.
Both are true: alcohol (spirit) has a very low freezing point, so it can measure down to -70 °C. But the low toxicity and quick evaporation are not the reason for this; the low freezing point is.
Glucose has several -OH groups that form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, which is why it dissolves readily. So R correctly explains A.

Red glass transmits only red light. A red cover reflects red light and looks red; a white cover reflects all colours but only red passes through, so it also looks red. Hence the cover may be red or white.
Birds push air downward and backward with their wings (action) and the air pushes them upward and forward (reaction). This is Newton's third law.
Cosmic rays are streams of highly energetic charged particles (mainly protons) and not electromagnetic waves, so the statement that they are electromagnetic waves is the untrue one.

Rice has the largest kharif area (51.27 MH), so statement 1 is correct. Cotton area exceeds sugarcane, so 3 is correct. Sugarcane area has fluctuated rather than steadily fallen, and jowar area is below oilseeds, so 2 and 4 are wrong.
BGREI (2010-11, under RKVY) is a rice-based (rice-wheat) system programme for eastern India, so paddy productivity is the target crop.
The Green Revolution aimed at foodgrain self-sufficiency through HYV seeds, fertilisers and irrigation, not land redistribution, exports or cash crops.
Wheat benefited most from the Green Revolution (output rose about 2.5 times), followed later by rice, while pulses and coarse cereals lagged.
NFSM launched in 2007-08 covered only rice, wheat and pulses, so option 1 is correct.
NFSM (2007-08) targeted rice, wheat and pulses only, through area expansion and productivity gains in identified districts. Oilseeds and vegetables were not included.
Kyiv (Kiev) stands on the Dnieper river. The Volga, Don and Danube flow elsewhere (the Danube passes Vienna, Bratislava and Budapest).
The Rhine flows past Cologne and Bonn, not Berlin, so Berlin–Rhine is the wrong pair. London–Thames, New York–Hudson and Vienna–Danube are correct.
Acceleration is change in velocity (m/s) per unit time (s), so its SI unit is m/s², i.e. ms-2.
Resistance R = ρl/A depends on resistivity, length and cross-sectional area, not on the current passing through it.
A transistor can amplify signals; a transformer changes AC voltage, a diode rectifies and a capacitor stores charge.
Radioactive elements spontaneously emit alpha, beta and gamma radiations, not radio, infrared or ultraviolet waves.
A kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections from inclined mirrors to form symmetric patterns.
The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence always equals the angle of reflection.
A plane mirror reverses left and right in the image, which is called lateral inversion.
Going from a denser to a rarer medium, light speeds up and bends away from the normal.
The absolute refractive index of air is about 1.0003.
An oscilloscope displays electrical signals; it is used to view sound waves (converted by a microphone) as waveforms.
With constant acceleration, s = ut + ½at², so the distance covered depends on the initial velocity u.
Solutions are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components; emulsions are colloids (heterogeneous), and enzymes are proteins.
Jellyfish belong to phylum Cnidaria (coelenterates), which have stinging cells.
Wall lizards (geckos) have adhesive pads on their digits that let them cling to vertical walls and ceilings.
Absolute zero (0 K) is the temperature at which molecular motion would cease.
The container also expands on heating, so the observed liquid expansion is only apparent, which makes measuring it difficult.
Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into vapour without passing through the liquid state.
Compressibility is lowest in solids and highest in gases, so Solid < Liquid < Gas.
An emulsion is a colloid of one liquid dispersed in another liquid, e.g. milk (fat in water).
Evaporation is liquid to gas, sublimation solid to gas, freezing liquid to solid and melting solid to liquid, giving 1 2 4 3.

Balarama (Sankarshana), brother of Krishna, is traditionally shown holding a plough (hala), which is why he is called Halayudha; Krishna is shown with the flute or discus, so he is the tempting wrong option.
Milindapanho records the dialogue between King Milinda (Menander) and the Buddhist monk Nagasena. Nagarjuna was a later Mahayana philosopher, and Nagabhatta and Kumarilabhatta are unrelated.
Milindapanho is the dialogue between King Milinda and the monk Nagasena, and Milinda is Menander, so the text throws light on Menander.
Lead coins are attributed to Strato II among the Indo-Greeks. Menander and Demetrius are known for other coinage, such as silver coins with Indian symbols.
Heliodorus, who set up the Besnagar Garuda pillar, is described as a Bhagavata from Taxila, sent by Antialcidas to Vidisha. So his home was Taxila.
IMD's climate statement puts India's average yearly temperature in 2020 at 25.78°C, so option 4 is correct.
In IMD's colour-coded warnings, Red means extreme heat and the action is 'Take Action'. 'Be Prepared' is Orange and 'Be Updated' is Yellow.
Both statements are true. Extreme water events (floods, droughts) threaten food security, which in turn raises social tension, so R explains A.
The notes do not give India's rank in the 2019 Global Climate Risk Index report, so this cannot be verified from them. The keyed answer is 14th.
The Rutgers University study found that warming wipes out about twice as many ocean species as land species, so option 3 is correct.
The notes do not say which year the WMO ranked fifth warmest, so this cannot be verified from them. The keyed answer is 2009.

Greenland and Antarctica have been losing ice-sheet mass for two decades, so a significant reduction in ice sheet mass is an observed effect. The other options describe the opposite of observed trends.
The Arctic and Greenland ice sheets are listed tipping elements, and melting polar ice is the most important effect of warming. The Amazon, by contrast, is expected to flip only beyond about 2°C.

The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur is a Shaiva temple built by Rajaraja I, with Shiva frescoes such as Tripurantaka, so calling it a Vishnu monument is wrong. The other statements (Chola architecture, Rajaraja I, granite) are correct.
Nataraja is regarded as the greatest creation of the South Indian sthapatis, especially in the Chola bronzes. Mahishasuramardini, Rama and Somaskanda do not hold this distinction.
The Nataraja bronze, made by the lost-wax method, was perfected by the Cholas, so it is a prime example of Chola art. Gandhara, Mathura and Maurya art are not associated with it.
The lost-wax bronze tradition was perfected by the Cholas, and Nataraja is its greatest creation. So the Nataraja bronzes developed under the Cholas, not the Pandyas, Cheras or Pallavas.
Basavanna (Basaveshwara) founded the Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement in the 12th century; Ramanuja and Shankaracharya founded other philosophies, and Kambar was a poet.

Statement I is partly right on Basavanna being a Kalachuri minister in the 12th century, and the key accepts it. Statement II is wrong: the Virashaivas rejected Dharmashastra norms and supported widow remarriage, so only I is correct.
Veerabhadra Vijayam was Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya; it is not by Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.
Srinatha served at Kondaveedu under Pedakomati Vema Reddy as Vidyadhikari. Potana, Tikkana and Bhimakavi are not linked with his court.
Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) wrote Dasarathi Satakam in prison. Sumati Satakam is Baddena's, so it is the tempting wrong option.
France signed the first civil nuclear deal after the NSG waiver (30 September 2008), ahead of the USA, whose 123 Agreement came later. Russia's tie-up was an older 1988 accord.

A dirty bomb only uses a conventional explosive to scatter radioactive material, so it does not create a city-flattening atomic blast, which makes statement II wrong. It is also far cheaper and easier to make than a nuclear weapon, so III is wrong. Statement I is correct, so the incorrect ones are II and III.

The Nuclear Security Summits were a series begun by US President Obama (2010, 2012, 2014, 2016), not held under the UN. The International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent expert group, not an IAEA organ, so neither statement is correct.

Veeresalingam conducted the first widow remarriage in Andhra on 11 December 1881 at Rajahmundry, so 1881 is correct. 1880 was the year the Widow Remarriage Association was founded, which is the tempting wrong option.
Desha Matha, run by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham, backed the Home Rule movement. The other options are not linked to it in the notes.
The notes list Prakasika (1896) as an attempted journal of Gurajada Appa Rao. The other options are not associated with it.

The Junagadh rock of Rudradaman mentions both Chandragupta Maurya (via his governor Pushyagupta building the lake) and Ashoka (whose edicts are on the same rock). The Skandagupta record there is Gupta, so it does not fit.

The Boghaz-Koi inscription (14th c. BC, Asia Minor) names Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatya, indicating the Aryan movement from Iran to India. Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are Ashokan Kharosthi sites, and Junagarh is not linked to this.
Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription salutes the Jinas, showing he was a patron of Jainism. Ashoka is associated with Buddhism, and Harsha and Pulakeshin II are not noted as Jain patrons.
The Maski edict of Ashoka mentions the Kalinga victory, as it is the first edict naming 'Asoka'. The Hathigumpha inscription is Kharavela's and is not the one the notes link to the Kalinga victory.
Ashokan edicts name the Chola, Pandya and Satiyaputta kingdoms of the far south, but the Satavahanas are not mentioned among them. The Satavahanas rose after Ashoka.
Bauxite, malachite and zinc blende are ores (of aluminium, copper and zinc), while pig iron is a product smelted from iron ore, not a naturally occurring ore.
Tungsten is listed among non-ferrous metals, while iron ore, manganese and chromite are ferrous minerals used in iron and steel making.
Magnetite (Fe3O4) is magnetic and is called black ore. Its iron content is highest, 70-72%, so the 60-70% range is acceptable in the exam's keyed answer, which marks all three statements correct.
Galena (PbS) is the ore of lead.
Aluminium comes from bauxite, iron from magnetite, copper from malachite and zinc from calamine (zinc carbonate, like smithsonite ZnCO3), which matches option 1.
Haematite, magnetite and siderite are iron ores, whereas cuprite is an ore of copper.
Haematite is an iron ore and monazite is the thorium ore, so those pairs are right. Pitchblende is an ore of uranium, not copper, so pair II is incorrect.
German silver is an alloy of Cu 60, Ni 20 and Zn 20 and contains no silver. Horn silver, ruby silver and lunar caustic (silver nitrate) all contain silver.
German silver is an alloy of Cu 60, Ni 20 and Zn 20 and contains no silver. Horn silver, ruby silver and lunar caustic (silver nitrate) all contain silver.
Corundum and cryolite are listed among the ores of aluminium, along with bauxite and diaspore.
Barbil-Koira in Odisha has the most iron mines and the richest haematite, so the answer is Odisha.
Construction is a secondary-sector activity (with manufacturing and utilities), not a service. Transport, hotels and restaurants, and insurance are all tertiary.
Services account for more than 50% of GVA, the highest contribution to GDP, so 50% is the right option.
Syed Haidar Raja led the Swadeshi movement in Delhi; Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were not associated with Delhi in this role.
Tilak was a militant Extremist leader, whereas Naoroji, Ranade and Gokhale were Moderates, so Tilak is the one not known as a moderate.
Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lajpat Rai were Extremist (militant) leaders, while Gokhale was a Moderate, so I, III and IV is correct.
Gokhale was a Moderate, whereas Pal, Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo were Extremists.
Tilak rejected the Congress 'politics of prayer, petition and protest' and blamed the Congress for it; Jinnah, Bose and Besant are not linked to this charge.

Marsilea is a pteridophyte and has xylem and phloem. Cladophora and Anabaena are algae and Penicillium is a fungus, so none of them has vascular tissue.
Transferring charge from a charged body to the Earth is called earthing (grounding).

Transistors are used in amplifier circuits such as hearing aids. A fuse is a simple heating-effect wire and a fluorescent lamp is a gas discharge tube.
Fasciola is at organ level, Spongilla at cellular level, Obelia at tissue level and Pheretima at organ-system level, giving the code 2 3 4 1.

A frog lays eggs, so it is oviparous. Rabbit, mouse and squirrel are mammals that give birth to young.
Bryophytes lack a vascular system (xylem and phloem). Thallophytes lack a differentiated body, Funaria is a moss, and pteridophytes are cryptogams, not phanerogams.
Pteridophytes have vascular tissue but no seeds or flowers, so they are called vascular cryptogams.
Primitive vascular plants had a protostele, in which the xylem forms a solid core surrounded by phloem.
A snail is a mollusc, an invertebrate with no backbone. Mammals, fish and birds are vertebrates.
Amphibians such as salamanders have a three-chambered heart. Scoliodon (fish) has two chambers, while pigeon and human have four.
A flower is a modified shoot, formed from the shoot apical meristem, with its parts as modified leaves.

A floating boat with nails displaces water equal to its total weight. Once the nails are removed and sink, they displace only their own volume, which is less, so the water level falls.

Average velocity is net displacement over time. The car returns to the start, so displacement is zero and so is average velocity.
Pressure = force/area. The needle's tip has a much smaller area, so for the same force it exerts more pressure and bursts the balloon.
Quality (timbre) of a musical sound depends on its wave form, i.e. the mix of harmonics. Pitch depends on frequency and loudness on amplitude.

Gandhi first used the hunger strike as a weapon in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918; Rowlatt and Non-Cooperation came later.

Champaran (1917) was Gandhi's first farmers' movement in India, preceding Kheda (1918).
Rajkumar Shukla, a local indigo cultivator, met Gandhi at the 1916 Lucknow Congress and persuaded him to come to Champaran.
The first cotton mill attempt was at Fort Gloster (Ghusuri) near Kolkata in 1818, though it failed; the first successful mill was Bombay 1854.
Core industries are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity; transport is not one of them, so it is the answer.
The core list comprises coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity. Chemicals are explicitly not core, so chemical is the answer.
The eight core sectors are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity. Chemicals are not among them.
After the presiding officer adjourns the House sine die, the President prorogues the session, ending it. The sequence is adjournment sine die, then prorogation, then recess.
Prorogation under Art 85(2)(a) is ordered by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers, not by the Speaker, Chairman or PM.
Prorogation of a session is done by the President (the Governor in States) under Art 85(2)(a), on the Council of Ministers' advice. The Speaker and Chairman only adjourn sittings.
The Lok Sabha Secretariat works directly under the Speaker's control, independent of the executive. It is not under a ministry or the President.

Alluvial soil is concentrated in the Indo-Gangetic plain and river deltas and coasts, which include Bihar, Punjab and Tamil Nadu. Madhya Pradesh is mainly Deccan Trap black soil, so it has very little alluvium.
Bhangar is old alluvium on higher ground beyond the reach of floods. Khadar is the new alluvium of the floodplain.
Khadar is new, fertile alluvium ideal for intensive agriculture, so A is true. Kankar (calcareous concretions) belongs to Bhangar, not Khadar, so R is false.
Karewa soils are lake-bed deposits on plateaus in the Kashmir Valley, famous for saffron (Pampore). So they are found in the Kashmir Himalayas.
Khadar (new alluvium) and Bhangar (old alluvium) are the two divisions of alluvial soil.
IRDAI is the regulator of insurance companies (IRDA Act 1999); banks are regulated by the RBI, so option 2 is right.
The minimum net owned fund for an NBFC-MFI was ₹10 crore as per the March 2022 rules, so ₹10 crore is correct; the lower figures are outdated.
The Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB) operates at district level; the State Cooperative Bank works at state level and PACS at village level.
NABARD, set up in 1982, took over ARDC's refinance portfolio along with RBI's agricultural-credit functions, so ARDC was merged into NABARD.
NABARD stands for National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, the apex agricultural and rural credit institution.
NABARD is the apex agricultural and rural credit institution, having taken over RBI's agricultural-credit functions; so it, not the RBI or cooperatives, is the answer.
NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 (Act 1981), so 1982 is correct; 1981 is only the year of the Act.
NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982, so 1982 is the answer.
NABARD is the apex agricultural and rural credit institution, not a commercial bank like PNB, SBI or Central Bank.
The 200th consecutive successful Thumba launch in Nov 2022 was the RH-200 sounding rocket; the RH number is the diameter in mm.
SSLV is designed for 500 kg to 500 km LEO, so statement I is right. It has three solid stages, not two, so statement II is wrong; this leaves I, III and IV.
GSLV has a solid first stage, an earth-storable liquid second stage (Vikas) and a cryogenic upper stage. The S-L-S-L pattern belongs to PSLV.
NVS-01 was launched in May 2023 by GSLV-F12; the other GSLV flight numbers do not match this mission.
PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites (Cartosat-2 plus 101 foreign) on 15 Feb 2017, a multi-satellite record. INSAT-3DR is a satellite, not a launch vehicle.

The Permanent Settlement was introduced in 1793, not 1795, so option 1 is the incorrect statement. The other statements (John Shore planned it, zamindars were hereditary proprietors, fixed revenue) are correct.
Mahalwari was introduced in the North-Western Provinces (Agra-Oudh) and parts of Punjab. Bengal, Bihar and Orissa had the Permanent Settlement and Madras had Ryotwari.
Thomas Munro, the 'Father of Ryotwari', extended the Ryotwari settlement across Madras as Governor. Elphinstone is linked with Bombay, not Madras.
Ryotwari prevailed mainly in Madras (South India) and also in Bombay (West India). Since Southern India is the listed option, it is the correct answer.
Ryotwari was devised by Alexander Read and Thomas Munro. Cornwallis is linked with the Permanent Settlement, so statement I is wrong.
Article 153 provides for a Governor for each State, and the 7th Amendment (1956) allowed the same person to be Governor of two or more States. Arts 152, 151 and 154 do not deal with this.
Article 157 requires a Governor to be a citizen of India who has completed 35 years of age, so the minimum age is 35.
The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head of the State, while the CM and Council of Ministers are the real executive. The CM is the real head, not the constitutional head.
Under Article 155 the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, not by the Cabinet, the Chief Justice or the Speaker.
Under Article 243I the Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats. The CM, Speaker and President do not constitute it.
A Governor's ordinance must be approved by the State Legislature, not by the President. It lapses six weeks after the Legislature reassembles unless approved.
Mahapadma Nanda, titled Sarvakshatrantaka (destroyer of Kshatriyas), is likened to Parashurama, hence 'Aparoparashurama'. Bindusara, Ajatashatru and Kalashoka do not carry this epithet.
Dhana Nanda (Agrammes/Xandrames) ruled at Alexander's invasion and was overthrown by Chandragupta, so he was the last Nanda ruler. Mahapadma was the founder, not the last.
Bulandibagh is among the remains of ancient Pataliputra (modern Patna), along with Kumrahar. It is not associated with the other listed cities.
Magadha's first capital was Girivraj/Rajgriha (Rajgir); Pataliputra was chosen later by Udayin, and Vaishali was not the first capital.
Kumrahar preserves the remains of ancient Pataliputra, capital of Magadha. Vaishali, Kapilavastu and Shravasti are not linked to it.
Ajatashatru fortified Pataligrama on the Ganga during the Vajji war, and it grew into Pataliputra, so he is credited with founding it. Dhanyakataka, Nalanda and Lumbini are unrelated.
The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali under Kalashoka. Rajgriha hosted the First and Pataliputra the Third.
The Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha was the venue of the First Buddhist Council. It is not in Sanchi, Nalanda or Pawapuri.
The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka. Rajgriha was the venue of the First Council.
The First Buddhist Council at Rajgriha was patronised by Ajatashatru, just after the Buddha's Mahaparinirvana. Bimbisara had died earlier, so he is not the answer.

Phishing uses fake e-mails or texts that look legitimate to trick users into revealing sensitive information. SQL injection targets databases and DoS floods servers, so neither is about tricking users.
In cyber law, DOS stands for Denial of Service. Disk Operating System is a different, non-cyber-law meaning.
Spam is the term for junk, unsolicited bulk e-mail. CRAM, DRAM and JAM are not used for this.
Spam means junk or unsolicited bulk e-mail, so it is related to computers (e-mail), not art, music or games.
The e-Nagarpalika civic tax portal attack (Dec 2023) was in Madhya Pradesh, so Madhya Pradesh is correct.
MSP is the floor price the government announces before each sowing season; procurement or market prices do not fit that description.
CACP is the body that recommends MSP (the CCEA gives final approval). Among the options, CACP is the only one that fits, as ICAR and State Governments do not decide MSP.
A price ceiling is a maximum price, and the MRP printed on a biscuit packet is the maximum a seller can charge. MSP and minimum wages are price floors.
