Mammals breathe with lungs; gills are for fish, the trachea for insects and skin for amphibians as a supplement.
Most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine, whose villi give a large surface area; the large intestine mainly absorbs water.
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones (a newborn has more, which fuse with age).

A is true since AB is the universal recipient, and R is true since O is the universal donor. However, O being a universal donor does not explain why AB can receive from all groups, so R is not the correct explanation.
Tooth enamel begins to demineralise when mouth pH falls below about 5.5 because of acids made by bacteria from sugars; the notes do not cover this.
Gastric glands secrete HCl (parietal cells) and pepsinogen, which is activated to pepsin. Casein is a milk protein, not a gastric secretion.
Gastric glands secrete HCl (parietal cells) and pepsinogen, which is activated to pepsin. Casein is a milk protein, not a gastric secretion.
The first passenger railway ran on 16 April 1853 from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane. Delhi–Agra and Howrah lines were other early lines, not the first.
The first passenger train ran in 1853 from Bombay to Thane (34 km), so option 2 is correct.
The notes give the first line in Eastern India as Howrah to Hooghly.
The Bengal Gazette (1780), the first newspaper in India, was started by James Augustus Hicky (JA Hickey). Tilak, Roy and Bentinck did not found it.
The Pioneer was founded by George Allen at Allahabad in 1865, not by Gandhi, so the Gandhi–Pioneer pair is incorrect.
Hindoo Patriot (1853) was the first English paper by Indians. The Hindu (1878) came later, and Young India was not a first.

Johannes Kepler showed through his first law that planetary orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus. Copernicus proposed the heliocentric model with circular orbits, and Galileo observed Jupiter's moons.
Proxima Centauri is part of the Alpha Centauri system, the nearest star system after the Sun, so it is the nearest of the listed stars. Sirius, Arcturus and Spica are much farther away.
A constellation is an apparent pattern of stars in the sky. The stars lie at very different distances from Earth and only appear grouped from our viewpoint, so they are not equidistant.
Nebulae are giant clouds of dust and gas lying far beyond the solar system, in which stars form. Asteroids, comets and planets are all members of the solar system.
A light year is the distance light travels in one year (about 9.46 trillion km), so it measures very large distances, not time.

Tanks cluster in undulating hard-rock terrain (impervious, poor groundwater), where wells are unviable, so tank and well irrigation are negatively related (II and III). Tank irrigation predating wells (I) does not explain the spatial pattern.
The Kelo project in Chhattisgarh is among the projects taken up under PMKSY (AIBP); the other options are not the listed PMKSY project.
The Kalpasar Project is a proposed fresh-water reservoir across the Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat.
Parwan is in Rajasthan, Renukaji in Himachal Pradesh, Lakhwar in Uttarakhand and Ken-Betwa links Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, giving a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I.

Canal irrigation is most important in North India because the canals are fed by perennial rivers like the Ganga, Sutlej and Beas, giving year-round water. Porous soil and a high water table favour wells rather than canals.

PMKSY aims at irrigation convergence, extending irrigated area and improving water-use efficiency (Har Khet Ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop). Protecting farmers against crop failure from calamities is the aim of crop insurance (PMFBY), not PMKSY.
Clay has very small, poorly connected pores, so it holds water but yields it poorly. Hence it is a poor aquifer, and II correctly explains I.

CGWA was constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and India has the world's largest groundwater-irrigated area, so II and III are correct. Statement I is incorrect since the percentage is not 36% of districts.
Uttar Pradesh has the largest replenishable groundwater resource among Indian States, owing to the extensive Ganga alluvial plains.
The quote is attributed to Aristotle, who linked the quality of citizens to the quality of the state. The notes do not cover this fact.
Religiosity and emotionality are listed as non-features of good governance. Transparency, responsiveness, equity, inclusiveness, participation and rule of law are among the 8 attributes.
Mission Satyanishta is the Indian Railways programme on ethics in public governance. The other options are not names of this programme.
The Government of undivided AP set up the CGG in Hyderabad in 2001, so 2001 is correct.
The CGG was set up in collaboration with DFID (UK) and the World Bank. The other options are not the collaborators named for it.
The Government of undivided AP established the CGG in 2001 in Hyderabad.
The CGG was established by the Government of undivided AP in 2001, in Hyderabad.

The Himalayas are young fold mountains raised from Tethys (geosynclinal) sediments, so options 1 and 2 hold. The notes do not say a Himalayan Frontal Fault separates the Himalaya from Tibet. The Shiwalik is the outermost range, so that statement is the incorrect one.

The Himalayas are India's northern boundary and climatic barrier, which blocks Siberian cold waves and shapes the monsoon. Shiwalik debris built the Indo-Gangetic plain, so without them it would lack such alluvium. All three statements are correct.
The Himalayas form India's northern boundary and a climatic barrier, separating the subcontinent from the rest of Asia. The Aravalli and the Ghats lie within peninsular India.
The Kashmir Valley lies in the Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) between the Great Himalaya and the Pir Panjal. It is not in the Himadri or the Shiwalik.
Duns are longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwalik, for example Dehra Dun and Patli Dun. Tals, Auris and Terais are not the Shiwalik valleys.

The Himadri is the most continuous range, with the loftiest peaks and an average height of 6,000 m. The other options are wrong: the Great Himalayan folds are asymmetrical, the Shiwalik is made of loose sediments, and there are three parallel ranges, not four.
The Trans-Himalaya is also called the Tibet Himalaya because most of it lies in Tibet.
The Krishna District Association, the first district association in Madras Presidency, was formed in 1892; the other years given are not its founding date.

The notes name A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu as the founder of the Telugu weekly Andhra Prakasika, which matches option 3 (Parthasarathi Naidu). The other options are associated with other journals or persons.
Horses were the chief import of the Vijayanagara Empire, ahead of pearls, silk and other goods, so option 3 is correct.
Pagoda (varaha) was the Vijayanagara gold coin, so A matches 2. The Mahmudi was a Gujarat coin, Muzaffari a Malwa coin, and Sikandri a North Indian coin, giving 2 1 4 3.
Devaluation is an official reduction in a currency's value relative to other currencies (more rupees per dollar). It is not a general decline in values or inflation.
Yuan is the currency of China. The renminbi (yuan) is in the SDR basket, and the notes list China's yuan as the Panda bond currency.
The euro is the single currency of the European Monetary Union. Dollar, guilder and mark are not the union's currency.
A market-driven rise in a currency's value against another is appreciation. Depreciation or weakening is the opposite, and the notes do not link debasement to this.
Devaluation helps only if export prices abroad respond to the lower currency value, so that exports gain competitiveness and volumes rise. This option is the one the key chose.

Jinnah joined the League in 1913, later led the movement for Pakistan and presided over the 1940 Lahore Resolution session. Aga Khan was the first League president, Salimullah proposed the League, and Liaquat Ali Khan became Pakistan's first Prime Minister.
Greta Thunberg, the school-strike climate activist, is from Sweden. The notes do not cover her.
The UK parliament declared a climate emergency in May 2019, the first national government to do so. The notes do not cover this.
Earth Hour is a WWF movement, not a UNEP/UNESCO initiative, so statement I is wrong. Statements II and III are correct: people switch off lights for an hour to raise climate awareness.

The Mangrove Alliance for Climate was launched at COP27 by the UAE with Indonesia, and is a voluntary alliance with no binding targets. Statement II is wrong because the US, Canada and others are not all members. The notes do not cover this.
Red Flag is a multinational air exercise hosted by the US Air Force, so the partner country is the USA.
Yudh Abhyas is the Indo-US Army exercise, so option 4 is correct; it is not held with Pakistan, Oman or Bhutan.
Tiger Triumph is the India-US tri-service amphibious exercise, so the code name is Tiger Triumph.
K.C. Neogy chaired the First Finance Commission (set up 1951, order of 22.11.1951). Santhanam and Chanda chaired the 2nd and 3rd.
The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution.
Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th Finance Commission (set up 2013, award 2015-20).
The 13th Finance Commission, chaired by Vijay Kelkar, gave its award for 2010-15.
C. Rangarajan chaired the 12th Finance Commission (set up 2002, award 2005-10). Khusro chaired the 11th and Reddy the 14th.
Vijay L. Kelkar chaired the 13th Finance Commission (2007, award 2010-15).
The 13th FC award to undivided Andhra Pradesh was split between the successor states under Sec 46(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, on population ratio and other parameters.
The 13th Finance Commission raised the States' share of central taxes to 32%, up from 30.5% under the 12th.
Racial classification uses skin, eye and hair colour/form, plus cephalic, nasal and stature indices and blood groups. Ear is not among these criteria, so it is the answer.
The notes do not give the population sizes of the racial groups. Caucasoid is the largest group worldwide.
ISFR 2023 puts forest cover at 21.76% of India's area, which is about 22%. The other options are far from this figure.
Forest cover percentages are Maharashtra 16.53 < MP 25.00 < Odisha 33.67 < Chhattisgarh 41.28. This gives the ascending order III, II, IV, I.
ISFR 2019 reported forest plus tree cover as 24.56% of India's geographical area, so option 3 is correct.
Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area (77,073 sq km), ahead of Arunachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. West Bengal, Kerala and Assam are not near the top.
Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover (77,073 sq km), ahead of Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
Arunachal Pradesh has the highest forest percentage among the options (78.67%) and the largest very dense forest area. Meghalaya is about 76%, so Arunachal ranks higher.
Forest percentage in the state's area is highest in Kerala, then Odisha, then Karnataka, with Andhra Pradesh lowest, giving III, II, I, IV. The notes do not give these figures.
The Tenth Plan estimate of about 20.50% forest area for 2001 is the correct answer. The notes do not state this figure.
FAO's report ranks India 3rd in annual net forest gain, after China and Russia, so Third is correct.
Van Mahotsav was started in 1950 by K.M. Munshi, then Union Minister of Agriculture and Food. The notes do not cover this.

Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra, flows through Karnataka, Telangana and AP, and reaches the Bay of Bengal at Hamsaladeevi. Godavari rises at Nashik but passes through Telangana, not Karnataka; Mahanadi and Kaveri do not fit.
Tungabhadra is the largest right-bank tributary of the Krishna, joining it at Sangameswaram. It is not a tributary of the Godavari, Penna or Vamsadhara.
The Raichur Doab is the land between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra rivers. Tunga and Bhadra join to form the Tungabhadra, so option 2 is wrong.
These islands (Aliabet, Sarfuddin, Dashan, Mehgam, Vegni) are the riverine islands of the Narmada.
The Narmada flows in a rift valley between the Vindhya range in the north and the Satpura range in the south. Sone, Mahi and Netravati do not flow in this trough.
West-flowing rivers form estuaries rather than deltas because they are short and swift and carry little alluvium. Both A and R are true, and R explains A.

Both statements are false: the Narmada and Tapi flow west through Madhya Pradesh, so statement II is wrong. Kerala's Kabini, a Kaveri tributary, flows east, so statement I is also wrong. Hence neither is correct.
The notes do not state this fact. Annual Brahmaputra floods deposit fertile silt on Majuli, and paddy is the main crop grown there.
Saubhagya (2017) is the Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana for universal household electrification. Clean cooking fuel is PMUY, so option 2 is wrong.
Participating states covered 97% of discom debt under UDAY, so option 4 is correct. The 75% figure is the share states took over via bonds, not the total covered.
The Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement is awarded for work in environmental science, energy and health, so it belongs to environment protection, not drama or rights fields.
The 2022 Magsaysay awardees were Sotheara Chhim, Bernadette Madrid, Tadashi Hattori and Gary Bencheghib; Tan Soo Heong is not among them, so only option 2 (I, II, IV, V) is right.
Salaam Bombay! was directed by Mira Nair, whereas Pather Panchali, Aparajito and Charulata are Satyajit Ray films.
Gully Boy (Zoya Akhtar) was selected as India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 92nd Academy Awards.
Ben Kingsley played Mahatma Gandhi in Richard Attenborough's 1982 film Gandhi; Attenborough was the director, not the actor.
Period. End of Sentence won the 2019 Oscar for Best Documentary Short Subject; Piper and Kamera are not Oscar-winning Indian short films.
Peter O'Toole did not act in The Guns of Navarone (which starred Gregory Peck, David Niven and Anthony Quinn), whereas he starred in the other three films.
The Pianist by Roman Polanski won the Palme d'Or (Golden Palm) at Cannes in 2002.
Disguised unemployment is mainly found in agriculture and family farms in rural areas, so I and II are correct; factory and urban areas are not where it predominates.
Disguised unemployment means surplus labour whose marginal productivity is zero, so removing them leaves total output unchanged.
Disguised unemployment is predominant in agriculture, where family members work on a plot that needs fewer workers. Industry, services and trade are not where it is typical.
Disguised unemployment means more workers are employed than needed, so the extra workers appear employed but add nothing to output.

Structural unemployment arises from long-term mismatches in the economy, such as a heavy-industry bias that creates too few jobs for the labour supply. The notes do not state this specific cause, but it fits the structural type better than the other options, which describe demand or supply shortfalls.
Frictional unemployment is the short-term gap while workers move between jobs or search for a better one. Seasonal, cyclical and technological unemployment have different causes.
The natural rate of unemployment hypothesis is associated with Milton Friedman. Phillips is linked to the inflation-unemployment trade-off and Keynes to deficient effective demand.
S.A. Bobde became the 47th CJI in November 2019, as the notes record; Gogoi preceded him and Khehar and Thakur were earlier CJIs.
H.J. Kania was the first CJI of India; M. Patanjali Sastri was the second, so he is the tempting wrong option.
Vitamin C is chemically ascorbic acid, and its deficiency causes scurvy; thiamine is vitamin B1.
Plant sterols (stigmasterol, sitosterol etc.) resembling cholesterol are called phytosterols, whereas animal fats contain cholesterol.
Cobalt is part of vitamin B12 (cobalamin); phosphorus and zinc are also essential minerals, so all three are required.
Scurvy is caused by vitamin C deficiency, and amla (Aonia, the Indian gooseberry) is the richest source of vitamin C; mango is a vitamin A source.
Glucose is a simple sugar, i.e. a carbohydrate, which is the main energy source of the body.
Xerophthalmia results from vitamin A deficiency, a nutritional cause, not an inherited genetic disorder like colour blindness, Down's syndrome or haemophilia.
Vitamin B12 is cobalamin, containing cobalt, so the complexing metal ion is Co3+.
The notes state that the fastest indigenous IP/MPLS router was launched in Bengaluru in March 2024, so Bengaluru is correct. The other cities are not linked to this launch.
The 1991 Industrial Policy raised the small-unit investment limit from ₹35 lakh to ₹60 lakh, so ₹60 lakh is correct.
The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) dealt with small and medium industries, focusing on deregulation and competitiveness.
The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) recommended abolishing reservation of items for the small-scale sector and wide deregulation.
The notes do not state anything about industrial clusters promoting monopoly, so no line is linked. Clusters aid MSMEs, so the monopoly claim is the incorrect statement.
NSIC provides marketing, raw-material and credit support for small industry products, so option 3 is correct.
In July 2022 SIDBI tied up with SVC Co-operative Bank for MSME lending, so option 2 is correct.
SIDBI stands for Small Industries Development Bank of India, the apex bank for MSME finance and promotion.
Sodium is not an essential plant nutrient (it is a beneficial element only for some plants), whereas potassium, calcium and magnesium are essential macronutrients.
Tungsten is very hard and can be drawn into thin filament wires (bulb filaments), so it is both hard and ductile; carborundum and cast iron are brittle, and nichrome is not very hard.
A whale is a mammal, so A is true. But whales have almost no body hair, so R is false even though they are viviparous.
The angiosperm embryo sac (female gametophyte) typically has 8 nuclei in 7 cells, which is a characteristic of flowering plants.
Kelvin is an absolute scale starting at absolute zero (0 K), so it has no negative values; Celsius, Fahrenheit and Reaumur can go below zero.
Not all liquids conduct (pure water, oils and many organic liquids are insulators), so A is false. R is a true statement about conduction under low pressure and high voltage.
Ants have the largest brain relative to body size in the listed options, taking brain-to-body mass ratio as the measure.
Bromine is a liquid at room temperature; hydrogen and oxygen are gases and iodine is a solid. Only bromine and mercury are liquid elements.
Latent heat of a given substance is fixed for a given temperature and is independent of temperature and volume, so I and III are correct.
Gold is the most ductile metal; it can be drawn into extremely fine wire, more so than silver, copper or aluminium.
Bees have been trained to detect landmines because of their sharp sense of smell for explosive vapours.
Cooking vegetables causes irreversible changes in their composition (a chemical change). Dispersion, drying of soil and dissolving salt are physical changes.
Sexual cannibalism, in which the female kills and eats the male after mating, is typical of spiders such as the black widow.
Radon is radioactive and short-lived, and is only present in trace amounts, so it is not counted as a stable atmospheric noble gas as argon, krypton and xenon are.
A plane mirror is flat, so its curvature is zero and its radius of curvature is infinity.
Carat is the measure of gold purity, so I is true. 18 carat gold is 18 parts gold out of 24 (75%), not 24 parts pure gold plus 6 parts other metal, so II is false.
Uranium has by far the highest density among the options, so it is the heaviest metal.
A simple periscope uses two plane mirrors to reflect light, so it works on the reflection of light. Total internal reflection is used in prism periscopes, not in the simple type.
The kangaroo rat, a desert animal, conserves water by excreting highly concentrated, almost solid urine.
A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair. AlCl3, BF3 and FeCl3 are electron deficient acceptors, whereas NH3 has a lone pair and acts as a Lewis base.
Usman Harooni accepted Moinuddin Chishti as his disciple at Haroon, so Moinuddin was the disciple of Khwaja Usman Harooni.

Statement II is correct as Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi follows Nizamuddin Auliya in the Chishti chain. Statement IV about the Qadiri order is correct by the given answer, though the notes do not cover it. Statement I is wrong because Sirhindi was a contemporary of Akbar and Jahangir, not Ibrahim Lodi. Statement III is wrong because Salim Chishti was linked to Akbar, not Aurangzeb.
Mahboob-i-Ilahi (Favourite of God) is the title of Nizamuddin Auliya, not of Moinuddin, Baba Farid or Kaki.
Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani (reformer of the second millennium) is the title of Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi, a Naqshbandi saint, not of any Chishti.
Shaikh-ul-Hind is the title of Salim Chishti, who is also linked with Fatehpur Sikri.
Chiragh-i-Delhi is the title of Nasiruddin Mahmud, the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, not of Nizamuddin himself.
Gesudaraz's dargah is at Gulbarga.
Nizamuddin Auliya's dargah is in Delhi.
The Ajmer dargah is that of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Salim Chishti's is at Fatehpur Sikri and Kaki's at Mehrauli.
Haji Waris Ali Shah's tomb is at Dewa Sharif, Barabanki (UP), where the fair is held.
The tripartite struggle for Kannauj involved the Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas; the Cholas were not a party to it.

Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha (founded 1936). The notes do not mention the 1944 Vijayawada session, so this link rests on his role as the Kisan Sabha's leading president.
The notes do not cover the Barahiya Tal revolt of Munger. The correct answer is the demand to return the Bakhasht land.
The Tebhaga movement of 1946-47 took place in Bengal, led by the AIKS/CPI among bargadars. It was not in Bihar, Punjab or Gujarat.
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929) and became the first AIKS president. This makes him a leader of the peasant movement in Bihar.

The Commission's objective was to examine the Centre-State relationship and balance of power, suggesting changes within the existing constitutional framework. The other options (reservations, interstate disputes, agricultural trade) are unrelated to its remit.
Dr S.R. Sen was one of the three members of the Commission, along with B. Sivaraman and the chairman Justice Sarkaria. The other names listed were not members.
The Commission did not recommend that the Governor should have travelled extensively in the State. The other three options (5-year term, outsider, eminent person) were recommended.
Vikramaditya VI ruled 1076–1126 CE, i.e. about 50 years, which matches option 1.

Mitakshara is Vijnaneshwara's commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti and deals with Hindu law, including inheritance (sons' right in ancestral property by birth). It is not a work on astronomy, agriculture or medicine.

Field artillery and muskets were the decisive factor at Panipat, with gunners Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa, so artillery is the answer given. The notes also credit skilled warfare and commandants, which is why option 4 is tempting.
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at First Panipat in 1526, the year his conquest of India began, so 1526 is the answer. 1527 is the year of Khanwa.
AGMARK is a quality certification mark for agricultural produce under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937, so it relates to agricultural goods.

AGMARK is certified by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection of the Ministry of Agriculture, not by FAO, so statement II is wrong. Statement I (BIS mark mandatory for tyres) is accepted as correct per the key, so only I is correct.
In contract farming the price, quantity and/or time are agreed in advance, so any one or all of them may be fixed. Hence option 4 is right, and the options naming only specific pairs are too narrow.
NAFED, set up on 2 October 1958, is the apex cooperative marketing body at national level. FCI is a grain procurement agency, not the apex marketing cooperative.
AGMARK is a quality mark, so statement 1 is correct. Its certifier is the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, not FCI, so statement 2 is wrong.
Fats and oils turn rancid when they are oxidised by air, which is why the manufacture date matters. The notes do not state this.
CO2 dissolves in water to form carbonic acid, so soda water is acidic.
Low temperature slows the respiration rate of fruits, so they deteriorate and ripen more slowly and keep longer.
Ethylene is the gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening. Cytokinin promotes cell division and abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor.
Poaching cooks food gently in a small amount of hot liquid at about 160-180°F. Blanching uses boiling water for a short time, so it does not fit.
Milk is a colloid, specifically an emulsion of fat in water, so it is an emulsion rather than a suspension, gel or foam.
Thiamine is vitamin B1, whose deficiency causes beri-beri.
Soyabean is the highest-protein grain and is also rich in fat and carbohydrate, so it provides all three. Rice is mainly carbohydrate.
Cyanocobalamin is the cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12 (cobalamin), so the answer is B12.
Vitamin D (calciferol) is needed for bone formation, and its deficiency causes rickets and osteomalacia.
Vitamin D is made in the skin on exposure to sunlight, so it is called the sunshine vitamin.
Riboflavin (vitamin B2) deficiency causes cheilosis and glossitis, along with stomatitis and dermatitis.
Nagpur is known as the zero-mile centre of India, marking the point from which distances were measured; the notes do not state this.
Mainland India extends from 8°4′ N to 37°6′ N, so it lies wholly in the Northern Hemisphere; West, East and South options are wrong.
India's area of about 3.28 million sq km is 2.4% of the world's area.
India's longitudinal extent is 68°7′ E to 97°25′ E, which matches option 1.

Statements II and III are correct: Aurangabad lies between Vadodara and Pune in latitude, and Bengaluru (about 13° N) is south of Chennai (about 13.1° N). Statement I is wrong because Jabalpur lies east of both Indore and Bhopal.

India occupies 2.4% of the world's area and 82°30′ E is the Standard Meridian used for IST, so II and IV are true. India is 7th by area, not 5th, and part of it lies north of the Tropic of Cancer, so I and III are false.
Kanyakumari, the southern tip of the mainland, is where the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean meet. Indira Point is in Great Nicobar and does not mark that meeting point.
By area Uttar Pradesh is the fourth-largest state, after Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; the notes do not give state area ranks.
Sikkim lies at about 27–28° N, a latitude that also passes through Rajasthan. The notes do not give state latitudes.
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra are the three largest states and together cover about 30% of India's area. The notes do not give this.
Descending order of area is Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, which gives I, III, IV, II. The notes do not give state areas.
The first sunrise in India is seen in the far east, in Arunachal Pradesh (Dong or Dang, near Kibithu, the easternmost point), not in the south or on the southeast coast.
Assam borders Bhutan and Bangladesh but not Myanmar, whereas Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Mizoram all border Myanmar.
Article 175/176 deals with the Governor's address and messages; Article 176 is the Governor's special address to the Assembly. Art. 172 is duration and 182/183 are not about the address.
Sikkim has only 32 members (Art. 371F), an exception to the 60-member minimum in Art. 170. The other States have 60 or more.
The minimum age to be an MLA is 25 years (Art. 173); 30 is for the Legislative Council.
Article 170 fixes Assembly strength at not more than 500 and not less than 60, so the minimum and maximum are 60 and 500.
Among the options, Himachal Pradesh has the largest legislature (68 members), more than Arunachal Pradesh (60), Manipur (60) and Meghalaya (60). The notes do not state this.
Council members are chosen by local bodies, MLAs, graduates, teachers and Governor nomination. Industrialists are not a category.
Under Art. 207(1), a Money Bill can be introduced in the Assembly only on the Governor's recommendation. The President and Parliament have no role.
The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II's order granting the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa is dated 12 August 1765, so option 2 is correct.
Under the treaty Shah Alam II received only Kora and Allahabad, not Varanasi, and Awadh was returned to Shuja after the Rs 50 lakh indemnity. So the Varanasi statement is the incorrect one.
The notes do not link HDI with SDG rankings of Indian States. The assertion is plausible because SDG targets overlap with education and health, which are core HDI dimensions, so R explains A.

Minority rights are not absolute: the State may regulate standards (and impose reasonable conditions for aid) though it cannot take away management. So 'Minority Rights are absolute' is the untrue statement.
Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, so the minorities safeguarded under it are linguistic minorities.

Article 30(1) gives all minorities, religious or linguistic, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. Article 29 is about conserving language, script and culture.
The Sachar Committee noted that Ajlaf (commoner or lower-caste converts) need attention like Hindu OBCs. Arzal are Dalit Muslims comparable to SCs, and Ashraf are the upper group.
The Ombudsman was first set up in Sweden in 1809, and India's Lokpal and Lokayukta were modelled on it.
The Indian versions of the Ombudsman are the Lokpal at the Union level and the Lokayukta in the States, so Lokpal is correct.
The First ARC (1966-70) first recommended state Lokayuktas. The Santhanam Committee recommended the CVC and CBI, not the Lokpal.
The Ombudsman began in Sweden (Scandinavia) in 1809, and the Lokpal and Lokayukta are the Indian versions of it.
The First ARC (1966-70) first recommended state Lokayuktas. The Santhanam Committee dealt with the CVC and CBI instead.
The First ARC, which recommended the Lokpal and Lokayukta, was chaired by Morarji Desai (later K. Hanumanthaiya). Santhanam chaired a different committee.

The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2011 by V. Narayanasamy, Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, not by P. Chidambaram. It was sent to the Standing Committee and civil society called it weak, so I, III and IV are correct.

The civil society members on the drafting committee were Anna Hazare, Arvind Kejriwal, Shanti Bhushan, Justice N. Santosh Hegde and Prashant Bhushan. So Hazare, Hegde and Shanti Bhushan are correct, while Prashant Joshi and Kiran Bedi were not members.
The notes do not state who designed the Lokpal logo, so no line supports the answer.
Rajasthan cut the Lokayukta's tenure from 8 to 5 years.

A grazing chain starts with the producer (grass) and then moves through grasshopper → frog → snake, as in the grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle chain. The other orders put consumers before the producer or swap the frog and snake.
Grass → goat → human is a grazing chain: a producer, then a herbivore, then an omnivore. The other options mix unrelated organisms or lack a producer-to-consumer sequence.
A goat is a herbivore at trophic level II, so it is the primary consumer. A human eating goat flesh is therefore one step further up, the secondary consumer, in grass → goat → human.

Biomagnification is the rise in concentration of persistent, non-biodegradable pollutants (toxicants such as DDT and mercury) at each higher trophic level. It is not an increase in algae, insects or weeds.
Decomposers are bacteria and fungi, which break down organic matter into simple inorganic nutrients. Viruses are not decomposers, so the answer is II and III.
Primary consumers are herbivores at trophic level II, and a caterpillar feeds on plants. The crab apple tree is a producer, and the frog and sparrowhawk are carnivores.

Only statement I is correct: a food chain shows who feeds on whom, in order, across different species and trophic levels. It is not found within a single species' population, and it does not show the numbers of organisms eaten (that is a pyramid of numbers).
Energy flows one way: sun → producers → herbivores → carnivores. The other options put the producers or herbivores in the wrong place.
Energy flow is unidirectional: sunlight → producers → herbivores → carnivores. Producers capture the solar energy first, so options with herbivores or carnivores ahead of producers are wrong.
In photosynthesis, green plants (photoautotrophs) convert sunlight into chemical energy stored in food. Energy is transformed, not destroyed, so the answer is chemical energy.
The primary source and driving force of energy in an ecosystem is the Sun. Producers capture solar energy, and it then flows to consumers.
Dara Shikoh, Shah Jahan's eldest son, bore the titles Shah-i-Iqbal / Shah Buland Iqbal, which matches Shahzada-e-Buland Iqbal.
The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Bano Begum), who is buried there. Nur Jahan has a different tomb, that of her father Itimad-ud-Daulah.
Mumtaz Mahal's real name was Arjumand Bano Begum, daughter of Asaf Khan, who married Prince Khurram in 1612. Mehrunnisa is Nur Jahan's name.
Dara Shikoh was executed in 1659 and buried in Humayun's Tomb in Delhi.
Kandahar was lost to Persia in 1622 under Jahangir and regained in 1638 when Ali Mardan Khan surrendered it to Shah Jahan.

Kandahar was lost in 1622 while Khurram was in revolt, and no line settles the other causes. The accepted answer is that Khurram refused to go, an expedition was hard to organise, and the cold was severe, whereas Mughal army inefficiency (I) is not a cause.
The assertion holds that Daulatabad fell to the Mughals in 1631, but Malik Ambar had died in 1626, so he could not have betrayed his sultan at that siege. The reason is therefore false.
Aurangzeb imprisoned Shah Jahan in Agra Fort, where he was nursed by Jahanara until his death.
The Battle of Dharmat (15 April 1658) was fought near Ujjain, which lies in Madhya Pradesh.
The All India Anti-Untouchability League was founded by Gandhi in September 1932 and became the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1933, so Gandhi is the founder. Ambedkar and Jagjivan Ram founded other bodies.
The All India Depressed Classes League was founded by Babu Jagjivan Ram. Ambedkar founded the Scheduled Castes Federation, and Phule had died long before.

A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister after the Justice Party won the 1920 elections, because party president Thyagaraya Chetty declined the office. So Thyagaraya Chetty is the tempting wrong option.
The Act has 12 Parts, 108 Sections and 13 Schedules, so 108 is correct.

Section 8 gives the Governor special responsibility for the security of residents in the common capital (law and order, vital installations). Section 6 concerns the expert committee for AP's capital and Section 10 the First Schedule.

Section 8 places the responsibility for security of residents of the common capital on the Governor, who acts in individual judgment after consulting Telangana's ministers. It is not placed on either successor state or on the Government of India.
Section 50 deals with tax arrears by place of assessment, which AP contested. The notes do not mention Section 51, so the pairing of 50 and 51 is taken from the given answer.
Part XII (Legal and Miscellaneous) amends Article 371D and Article 168, so I and II are correct. Nothing in it amends Article 56 of the Constitution, so III is wrong.
The Act has 12 Parts, 108 Sections and 13 Schedules, so 108 is correct.

Section 8 places the responsibility for security of residents of the common capital on the Governor, who acts in individual judgment after consulting Telangana's ministers. It is not placed on either successor state or on the Government of India.
Polavaram is a multipurpose irrigation project on the Godavari river, not the Krishna, Pennar or Tungabhadra.
Polavaram is a multipurpose irrigation project on the Godavari river, not the Krishna, Pennar or Tungabhadra.
JRY was reshaped in 1999 as the Jawahar Gram Samriddhi Yojana (JGSY), with more stress on rural infrastructure, so option 4 is right.
PMRY (1993) is a self-employment scheme for educated unemployed youth. MGNREGS, RLEGP and NREP are wage employment programmes.
PMRY was implemented through District Industries Centres, with banks providing loans to educated unemployed youth. The other agencies are not its implementing agency.
DDU-GKY is a placement-linked skilling programme for rural poor youth in general, not exclusively for rural girls, so statement 1 is incorrect.
The first Food for Work Programme was launched in 1977 under the Janata government.
SGSY was launched in April 1999, merging IRDP, TRYSEM and DWCRA.

NFFWP was launched in November 2004, during the Tenth Plan (2002-07), so statement I is correct. The Planning Commission was not a constitutional body (it was extra-constitutional), so statement II is wrong.
TRYSEM came with IRDP (about 1979-80), RLEGP in 1983, JRY/JRS in 1989, and EAS in 1993. The order is TRYSEM, RLEGP, JRS, EAS.
The UPA's National Common Minimum Programme (2004) promised 100 days of work a year, which led to NREGA 2005.
MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment per financial year.
The guarantee is 100 days per household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work, not per adult. 150 days is not the mandate.
The National Forest Policy 1988 sets a target of 33% of the country's area under forest/tree cover (66% in hills) for ecological balance, so 33% is correct.
The National Forestry Action Programme aims at one-third of India under forest, so II is correct. Statement I is wrong: forest cover is about 21.76% and dense forest is about 57% of it, not 40%.
Rosewood, ebony and mahogany are characteristic species of tropical wet evergreen forests, which receive over 200 cm of rainfall. They are not typical of deciduous, montane or mangrove forests.

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have mangrove, evergreen and deciduous forests together (North Andamans wet evergreen, Middle Andamans moist deciduous, tidal forests along the coast). The other regions do not combine all three types.
Akbar introduced mansabdari to grade nobles and army, giving each officer a rank, so I and II are right. The ranks were zat and sawar; Chehra is a descriptive roll, not a rank, so III is wrong.
Mansabdari was introduced by Akbar as the graded official nobility, so I is true. Mansabs were not hereditary, as rank and jagir ended with the holder, so II is false.
Zat is the personal rank fixing status and salary, and sawar is the number of cavalrymen to be maintained, so I and II are correct. The notes do not support III.
Dakhili troops were state-paid troops placed under mansabdars, so Dakhili is correct. Walashahi (the option spelled Balashahi) refers to the emperor's bodyguard.
The notes do not mention the Muhtasib. He was the officer who enforced conduct according to the shariat, unlike the Ahadis, mansabdars or the Walashahi bodyguard.
The Mir Bakhshi headed the military department, handling the army, mansabdars and intelligence. The Diwan handles revenue and the Mir Saman the household.
Mauza means a village, not rebellious territory, so this pair is wrong. Khalisa (crown land) and jagir (assignment in lieu of salary) are correctly matched.
IST is reckoned from the 82°30'E meridian, which passes near Mirzapur close to Allahabad (Naini), so Allahabad is the best option; Lucknow appears only in older keys.
India's standard (central) meridian is 82°30'E, from which IST is taken.
India's longitudinal span of about 29° equals roughly 116 minutes, so the time gap between Arunachal and Gujarat is about 2 hours, not 3 or 4.
The International Date Line is the imaginary pole-to-pole line along roughly 180° in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
Root hairs are the main water-absorbing part of the root; water enters them by osmosis from the soil, so they absorb the most water for the plant.
Mitochondria contain their own small circular DNA, apart from nuclear DNA. Centrioles, Golgi apparatus and lysosomes do not carry DNA.
Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, so they can synthesise some of their own proteins. They cannot make a nucleus, chloroplasts or digestive enzymes.
Natural selection, proposed by Darwin, is the main driving mechanism of evolution. Mutation only supplies variation, and acquired characters are not inherited.
Ultrasonic waves are generated by the piezoelectric effect: a quartz crystal vibrates at high frequency when an alternating voltage is applied to it.
Parallel currents in the same direction produce magnetic fields that make the wires attract each other; opposite currents would repel.
Ethane has a C-C single bond (about 154 pm), longer than the double bond in ethene, the triple bond in ethyne or the intermediate bond in benzene.
Animal cells have no cell wall, so animal bodies do not contain cellulose; cellulose is a plant feature. The other options are true of animals.
An ohmic conductor obeys Ohm's law (V proportional to I). Metals like silver do; semiconductors such as germanium and silicon and carbon do not follow it.
Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (σ = 1/ρ), so their product is always 1 for every conductor.
Metals have free electrons and are good conductors of electricity, so they carry current with little loss; this is why household wires are metal.
Mitochondria release energy as ATP by cellular respiration, so they are called the powerhouses of the cell.
Analogous organs have different structure and origin but perform similar functions, such as the wings of a bird and an insect. Homologous organs have the same structure but different functions.
Antipyretics such as paracetamol reduce high fever. Antiseptics act on living tissue against microbes and antibiotics kill bacteria.
A whale is a mammal living in water, so it breathes air with lungs and not gills.
Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells through blood or lymph to other organs.
Adipocytes are the fat-storing cells of adipose connective tissue. Chondrocytes are in cartilage and osteocytes in bone.
Mescaline comes from the peyote cactus, not from Thea chinensis (tea), whose leaves yield caffeine. So the pair is mismatched.
Cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase, which blocks the electron transport chain. Cells then cannot make ATP, so death is very quick.
Earthworms (red worms) have a muscular gizzard that grinds food with the help of small stones.
The UN General Assembly declared 2 October, Gandhi's birth anniversary, the International Day of Non-Violence (2007). The notes do not state this fact.
The hydrogen bomb works by uncontrolled fusion of deuterium and tritium into helium, triggered by a fission bomb. Controlled options describe reactors, and fission describes the atom bomb.
The atom bomb relies on uncontrolled nuclear fission of uranium or plutonium. Fusion is the principle of the hydrogen bomb.
The Sun and other stars produce energy by nuclear fusion, with hydrogen fusing into helium. Fission is not the process in stars.
Hiroshima was bombed first, with the Little Boy U-235 bomb. Nagasaki followed on 9 August 1945.
The atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima (Little Boy) and Nagasaki (Fat Man). Tokyo, Sendai and Miyazaki were not atom-bombed.
A nuclear reactor runs on a controlled fission chain reaction, kept in check by moderators and control rods. Uncontrolled fission describes a bomb, and fusion power is still at the R&D stage.

Statement II is correct because the reactor chain reaction is controlled and the bomb's is not. Statement III is also correct since a reactor's self-sustaining chain reaction is criticality, so operating reactors are 'critical'. Statement I is wrong because reactors do use a chain reaction, and IV is wrong because reactors use moderators.
Linor Abargil was crowned Miss World in 1998. The other options are wrong: Diana Hayden won in 1997 and Aishwarya Rai in 1994.
Panchayati Raj was adopted to decentralise the power of democracy by passing power to elected local bodies. Making people politically aware or educating peasants are not its stated purpose.
Imperium in imperio means a State within a State, i.e. a sub-authority with its own sphere inside a larger State. The other options are not what the Latin phrase means.

The fundamental objects of Panchayati Raj are people's participation in development and democratic decentralisation (I and III). Political accountability and financial mobilisation are not the keyed fundamental objects, so options including II or IV are wrong.

The main purpose of Panchayati Raj is people's participation in development, together with democratic decentralisation. Hence enabling people to participate in developmental administration is correct, not just agricultural output, jobs or political awareness.
Ajanta is a Buddhist cave site whose paintings mainly illustrate Jataka tales (the Buddha's previous births) and Buddhist themes, so they relate to Gautama Buddha, not the epics or Mahavira.

The notes place the main Ajanta phase under the Vakatakas (Harishena, 5th c.), contemporary with the Gupta age, and the site is listed under Gupta art; the Gupta period is the best answer among the options.
Ajanta's themes are Jataka tales, the stories of the Buddha's previous births (e.g. the Chhaddanta Jataka in Cave 10). Panchatantra and Hitopadesha are fable collections, not Ajanta themes.
Gupta coins of Samudragupta show him playing the veena, revealing the Guptas' love for music; the other dynasties' coins are not noted for this.
The tertiary (services) sector is the largest contributor to India's GDP (about 53-54% of GVA), well above secondary and primary.
Mining extracts natural resources, so it is a primary activity; processing, fabrication and manufacturing convert raw materials into goods and are secondary.
Services (about 53%) contribute most to GDP, followed by industry/secondary (about 26%) and agriculture/primary (about 21%), giving Service-Industry-Agriculture.
Bhilai Steel Plant is government-owned or controlled, so it is a public sector enterprise.

The given 2016-17 (AE) GVA shares are not stated in the notes. Services was the largest share at 46.0%, with agriculture at 31.77% only if the figures are matched as in the correct option, which is the only one in line with services dominance.
Fixed costs do not vary with output; expenditure on machines (capital equipment) is fixed, whereas raw material and labour wages vary with output.
The word 'Economics' derives from the Greek word 'oikonomia' (oikos = household, nomos = management).
Goods that can be used completely in place of each other are perfect substitutes; perfect complements are consumed together, while Giffen and Veblen goods are special cases of demand.

A Giffen good is inferior, and its income and substitution effects oppose each other. If the income effect outweighs the substitution effect, demand rises with price; otherwise it falls. Both statements are correct.
When total product begins to decline, marginal product becomes negative, not positive, so pair 4 is wrong.
Under increasing returns, output rises more than proportionately to inputs, so the average cost of production falls; the law is equivalent to decreasing cost.
Total revenue rises while MR is positive, is maximum when MR is zero, and falls when MR is negative, so all three statements are correct.
Price elasticity of demand depends on the nature of the good (necessity or luxury) and on the availability of close substitutes, among other factors, so both statements are correct.
Economic models can be expressed through words, diagrams, tables or equations, not only equations, so statement 3 is incorrect.
Dhana Nanda (Agrammes) was the last Nanda ruler of Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion. Chandragupta Maurya came to power only later.
Alexander died in Babylon in 323 BC. He was not in India or Macedonia when he died, and Taxila is wrong. The notes do not state this fact.
Alexander defeated Porus in the Battle of Hydaspes on the Jhelum. The notes date it to 326 BC; the 327 BC in the question is the Hindu Kush crossing, but Hydaspes is still the correct battle.
Deimachus (Diamcus) was a later envoy of Antiochus I to Bindusara and never came with Alexander. Nearchus, Onesicritus and Aristobulus accompanied him.
Alexander entered India through the Khyber Pass in 326 BC according to the notes, so 326 BC is the matching option. The two 326 BC options are duplicates, and the first is the keyed answer.
The President is elected indirectly by proportional representation using the single transferable vote (Art. 55(3)), so option 2 is right; direct public voting is wrong.
The 70th Amendment (1992) added the elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry to the electoral college.
Article 54 provides for the election of the President by an electoral college; Arts. 74 and 78 concern the Council of Ministers and the PM's duty to inform the President.
The 70th Amendment (1992) added the elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry to the electoral college.
Under Art. 71 all disputes about the President's election are decided only by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final.

The electoral college consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament plus the elected MLAs of States. Option 4 is the only one that includes elected MPs of both Houses, so it is the best choice.
The electors are the elected MPs of both Houses and the elected MLAs (Vidhan Sabha); members of Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad) do not vote, so 1, 2 and 3 are correct.
Under Art. 56 the outgoing President continues in office until his successor enters office, so a delay in the election does not create a vacancy and the VP or CJI does not act.
Statements I, II and III are all correct. Art. 58 requires age 35 or more and no office of profit, and Art. 57 allows re-election any number of times.
The President resigns in writing to the Vice-President, who informs the Speaker.
Under Art. 57 the President can be re-elected any number of times, as there is no term limit.
The President's resignation is addressed in writing to the Vice-President, who informs the Speaker.
A general rise in prices is inflation, which decreases the purchasing power of money, so the same money buys fewer goods.
Headline inflation is measured on the CPI-Combined, which RBI has used as the headline measure since April 2014. WPI was the earlier headline index, and CPI-IW is only for industrial workers' DA.
Demand-pull inflation arises when aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply, so a rise in aggregate demand is its main cause. Cost-push comes from rising input costs, not demand.

Aggregate demand exceeding aggregate supply at full-employment output is the inflationary gap, which is the situation behind demand-pull inflation. Stagflation and the other options do not describe this gap.

The Pal Ghat (Palakkad Gap) lies between the Nilgiris in the north and the Anaimalai in the south, so it is the gap at the Nilgiris' southern end. The other options are not passes there; Goran Ghat is not even in the Western Ghats.
Guru Shikhar is the highest peak of the Aravalli range, near Mt Abu in Sirohi district, Rajasthan.
Satmala Hills are in Maharashtra (between the Tapi and Godavari), so they are not part of the Eastern Ghats. Velikonda is a named Eastern Ghats range in AP.

Mahadeo Hills lie in central India (Satpura, MP) and Mikir Hills are in North-East India, so III and IV are correct. Cardamom Hills are in the Western Ghats (Malabar side), not the Coromandel Coast, so I is wrong, and II is also wrong, which rules out the other options.
Dhupgarh (1,350 m) at Pachmarhi is the highest peak of the Satpura range, in the Mahadeo hills of MP. So the Satpura range is the answer.
Entomology is the study of insects. Ichthyology (fish), parasitology (parasites) and malacology (molluscs) are different fields.

Digital embossing is raised touch printing with no chemicals or solvents and is used for braille maps, so statements I and II are correct. The notes do not cover statement III (NATMO introduction), but the answer given is I, II and III.
Biometrics identifies a person by unique physical or behavioural traits such as fingerprint, iris, voice or gait. The other options are not identification sciences.
Bharati is India's third Antarctic research station, after Dakshin Gangotri and Maitri, so (2) is correct. The other names are not Indian Antarctic bases.
Jai Singh II built observatories (Jantar Mantar) at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura. He did not build one at Allahabad, so (4) is correct.

Abwab were miscellaneous cesses outside the sharia taxes, such as the house tax (ghari), grazing tax (charai) and irrigation tax (haq-i-sharb). So option 4 is right; zakat is a separate religious tax.
Alauddin raised the land revenue to half and introduced price-controlled markets (fixed grain prices). Statement II is also true, since he paid soldiers in cash, so all three are correct.
Wheat, barley and gram were grown in the Sultanate period. Maize was brought later by the Portuguese, so it was not cultivated then.
The two basic Sultanate coins were the silver tanka and the copper jital, both introduced by Iltutmish. Rupiya and dam (daam) belong to Sher Shah's later currency, so option 4 is correct.
Gymnosperms (e.g., pines, cycads) bear naked seeds not enclosed in an ovary or fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits.
Panthera pardus is the leopard; the tiger is Panthera tigris and the lion is Panthera leo. Panther is a general term for leopards/black panthers.
Shark is a fish and therefore cold-blooded (poikilothermic), whereas dolphins, whales and porpoises are mammals and warm-blooded.
An endothermic reaction absorbs heat (energy) from its surroundings; the notes describe energy-absorbing reactions as endergonic, while heat-releasing ones are exothermic.

CO2 is an acidic oxide (forms carbonic acid with water) and turns lime water milky due to calcium carbonate formation. It is not poisonous, only an asphyxiant at high concentration, so statement I is wrong.
In an X-ray tube only about 1% of the electron energy becomes X-rays, and the rest is converted to heat at the target, so heat is generated there.
Methane (firedamp) mixes with air in coal mines and forms an explosive mixture; CO2 and nitrogen are not flammable.
Oxygen is directly used as the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain; glycolysis and fermentation are anaerobic, and the citric acid cycle uses oxygen only indirectly.
Moving left to right across a period, electrons and protons increase by one per element, but the number of shells (the period number) stays the same.
The cut-off wavelength is λ = hc/eV, so it is inversely proportional to the applied potential; doubling V halves the cut-off wavelength.
Ice is just solid water, a pure compound, so it is not a mixture; ice-cream, air and honey are mixtures of several components.
Water contracts, not expands, when heated from 0°C to 4°C (anomalous expansion of water), so the statement about ice expanding uniformly up to 4°C is incorrect.
Water moves by osmosis from low to high solute concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. A cell in a more concentrated medium therefore loses water and shrinks.
Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature; lead, sodium and calcium are solids.
Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; cadmium, germanium and tin are solids.
Hexane is a saturated alkane with a low carbon percentage and burns with a clean flame. Benzene, naphthalene and anthracene are aromatic and carbon-rich, so they burn with a sooty flame.
Apples contain malic acid; nitric and sulphuric acids are strong mineral acids not found in fruits, and formic acid is found in ant stings.
Ripe bananas contain malic acid as their main organic acid; formic acid occurs in ants and the others are mineral acids.
In the Calvin cycle CO2 combines with RuBP to give 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA), the first stable product of carbon fixation. Glucose and starch form later.
Glycolysis breaks down glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate). Ethanol and CO2 form only afterwards in fermentation.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Article 15 only bars discrimination and Article 14 gives equality before law, so they are not the answer.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and prohibits its practice in any form. Article 15 only prohibits discrimination on grounds such as caste, so it is the tempting but wrong option.
Tagore gave up his knighthood in protest at the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (returned 31 May 1919). It had nothing to do with Bengal's partition or the Non-Cooperation Movement.
The Hunter Committee (Disorders Inquiry Committee), set up on 14 October 1919, probed the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. The Welby, Simon and Butler bodies dealt with other matters.
Udham Singh shot Sir Michael O'Dwyer, former Lt. Governor of Punjab, at Caxton Hall in 1940. Dyer, who ordered the firing, was not his target.
Udham Singh shot Sir Michael O'Dwyer in London on 13 March 1940. General Dyer was not the man he killed.
Swadeshi (1905) came first, then Jallianwala Bagh (1919), Dandi March (1930) and Quit India (1942). So the order is D, B, A, C.
Pherozeshah Mehta died in 1915, then came Jallianwala Bagh (1919), the Simon Commission (1927-28) and the Dandi March (1930). The order is IV, II, I, III.
Only C. Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest at the massacre. So only option 1 is correct.

Harappa is linked with its cemetery (Cemetery R-37, with Cemetery H also noted there), Lothal with the dockyard, Kalibangan with the ploughed (furrowed) field, and Mohenjodaro with the bronze Dancing Girl. This gives A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3, which is option (4).

Harappan sculptures were made of bronze (lost-wax), steatite and red sandstone, so stone and metal were used, but iron was not used for sculpting; Harappan culture was a Bronze Age culture. Hence the iron statement is incorrect.
Harappan pottery was wheel-made and typically red with black painted designs; plain red ware was the most common. Hence red is correct.
Harappan pottery was wheel-made and typically red with black painted designs; plain red ware was the most common. Hence red is correct.

Statement I is the accepted description of BIMSTEC, linking South and Southeast Asia. Statement II is wrong: BIMSTEC began in 1997 as BIST-EC under the Bangkok Declaration, not as the 'Bangkok Agreement'.
The Windsor Framework (February 2023) is the UK-EU arrangement concerning Northern Ireland.

The EU grew out of the European Community (EEC, Treaty of Rome) and was formed through the Single European Act and Maastricht, so I and II are correct. Switzerland is not an EU member, so IV is wrong; the answer is I, II and III.
The European Union was founded by the Maastricht Treaty (1992, in force 1993). The Treaty of Rome 1957 only created the EEC, its forerunner.
Brexit is the UK's exit from the European Union under Article 50 TEU, completed on 31 January 2020.

The EU has its own flag, anthem and currency, and is among the world's largest economies, with armed forces combined from its members. It has no formal Constitution, so IV is wrong and the answer is I, II and III.
After the 2016 Brexit referendum, Cameron resigned and Theresa May, the Home Secretary, became Conservative leader and PM. The Conservatives stayed in power, so the opposition did not come to power.
The June 2015 Greek referendum asked voters whether to accept the bailout conditions proposed by the EU and IMF creditors. It was not about leaving the EU.

Southeast Asia's geostrategic importance rests mainly on its position between the Pacific and Indian oceans and its maritime character, which makes it the link for sea lanes. The other options are historical or partial explanations.
The SCO Summit of 15-16 September 2022 was held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
UNICEF (UN Children's Fund) has the mandate of children's rights and well-being. WTO and IMF are economic bodies, and UNESCO deals with education, science and culture.
UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, set up in 1972 after the Stockholm Conference.
The United Nations headquarters is in New York. Geneva hosts only its European office and several agencies.
ECOSOC is a principal organ of the UN and is headquartered at UN headquarters in New York.
WFP is headquartered in Rome, not Geneva, along with FAO and IFAD (the Rome food trio).
UNIDO is headquartered in Vienna. UNESCO is in Paris, ILO in Geneva, and IMF in Washington DC.
WFP is headquartered in Rome, not Geneva, with the other food agencies FAO and IFAD.
WMO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
Y.K. Modi was elected to the ILO Governing Body, the ILO's tripartite executive body.
India chaired the 68th session of the Commission on Narcotic Drugs (CND) in March 2025. It was the CND, not UNODC or a UN Drug Control Programme.
Jagjit Pavadia was elected to the INCB in 2014 and re-elected for 2020-2025.
ILO stands for International Labour Organisation, a UN specialised agency headquartered in Geneva.
The 97th Amendment (2011, notified 2012) gave constitutional status to co-operative societies: Art. 19(1)(c), Art. 43B and Part IXB. It has nothing to do with education, terrorism or Lokpal.

All four statements are true: the 97th Amendment made forming co-operatives a Fundamental Right under Art. 19(1)(c), added DPSP Art. 43B and inserted Part IXB (Arts 243ZH-243ZT), thereby giving co-operatives constitutional status.

The Bill that became the 102nd Amendment (2018) gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (Art. 338B), so option 1 is correct. The 103rd number in the question is the Bill's number in the Parliament, not the Amendment Act number.
The Barail range in Assam links the Naga and Mizo hills and so separates Manipur from Nagaland. Patkai lies on the Myanmar border and Arakan is in Myanmar, so neither fits.
Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya lie in that order from west to east, and the Naga Hills lie further east in Nagaland. This gives Garo-Khasi-Jaintia-Naga.
Manipur is largely made up of hills (the Manipur Hills), with the plain limited to the Loktak/Imphal valley, so most of its topography is mountainous.
The Indian Nation was founded in 1931 by Kameshwar Singh of Darbhanga and was published from Patna; the other papers are not linked to Patna in the notes.
Abdul Ghaffar Khan started the Pashto periodical 'Pukhtun' (Dash Roza); the notes do not cover this, so no line is linked.

The Censorship of Press Act of 1799 was passed under Wellesley as wartime pre-censorship, so he primarily implemented press censorship. John Adams' 1823 regulations were licensing rules, not the primary censorship.
Wood's Despatch was 1854, the VPA 1878, the first Factory Act 1881 and the Famine Code 1883. This matches a-III, b-II, c-IV, d-I.
Macaulay made this remark in his 1835 Minute on education, arguing for English-medium teaching of Western learning.

NTR Sujala is Andhra Pradesh's scheme to supply safe, purified drinking water to villagers, so option 1 is right. The notes do not mention NTR Sujala; they cover only JJM and other drinking-water programmes.
The Rio Grande forms much of the border between Mexico and the United States (Texas). It does not separate Canada from the US or Mexico from Guatemala.
Volga flows into the Caspian and Zambezi into the Indian Ocean, so III and IV are right. Mekong flows into the South China Sea (not Andaman), and the Thames into the North Sea (not Irish Sea).
The Limpopo flows in southern Africa and crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice as it loops around. The Congo crosses the Equator twice, and the Niger and Zambezi do not cross the Tropic twice.
Pygmies are native to the equatorial rainforests of the Congo basin in central Africa. The Niger, Nile and Zambezi basins are not their typical home.
Ganga is in Asia, Nile in Africa, Amazon in South America and Volga in Europe, giving 1-c, 2-d, 3-b, 4-a.
The Mughal order is Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb. Akbar, Shah Jahan, Jahangir reverses the last two, so it is the incorrect sequence.
Jahangir banned tobacco smoking in his reign. The notes do not state this, but Akbar, Babur and Aurangzeb are not known for the ban.
Akbar, a great patron of music, learnt Hindu music from Lala Kalavant. The notes do not mention this fact.
The notes say the Naqshbandi order came to India with Babur, so Babur is the Mughal emperor who followed the Naqshbandi saint Ubaidullah Ahrar. Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul was opposed by the Naqshbandis.
Lord Mayo is the only Viceroy murdered in office, killed by the convict Sher Ali Afridi in the Andamans in 1872. The other options were not assassinated in India.
The Ilbert Bill (1883) controversy, the so-called 'White Mutiny', occurred under Lord Ripon. Lytton is the tempting wrong option but is not linked with it.
The INC was founded in 1885 when Lord Dufferin (1884-88) was Viceroy. Ripon had left office in 1884.
Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946. Ambedkar chaired only the Drafting Committee and Nehru was not the presiding officer.
Dr B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Prasad presided over the Assembly itself and Nehru was not even a member of the Drafting Committee.
Nehru was not a member of the Drafting Committee, whereas Saadullah, Munshi and Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar were members.
Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, not the Assembly.
The Advisory Committee (on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas) was chaired by Sardar Patel. Nehru chaired the Union committees and B.N. Rau was only the Constitutional Adviser.
The Union Powers Committee, dealing with federal subjects, was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru. Patel chaired the Advisory and Provincial Constitution committees.
The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946 in the Constitution Hall, New Delhi. 26 January 1950 was the commencement of the Constitution and 15 August 1947 was independence.
The first session of the Constituent Assembly began on 9 December 1946 in the Constitution Hall, New Delhi. The other dates given do not match any opening of the Assembly.
The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. Option 4 lists exactly these; the others omit some or add German or Hindi.
The Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, which is observed as UN Day.
The UN came into being when the Charter entered into force on 24 October 1945.
The Charter was signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945 by 50 nations, with Poland later becoming the 51st original member.
The Security Council is the only UN body whose decisions bind members, so a resolution deploying monitors was adopted by it, not by the General Assembly or the ICJ.
The UN has six principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ and Secretariat.
Only the P5 (China, France, Russia, UK, USA) have veto power. Canada is not one of them.
The P5 are China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA.
Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was President of the UNGA, the first Indian woman to hold the post.
Antonio Guterres of Portugal is the present Secretary-General, serving since 2017. Ban Ki-moon and Kofi Annan are former SGs.
Flooded low-land rice fields are anaerobic (no oxygen), so decomposition there releases methane; the other options are not the main gas from paddies.
Rice fields, coal mines and domestic animals are human sources of methane, and wetlands are the largest natural source, so all four are sources.
Fossil-fuel burning, oil-driven automobiles and deforestation are causes of warming, while solar flares are not a cause, so I, II and IV are correct.
Flooded paddies are anaerobic and emit methane, and nitrogen fertilisers release N2O, so rice cultivation contributes through both; both statements are correct.

Wetlands are the largest natural source of methane; automobile exhaust and industrial chimneys are not listed as methane sources, while mining is also a source but wetland is the best-fit answer given.
Beyond about 3°C the land biosphere may turn from carbon sink to source, so statement I is right. Statements III and IV are extreme claims, so only I and II hold.
Black carbon is a short-lived pollutant formed by incomplete combustion; it darkens snow and ice, lowering albedo. It is not methane, not from CFCs, and does not directly deplete ozone.

The CCAC tackles short-lived climate pollutants such as black carbon, methane and HFCs, so statement II is correct. Nothing in the notes supports statement I that it is a unique G20 initiative, so I is wrong.

Global warming gives rising sea levels, air pollution gives respiratory illness, and sub-regional temperature shows patches of cooling; habitat loss leads to biodiversity extinction. This matches A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4.
Global warming causes melting glaciers, weather changes (such as early flowering) and health risks. Better global communication is not an effect of global warming.
All four, melting glaciers, sea-level rise, weather changes and rising temperature, are impacts of global warming.
Global warming raises sea level, which changes coastlines, and alters weather, which affects crop patterns, so all the options are expected results.

A tax is a compulsory pecuniary burden imposed by legislative authority to support the government, with no quid pro quo. A fee is paid for a specific service and a cess is for a specific purpose, so neither fits.
The Swachh Bharat cess of 0.5% was levied on all taxable services. The notes do not state this fact, but the cess was an add-on to service tax, so it applied only where service tax was payable.

Income tax is shared with the States on Finance Commission advice. Expenditure tax falls under the Union's residuary power, and corporation tax and customs duty are Union-levied. Income tax is the intended answer, as the notes list it first among the shared taxes.

Corporation tax is levied and collected by the Union alone and is not levied by States. The question's intended answer treats it as accruing to the Centre, unlike income tax or excise, which are shared.
Article 276 caps the profession tax, a State levy, at ₹2,500 per year, so ₹2,500 is correct.

PR gives seats in proportion to votes, so minority groups obtain representation, which is why it helps minorities in multi-party systems. It does not guarantee majority rule or stable government; instability is a reason PR was rejected for Lok Sabha.

The right to vote and the right to contest are statutory political rights, and the right to complain to executive bodies is also political. The right to life is a Fundamental Right under Art. 21 (a civil right), not a political right.

Statement II is wrong: under Sec. 8 a person sentenced to at least 2 years is disqualified only during imprisonment plus 6 years after release, not permanently. Statement I is also wrong, since a minister may serve six months without being a member of the Legislature, but the eligibility condition as framed is not the constitutional test, so neither is correct.

An overseas elector must be an Indian citizen enrolled in the electoral roll at the passport address (Sec. 20A, RPA 1950). He must also be present in person at the polling station to vote, so all three conditions apply.

India uses direct election on adult suffrage (Lok Sabha, Assembly) and PR by single transferable vote (President, Rajya Sabha, Councils). The list system and cumulative voting are not used, so only I and II are correct.

Universal adult franchise under Art. 326 gives every citizen aged 18+ the right to vote, subject to statutory disqualifications such as non-residence, unsound mind, crime or corrupt practice. The other options are unrelated to franchise.
A floating constituency has no fixed geographical boundary, and Sangha in Sikkim is the example where only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest. Both statements are therefore correct.
The Anganwadi Worker is the grassroots, honorary ICDS functionary running the Anganwadi Centre; the CDPO is a block-level officer and the ANM belongs to NHM.
NIPCCD trains the CDPO, the block-level ICDS officer, so option 3 is correct.
The Anganwadi Worker is the grassroots ICDS functionary running the Anganwadi Centre; the CDPO works at block level and the ANM belongs to NHM.
ICDS is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by States/UTs, with costs shared between Centre and States (e.g. 60:40 for general States), so it is neither fully Central nor fully State funded.
POSHAN Abhiyaan (earlier National Nutrition Mission) is the 2018 flagship nutrition programme, launched on 8 March 2018.
ALIVA is a data-driven model to end child marriage in Nayagarh district, Odisha.
Creches were first started by the Central Social Welfare Board for children of working mothers, later becoming the Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme and then Palna.
Nellore is first in mica production and reserves in AP (Gudur belt). Kadapa is the tempting wrong option, since it is known for barytes and uranium.
Nellore is first in mica production and reserves in AP (Gudur belt). Kadapa is the tempting wrong option, since it is known for barytes and uranium.
Ramagiri in Anantapur is an old gold field, so Anantapur is famous for gold. Copper, zinc and lead are associated with Guntur and Kurnool regions.

Manganese is in Vizianagaram (Garividi/Garbham), bauxite in the forest areas of Visakhapatnam and East Godavari, mica in Nellore, and limestone in the Kadapa region. This gives a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III.
Apatite is not stated as an AP-only mineral in the notes, which only list apatite at Kasipatnam, Visakhapatnam. Apatite is the answer because AP is the sole producer in India.
After beach sands, bauxite (Araku–Chintapalle, Visakhapatnam region) makes up the largest share of AP's major mineral resources, ahead of limestone and hematite. Calcite is not a major mineral.
Upparpalle is listed among GSI diamond signs in Kadapa district, so Kadapa is correct.
The National Mineral Inventory figure is 18.23 lakh carats, which is 1,822,955 carats.
AP is first in India in mica, with 40.5% of reserves and 70.2% of production, ahead of Rajasthan.
Mica is found in the Gudur belt of Nellore. Calcite, soapstone (Kadapa) and black granite (Prakasam) are not Nellore resources.
India's first and largest private-sector gold mine after Independence is Swarnagiri (Jonnagiri) in Tuggali mandal, Kurnool district.
Beach sands run from the Srikakulam coast to the Krishna coast, including Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram, but Kurnool is inland and has none.
The principal uranium deposit of AP, Tummalapalle, is in YSR Kadapa district, so Kadapa is correct.
The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya ruler. The other options are not linked to the Kakatiya genealogy.
The Kazipet Dargah inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I, naming him the first Kakatiya ruler. The other inscriptions listed are not the source for this claim.
The Magallu grant (956) of the Eastern Chalukya Danarnava is the first mention of the Kakatiyas (Gundyana). Bayyaram (1219) is a later inscription giving the fuller genealogy.

Seasons arise from the Earth's revolution combined with its tilted axis, which changes the angle of insolation and day length. Aphelion/perihelion distance is not the cause, since Earth is nearest the Sun in northern winter.
The tilt of the axis combined with revolution changes day length through the year. Oceans, mountains or altitude do not cause this.
Perihelion is the point in Earth's orbit nearest the Sun (about 3 January), so the answer is nearest to the Sun; aphelion is the farthest point.
The Sun is overhead at the Equator in March and September, never at the Arctic Circle. So the September–Arctic Circle pair is wrong.
The longest day in the Northern Hemisphere occurs at the summer solstice, 21 June, when the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer.
Between 21 March and 23 September the Sun is north of the Equator and the North Pole is tilted towards it, so it has continuous daylight. On 21 June alone is too narrow.
Dayananda Saraswati gave the call 'Back to the Vedas', treating the four Vedas as infallible, and so led the Vedic revival; Ramakrishna, Ramanuja and Vivekananda are not associated with this.
The slogan 'Back to the Vedas' was Dayananda Saraswati's call on the Vedas, not that of Lala Hansraj or Lajpat Rai, who were his later followers.
Satyarth Prakash was written by Dayananda Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj, and sets out its philosophy, so it is the Arya Samaj's sacred book.

Statement I is wrong, since the Arya Samaj was founded in 1875, not 1835. Statement II is wrong, since Lajpat Rai was influenced by the Arya Samaj and did not oppose it. Statements III and IV are accepted, so the answer is III and IV.

Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 and held that caste was to be decided by merit and conduct, not birth, so it repudiated caste by birth. He was also born in a Brahmin family (Mool Shankar Tiwari), so all three statements are correct.

The Arya Samaj introduced Shuddhi, and its moderate College party under Hansraj and Lajpat Rai set up the DAV colleges. It also had a base among the trading castes, so I, II and III are correct. Statement IV is not supported.

The Arya Samaj's strongest base was Punjab and the United Provinces, and it drew mainly on trading castes, so I and II are correct. III is wrong because its base was not more limited than the Brahmo Samaj's.
The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875.
The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875.
Japan is regarded as the most earthquake-prone nation, as it lies on the Circum-Pacific Ring of Fire subduction belt.
L'Aquila is a city in the Abruzzo region of central Italy, hit by a deadly earthquake in 2009. So option 4 is correct; the castle and beach options are wrong.
The largest earthquake ever recorded, M 9.5 on 22 May 1960, struck Chile (Valdivia), not Alaska or Japan.
Zone V, the very high risk zone, covers the entire North-East and Kutch. Zone IV covers areas such as Delhi and the Indo-Gangetic belt.
Delhi is in Seismic Zone IV per the Earthquake Disaster Risk Index Report 2019. Kolkata, Mumbai and Chennai are in lower zones.
Bhuj (Kutch) lies in Zone V, so it is not in Zone IV. Delhi and the Himalayan foothill areas are in Zone IV.
Zone II is the low-risk, least active zone in the current four-zone map. Zone I was merged into Zone II.
About 56% of India's area lies in Zones III-V, which are moderate to very high risk.
As per BIS, Visakhapatnam is in Zone II, the low-risk stable Peninsula zone. Vijayawada is Zone III.
New Delhi falls in Seismic Zone IV (high risk).
The National War Memorial was inaugurated in February 2019, not 2021, so statement I is wrong. Statements II, III and IV are correct, so the answer is II, III and IV only.
