Census 2011 recorded about 332 million male workers, so option 4 is correct; the notes give no support for the other figures (382 million total, 1.78% and 1.98% growth rates).
The first Census of the modern system was held in 1872 under Lord Mayo. 1881 was the first regular Census, which is the tempting alternative.
The first regular, scientific Census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon. The 1872 Census was the first of the modern system but not the first regular one.
In Census 2011, 72.4% of workers were in rural areas. The 68.8% figure is the rural share of the population, not of workers.

The unorganised sector is made up of small, scattered units largely outside government control, with low pay and no job security. Organised-sector units are registered and regulated; disguised and seasonal are types of unemployment, not sectors.
Kandla (Deendayal) is a tidal port in Gujarat, located on the Gulf of Kutch; the notes confirm it is a tidal port in Gujarat but do not name the gulf.
Mormugao (Marmugao) is a major port on the west coast in Goa.
Tamil Nadu (Chennai, Kamarajar, VOC) has three major ports; Maharashtra also has three in the notes, but West Bengal and Odisha have one each, and Tamil Nadu is the intended answer.
The Central Inland Water Transport Corporation has its headquarters in Kolkata.
Statement I is wrong: 111 National Waterways have been declared, not three. Statement II is wrong: NW-1 (1,620 km) is longer than the Brahmaputra NW-2 (891 km), so neither is correct.
Alang-Sosiya, the major ship-breaking yard, is in Gujarat on the Gulf of Khambhat.
Air transport was nationalised in 1953 under the Air Corporations Act, not 1947.
KLM, the Dutch airline founded in 1919, is the oldest airline still operating under its original name.
The Civil Aviation Training Centre is at Allahabad (Prayagraj).
The Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi (IGRUA) is at Fursatganj, Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh.
Lufthansa is the flag carrier airline of Germany.
In 2009-10 Asia and ASEAN was the largest region in India's import share, so option 1 is correct.
The notes list the USA as India's largest trading partner in 2023-24 and 2024-25, ahead of China and UAE. (The notes also mention China overtaking in FY 2025-26, but the answer given is USA.)
China is India's top import source (15.73% of imports in 2024-25), ahead of Russia and the UAE.
The composition of imports has undergone structural transformation (shift in major items over time), while exports grew rather than stagnated. The notes have no line stating this directly.
Services were in surplus, so lacklustre services is not a cause of the deficit. The 1997-98 crisis, China competition and non-tariff barriers are listed causes.
The notes give India's share in world exports as 1.7% in 2018, so option 1 is correct.
Amitabh Bachchan received the 50th Dadasaheb Phalke Award (for 2018), so he is the correct choice; the notes do not list this recipient.
Hellaro (Gujarati) was named Best Feature Film at the 66th National Film Awards (2018 films); Uri won other awards, such as Best Director.
At the 66th National Film Awards, Best Actor was shared by Ayushmann Khurrana (Andhadhun) and Vicky Kaushal (Uri).
Emil Jannings won the first Best Actor Oscar, at the first Academy Awards (1929), for The Last Command and The Way of All Flesh.
Amitabh Bachchan received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 4th Asian Film Awards (2010); the notes do not cover this.
The Ekalavya Award is the sports award of Madhya Pradesh; Arjuna is a national award, and the other options are not MP sports awards.
Jasprit Bumrah received the Polly Umrigar Award (International Cricketer of the Year) for 2018-19 from the BCCI.
The first Dronacharya Awards in 1985 went to O.M. Nambiar, O.P. Bhardwaj and B.B. Bhagwat, so 'All of the above' is correct.
The Arjuna Award is a national sports award for outstanding sportspersons; the other options are not sports awards.
P.V. Sindhu won the BWF Most Improved Player of the Year award for 2016.
Virender Sehwag was named a Wisden Leading Cricketer in the World for 2008 and 2009, so he is the correct answer; the notes do not cover this.
Green hydrogen is made by electrolysis of water using renewable power. Coal gasification gives brown hydrogen and methane pyrolysis gives turquoise hydrogen, so those options are wrong.
Green hydrogen is made by electrolysis of water using renewable power. Coal gasification gives brown hydrogen and methane pyrolysis gives turquoise hydrogen, so those options are wrong.
The Union Cabinet approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission on 4 January 2023, so the correct month is January 2023.
The Mission was approved by the Union Cabinet on 4 January 2023, not in 2022 or May 2023.

Statement I is correct: with pure hydrogen the fuel cell produces electricity, water and heat. Statements II and III are wrong because fuel cells can power small devices too, and they produce DC, not AC.

The CSP worked for socialism inside the Congress, among workers and peasants. None of the three statements fits: boycott of goods and tax evasion is not its programme, it did not aim at a dictatorship of the proletariat, and it never sought separate electorates. So 'None of these' is correct.
The Bihar Socialist Party was founded in 1931 by Jayaprakash Narayan inside the Congress, so 1931 is correct.

The Second International was the socialist body formed in 1889 (Paris) to coordinate socialist parties across Europe. The Social Democratic Party and the Labour Party are national parties, and the Commune was the 1871 Paris uprising.
Plekhanov, Zasulich, Kollontai and Lenin were all Russian Marxists. The other groups mix different traditions: Rousseau with Bonaparte, Jefferson with Lincoln, and Marx with Mill, who was a liberal.

Both parties were communist-oriented workers' and peasants' parties. The Labour Swaraj Party (Calcutta, 1925) became the Workers and Peasants Party, and the Kirti Kisan Party was a Punjab communist-leaning peasant party.
The Russian Revolution of 1917 occurred during the reign of Tsar Nicholas II, the last Romanov emperor, who abdicated in March 1917.
Marx held that history is the history of class struggle, a succession of conflicts between oppressor and oppressed classes. It is not merely a record of wars or of past events.

AITUC was founded in 1920 and Lala Lajpat Rai was its first president, so statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1929 split by moderates led to a different body, and the notes do not credit Dange with forming the All India Trade Union Federation.

Abolition of titles is in Art. 18 (Part III, Fundamental Rights); organisation of village panchayats is Art. 40 (DPSP); the duty of a parent/guardian to provide education to a child aged 6-14 is Art. 51A(k) (Fundamental Duties); 'India, that is Bharat, is a Union of States' is Art. 1 (The Union and its Territories). This gives A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2.

The Civil Disobedience Movement began when Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930 after the march. The Purna Swaraj declaration at Lahore (1929) preceded it and only authorised the movement.
Purna Swaraj was adopted at the Lahore session in December 1929, not at Calcutta in 1928.
Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) was adopted as the Congress goal at Lahore in 1929, not at Calcutta in 1928.
Jawaharlal Nehru, as president, hoisted the tricolour at midnight on 31 December 1929 on the banks of the Ravi at Lahore.
Jawaharlal Nehru, the Lahore session president, hoisted the tricolour on the Ravi bank at midnight on 31 December 1929.
Jawaharlal Nehru presided at Lahore, moved the Purna Swaraj resolution and declared the aim.
Complete independence (Purna Swaraj) was first adopted as the Congress goal at the Lahore session in December 1929.
The Purna Swaraj demand was adopted at Lahore in 1929; Calcutta 1928 only accepted the Nehru Report on Dominion Status.
The Purna Swaraj resolution was passed at the Lahore session on 31 December 1929.
After the Lahore resolution, Congress observed 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day.
Jawaharlal Nehru was Congress president at Lahore 1929, where the Purna Swaraj resolution was passed.
The 'Mahatma Gandhi' prefix was added to NREGA on 2 October 2009 by amendment, making it MGNREGA.
The Act's unit is the rural household, whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work; it is not limited to SC/ST, BPL or backward communities, so 'any household' is right.
NREGS was extended to the whole country (all 625 districts) on 1 April 2008, so 01-04-2008 is correct.
MGNREGA offers guaranteed wage employment for unskilled manual work, not skilled labour, so option 1 is not an objective; livelihood security is an objective.
Geo-tagging of MGNREGA assets is done via the ISRO's Bhuvan mobile platform (GeoMGNREGA).
SGRY (Sept 2001) replaced JGSY and EAS. SGSY was a separate self-employment scheme, so B and C only is correct.
Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan was launched in 2020 as a campaign for returnee migrant workers.
JRY (1989) aimed to generate employment for the rural unemployed and strengthen rural economic and social structure, so all the statements hold and 'All of the above' is right.

National Career Service is a job-matching portal under the Labour & Employment ministry, not the Department of Personnel and Training, so statement I is wrong. Statement II is also wrong, since it is not meant only for uneducated youth.

The notes give the 1973 AP Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act and its provisions, but none states that it followed the Central Land Reforms Committee's suggestions. The answer is therefore not supported by the notes.
Art. 58 sets only a minimum age of 35 years and prescribes no maximum age, so there is no upper age limit.
The President resigns in writing to the Vice-President, who then informs the Speaker; it is not sent to the Speaker, CJI or PM.
The President's emoluments are fixed by Parliament by law and listed in the Second Schedule, so the answer is the 2nd Schedule.
Under Art. 57 a person can be re-elected any number of times; there is no term limit, so there is no restriction.
Under Art. 61 the only ground for impeachment is violation of the Constitution; the other options are not grounds.
Under Art. 61 the charge can be preferred in either House, by a resolution signed by one-fourth of its members after 14 days' notice.
The President is removed by impeachment, which needs a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament. Neither the PM, the CJI nor the Lok Sabha alone can remove him.
The President can be removed before the term expires only by impeachment under Art. 61, not by the party, the PM or a court.
Impeachment is carried out by the two Houses of Parliament: the charge is passed by two-thirds in one House and investigated and passed by two-thirds in the other.
The impeachment charge can be preferred in either House of Parliament, so any House can initiate it.
Art. 61 lays down the procedure for impeachment of the President.
Removal of the President by impeachment is governed by Art. 61; Art. 71 deals with election disputes.
Art. 61 deals with impeachment; Art. 60 is the oath.
Impeachment can be initiated in either House, and both Houses take part, the second investigating the charge. Of the options, the Houses of Parliament are the body with this power, not the Speaker.
If both the President and VP offices are vacant, the CJI (or the senior-most SC judge) acts as President under the 1969 Act, not the PM.
Azolla is a water fern that lives with the cyanobacterium Anabaena, which is a blue-green alga, and this partnership fixes nitrogen for paddy.

All three statements are correct. Neem oil is a pesticide against insects and mites, neem seeds are used for bio-fuel and detergents, and neem oil is used in pharmaceuticals. The notes only confirm the pesticide use.
Birds, dust, rain and wind all carry fungal spores, bacteria or other pathogens from plant to plant, so all four spread plant diseases.
Green hair (downy mildew) is a disease of bajra, not rice, so the pair 'Rice – Green hair' is wrongly matched. Ergot in bajra, powdery mildew in pea and wilt in gram are correct pairs.
Yellow vein mosaic of okra is a viral disease transmitted by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci), so it is not caused by aphids, leafhoppers or fungi.
Zinc phosphide is a rodenticide used as rat poison. The sulphides and calcium phosphate are not rodenticides.

The APPSC key lists trousers, heavy long coat, helmet and boots as the items introduced by the Shakas and Kushanas, and excludes the turban. So options including the turban are wrong and II, III, IV and V is correct.
Kanishka's coronation is dated to 78 AD, which marks the start of the Saka era usually credited to him. The other dates do not match.
Germanium is a metalloid semiconductor used in chips (with silicon); radium, sodium and sulphur are not used for this.
Radon is a noble gas with a very low melting point (about -71 C), far lower than sodium, tin or radium.
The joule is the SI unit of energy; pascal measures pressure, and calorie and horsepower are not the SI energy unit (horsepower is a unit of power).
A rectifier (using diodes) converts AC into DC; a transformer only changes AC voltage.
A transformer works on AC and steps voltage up or down by mutual induction; generators and motors do not do this.
Proteins are synthesised by ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum, not in the cell membrane or Golgi, and they are not absorbed directly from food.
Metallic oxides are basic, while non-metallic oxides are acidic, so II is false; all acids share similar properties (H+ release), so I and III are correct.
Esters have sweet, fruity smells; ammonia is pungent and alcohols are not typically sweet-smelling.
A compound always has the same elemental proportion by mass regardless of source, which is the law of constant (definite) proportions.
Hydrogen fluoride attacks and etches glass (silicon dioxide), so it is used to write on glass; graphite and others do not.
Hydrogen bonding makes ice an open lattice, so ice is less dense than liquid water.
NaOH is a strong base that dissociates into ions, conducting electricity and giving a basic solution; HCl and CH3COOH are acids, and CH3OH does not ionise.
The oxyacetylene flame (acetylene burning in oxygen) gives the highest flame temperature (~3000 C), used for welding; nitrogen does not support burning.
Insulators have electrons, but they are tightly bound and do not flow easily; so option 2 is right.
A body becomes negatively charged by gaining electrons; protons are not transferred in charging.
Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, but have a cell wall, plasma membrane and ribosomes.

Plant cells have a cell wall (and chloroplasts), but of the options only the cell wall is the one distinguishing feature listed besides chloroplast; the key gives the cell wall, as animal cells lack it while having a membrane and nucleus.
The plasma membrane is made of lipids and proteins and has no nucleic acid; the nucleolus, chloroplast and ribosome contain RNA or DNA.
Chloroplasts contain their own DNA and ribosomes and can divide independently, so they are considered a cell within a cell.
Active transport moves ions against the concentration gradient and requires energy (ATP); diffusion is passive.
The ruling elite of the Mamluk Sultanate were Turks, as the notes show with the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty), the Turkish military nobility. So Turkish is the correct class.
Aibak died in 1210 at Lahore after falling from his horse while playing chaugan (polo), not in battle or by assassination.
The notes confirm the title Lakh Bakhsh for Aibak. Zil-i-Ilahi (IV) was Balban's concept of kingship, so the option with I and IV is wrong. The notes do not mention Kuran Khan.
Iltutmish was the first Sultan to bring in regular coins and to make Delhi the capital.
Iltutmish moved the capital from Lahore to Delhi.
The notes do not mention Iltutmish's appointment of a governor in Bihar. Malik Jani is recorded elsewhere as the first governor of Bihar under Iltutmish.

During Iltutmish's reign Chengiz (Genghis) Khan came in pursuit of Jalaluddin Mangbarni, and Iltutmish refused shelter to Mangbarni, which kept Chengiz Khan out of India. The other options were not Mongol invaders.
Chengiz Khan's Mongols appeared at the Indus in pursuit of Mangbarni during Iltutmish's reign.
Razia was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Chand Bibi, Durgawati and Nur Jahan came later.
Turkish nobles resented Razia's favour to the Abyssinian Yaqut and rebelled, which led to her imprisonment and fall. So Turks were responsible.
Imaduddin Raihan was the Indian Muslim leader who briefly displaced Balban in Nasiruddin Mahmud's reign. Altuniya and Qabacha belong to other periods.
Balban, the naib (principal minister) of Nasiruddin Mahmud, held the title Ulugh Khan.
Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian state RTI law in 1997 (Goa followed the same year), so 1997 is correct.
The Freedom of Information Act 2002 was never notified and was repealed by the RTI Act 2005, so 2002 is correct.
The Right to Information Act was enacted in 2005 (assent on 15 June 2005, fully in force on 12 October 2005), so 2005 is correct.
The RTI Act is a statutory right that mandates a timely response to citizens' requests for information. The other options are not about information access.

Under Section 2(j), the right to information covers inspection of work and records, notes, extracts, certified copies, certified samples and electronic information. This includes inspection of documents and information in tapes or electronic form, but not taking files out of the office.

The first appeal is within 30 days and life or liberty cases need 48 hours, so B and C are correct. The normal reply time is 30 days, not 45, and the second appeal is within 90 days, so A and D are wrong.

In CPIO, Supreme Court v Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2019), the Constitution Bench held that the CJI's office is a public authority under the RTI Act. CBI is in the Second Schedule, so it is not the answer.

Farakka (WB) is where the Ganga splits into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly and the Padma; the barrage was built to divert Ganga water into the Hooghly and augment its flow. The notes only give the split, not the stated purpose.
The Saran and Triveni canals take water from the Gandak (barrage at Balmiki Nagar), so Gandak is correct.
The Indira Gandhi canal system, serving Bikaner, draws on the Sutlej, Beas and Ravi from Harike; the Bikaner canal is taken off from the Sutlej (the Gang canal, also from the Sutlej, served Bikaner).
The Indira Gandhi Canal starts from the Harike Barrage at the Beas–Sutlej confluence, not from Bhakra, Rihand or Hirakud.
Tilpara Barrage is on the Mayurakshi river (Siuri, West Bengal), so option 4 is correct; the notes only mention the Mayurakshi in passing.
Dul Hasti (Dulhasti), 390 MW, is on the Chenab in Kishtwar district, so Chenab is correct.
Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti are all on the Chenab in J&K, so 'Chenab only' is correct; Jhelum and Indus are not involved.
The Green Revolution rested on HYV seeds (wheat first, then rice) with fertiliser and irrigation. Grey, Silver and White refer to fertilisers, eggs and milk.
NAP 2000 set a growth target of over 4% per annum for agriculture, so 4 is correct.

AOI (SDG 2.a.1) is agriculture's share of government spending divided by agriculture's share of GDP, so III is right. It is compiled by FAO, not IFPRI, so I is wrong. II is correct as it tracks SDG 2.
The order of rulers is Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I, Skandagupta, which is (iii), (i), (iv), (ii).
Vishnugupta (c. 540-550 CE) was the last ruler of the Gupta line. Samudragupta was an early king, and Bimbisara and Ashoka were not Guptas.
Fa-Hien came to India c. 399-412 CE, which falls within the reign of Chandragupta II (c. 380-415 CE).
Chandragupta II is known as Vikramaditya, a title linked with his victory over the Sakas. The other options are different rulers.
Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I (c. 450 AD). Chandragupta II, Dharmapala and Pushyagupta are not its founders.
Skandagupta repulsed the Hunas twice. Samudragupta, Chandragupta II and Ramagupta are not credited with this.
Skandagupta repulsed the Hunas. Kumaragupta I faced only the first attack late in his reign, and the others are not credited with defeating them.
Skandagupta checked the first Huna attack as a prince and defeated them again as king, so the Huna invasions fell in his reign. The other options do not fit as well.
Skandagupta defeated the Hunas, as recorded in the Bhitari pillar inscription. The other rulers are not credited with this.

The first Huna attack came late in Kumaragupta I's reign and was checked by prince Skandagupta, but the Skandagupta option is the intended answer. Per the notes, the Hunas were beaten again when he was king.
Pith and substance is the doctrine used to decide which List (Union or State) a law really falls under, so it settles whether there is encroachment. Eclipse concerns pre-Constitution laws and FRs.
Parens patriae means the State acts as legal protector of citizens who cannot protect themselves, which is option 1. The other options describe different ideas.

Copper is mined at Alwar (B-3), and manganese belongs to the Dharwar system and region (C-4). Coal (Gondwana, Damodar valley area) fits Giridih (A-1), leaving lignite with Jayamkondam (D-2). This gives 1-3-4-2, option (3).
Red soil occupies about 66% (more than 60%) of AP's area, making it the most extensive soil; the other percentages are not stated in the notes.
Red soil is the most extensive soil of AP (~66%); black is second (~25%), alluvium ~6% and laterite ~1%.
Skeletal soils are eroded hill-slope soils with no nutritive value, found in heavily eroded tracts such as the Nallamala slopes; red soil is not described this way.
Red soil covers about 66% of AP's land area.
Red soil covers about 66% of AP (described as more than 60%); 66 is the matching option.
Rayalaseema's red soils are the ones making up about 66% of AP's farmed regions; black soil is only ~25%.
Red soil is the most extensive soil in AP (~66%), ahead of black, alluvium and laterite.
Red soil occupies the largest share of AP's land (~66%), more than black (~25%) or coastal alluvium (~6%).
Red soil occupies the largest share of AP's land (~66%), more than black (~25%) or coastal alluvium (~6%).
Red soil is the most extensive soil of AP (~66%); black cotton soil is second at ~25%.
Red soil (~66% of AP) forms from weathering of granite, gneiss and Dharwar schists, mica schists and greenstones; basalt gives black soil instead.
Regur and Vertisols are synonyms for black soils (black cotton soil).
Regur (Regadi/Reguda) is the name for black cotton soil.
Deltaic alluvium is the most fertile and most important soil of AP for production, so it is the correct choice over red, black or laterite soils.
Deltaic alluvium, laid by the Godavari and Krishna in their deltas, is the most fertile soil of the K-G deltas.
Delta alluvium is river-borne silt laid down by the Godavari and Krishna, so river deposition is the cause.
Laterite forms under high temperature and heavy rainfall, with intense leaching leaving iron and aluminium oxides; red soil forms from weathering of crystalline rocks.

Under Art. 315(4), UPSC may serve a State's needs on the request of the Governor with the approval of the President. The Chief Minister, the Prime Minister and the Election Commission have no such role.
UPSC is an independent constitutional body created directly by the Constitution (Art. 315), not by an ordinance or ordinary law.
The Chairman and members of the UPSC and of a Joint Commission (JSPSC) are appointed by the President. The Governor appoints only for a State PSC.
Under Art. 316(1), the Chairman and members of a State PSC are appointed by the Governor, though they are removed only by the President.
SPSC members are appointed by the Governor but can be removed only by the President, so option 4 is right. Options saying the Governor removes are wrong.
An SPSC member is removed by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry on misbehaviour, not by the Governor or a High Court inquiry.
For the UPSC Chairman, removal follows a Supreme Court inquiry and Parliament has no role. Judges and the CAG are removed through Parliament's address.

The Bombay Mill Hands' Association (founded by N.M. Lokhande, 1890) is regarded as the first labour association; the notes do not cover it, and the Madras Labour Union (1918) is the first modern trade union.
N.M. Joshi represented Indian workers at the 1919 ILO Washington conference; the notes do not state this.
The March 1929 Bombay general strike by the Girni Kamgar Union and railway workers protested the dismissal of workers who had taken part in the 1928 strikes; the notes do not state this.
N.M. Lokhande is regarded as the first to organise the labour movement in India (Bombay Mill Hands' Association, 1890); the notes do not cover him.
N.M. Joshi was a co-founder of the AITUC, which was founded in Bombay on 31 October 1920; INTUC (1947), HMS (1948) and CITU (1970) came later.
Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the first AITUC session in 1920; N.M. Joshi was a co-founder and later General Secretary, not the first president.
Lala Lajpat Rai was the first president of the AITUC, founded on 31 October 1920 in Bombay.
Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the AITUC Nagpur session of 1929, where the moderates split away; the notes mention the 1929 split but not the president.
Ravindra Bharathi, built for Tagore's birth centenary, was inaugurated by Dr S. Radhakrishnan, so option 1 is right; Nehru and the others are not the inaugurator.
The Sixth Telugu Conference of the World Telugu Federation was held on 24-26 December 2004 in Bangalore, so option 1 is correct.
The first World Telugu Conference, aimed at encouraging Telugu language, literature and culture, was held in Hyderabad in 1975, so option 2 is correct.
Papineni Sivasankar won the 2016 Telugu Sahitya Akademi Award for his poetry collection Rajanigandha, so option 1 is correct.
The quoted definition comes from the Brundtland Commission's 1987 report 'Our Common Future'. UNEP, the World Bank and the IMF did not give it.
The Brundtland definition is development that meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs. The other options favour one side only, whereas SD balances them.
The core principle of SD is meeting present needs without compromising future generations. Unlimited exploitation and short-term growth contradict it.
Our Common Future (1987) linked economic development with environmental stability and popularised the term sustainable development.
Intergenerational equity means the present generation must not deplete resources at the cost of future generations. The option 'National resource' is the closest to the natural resources concerned.
Silent Spring (1962) was written by Rachel Carson and helped start the modern environmental movement. The notes do not cover this.
'Green Development' was written by W.M. Adams. The notes do not cover this.
The Rio+20 outcome document of June 2012 was 'The Future We Want'. 'Our Common Future' is the 1987 Brundtland report.
The UN Commission on Sustainable Development reviews implementation of Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration.
Agenda 21 emerged from UNCED, the 1992 Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit. Rio+10 in 2002 produced the Johannesburg Plan.
Rio 1992 was the first Earth Summit, held at Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
PAGE emerged at the 2012 UN Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20) in Rio de Janeiro. It involves UNEP, UNDP, ILO, UNIDO and UNITAR.
The Andhra Congress Committee appointed Konda Venkatappayya (Venkatappaiah) as Dictator for Andhra for the Salt Satyagraha. Prakasam is the tempting wrong option; he was not the Dictator.
The Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March and the salt law violations) took place in 1930. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931 came later and suspended the movement.
Webb Miller of United Press reported the non-violent march on the Dharasana Salt Works led by Sarojini Naidu, where volunteers took unarmed beatings. So the place is Dharasana, not Dandi.
Webb Miller, the American United Press journalist, had been with Gandhi during the Dandi March and later reported on Dharasana.
C. Rajagopalachari led the Tamil Nadu salt march from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam in April 1930. Kamaraj was only jailed in that march, so he is not the leader.

The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 5 April. 6 April 1930 was the salt-law breaking and the first Andhra salt satyagraha, and 26 January 1930 was Independence Day flag-hoisting.
Lord Irwin was Viceroy when the CDM began in 1930 (Dandi March, letter to Irwin, Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931). Willingdon succeeded him for the 1932-34 repression.
Under Article 3 the President refers the Bill to the affected state legislature to ascertain its views. These views are not binding, so neither concurrence nor a two-thirds majority is required.
Article 3 empowers Parliament to form a new state by law. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new states from outside India.
The appointed day for the bifurcation under the AP Reorganisation Act was 2 June 2014, when Telangana came into being.
Section 3 of the APRA formed Telangana with 10 districts, so AP lost 10 districts to it.
The appointed day for the bifurcation under the AP Reorganisation Act was 2 June 2014, when Telangana came into being.
Telangana is bordered by Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh (Odisha touches only a tiny stretch, if at all), so option 1 is right. Madhya Pradesh does not border Telangana.
Haryana was formed in 1966 on the basis of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, following the recommendation of the Parliamentary Committee headed by Sardar Hukum Singh.
The 2018 policy names NREDCAP as nodal agency, 4,000 MW initial solar parks and ~300 sunny days; the claim of 1,00,000 solar pump sets in five years is not part of it, so (4) is NOT correct.

Coal was nationalised in 1971-73 under Indira Gandhi, so I is correct. Coal blocks are now allocated by auction, not lottery, so II is wrong. India still imports coal (coking, blending grades), so III is wrong. Only I is correct.
Prana Raksha is a Chittoor Police web app meant to save road accident victims and help women in distress. The notes do not mention this app, so no line supports it.

Alzheimer's disease is the degenerative brain disorder and a leading cause of dementia, with progressive memory loss and confusion. Schizophrenia is a psychotic disorder, amnesia is only memory loss, and concussion is a traumatic injury. The notes do not cover this.
The GATT office was set up at Geneva in 1948, so option 4 is right; the other cities/years do not match.
The WTO was earlier known as GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade); the other bodies are separate organisations.
The WTO replaced GATT as an organisation on 1 January 1995; GATT was the earlier agreement and the WTO's predecessor.
The Uruguay Round concluded with the Marrakesh Agreement (1994), which created the WTO; the other bodies are unrelated to it.
The WTO was established on 1 January 1995; 1994 is the year the Marrakesh Agreement was signed, a common trap.
The 'Cloud Goat' (Nilgiri tahr) is found in Eravikulam National Park in Kerala's Western Ghats; the other options are not its characteristic habitat.
The lion-tailed macaque is endemic to the Western Ghats, found in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka. It is not found in Andhra Pradesh, so I, II and III is correct.
Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, so Rhinoceros is correct.
Chakrashila Wildlife Sanctuary is in Assam (Kokrajhar and Dhubri districts), known for the golden langur.
Jaldapara is a wildlife sanctuary in West Bengal, known for the rhino. Corbett is a national park, and Garumara is a national park, so only Jaldapara is a sanctuary.
Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary lies in the Kodagu (Coorg) district of Karnataka in the Western Ghats.
Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is in Munger district of Bihar. Valmiki is in West Champaran, so it is not the answer.
Gomarda Wildlife Sanctuary is in Raigarh district of Chhattisgarh.
Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary is in Kerala (Thiruvananthapuram), not Chhattisgarh, so this pair is wrongly matched.

Concentration by share of a State's population is highest in Punjab (31.9%). Uttar Pradesh has the largest number of SCs, not the highest share, and Himachal Pradesh (25.2%) and West Bengal (23.5%) rank below Punjab.

The notes define globalisation as the free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas and people across borders, so goods, investments (capital) and technology all apply, making 'All these' correct.

Globalisation is the coming together of worldwide social relations that bypass territorial boundaries (II) and involves thinking transterritorially about global risks (III). Statement I describes international relations between states, and IV is only a wishful vision of suprastate governance, so neither captures its essence.

The 'Global Village' idea rests on advances in transport and communication, which shrink distances and link societies worldwide. It does not depend mainly on social or political development or on international organisations.

Alluri Sitarama Raju led the 1922-24 Rampa rebellion among the Koya and Konda Dora tribes. Velu Thampi was Travancore's Diwan, and the 1879 Rampa rising was led by Tammandora, so the other options are wrong.
Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill in Kesari as foreign interference in Hindu custom, so the statement that he supported it is incorrect.
Rakhmabai refused to live with her child-marriage husband, who sued for restitution of conjugal rights, so it concerned age of consent/child marriage and conjugal rights, not women's education.
The Sarda Act (1929) fixed marriage ages at 14 for girls and 18 for boys.
D.K. Karve founded the first Women's University in 1916 (now SNDT, Bombay).
Deva Samaj was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri, not Radhakant Deb, so this pair is wrongly matched.
Anjuman-e-Khawatin-e-Islam (1914) was a Muslim women's organisation for women's education, i.e. a Muslim ladies' conference, not a League wing or a students' body.
Somaprakash was the journal of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
The financial committees are Estimates, PAC and COPU; the Business Advisory Committee is listed among the other standing committees, so it is not a financial committee.
Standing committees such as the DRSCs draw members in about a 2:1 ratio from Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (21 LS + 10 RS, or 16 under LS and 8 under RS).
The Estimates Committee is made up entirely of Lok Sabha members, whereas PAC and COPU have 7 Rajya Sabha members each and Government Assurances has Rajya Sabha members too.
The Estimates Committee has only Lok Sabha members; PAC and COPU include 7 Rajya Sabha members each and Government Assurances also has a Rajya Sabha component.
The Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha member, whereas COPU and PAC have 7 each and Petitions also has a Rajya Sabha side (10).
Only the Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha members; PAC and COPU each have 7 Rajya Sabha members, so only II is correct.
Members of the financial committees, including Estimates, are elected yearly and serve a term of one year.
The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, making it the largest financial committee.
The Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha members; all 30 are from the Lok Sabha.
The Opposition chair of the PAC since 1967 is a convention, not a rule of law or procedure.
The PAC chairman is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, not by the President, PM or RS Chairman.
The PAC examines the Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and CAG audit reports, which matches option 1; it does not appoint staff or examine policy itself.
The Supreme Court is the custodian/guardian of the Constitution through judicial review, so option 3 is right; the President, Parliament are not.
Article 348(1)(a) requires all proceedings in the Supreme Court and High Courts to be in English. Art. 145 only lets the Court frame its rules, and no ordinary law is the source.
The Supreme Court is the guardian of the Constitution and of Fundamental Rights through judicial review, so option 3 is right.
The Supreme Court is the custodian of the Constitution through judicial review and as final interpreter, so option 4 is right.
A Supreme Court judge resigns by writing addressed to the President, who also appoints the judge. The PM, Law Minister and Attorney General have no role.
Formal appointment of every SC judge is by the President under Art. 124(2) by warrant. The collegium only recommends and is not the appointing authority.

Statement I is correct: LNG is natural gas cooled to about −160°C so that its volume shrinks about 1,000 times, which makes it easier to store and transport. Statements II and III are not supported by the notes.
Water gas is a syngas mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen, which matches the syngas components listed in the notes.
Molecular weight rises with the number of carbon atoms: methane (CH4, 16), ethane (C2H6, 30), propane (C3H8, 44), butane (C4H10, 58). So option 1 gives the increasing order.
Koyali is in Gujarat and Numaligarh is in Assam. Tatipaka is in Andhra Pradesh and Nagapattinam in Tamil Nadu, so the code is 3 1 2 4.
NELP blocks, JV blocks, nomination blocks and CBM blocks are all hydrocarbon exploration blocks, so they relate to petroleum exploration, not to mineral belts like gypsum, gold or lignite.
Urja Ganga (JHBDPL) is a GAIL gas pipeline project serving UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB and Odisha, and it was started in 2016. It does not extend to Iran, so III is wrong and the answer is I and II.
The HBJ (Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur) pipeline carries gas from the South Basin (Bassein) fields offshore Mumbai. Ankleshwar and Kalol are Cambay fields, and Godavari is on the east coast.
ONGC has its headquarters in Dehradun, Uttarakhand.
Dachigam is in J&K, Keoladeo (Bharatpur) in Rajasthan, Kanha in Madhya Pradesh and Periyar in Kerala, which gives A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.
Dachigam is in Jammu & Kashmir, Papikonda in Andhra Pradesh, Sariska (Alwar) in Rajasthan and Bandipur in Karnataka, giving A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.

Rajamannar did not recommend strengthening the Governor system; it recommended a permanent Inter-State Council, deletion of Art. 356 (curbing its misuse) and abolition of the IAS and IPS. So option 4 is the one that is NOT a recommendation.
Article 51A(d) only requires citizens to defend the country and render national service when called upon, not compulsory military service. The other options are real duties: 51A(a), (i) and (c).
Statement III (weaker sections) is a DPSP under Article 46 and IV (protecting monuments) is a DPSP under Article 49, so neither is a Fundamental Duty. I and II are real duties, 51A(b) and 51A(f).
Abolition of titles (except military and academic) is in Article 18, a Fundamental Right, not a duty under Article 51A. The other options are real duties: 51A(a), (e) and (c).
Organising village panchayats is a DPSP under Article 40, not a Fundamental Duty. The other options are duties under 51A(d), (f) and (i).
Etikoppaka (Anakapalli district) is known for GI-tagged lacquerware toys, which are a wooden craft, so option 1 is right.
Bandar Laddu received its GI tag only in 2017, so it was not registered as of November 2016, while Tirupati Laddu (2009) was.
Bobbili Veena (Saraswati Veena) is traditionally carved from jackfruit wood, which is why option 1 is correct.
Sanganer near Jaipur is renowned for fine block printing with delicate floral motifs; Bagru is known for a different style (earthy, dabu prints).
Saharanpur is the well-known centre of the wood carving industry in Uttar Pradesh.
Theva Kala, the art of fusing molten gold onto coloured glass, is associated with Pratapgarh in Rajasthan.
Mon is in Nagaland, Nalbari in Assam, Pasighat in Arunachal Pradesh and Tura in Meghalaya, giving 4-2-1-3.
Molela in Rajasthan is famous for its terracotta clay work (clay plaques and figures).
Chumpa is an ornament worn on the teeth, so option 2 is correct.
Kashida is the traditional embroidery of Jammu and Kashmir.
Chikankari embroidery is the specialty of Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.
The woman's odhni called Pomcha is traditionally yellow.
Kalamkari is a hand-painted or block-printed cotton textile art of South India (Srikalahasti, Machilipatnam), so option 1 is right.
Tarabhant ki Odhni is the traditional costume of Adivasi (tribal) women in Rajasthan.
Eluru is known for hand-knotted carpets, Udayagiri for wooden cutlery, Narasapur for crochet lace and Etikoppaka for lacquerware toys, giving 1-2-3-4.
Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Kathak from Uttar Pradesh, Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh, and Mohiniyattam from Kerala, giving 1-4-3-2.
The notes do not state Canada as a uranium producer; it is a leading uranium producer (Athabasca Basin), whereas the USA, Germany and Zambia are minor producers.
Uranium City is a town in Saskatchewan, Canada, founded for uranium mining in the Athabasca Basin region, so Canada is correct.
The Kinta Valley in Malaysia is a tin-mining area whose ore feeds the smelters of Penang and Singapore, so tin production is correct.
Chile is the world's top copper producer, so option 1 is correct; Brazil, Botswana and India are far smaller producers.
The Lake Superior region contains the Mesabi (Minnesota) and Marquette (Michigan) ranges, both iron ore areas.
Karaganda is a coal basin of Kazakhstan, but the notes do not cover the other pairs. Normandy is in France, not Germany, so the Germany-Normandy pair is the mismatch.
Chile is the leading producer of iodine, from caliche (nitrate) deposits in the Atacama, ahead of Japan; so option 3 is correct.
Mexico is the world's largest silver producer, ahead of China and Peru, so option 3 is correct.
Chuquicamata is a giant open-pit copper mine in northern Chile, consistent with Chile being the top copper producer.
The Rukwa region of Tanzania has coal deposits (Rukwa coalfield), so coal is correct; it is not noted for mica, iron ore or gold.
Coolgardie is a gold-mining town in the Goldfields of Western Australia, so option 4 is correct.

Article 75(1) provides that the President appoints the Prime Minister and appoints other Ministers on the PM's advice, so Article 75 is correct. Articles 70, 79 and 85 deal with other Parliament-related matters.
The PM may belong to either House and need not be an MP when appointed, but must become a member of either House within six months (Art 75(5)). Option 2 wrongly says the Lok Sabha only.
Under Art 75(1) the President appoints the PM, usually the leader of the Lok Sabha majority. Parliament and the Lok Sabha do not elect the PM.
The Planning Commission (1950) had the Prime Minister as its ex-officio Chairman.
The Prime Minister was the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission.
The Prime Minister was the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission, with a Deputy Chairman of Cabinet rank.
The National Development Council is chaired by the Prime Minister, not the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission or the Finance Minister.
Under Art 75(5) a Minister who is not a member of Parliament must become one within six consecutive months or cease to be a Minister.

Statement 1 is correct: Art 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is wrong because Ministers hold office during the President's pleasure (Art 75(2)), not the PM's.
Aluminium (8.1%) is the most abundant metal in the crust; iron (5.0%) is second, so iron is the tempting but wrong option.
Dolomite is a carbonate rock of sedimentary origin (like limestone), whereas gabbro, granite and basalt are igneous rocks.
Granite and basalt are both igneous rocks, formed by cooling of magma or lava (intrusive and extrusive respectively).
Fossils are preserved remains, impressions or traces of ancient organisms found in rocks and soil; a specimen is just a sample and phylogeny is evolutionary history.
Dinosaurs lived during the Mesozoic era (Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous), not the Palaeozoic or Cenozoic.
Graphite is an inorganic, layered form of carbon that works as a solid lubricant; lanolin, mineral oil and PTFE are organic or synthetic compounds.
Louis Fischer, Gandhi's biographer, is listed in the notes as linked to Quit India, so he is the American publicist associated with Gandhi in that phase; the other names are not linked to it.
Raiyati Sarkar is not linked with Kheda (Gujarat), so that pair is wrong. The other pairs (Satara Prati Sarkar, Talcher parallel government, Tamluk Jatiya Sarkar) are correct.
Parallel governments arose at Ballia, Tamluk and Satara during Quit India, which makes option 4 the significant feature. Women did play an important role, so option 1 is wrong.
The Academic Association (1828) was the forum of the Derozians, founded by Henry Louis Vivian Derozio of Hindu College, Calcutta. Ram Mohan Roy and Vidyasagar are linked to other movements.
Paramahansa Mandali (1849) fought caste discrimination and promoted women's education. Prarthana Samaj dates from 1867 and Arya Samaj from 1875.

Prarthana Samaj was a Maharashtra-based reform body within Hinduism. The notes do not state the monotheism point directly. Statement IV is wrong because it was an offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj, so the influence ran the other way.
The Prarthana Samaj's four-point agenda was disapproval of caste, women's education, widow remarriage and a higher marriage age. Abolition of untouchability is not among them, so (4) is the answer.
Bal Shastri Jambhekar, who published Darpan in 1832, attacked Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism in Bombay. The others were not reformers of this kind.
Bal Shastri Jambhekar, who published Darpan in 1832, attacked Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism in Bombay. The others were not reformers of this kind.
The notes do not mention Vishnushastri Pandit or an 1866 widow remarriage society. They only mention Ranade's Widow Remarriage Association of 1861.
The Deccan Education Society was founded by Tilak, Agarkar, V.K. Chiplunkar and Namjoshi. Ranade was only a patron, so Chiplunkar is the correct choice among the options.

Soaps are biodegradable, but synthetic detergents are the ones suited to delicate clothes and lather well in hard water, so option 4 is the untrue claim. The notes do not state that soaps clean more strongly than detergents.
Flint (lead) glass is used for lenses and prisms, which are optical instruments. Pyrex is used for labware.
Pyrex (borosilicate) glass is harder and more heat-resistant than soda glass, so the claim that soda glass is harder is incorrect.
Glass wool is made of fine glass fibres with high tensile strength, is fireproof, and is used to make fibre glass. It is a poor electrical conductor, so statement III is wrong.
PVC is polyvinyl chloride, made from vinyl chloride.
Plaster of Paris is CaSO4·½H2O, i.e. (CaSO4)2·H2O, so two formula units share one water molecule.
Methyl methacrylate polymerises to PMMA (perspex), a light but strong plastic. Nylon, polythene and PVC are not the usual answer for this.
Manganese dioxide is a decolouriser added to glass. It oxidises the green ferrous iron impurity to the pale yellow ferric form.
Oil of vitriol is the old name for concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4).
A soda-acid extinguisher contains sulphuric acid and sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda) solution. They react to release CO2, which puts out the fire.
Calgon (sodium hexametaphosphate, Na6P6O18) softens permanent hard water, as the notes list. Mg(HCO3)2 is a cause of hardness, not a softener.
Nail polish remover is mainly acetone, which dissolves the nail polish.
Acetic acid (the acid in vinegar) is an organic acid. HCl, HNO3 and H2SO4 are mineral acids.

Tamarind's acid is tartaric acid, not citric acid, so pair III is incorrect. Vinegar is acetic acid and curd is lactic acid, so pairs I and II are correct. The notes give citric acid for lemon, not tamarind.
Milk of magnesia is Mg(OH)2, a common antacid.
Soap is made by saponification of vegetable oils or fats. Mineral oils (mobil, kerosene, cutting oil) are petroleum products and are not used.
Nylon, the first synthetic fibre, was prepared in the 1930s from coal, water and air. It is strong, elastic and light, so all three statements are correct.
Morphine is an analgesic (3), sodium is kept in kerosene (4), boric acid is an antiseptic (1), and German silver is an alloy (2). This gives 3 4 1 2.
Galvanisation coats iron with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting.
NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution, so 2015 is correct; 2012 and 2014 are wrong.
NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution, so 2015 is correct; 2012 and 2014 are wrong.
NITI stands for National Institution for Transforming India, as in the full form of the body.
NITI Aayog is non-constitutional and non-statutory, set up by an executive Cabinet resolution. The Finance Commission, UPSC and Election Commission are constitutional bodies.
NITI is the acronym for National Institution for Transforming India.
The notes do not state this committee fact; Rajiv Kumar was a NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman (2017-2022) who headed the committee.
State Governors are not members of the NITI Aayog Governing Council. CMs of all States, CMs of Delhi and Puducherry and Lieutenant Governors of other UTs (e.g. Andaman and Nicobar) are members.

Article 32 is part of the Fundamental Rights, which are amended by a special majority (two-thirds present and voting plus a majority of total membership) with no State ratification. So 'two-thirds majority' is the right choice.

Under Art. 169 a State Legislative Council is created or abolished by Parliament through a law passed by simple majority, after the State Assembly passes a resolution. This is not an Art. 368 amendment.
Arts 2-4 let Parliament admit or establish new States by ordinary law with a simple majority. Such laws are not deemed amendments under Art. 368, so no special majority or ratification is needed.

Election of the President (Arts 54, 55) and the Seventh Schedule Lists are federal provisions needing a special majority plus ratification by half the States. Fundamental Rights need only a special majority, so III is wrong.

The election of the President (Arts 54, 55) is a federal provision needing a special majority plus State ratification, so it cannot be amended by simple majority. The other options (new States, official language, quorum) are simple-majority matters.
Election of the President (Arts 54, 55) is a federal provision. Amending it needs a special majority in Parliament plus ratification by at least half of the States.

The amending power is limited by the Constitution itself, through the basic structure doctrine, which Kesavananda Bharati and Minerva Mills drew from the Constitution's own framework. Parliament's power under Art. 368 is therefore not unlimited.

Minerva Mills held that the limited amending power is itself a basic feature, and struck down the 42nd Amendment's clauses claiming unlimited power. So an unquestioned right to amend any part is not a basic feature.
Female literacy in the 2011 provisional figures was about 65.5% (final 64.6%), so 65.5 is correct.
Nagaland was the only State with negative growth (−0.6%) in 2001-11, so it had the lowest growth; Kerala, Goa and Tamil Nadu grew positively.
ICMR stands for Indian Council of Medical Research, the apex body for biomedical research in India; the other options are invented expansions.

The notes list IPR Gandhinagar, IUCAA Pune and RRCAT Indore as the Indian institutions leading LIGO-India with DAE and DST, so I, III and IV are correct. Kepler's Observatory and IISST are not among them.
The Sampurnanand Telescope is at ARIES, Nainital in Uttarakhand, not Ladakh, so statement I is wrong. It completed 50 years (1972-2022), so II is correct. III on optical observations is also correct.
eLISA is a space-based interferometer mission designed to detect gravitational waves, not neutrinos, missile defence effects or solar flares.
LIGO stands for Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory, which detects gravitational waves using laser interferometry.

The second LIGO detection was announced in June 2016, and it came from a merger of two black holes about 1.4 billion light-years away. So I and II are correct. III is wrong because white dwarfs were not involved.
National Sugar Institute is in Kanpur, MIDHANI in Hyderabad, Institute of Military Law in Kamptee, and the Institute of National Integration in Pune. This gives A-5, B-4, C-2, D-3.
Only II is correct: mica occurs in the Koderma belt. Natural gas is tied to marine sedimentary (Tertiary) basins, not Gondwana, and Dharwar rocks are metallic-mineral belts, not petroleum-bearing.
The North-Western belt (Aravalli, Rajasthan) is noted for copper, a non-ferrous metal. Iron, manganese and chromite are not its non-ferrous mineral (iron is ferrous).
Gold is unreactive and occurs native (free); sodium and aluminium are highly reactive and never occur free. Copper can occur native but gold is the best-known free-state metal.
Native elements such as gold, silver, platinum and copper occur uncombined, so they consist of a single type of atom. Compounds and mixtures of minerals contain several kinds of atoms.

NRLM is listed among items not in Bharat Nirman, whose components are irrigation, drinking water, electrification, roads (PMGSY), housing (IAY) and telephony. NRLM is a livelihood mission, so it is the odd one out.
Bharat Nirman (Dec 2005) was a rural infrastructure programme, so the answer is infrastructure development.
Bharat Nirman has six components: irrigation, drinking water, electrification, roads, housing and rural telephony. Agro-based industries are not one of them.

The notes do not list the components of the Minimum Needs Programme. Its components are rural water supply, education, health, roads, electrification, housing and urban slum improvement, while social forestry is not among them, so it is the answer.
Bharat Nirman's targets were to be achieved by the end of 2009.
The Community Development Programme was launched on 2 October 1952, the first rural development programme.
Rural hospitals are explicitly outside Bharat Nirman, whose six components are irrigation, drinking water, electrification, roads, housing and telephony.
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan is not a Bharat Nirman component. Water supply, irrigation benefits and electrification are components.
Mission Antyodaya is a rural development convergence framework to make Gram Panchayats poverty-free.
CAPART funds voluntary organisations and promotes rural technology, so its objective is rural development.
Lord Dalhousie (1848–56) is the Governor-General who pushed railways, along with the telegraph and the Public Works Department, so (2) is correct.
The Doctrine of Lapse, under which a state whose ruler died without a natural heir passed to the Company, is linked to Lord Dalhousie (1848–56), so (2) is correct.
The Maukharis, originally Gupta feudatories from Gaya, had Kannauj as their capital. Thaneshwar was the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) capital, not Maukhari.
A hundi was a bill of exchange used in credit and trade, not a royal advisory, a diary or a feudal order.
Harsha moved his capital from Thanesar to Kannauj, the former Maukhari capital, to help his sister Rajyashri run it. Prayaga was only the site of the quinquennial assembly.
Harsha's elder brother Rajyavardhana was killed by Shashanka, and Harsha then succeeded him. The other names are not in the Vardhana line.
Shashanka (Sasanka) of Gauda (Bengal) was Harsha's rival. Bhaskaravarman ruled Kamarupa, Dhruvasena II ruled Valabhi and Pulakesin II was the Chalukya ruler of Badami.
Nagananda is a play by Harsha on a Buddhist theme of self-sacrifice. Leelavati is by Bhaskaracharya II, and the other two options are not Harsha's works.
Priyadarshika is a Sanskrit romantic play by Harsha. Harshacharita and Kadambari are by Banabhatta, and Devichandraguptam is by Vishakhadatta.
Kalhana's Rajatarangini gives information on Harsha. Harisena was Samudragupta's poet and Kalidasa belongs to the Gupta period, so neither is a source on Harsha.
Pericycle is a layer of cells just inside the endodermis and is not a conducting element; xylem (tracheids, fibres) and phloem (sieve tubes) are the conducting tissues.
Gastric juice contains HCl (pH ~1.5-3.5), so it is the most acidic and has the highest H+ concentration; lemon juice is a weaker acid and the others are basic.
Ant bites inject formic acid (methanoic acid), as the notes state.
A group of similar cells performing a specific function is called a tissue; organs are made of several tissues.
Genes are segments of DNA, which is a nucleic acid.
Walking on a carpet builds up static charge on the body by friction; touching the metal handle discharges it, so charge is transferred from the body to the handle.
In parallel, the reciprocals of resistances add, so the equivalent resistance is lower than the smallest resistance; series increases it.
A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component; fuse and ammeter are in series.
Water accepts a proton from HSO4- to form H3O+, so water acts as a Bronsted-Lowry base.
Guard cells enclosing a stoma are kidney (bean) shaped in dicots.
Cytokinin is a plant hormone promoting cell division; insulin, thyroxine and estrogen are animal hormones.
Luminous emittance (luminous flux per unit area) has SI unit lux (lumen per square metre); candela is luminous intensity and lumen is flux.
X-rays, microwaves and radio waves are electromagnetic waves; sound waves are mechanical and need a medium.
Loudness depends on the amplitude of the sound wave (pitch depends on frequency).
Sound below 20 Hz is infrasound.
Bats use ultrasound, receiving reflected ultrasonic waves to detect obstacles.
Magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity so it does no work; speed and kinetic energy stay constant, while direction (velocity and momentum) changes.
Fleming's left hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, i.e. the effect of magnetic field on current.
In a uniform field the forces on the two poles are equal and opposite, so net force is zero (only a torque acts).
Photon energy E=hf is proportional to frequency; X-rays have the highest frequency among the options.
Bahauddin Zakariya was the Suhrawardi saint who worked in Multan and Sindh. The others (Moinuddin, Baba Farid, Nizamuddin) were Chishtis.
The Chishti order was founded at Chisht by Abu Ishaq Shami with his disciple Abu Ahmad Abdal. Abu Abdal is the closest option, so (3) is correct.
Bahauddin Zakariya brought the Suhrawardi silsila to India, based in Multan. He was not Chishti or Firdausi.
Shihabuddin Suhrawardi is credited with developing the Farr-i-Izadi idea of divine kingship. The notes do not cover this, and Nizamuddin Auliya, who avoided courts, is the wrong choice.
The Firdausi order, a branch of the Suhrawardi, was founded in Bihar by Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri. So Bihar is linked to the Firdausi order.
The Naqshbandi order was the most orthodox and opposed sama (music) and tomb visits. The Chishtis encouraged sama, and the Suhrawardis also practised it.
Kashf-ul-Mahjub was written by Ali Hujwiri (Abul Hasan Hujwiri, Data Ganj Bakhsh), the first prominent Sufi in India.
Regur (black) soil forms from weathered Deccan Trap basalt. Red soil forms from granite/gneiss and laterite from heavy leaching, so they are wrong.
Black soil develops deep summer cracks that let the soil mix and turn over, so it is called self-ploughing. Alluvial, laterite and desert soils do not behave like this.
Regur (black cotton) soil is the classic cotton soil, with high moisture retention, and cotton is its main crop. Laterite, alluvial and red soils suit other crops.
Black soil is clayey and sticky when wet, so I is correct. It is poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus, so II is wrong.
Very deep black soils occur in the north-western Deccan Plateau, the Deccan Trap region, so option 1 is right.
Histosols are organic soils (peat/bog soils) made mostly of organic matter. Vertisols are cracking clays, and the other options are not organic soils.
Histosols are organic soils with very high organic matter, such as peat. Vertisols are clay soils, Gelisols are frozen soils and Spodosols are acidic leached soils.
Vertisols (black soils) are poor in humus, nitrogen and phosphorus, so the statement that they are rich in humus is incorrect. The other statements are true.
Sorghum is a widely spaced row crop that leaves much bare soil between rows, so erosion is high. Clover and wheat give dense cover that protects the soil.
APRDC (AP Road Development Corporation) was set up in 1998, which matches the 2.1.1998 Act establishing the State Road Development Corporation. APSRTC dates from 1958, so option 2 is wrong.
The AP Reorganisation Act 2014 mandated a new railway zone, the South Coast Railway, with its headquarters at Visakhapatnam. So Visakhapatnam is correct.

The Cherlopalli-Rapuru tunnel was India's longest electrified rail tunnel when opened and lies on the Obulavaripalle-Venkatachalam line linking Rayalaseema to Krishnapatnam port. So the answer is Krishnapatnam.
The Errupalem-Nambur line is 57 km, costs ₹2,245 crore and passes through NTR, Guntur and Khammam districts. The '6-year timeline' was the wrong statement.
Vijayawada station has IGBC Platinum green certification, not LEED (USA), so statement I is wrong. Statement II is not supported by the notes, so the answer is None of the above.
Gangavaram is a greenfield deep-water port with the deepest draft. Ravva is a captive offshore oil and gas port, and Meghavaram and Narsapur are not operational deep-water ports.
Visakhapatnam port ranked third in port traffic in FY 2022.
Visakhapatnam port helped transport of agricultural products (APPSC 2022 key), so it is the correct choice.
The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram is about 50 km from Visakhapatnam, and its nodal SPV is APADCL.
AP has six operational airports, of which three are international (Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati).
AP airports lost ₹730 crore over five years and Vijayawada alone lost ₹272 crore, so statements 1 and 2 are correct. The notes do not support the Tirupati profit claim, so 1 and 2 only.
AP airports lost ₹730 crore over five years and Vijayawada alone lost ₹272 crore, so statements 1 and 2 are correct. The notes do not support the Tirupati profit claim, so 1 and 2 only.
NW-4 covers the Godavari and Krishna with the Kakinada-Puducherry canal system, including the Krishna stretch Wazirabad-Prakasam Barrage. So it is National Waterway 4.
NW-4 covers the Godavari and Krishna with the Kakinada-Puducherry canal system, including the Krishna stretch Wazirabad-Prakasam Barrage. So it is National Waterway 4.

Both statements are true: laparoscopy uses small cuts and a camera, and it is usually done under general anaesthetic. But the anaesthetic does not explain why only small cuts are needed, so R is not the explanation of A.
A pressure cooker raises the pressure inside, which raises the boiling point of water (~120 C), so food cooks faster. It does not spread heat more evenly or use a bigger flame.
The Statue of Liberty is made of copper, which oxidises over time to form a green patina. It is not paint or algae.

Sodium is highly reactive and reacts vigorously with oxygen and moisture in air, so it is stored under kerosene to keep air out. Absorbing moisture is only part of the reason, and the explosive reaction with oxygen is the best answer here.
PVC stands for polyvinyl chloride, the polymer of vinyl chloride; the other options name compounds that do not exist as PVC.
Teflon is PTFE, polytetrafluoroethylene, the polymer of tetrafluoroethene, so ethylene is the right base name.
Royal water is aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), which dissolves gold. That is why the ornaments lost weight.
Boiler superheater tubes are made of Cr-Mo (chromium-molybdenum) steel, which withstands high temperature and pressure.

Section 90 (the question says 91, but the content matches) provides all three: Union control for irrigation, deemed consent of Telangana, and Central execution with clearances including R&R. So I, II and III are all true.
Section 90(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 declares Polavaram Irrigation Project a national project. Sections 30 and 89 are common traps, and 60, 70 and 80 are not the right section.
Section 90(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 declares Polavaram Irrigation Project a national project. Sections 30 and 89 are common traps, and 60, 70 and 80 are not the right section.
Mehrgarh (Kachhi plains, Balochistan, c. 7000 BC) gives the earliest settled life and agriculture in the subcontinent; Lothal and Harappa are later Harappan sites.
Agriculture was the economic base of the Harappans: double cropping and surplus stored in granaries supported trade, crafts and urbanisation.
Harappans in India first cultivated cotton and made cotton textiles, so India is the answer, not Egypt or Mesopotamia.
The Harappans were the first to cultivate cotton and make cotton textiles. Seals were not coins, so coins is wrong.
Copper was the first metal used by man. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, and iron came much later.
Chert for blades came from Rohri (Sukkur-Rohri hills) in Sindh. Khetri was the copper source, not a chert source.
Lothal in Gujarat had the world's earliest tidal dockyard and was a port trading with West Asia; the other options are not Harappan ports.
The SHAKTI processor is from IIT Madras, not IIT Delhi, so Statement 1 is wrong. The chip is based on open-source RISC-V under MeitY's DIR-V programme, so Statement 2 is right.
The early Kakatiyas were Jains and turned Shaiva only from Prola II / Rudradeva, so Jainism was the religion they first patronised; Saivism is the tempting but later choice.

Statement III is correct: it was launched on SpaceX's Falcon 9 because Indian rockets lacked the capacity for such a large communication satellite. The Bellatrix green propulsion system, developed under DRDO's TDF, was demonstrated on PSLV-C58 and is a non-toxic, environmentally friendly system. The notes mark all statements in this question as correct, so all the above is the answer.

Vikram-S is India's first private rocket, a suborbital launch vehicle, and its mission was named Prarambh. It was developed by Skyroot Aerospace, not Agnikul, so statement IV is wrong and I, II and III only is the answer.
Agnikul Cosmos, based in Chennai (IIT Madras), built the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine. Both statements are therefore true.

TSAT-1A, a sub-metre optical surveillance satellite and India's first privately built one, was built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic and launched on SpaceX Falcon 9. The other firms make propulsion, rockets or nanosatellites.

The Space Activities Bill was finalised in May 2025 to boost private participation and give statutory powers to IN-SPACe. It is a bill, not yet an Act, so the 'Act' option is wrong.
M.N. Roy founded the Radical Democratic Party in 1940 and later led the Radical Humanist movement. The other options are not linked to it.
The Indian Sociologist was published from London (India House) by Shyamji Krishnavarma, who founded India House and the Indian Home Rule Society.
Factor income is the income earned by a factor of production for services rendered to the production unit. The other options describe taxes, saving/investment and transfer payments.
Pension is a transfer payment with no service rendered in return, so it is excluded from national income. Rent, mixed income and undistributed profits are factor incomes.
The three methods are product (value added), income and expenditure. A savings approach is not a method of measuring national product.
J.R. Hicks, in The Social Framework, stated that Net Social Product equals Social Income.
Income originating is the value produced within the State's boundaries (GSDP). Income accruing also includes residents' income earned outside the State.
Income accruing includes the income of the State's residents earned in other States or abroad. Income originating counts only production within the State's boundaries.

1961-71 recorded the highest decadal growth, 24.80%, higher than any other decade.
2001-11 had a decadal growth of 17.70%, the lowest of the options and India's lowest after 1921.
Census 2011 recorded decadal growth of 17.7% for 2001-11.
Census 2011 recorded India's density as 382 persons per sq km.
The provisional sex ratio of Census 2011 was 940; the final figure is 943.
