North Korea admitted exporting missiles to Pakistan and Iran and asked the US for compensation to stop their further spread. The other options are not the ones the notes name.
North Korea claimed its first hydrogen bomb test (January 2016). South Korea and Japan have no nuclear weapons, and China tested its H-bomb decades earlier.
NSG membership gives access to nuclear trade and technology, so I is correct. It does not make a state an NPT member, as the notes say of the 2008 waiver, so II is wrong.
Only China and France of the listed states are NPT-recognised nuclear weapon states. India, Israel and Pakistan are outside the NPT, so the answer is I and II.
New START, signed in April 2010, is a bilateral treaty between the USA and Russia, not China or North Korea.

Audi alteram partem means 'hear the other side', i.e. the right to be heard, a core rule of natural justice. The other options describe different safeguards such as consulting a lawyer or the 24-hour rule.
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty, so Right to Life is correct. Property is no longer a fundamental right, and equality and speech fall under other Articles.
Article 20(2) bars prosecution and punishment twice for the same offence, which rests on the principle of autrefois convict (previously convicted). The notes do not state the maxim itself.
Article 20(3) bars compelling an accused to be a witness against himself, i.e. testimonial compulsion (oral and documentary testimony).

Article 20(1) bars conviction or heavier penalty under a law not in force when the act was done, so Parliament cannot make a criminal law with retrospective effect. The other three statements are correct: 20(2), 20(3) and the 22(3) exclusion of preventive detainees.

In Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010) the Supreme Court held that involuntary narco-analysis, polygraph and brain-mapping violate Article 20(3). The notes link this to 20(3) only, not Article 21 explicitly.
Double jeopardy, no prosecution and punishment twice for the same offence, is protected by Article 20(2). Articles 21 to 23 deal with other matters.
The principle that no one is punished twice for the same offence is the doctrine of double jeopardy under Article 20(2). Repugnancy, eclipse and retribution are unrelated.
C. Praveen Kumar was the first (acting) Chief Justice of the separate AP High Court from 1 Jan 2019, working from temporary premises at Vijayawada.
C. Praveen Kumar was the first (acting) Chief Justice of the separate AP High Court from 1 Jan 2019, working from temporary premises at Vijayawada.
On 28 Nov 2022 the SC stayed the AP High Court direction to build the Amaravati capital within six months, so six is correct.
In March 2022 the division bench under CJ Prashant Kumar Mishra refused interim orders against the 13 new districts, so 13 is correct.
Under Art. 233, district judges are appointed, posted and promoted by the Governor in consultation with the High Court. The President and the CJI have no role in this.

The notes state that over 4.7 crore cases were pending in May 2022, with about 87% in subordinate courts. The claim of about 1,82,000 cases pending over 50 years was marked not correct, so option 4 is the wrong statement.
Under Art. 233 the Governor appoints district judges, in consultation with the High Court. The Chief Justice, the Council of Ministers and the Advocate General do not appoint them.
A Lok Adalat award is deemed a civil court decree and is final, with no appeal. The other options are wrong because Lok Adalats have statutory status under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
Chhattisgarh is the correct answer, as the first-ever E-Lok Adalat during the COVID-19 period was held there. The notes do not cover this fact.
W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session in 1885 at Bombay; Hume was only General Secretary.
The venue was shifted from Poona to Bombay because of a cholera outbreak (not plague).
The first session in 1885 was attended by 72 delegates.

Dufferin was Viceroy and Bonnerjee was first president, so I and II are correct. The first session was held in Bombay, not Calcutta, so III is wrong. The notes do not address official attendance, but the answer key makes IV correct.
The statement that no Indian could have started the Congress is attributed to G.K. Gokhale, not Wedderburn, Dutt or Hume.
Dadabhai Naoroji was the first Indian elected to the British Parliament (Finsbury Central, 1892).
Naoroji, as president of the Calcutta 1906 session, declared Swaraj the goal; he is the leader linked with self-rule.
Dadabhai Naoroji was called the Grand Old Man of India.
Naoroji presided at Calcutta 1886, Tyabji at Madras 1887, Yule at Allahabad 1888 and Wedderburn at Bombay 1889, giving a-IV, b-I, c-III, d-II.
The second session (Calcutta, 1886) was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.
K. Shankar Pillai (Shankar) was India's famous political cartoonist who founded Shankar's Weekly; the notes do not cover him, so the answer rests on general knowledge.
Bapu's birth name was Sattiraju Lakshminarayana. Ramana is Mullapudi Venkata Ramana, his film partner, so he is not the right choice.
The ASI is an attached office under the Union Ministry of Culture, which is the correct answer. It was earlier under Tourism and Culture, so Tourism is the tempting wrong choice.
Hyderabad's famous museum is the Salar Jung Museum, built from the collection of Mir Yousuf Ali Khan (Salar Jung III). The other options are museums in other cities.
India Gate in Delhi, a war memorial, was modelled on the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. The Gateway of India in Mumbai is an arch inspired by other styles, so it is not the answer.
Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga, Spain, so he was Spanish. He lived and worked mostly in France, which is why French is the tempting wrong option.
Jharia is a coalfield (coal mining area) in Jharkhand, not an iron and steel centre, whereas Jamshedpur, Durgapur and Bhilai all have steel plants.
Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Ltd (VISL) is the Mysore State plant at Bhadravati in Karnataka, so option (2) is correct.
Renukoot is the site of HINDALCO's aluminium industry, not iron and steel. Bhadravati, Salem and Visakhapatnam all have steel plants.
Sri Ganganagar is a fertiliser centre, Jaipur is known for glass, Udaipur for cement (limestone) and Kota for synthetic silk, giving 4-3-2-1.
Bengaluru has the aircraft factory (HAL), Korba has aluminium (BALCO), Jamshedpur has iron and steel (TISCO) and Malanjkhand has copper, giving 3-4-1-2.
Arma Konda (Aroma/Sitamma Konda, 1,680 m) in Chintapalli, ASR district, is the highest peak of AP and of the Eastern Ghats. Velikonda, Palakonda and Rushikonda are lower hills.
The notes do not mention the local name Enugula Mallamma for any hills. Horsley Hills in Annamayya (Madanapalle) is the accepted answer, since the name is traditionally tied to it.
Talakona in Tirupati district (Sri Venkateswara NP, Seshachalam hills) is AP's tallest waterfall. Dudhsagar and Shivasamudram are in other states.
Borra Caves are limestone karst caves in the Ananthagiri Hills of ASR district, on the Gosthani river. The other hills listed do not hold them.
Meristematic tissues are classified as such because their cells keep dividing, while permanent tissues have lost the capacity to divide. So the basis of classification is dividing capacity.
Nereis (an annelid) is bilaterally symmetrical. Asterias and Echinus are echinoderms with radial symmetry as adults, and sea anemone is radially symmetrical.
Sea anemones (Adamsia) and sea pens (Pennatula) are cnidarians, formerly called Coelenterata, with a hollow gut cavity and tentacles.
Water is densest at 4 °C, so the densest water sinks to the bottom. The bottom stays at about 4 °C while ice forms at 0 °C on the surface.
Floating depends on the densities of the body and the liquid, not on g. The weight and the buoyant force both scale with g, so on the moon the body floats as before.
Asexual reproduction does not need gametes, and it can occur in either sex, e.g. budding and fragmentation. Both the assertion and the reason are false.
Pine is a gymnosperm and bears naked seeds in cones without flowers. Cashew, coffee and groundnut are angiosperms that flower.
Hooves are found in ungulates such as deer, zebra and horse. The jackal is a carnivore with claws and paws, so it has no hooves.
Charles Darwin wrote 'On the Origin of Species' (1859), presenting natural selection.
The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird in the world, about 5-6 cm long.
Non-metal oxides such as CO2 and SO2 are acidic, forming acids with water. Metal oxides are generally basic.
Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number. Fe-59: 33; Cu-61: 32; Zn-61: 31; Zn-60: 30. So Fe-59 has the most.
Gold, silver and aluminium are malleable and can be beaten into sheets. Potassium is a soft, reactive alkali metal that is not beaten into sheets.
Lead becomes a superconductor at very low temperature, about 7.2 K.
In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, Mg is oxidised and O2 is reduced, so it is a redox reaction. The other options are neutralisation, combination and double displacement with no change in oxidation state.
Gold is a noble metal that dissolves only in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), so nitric acid alone does not react with it. Copper, zinc and iron react.
Iron is extracted by reducing its oxide ore with coke, which acts as the reducing agent. So the process is reduction.
Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Brass is copper and zinc.
The maxwell is the CGS unit of magnetic flux (1 Mx = 10^-8 Wb).
Tin melts at about 232 °C, lower than lead (327 °C), zinc (420 °C) and silver (962 °C).
Food security means physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food, not access to 'the food of their choice'. So option 4 is what it does not imply.
The PDS is a government shop chain supplying basic food at low prices, and its main aim is food security for the poor. The other options are only items it distributes or secondary effects.
The NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population, so 75 per cent is correct.
The Mid-Day Meal scheme began in 1995, as per the notes' table of food-based safety nets.
The Mid-Day Meal scheme (now PM POSHAN) was started in 1995.
PDS/NFSA, ICDS and Mid-Day Meal are all listed as food-based safety nets, so all the given answers are correct.

The Essential Commodities Act is 1955, AGMARK's Grading and Marking Act is 1937, the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is 1954, and the Food Safety and Standards Act is 2006. This matches I-C, II-D, III-A, IV-B.
Procurement at support prices (MSP) gives farmers remunerative, stable prices, and the grain procured builds the stocks used for PDS and buffer stock. So all three statements are correct.
Measuring soil nutrient levels by chemical testing is a laboratory method, not remote sensing. Crop health, soil moisture (microwave/SAR) and water availability can all be sensed from satellites.
GIS is used for storing and manipulating data, with themes held as layers and combined through overlay analysis. So the options saying analysis or storage is impossible are wrong.
News channels are not a source of real-time data for GIS in disaster response. Satellite imagery, weather data and sensor networks are real-time data sources.
QGIS is the free, open-source, cross-platform desktop GIS used to analyse and edit spatial data and compose maps.
A digitizer is the tablet or table that converts analog data to digital format; it is a GIS hardware component.
In GIS, 'G' stands for Geographic, i.e. Geographic Information System. The notes do not state this expansion directly.
Roger Tomlinson is regarded as the father of GIS. The other options are distorted names.
Roger Tomlinson is regarded as the father of GIS. The other options are distorted names.
The Survey of India prepares India's topographical maps. The Geological Survey and Archaeological Survey have different mandates.
MOSDAC stands for Meteorological & Oceanographic Satellite Data Archival Centre, run by SAC, and it carries disaster announcements and alerts.
MOSDAC stands for Meteorological & Oceanographic Satellite Data Archival Centre, run by SAC, and it carries disaster announcements and alerts.
Bhuvan is ISRO's geoportal, developed and run by NRSC, so it is not a spacecraft, satellite or telescope.
According to NRSC, the Ganga-Brahmaputra basin is the most flood-prone area in India.
Earthquake prediction is not one of NRSC's disaster-support activities. Flood and cyclone monitoring, fire alerts and flood warning are.
Floods, tsunami inundation and forest fires can be monitored from space, but the spread of a disease among humans cannot.
Meghdoot is the agro-meteorological advisory initiative jointly run by IMD and ICAR.
Transport, communication and hotels belong to the service (tertiary) sector, whereas mining and quarrying and forestry and fishing are not services. So II and III is correct.
Manufacturing is part of the secondary sector, whereas real estate is a tertiary (service) activity. So real estate is not included in manufacturing.
Per the Clark-Fisher three-sector model, labour shifts out of the primary sector into secondary and tertiary sectors as income rises, so it signals economic growth. It does not indicate backwardness.
At Independence agriculture was the largest contributor to GDP, about half of output, so agriculture is the answer.
In 1950-51 industry contributed about 13% of GDP, so option (1) is correct.
Services now make the largest contribution to GDP, at about 54%, ahead of industry and agriculture.
The agriculture share of GDP has fallen steadily, from over half in 1950-51 to about 18% recently. So its contribution is decreasing.

The notes do not give a 15% agriculture figure. The question is dated and the notes show roughly 17-18% in recent old-series years. Among the options, 15% is the intended answer as the share fell below 20%.
Agriculture's large contribution to GNP is in terms of the value of output, since it is the largest sector by output at Independence. Its share of exports, revenue and foreign exchange is small.
The current order of contribution to GDP is services > industry > agriculture, as the tertiary share keeps rising.
Post-1991 growth was service-led, not import-led, export-led or agriculture-led, because the services share kept rising.
The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX (Panchayats, Arts. 243–243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule. Parts X and XI were in the original Constitution.
Part XV (Arts. 324–329-A) deals with Elections. Part V is the Union, Part XX is Amendment and Part X is Scheduled and Tribal Areas.
Part VIII (Arts. 239–242) deals with Union Territories. Part VII was repealed and Part IX is Panchayats.
The Right to Property (Arts. 31, 19(1)(f)) was deleted as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now the legal right under Art. 300A.
The Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment (1951), linked to Art. 31B. The 8th, 9th and 42nd Amendments did not add it.
The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats to States and UTs. The Fifth deals with Scheduled Areas, the Sixth with tribal areas and the Third with oaths.
The Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment (1951), linked to Art. 31B. The other amendments listed did not add it.
The Ninth Schedule (Art. 31B) shields listed laws from judicial review, so the Tamil Nadu reservation law was placed in it. The Tenth to Twelfth Schedules deal with other subjects.
Anti-defection law is in the Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985). The Sixth is tribal areas and the Ninth protects listed laws.
Vigyan Jyoti, a DST scheme, brings meritorious girls of Classes 9-12 into STEM, so it addresses women's underrepresentation. The other groups listed are not its target.
Pulse Polio was launched in 1995; the polio-free certification came much later, in 2014.
PM-JAY is the world's largest (not second-largest) government-funded health assurance scheme, so option 1 is the incorrect statement.
PM-JAY gives a cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year, not ₹10 lakh, so option 4 is not a feature.
Regional Engineering Colleges (RECs) were converted and renamed National Institutes of Technology (NITs) in 2002.
The notes do not cover Unnat Bharat Abhiyan 2.0; it was launched by the Ministry of Education (formerly MHRD).
PMAY-Urban, which targets EWS/LIG/MIG households including slum dwellers, was launched in 2015.
PMAY-U is affordable urban housing, PMKVY is youth skilling, Ujjwala gives free LPG connections to BPL households and Ayushman Bharat is health insurance for poor families, so A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.
The Mukhyamantri Vishwakarma Pension Yojana is a Rajasthan scheme.
The NPS-Traders scheme covers traders with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, aged 18-40, with ₹3,000 pension. The notes do not list NPS members as eligible, so option 3 is the incorrect statement.
The ESI wage ceiling is ₹21,000 a month; ₹25,000 is the EPF ceiling and ₹15,000 is the older EPF ceiling.
The notes do not state how many ESI hospitals Andhra Pradesh approved in February 2021; the answer is seven.
The Meghalaya Plateau comprises the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills, whereas the Bhuban Hills (Barak Valley, Assam) are not part of it.
The Deccan Trap fissure eruptions of basaltic lava began at the end of the Cretaceous (continuing into early Eocene), making the north-western Peninsula a great volcanic centre then.

Deccan Traps date to the Cretaceous-Eocene (A-3), which matches option 2. The notes support only this item, while the other pairings (Western Ghats-Late Cenozoic, Aravalli-Pre-Cambrian, Narmada-Tapti alluvium-Pleistocene) follow from standard dating.
Both statements are true descriptions of the Peninsular plateau regions, but the north-eastern region does not explain the extent of the south-western region, so R is not a correct explanation of A.
Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat and Pal Ghat are passes of the Western Ghats, while Goran Ghat is not in the Western Ghats.
Lima is the capital of Peru; the notes do not state this, but Lisbon (Portugal) and Madrid (Spain) are European capitals.
Lithuania borders Poland, Belarus, Latvia and Russia's Kaliningrad, but not Ukraine.
Tokyo, not Kyoto, is the capital of Japan, so the Japan–Kyoto pair is wrong.
Helsinki is the capital of Finland; Denmark, Norway and Sweden have Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm.
Korea is traditionally called the Land of the Morning Calm; Japan is the Land of the Rising Sun.
Vienna is the capital of Austria, not of Australia, whose capital is Canberra.
Zimbabwe was formerly Southern Rhodesia. Gold Coast was Ghana and Belgian Congo was the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Great Britain comprises England, Wales and Scotland only, not Northern Ireland, so I is wrong. England is about 130,000 of 243,000 sq km, roughly 54%, under 60%, so II is correct.
Seoul is the capital of South Korea; North Korea's capital is Pyongyang.
Russia is the largest country by area, ahead of Canada, the USA and China.
South Africa's legislative capital, where Parliament sits, is Cape Town. Pretoria is the executive capital.
Aleppo is in Syria and Mazar-e-Sharif is in Afghanistan. Kirkuk and Mosul are in Iraq, so II and III are wrong.
Sierra Leone is in West Africa. Panama, Honduras and Guatemala are in Central America, part of North America.
Malé is the capital of the Maldives. Malabo is the capital of Equatorial Guinea, so this pair is wrong.
Japan is an island country with no land borders and is larger than New Zealand, the Philippines and Cuba.
Ethiopia's capital is Addis Ababa. Lusaka is the capital of Zambia.
Nairobi is Kenya's capital, Kampala is Uganda's, Tashkent is Uzbekistan's and Kiev is Ukraine's, giving A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.
Siam is the former name of Thailand, changed officially in 1939 and again in 1949.
The Lahore Conspiracy Case hanging of 23 March 1931 took Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. Dutt got life transportation and Bismil was hanged in 1927 for Kakori.
Azad was the sole Kakori revolutionary who escaped arrest.
Bhagat Singh was hanged on 23 March 1931 with Sukhdev and Rajguru. B.K. Dutt got life and Azad died in 1931 at Alfred Park.
Azad was born at Bhavra in Jhabua district, MP. The notes give only Bhavra, MP, without naming the district.
Azad died in a police encounter at Alfred Park, Prayagraj, in 1931, where he shot himself. He was not hanged.
The Philosophy of the Bomb was written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra as a reply to Gandhi's The Cult of the Bomb.
Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb in reply to Gandhi's The Cult of the Bomb.
Pritilata Waddedar led the raid on the Pahartali European Club in Chittagong and then took cyanide.
The raid took place on 18 April 1930 and was led by Surya Sen (Masterda). The other options give wrong years or people from other events.
PMGSY was launched on 25 Dec 2000, earlier than the other listed schemes (SAGY 2014, Antyodaya and DDU-GKY in the 2010s), so it is the earliest.
CAPART was set up in 1986 under the Ministry of Rural Development, New Delhi, to fund voluntary organisations and promote rural technology.
The notes do not state this target year. The commonly cited Bharat Nirman target for connecting all villages with a population of 1000+ was 2009, but the answer of 2007 is taken as given.
SPMRM aims to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services and create well-planned Rurban clusters. It does not target literacy, sex ratio or free electricity.
PURA, the idea of providing urban amenities in rural areas, was advocated by Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, who explained it in 2003. The other options are not associated with it.
Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism). Kevaladvaita/Advaita belongs to Shankara, not Ramananda or Chaitanya, and Avadhuta is not Shankara's philosophy.
Shankaracharya was born at Kaladi in Kerala, so Kerala is correct.
Ramananda was born at Prayag (traditionally 1299) in a Kanyakubja Brahmin family; Varanasi was only his main centre, not his birthplace.
Ramanuja was born at Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu, with Srirangam as his main centre.

A virus is a program that replicates itself and spreads from computer to computer, and malware is designed to disrupt or damage systems. Search engines, chat software and e-mail are not malicious by nature.
A computer virus is a program that can replicate itself and spread, not a biological agent affecting human health.
Worm is a recognised malware type that self-replicates across networks. Caterpillars and lions are not malware, and 'horses' is not the term (the correct term is Trojan horse).
A virus attaches to files and replicates itself to spread. A worm spreads without attaching, a trojan does not self-replicate, and phishing is a deceptive-message attack.
A rootkit gives administrator-level access and hides other malware, which makes it the hardest type to detect.

Malware is software designed to disrupt, damage or gain unauthorised access, not merely defective software with bugs, so statement I is wrong. Rootkits, viruses, worms, trojans and spyware are all malware types, so II is right.
Creeper (1971) was the first self-copying program/virus, on ARPANET. The other options are later malware.
Creeper (1971) is the first virus; Elk Cloner (1982) was only the first virus in the wild.
Creeper (1971) is regarded as the first self-copying program/virus, spreading on ARPANET and later removed by Reaper.
The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1981 (29 March 1981, in force 16 May 1981), so option 2 is correct.

The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella law enacted to protect and improve the environment and control pollution. The Water Act 1974 deals only with water pollution, so it is not the answer.

The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella law enacted to protect and improve the environment and control pollution. The Water Act 1974 deals only with water pollution, so it is not the answer.
Coringa sanctuary lies at the Godavari mouth and has tidal mangrove forest (Rhizophora, Avicennia), not evergreen, thorn or montane forest.
AP's recorded forest area of 37,258 sq km ranks 8th in India.
AP's recorded forest area of 37,258 sq km ranks 8th in India.
Recorded forest area of 37,258 sq km is 22.86% of AP's geographical area.
AP's recorded forest area (37,258 sq km) ranks 8th in India.
AP's recorded forest area is 37,258 sq km (22.86% of the state).
AP is 8th in India with a recorded forest area of 37,258 sq km.
ISFR 2019 puts AP's forest cover at 29,137.40 sq km (17.88%).
In ISFR 2019 East Godavari had the highest forest cover (4,994.10 sq km); Kadapa leads in forest area and Visakhapatnam in forest percentage, which are the tempting options.
East Godavari has the highest ISFR 2019 forest cover, 4,994.10 sq km.
In the 2023-24 fire season AP was first in India, with 5,286.76 sq km of forest area affected.
Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to AP's Seshachalam and nearby ranges. Teak, mahogany and deodar are not AP endemics.
APFDC's largest plantation area up to Dec 2021 is Eucalyptus (33,584 ha), more than coffee, cashew or bamboo.
Red sanders is endemic to the Seshachalam-Palakonda-Veligonda ranges of southern AP, so statement I is right. It is a dry deciduous species, not a tropical rainforest tree, so II is wrong.
The forebrain (cerebrum) is the seat of thinking, intelligence and memory, whereas the midbrain and hindbrain handle reflexes and coordination. The notes do not cover this.
Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testes secrete androgens such as testosterone, while Sertoli cells nourish sperm. The notes only mention testes making testosterone in general.
The common bile duct and the pancreatic duct both open into the duodenum, not the stomach, so only statement II is correct.
The human neck has 7 cervical vertebrae, the same number as in most mammals.
Digestion starts in the buccal cavity, where salivary amylase begins breaking down starch. Protein digestion starts in the stomach, which is the tempting wrong option.
The appendix is a vestigial organ with no significant function in humans. The heart, kidney and lungs are vital functioning organs.
Muscle contraction is triggered by Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and relaxation occurs when Ca2+ is pumped back into it. It does not depend on Ca2+ from the blood or on Zn.
Tooth enamel is mainly calcium phosphate in the form of hydroxyapatite, the hardest substance in the body.
Narrower vessels increase resistance to blood flow, so blood pressure rises.
The kidneys filter urea and other nitrogenous wastes out of the blood, so when they fail these wastes accumulate in the blood. This is why dialysis is needed.
The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.
The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.
Food first meets salivary amylase in the mouth, which begins starch digestion. Pepsin acts in the stomach and trypsin in the intestine, so both come later.
Blood, bone and cartilage are connective tissues. Skin is an organ made of epithelial and other tissues, not a connective tissue.
Muscle tissue contains the contractile proteins actin and myosin, which produce contraction.
During sudden strenuous activity muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up, causing cramps.
Sweat is mostly water with dissolved salts (NaCl) and a little urea. Its salt content makes it taste salty.
All blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, originate from stem cells in the bone marrow. Lymph nodes and the spleen only store or mature lymphocytes.
G.N. Taylor, Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry, started Anglo-Vernacular schools across most of Andhra; the other names are distractors.
Bt technology is used in cotton (Bt cotton), which carries a bacterial gene giving resistance to bollworm. The notes do not cover this, so it is not linked.
Sunhemp (sanai) is the common green manure crop in India, grown and ploughed in to enrich the soil. Wheat, cotton and rice are food or fibre crops, not green manure.
Hansa, Jaya and Padma are listed rice varieties, while Jawala is not a rice variety, so it is the correct answer.
Pusa RH-10 is the hybrid Basmati rice variety, while Pusa Sugandh-3, Sugandh-5 and Pusa Basmati-1 are non-hybrid varieties. The notes do not cover this.
Pusa Sugandh-5 is an aromatic Basmati-type rice variety developed at IARI. The notes list only Mahi Sugandha as a Basmati variety, so they do not settle it.

Gandhi's non-violence and civil disobedience drew on Ruskin (Unto This Last), Tolstoy (love and non-violence) and Thoreau (right to break unjust laws). The other options include people such as Churchill, Irwin or Truman who were not his influences.
Ghanshyam Das Birla was the industrialist close to Gandhi who supported working with capitalism for a common goal. The notes do not cover this fact, so no line is linked.
Vinoba Bhave launched the Bhoodan movement in 1951, with the first land gift at Pochampalli. Gandhi and JP are not associated with starting it.
Anthracite has 86–97% carbon, the highest of all coal types, above bituminous, lignite and peat.
Gondwana coal holds about 98% of reserves, while Tertiary coal is younger and includes lignite, so the claim that bituminous coal occurs in both is the incorrect statement.
